children.translated_text: As they make heaven and liberation manifest at the arising of the world,
I praise <s>Caṇḍikā</s> and <s>Candraśekhara</s>, removers of the disease of worldly existence.
Together with oils, roots, and fruits for <s>rasa</s>, subsidiary minerals, and metals,
the discipline of preparing <s>rasa</s>, effective even for what is impossible, is now explained with assurance.
For the fame and livelihood of physicians, and for the welfare of the sick,
for the curiosity of disputants and for bodily perfection in the aged,
for the sake of mantra-attainment among mantra practitioners, and as the cause of many wonders,
this five-section treatise bestows benefit on practitioners.
In the section on <s>rasa</s>, mercury-attainment arises for physicians and the sick;

children.text: vādināṃ vādakhaṇḍe ca vṛddhānāṃ ca rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: in the section on debate it arises for disputants, and in the <s>rasāyana</s> section for the aged;
and in the mantra section it arises for mantra practitioners.
There is absolutely no doubt for those who examine each of those sections.
When killed, it kills old age and death; when stupefied, it destroys diseases;

children.text: dhatte ca khegatiṃ baddhaḥ ko'nyaḥ sūtātkṛpākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: when bound, it grants movement through the sky. What other than <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is so compassionate?
It is regarded as the destroyer of old age, death, poverty, and disease.

children.text: mūrchito harate vyādhīn naso dehe carannapi ||
children.translated_text: When stupefied it removes diseases, even while moving in the body.
When bound it can bewilder others, and when dead it can revive others;

children.text: mūrchito bodhayedanyāṃstaṃ sūtaṃ ko na sevate ||
children.translated_text: when stupefied it can awaken others. Who would not serve that <s>sūta</s> (mercury)?
Long life, wealth, freedom from disease, digestive fire, intelligence, great strength,
beauty, youth, and loveliness come through the worship and practice of <s>rasa</s>.
One should kill mercury after it has been digested, and stupefy it with sulfur;

children.text: baddhaḥ syād drutisatvābhyāṃ rasasyaivaṃ tridhā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it becomes bound by liquefaction and essence. Thus the course of <s>rasa</s> is threefold.
Faultless <s>rasa</s> is <s>Brahmā</s>; when stupefied, it is <s>Janārdana</s>;
when killed, it has the form of <s>Rudra</s>; when bound, it is directly <s>Maheśvara</s>.
As a penetrator of body and metals, <s>sūta</s> (mercury), O goddess, is <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
By seeing the king of <s>rasa</s>, one drives away the sin of killing a Brahmin.
By touching it, O goddess, one destroys the sin of killing a cow; there is no doubt about this.
How much more, O goddess, by eating it: the supreme state is attained.
Because it is useful in a small dose and is not accompanied by aversion,
and because it quickly gives health, <s>rasa</s> is superior to other medicines.
Whatever was formerly taught by <s>Śambhu</s> in the section on <s>rasa</s> and in <s>rasāyana</s>,
and in the <s>Dīpikā</s> and <s>Rasamaṅgala</s> for the praise of <s>rasa</s>,
whatever was taught by <s>Nāgārjuna</s> for the welfare of the sick,
and whatever was stated by <s>Carpaṭisiddha</s> in the <s>Svargavaidyakapālika</s>,
whatever is taught in many <s>rasaśāstras</s>, compendia, and <s>āgamas</s>,
whatever is taught in the tantra of <s>Vāgbhaṭa</s>, in <s>Suśruta</s>, and in the <s>Vaidyasāgara</s>,

children.text: anyaiśca bahubhiḥ siddhair yad uktaṃ ca vilokya tat
children.translated_text: and whatever was taught by many other perfected masters, having examined all that,
wherever something was impossible, and wherever a medicine was difficult to obtain,
I have set aside all of that and extracted the essential part.

children.text: kvacicchāstre kriyā nāsti kramasaṃkhyā na ca kvacit ||
children.translated_text: In some treatise there is no procedure, and in another no sequence or number;

children.text: mātrā yuktiḥ kvacinnāsti sampradāyo na ca kvacit
children.translated_text: in some there is no measure or rationale, and in another no received tradition.

children.text: tena siddhirna tatrāsti rase vātha rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: Therefore attainment is not found there, whether in <s>rasa</s> or in <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: vaidye vāde prayoge ca yasmādyatno mayā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Since effort has been made by me in medicine, debate, and practical application,
whatever I have learned from the mouth of the guru, and whatever I have experienced myself,
all that is now being made manifest for the welfare of the world.

children.text: śrīmān sūtanṛpo dadāti vilasaṃllakṣmīṃ vapuḥ śāśvataṃsvānāṃ prītikarīm acañcalamano māteva puṃsāṃ yathā
children.translated_text: The glorious king <s>Sūta</s> gives shining wealth and an enduring body, pleasing to his own people, just as a mother is to men of steady mind.

children.text: anyo nāsti śarīranāśakagadapradhvaṃsakārī tataḥ kāryaṃ nityamahotsavaiḥ prathamataḥ sūtād vapuḥsādhanam ||
children.translated_text: There is no other destroyer of the diseases that ruin the body; therefore the attainment of the body through <s>sūta</s> should first be pursued with constant celebrations.

children.text: sākṣādakṣayadāyako bhuvi nṛṇāṃ pañcatvamuccaiḥ kuto mūrcchāṃ mūrchitavigraho gadabhṛtāṃ hantyuñcakaiḥ prāṇinām
children.translated_text: Since he directly gives imperishability to people on earth, how could death have great power? With a stupefied body he forcefully destroys the ailments of diseased living beings.

children.text: baddhaṃ prāpya surāsurendracaritāṃ tāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ prāpayet
children.translated_text: When one has obtained the bound form, it causes one to reach those various states enjoyed by the lords of gods and demons.
May this glorious king <s>Sūta</s>, skilled in benefiting others, protect the world.
What is elsewhere is here; what is here is nowhere else.
This is the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>, composed by <s>Nityanātha</s>.
Therefore one should carefully perform the excellent processing of <s>rasa</s>.
A physician who is skilled in procedures but has not understood the meaning of the treatise

children.text: yama eva sa vijñeyaḥ martyānāṃ mṛtyurūpadhṛk ||
children.translated_text: should be known as <s>Yama</s> himself, the embodied form of death for mortals.

children.text: nāgo vaṅgo malo vahniścāṃcalyaṃ ca viṣaṃ giriḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, impurity, fire, instability, poison, mountain,
and unbearable heat are forbidden great faults residing in mercury.
From <s>nāga</s> arise swelling and breast-lumps; from <s>vaṅga</s>, skin disease; from impurity, pain;
from fire comes burning, from instability destruction of seed, and from poison, death.
From mountain comes eruption; from unbearable heat, delusion arises from these faults.
When <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is free from faults, it removes death and old age.
Although this <s>rasa</s> is directly nectar, when joined with faults it is poison.
Therefore purification of <s>rasa</s> is prescribed for the sake of cleansing away its faults.
<s>Rasa</s> should be taken under an auspicious lunar mansion, in the measure of one hundred <s>palas</s>,
or fifty, or twenty-five, or twelve, or even one.
One should not undertake the excellent processing of <s>rasa</s> with less than a <s>pala</s>.
The processing and worship of <s>rasa</s> should be done with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra.
To the non-terrifying, and then to the terrifying, to those more terrible than the terrible,
to all, to every form of all, homage to you, the forms of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: niḥsāraṃ vīkṣya viśvaṃ gadavikalavapur vyāptam evātitaptam
children.translated_text: Seeing the world as essenceless, with bodies impaired by disease and entirely afflicted,
again, the method of the king <s>Sūta</s>, ocean of compassion and treasure of all virtues...
Having carefully studied the treatises on <s>sūta</s> (mercury), for the attainment of what living beings desire,
let the lords of enjoyers and the lords of gods, whose minds are very expansive, listen aloud to what I have said.

children.text: yāvatsūtaṃ na śuddhaṃ na ca mṛtamatha no mūrchitaṃ gandhabandhaṃ
children.translated_text: So long as the <s>sūta</s> has not been purified, killed, swooned, or bound with sulphur,

children.text: no vajraṃ māritaṃ vā na ca gaganavadho nāpasūtāśca śuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: and so long as diamond has not been killed, the sky-born substance has not been subdued, and the apasūtas have not been purified,

children.text: svarṇādyaṃ sarvalohaṃ viṣamapi na mṛtaṃ tailapāto na yāvat
children.translated_text: so long as gold and all other metals, even poison, have not been killed, and the oil-fall has not yet been accomplished,

children.text: tāvadvaidyaḥ kva siddho bhavati vasubhujāṃ maṇḍale ślāghyayogyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: until then how can a physician be perfected and worthy of praise in the circle of kings?
Now, therefore, I shall explain the removal of the eight defects.
With powders of brick and turmeric, each amounting to one-sixteenth part of the mercury,
one should grind it for a day in a heated mortar with the liquids produced from jambīra citrus.
The mortar may be made of iron, or else of stone or rock.
One should wash the <s>sūta</s> with sour gruel in order to pacify the defect of lead.
With powder of viśālā and aṅkola one should destroy the defect of tin.

children.text: rājavṛkṣo malaṃ hanti citrakaṃ hanti vahnijam
children.translated_text: Rājavṛkṣa removes impurity, and citraka removes the defect born of fire.
Black dhattūra removes instability, and the three myrobalans remove poison.
The three pungents destroy heaviness, and trikaṇṭaka removes unbearable heat.
For each defect, powder equal to one kalā part, together with kanyā, should be used there.
After straining the <s>sūta</s> through a good cloth and placing it in the mortar in due order,
one should carefully grind each item every day for seven nights.
After taking it out, the wise person should wash it in an earthen vessel with warm sour gruel.
Freed from all defects and rid of the seven coverings,
this <s>sūta</s> becomes purified and is fit for medical practice.
Having lit a fire of goat dung and husks, one should place it on the ground,
and should grind the <s>rasa</s> there as prescribed, in a mortar set above it.
With śrīkhaṇḍa, devadāru, kākatuṇḍī, and the liquids of jayā,
and after adding the juices of karkoṭī, mūṣalī, and kanyā, one should grind it.
For one day, in a distillation apparatus, one should employ it when purified.
One should grind the <s>sūta</s> for a day with kanyā and powder of niśā.
One should distill it in a distillation apparatus; the <s>rasa</s> will become properly purified.
Hiṅgula should be ground with the juices of pāribhadra for the measure of one yāma,
or it should be distilled in a pātāla apparatus with the juices of jambīra fruits.
One should use that <s>sūta</s>, free from the seven coverings, in the preparation.
Thus these purifications are known; one may perform any one of them as desired.
Now I shall describe these herbs for killing purified <s>sūta</s>.
Brahmadaṇḍī, meghanādā, citraka, and tṛṇamustikā,
vajravallī, balā, dry ginger, kaṭutumbī, and ardhacandrikā,
viṣamuṣṭi, arka, lākṣā, gokṣura, and kākatuṇḍikā,
kanyā, caṇḍālinī tuber, sarpākṣī, and sarapuṅkhikā,
vastā, raktā, agranirguṇḍī, lajjālī, and devadālikā,
jātī, jayantī, vārāhī, bhūkadamba, and kuraṇṭaka,
koṣātakī, nīrakaṇā, lāṅgalī, and sahadevikā,
cakramarda, amṛtākanda, kākamācī, and ravipriyā,
viṣṇukrāntā, hastiśuṇḍī, the milk of snuk, bhṛṅgarāṭ, and paṭu:
these herbs have been declared as agents for killing mercury.

children.text: etāḥ samastā vyastā vā deyā hyaṣṭādaśādhikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All of these, or individual ones, should be added; more than eighteen are prescribed.
One should grind the red herb in the urine of cows that have not calved.
With its liquids, purified <s>sūta</s>, joined with an equal amount of sulphur,
should be ground without interruption for four yāmas in a heated mortar.
That lump should be distilled in an apparatus in a great puṭa of thirty dung-cakes.

children.text: evaṃ daśapuṭair māryaṃ mardyaṃ pātyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: In this way it should be killed through ten puṭas, being ground and distilled again and again.
After taking it out, it should again be ground and placed inside a diamond crucible.
It should be cooked in the puṭa called bhūdhara; after ten times it becomes ash.
It should again be ground with each liquid; this diamond-like <s>sūtaka</s> is perfected.
Mercury killed by herbs, without the procedure of digestion,
will certainly not act upon the body and metals, though it removes disease.
One should grind the <s>rasa</s> with twice its quantity of sulphur oil,
for one day, or else with liquids produced from sarpākṣī, viṣṇukrāntā, and bhṛṅga.
One should grind it for three days with the liquids, in a great puṭa of thirty dung-cakes.
Cooked in this way eight times, the <s>rasa</s> certainly becomes ash.
One should grind <s>sūta</s> for three days with the water of white aṅkoṭa root,
and heat it in a crucible in the bhūdhara apparatus; it becomes ash.
One should grind devadālī and harikrāntā with āranāla sour gruel.
With that one should cause the <s>sūtaka</s> to be raised up by blowing seven times.

children.text: taṃ sūtaṃ kharpare kuryāddattvā dattvā caturdravam
children.translated_text: That <s>sūta</s> should be placed in a potsherd, adding the four liquids again and again.
It should be cooked over a hearth fire; the ash will resemble dawn-red color.
One should impregnate sugar and hiṅgu with the milks produced from wood-udumbara,

children.text: saptavāraṃ prayatnena śodhyaṃ peṣyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: purifying and grinding it again and again with care seven times.
A decoction, one-sixteenth in amount, should be made from the five parts of wood-udumbara.

children.text: dattvā tena punar mardyaṃ hiṃgu vaṅgaraseśvaram ||
children.translated_text: Adding that, one should again grind hiṅgu, tin, and the lord of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: kṣiptvā nirudhya mūṣāyāṃ bhūdharākhye puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: After placing it in a crucible and sealing it, one should cook it in the puṭa called bhūdhara.

children.text: aṣṭadhā mriyate sūto deyaṃ hiṃgu puṭe puṭe ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sūta</s> is killed by eight repetitions; hiṅgu should be given in each puṭa.
One should powder the seeds of apāmārga and likewise of castor.
That powder should be added to mercury and sealed in a crucible itself.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a small puṭa; by four repetitions it becomes ash.
In the bulb produced from kaṭutumbī, in the womb, indeed with a woman's milk...
Mercury is killed in seven ways. One should steam it with a cow-dung fire.
Having ground it with the juices of the roots of <s>aṅkola</s>, one should triturate it in a mortar.
At the end of the day one should seal up the mercury combined with sulfur.
One should heat it in a closed firing in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, and at the end of the day remove it.
One should triturate equal quantities of <s>dhānyābhra</s> mica and mercury with killing liquids.

children.text: dinaikaṃ tena kalkena vastre liptvā ca vartikām ||
children.translated_text: For one day, with that paste, one should smear a wick on cloth.

children.text: vilipya tailairvartiṃ tām eraṇḍotthaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: One should again and again smear that wick with oils produced from castor.
After lighting it, one should collect in a vessel what has fallen down from it.
That becomes black ash, and it should again be triturated for three watches.
It should be cooked for one day in the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s>; there is no doubt.
Mercury becomes killed immediately, and one should apply it in the appropriate formulations.
Take two <s>palas</s> of purified mercury and purified sulfur in half the measure of the mercury.
One should triturate them continuously for one day with killing liquids.

children.text: baddhvā tu bhūdhare yantre dinaikaṃ mārayet puṭāt ||
children.translated_text: Having bound them in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, one should kill them for one day by closed firing.
There should be two parts of burnt husk and one part of anthill clay,
one part of iron slag and one part of white stone.
With a little human hair, one should grind it with goat's milk.
It should be firmly triturated for two watches; with this one prepares a blind-sealed crucible.
After drying it, smearing it with those pastes, and sealing it completely,
it is called a diamond crucible, a proper killer of mercury.

children.text: śvetaṃ pītaṃ tathā raktaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ceti caturvidham
children.translated_text: White, yellow, red, and black: these are its four kinds.
These are the characteristics of mercury ash; each succeeding one is superior.
Now, therefore, the killing of the seed prior to digestion is described.

children.text: ajīrṇaṃ cāpyabījaṃ ca sūtakaṃ yastu mārayet ||
children.translated_text: Whoever kills mercury that is undigested and without seed

children.text: brahmahā sa durācāro mama drohī maheśvari
children.translated_text: is a killer of a Brahmin, wicked in conduct, and hostile to me, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.
Therefore, by every effort, one should kill the mercury after it has been digested.

children.text: saṃsthāpya gomayaṃ bhūmau pakvamūṣāṃ tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Having placed cow-dung on the ground, then a baked crucible,

children.text: tanmadhye kaṭutumbyutthaṃ tailaṃ dattvā rasaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: one should put oil from bitter gourd in its middle and place the mercury there.

children.text: kākamācīrasaṃ deyaṃ tailaṃ tulyaṃ tataḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Juice of <s>kākamācī</s> should be added, and then an equal amount of oil.

children.text: gandhakaṃ vrīhimātraṃ ca kṣiptvā taṃ ca nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: After adding sulfur the size of a rice grain, one should seal it.

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe pāvako deyaḥ pūrṇaṃ vā vahnikharparam
children.translated_text: Fire should be placed on its top, or a fire-vessel filled with fire.

children.text: svāṅgaśītalatāṃ jñātvā jīrṇe taile ca gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: When one knows that it has cooled of itself and that the oil and sulfur have been digested,

children.text: kākamācīdravaṃ cāgnau dattvā dattvā ca jārayet
children.translated_text: one should repeatedly add <s>kākamācī</s> liquid and digest it in the fire.

children.text: mūṣādho gomayaṃ cātra dattvā codadharvaṃ ca pāvakam ||
children.translated_text: Here cow-dung should be placed below the crucible and fire above it.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇaṃ gandhakaṃ jāryaṃ sūtasyaivaṃ mukhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Sulfur six times the quantity should be digested; in this way mercury obtains its mouth.
One should triturate that mercury again and again with liquids produced from citron.
First in portions of one sixty-fourth, then again one thirty-second,
and then one sixteenth part of purified gold leaf should be placed into the mercury.
The gold, ground with peacock bile and with oils produced from mustard,
should be smeared; one should add the mercury and triturate for a watch with citron juices.
One should cook it as before in a crucible, having filled it with citron juices.
One should seal it and, applying fire carefully, digest it.

children.text: grāse grāse ca tanmardyaṃ jambīrāṇāṃ dravaiḥ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: At each feed one should triturate it firmly with the juices of citrons.
If bile and oil are absent, use radish, salt, and sulfur.
Having ground them with citron water, one should smear the gold leaf.

children.text: ityevaṃ jāraṇā kāryā tataḥ sūtaṃ ca mārayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus the digestion is to be performed; afterward one should kill the mercury.
Or one may kill mouthless mercury by means of a <s>viḍa</s> compound.
I shall explain the <s>viḍa</s> here; the best of physicians should prepare it.
Conch powder should be treated for a day in the sun with the latex of <s>arka</s>.
In the same way, <s>dhūmasāra</s> should be treated for one day with liquids produced from citron.
<s>Suvarcala</s> should be boiled with goat urine for four watches.
And <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> should be boiled for one day with human urine.
<s>Sajjīkṣāra</s>, <s>tintiḍīka</s>, <s>kāśīśa</s>, and <s>śilājatu</s>
should each separately be treated with liquids produced from citron for four watches.
<s>Jayapāla</s> seeds, deprived of their skins, should be treated for a day with radish liquids.
Rock salt, borax, and <s>guñjā</s> should be treated for a day with liquids from <s>śigru</s> root.
All this, in equal parts, should be ground with liquids produced from citron.
One should carefully preserve that ball; this <s>viḍa</s> is the submarine fire.
With this one should triturate mercury; in a heated mortar it consumes
gold, mica, and all metals as desired and digests them.
One should kill it by the preceding method; the killing is described here.
Having pulled up <s>kumbhī</s> together with its root, one should grind it well with cow urine.
One should triturate mercury with its liquids for one day in a <s>kānta</s> sealed vessel.
After coating it, controlling layers should be placed, and the same should be applied above and below.

children.text: mṛdvagninā dinaikaṃ tu pacecculyāṃ mṛto bhavet ||
children.translated_text: One should cook it for one day on a hearth with a gentle fire; it will become killed.

children.text: goghṛtaṃ gandhakaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭvā piṇḍīṃ prakalpayet
children.translated_text: Having ground cow ghee, sulfur, and mercury, one should form a lump.
Placing it in the middle of an aloe leaf, one should wrap it with thread.

children.text: taṃ kāntasampuṭe ruddhvā tribhir laghupuṭaiḥ pacet
children.translated_text: Sealing it in a <s>kānta</s> vessel, one should cook it with three light closed firings.

children.text: tato dhmāte bhavedbhasma cāndhamūṣe kṣayaṃ dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Then, when blown, it becomes ash; in a blind crucible, its reduction is certain.
Taking ripe fruits of the <s>śāka</s> tree, one should purify them.
One should grind them with the latex of <s>arka</s> and smear the crucible with that.
It is filled with powder of the afterbirth produced by a first-calved cow.
Having sealed mercury inside it, when it is blown it attains the state of ash.
<s>Karkoṭakī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, and <s>kaṭutumbikā</s>...
<s>Kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, <s>kākinī</s>, and <s>kākamañjarī</s>:
having ground these, one should make a coating for diamond-crucibles with them and place the <s>rasa</s> in it.
The <s>rasa</s> should be rubbed for one day with those same freshly arisen juices.

children.text: ruddhvātha bhūdhare pacyād aṣṭavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after sealing it, one should cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus eight times again and again.
One should rub it and place it in those coated crucibles; when sealed and blown upon, it becomes killed.
It should be rubbed firmly for four <s>yāmas</s> with regulating juices,
and cooked slowly over a gentle fire with double quantities of sulfur-oils.
Until it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> lump, each should be sealed in an iron capsule.
Having ground <s>harītakī</s> in water, one should make a small crucible with iron slag.
Putting it in the middle of that, one should close the capsule again.
Above it, having made it in the form of a receiver, one should pour in molten <s>nāga</s> (lead).
One should blow strongly until the lead has melted.
And one should not blow again until it has become hard.
Thus, when blown again and again, the <s>rasa</s> is killed in three <s>yāmas</s>.
Next I shall state the regulating substances for the killing operation of <s>sūta</s>.
<s>Sarpākṣī</s>, <s>kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>matsyākṣī</s>, and <s>śarapuṅkhikā</s>,
<s>kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>śikhiśikhā</s>, <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, and <s>ākhuparṇikā</s>,
<s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>utpalaciñcikā</s>,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>vajralatā</s>, <s>vajrakandā</s>, and <s>triparṇikā</s>,
<s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>grīṣmasundara</s>,
<s>kākamācī</s>, <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>, <s>haridrā</s>, and <s>tilakarṇikā</s>,
<s>śvetārka</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>dhattūra</s>, <s>mṛgadūrvā</s>, and <s>harītakī</s>,
<s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>mūṣalī</s>, <s>puṅkhā</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, and red <s>citraka</s>,
<s>tagara</s>, <s>śūraṇa</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>mayaṅkā</s>, and <s>potakokila</s>,
<s>saindhava</s>, white <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>sāmbhara</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>,
<s>viṣṇukāntā</s>, <s>somavallī</s>, <s>vraṇaghnī</s>, and <s>yakṣalocana</s>,
<s>vyāghrapādī</s>, <s>haṃsapadī</s>, <s>vṛścikālī</s>, and <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>,
<s>svayambhūkusuma</s>, <s>kuñcī</s>, <s>hastiśuṇḍī</s>, and <s>indravāruṇī</s>,
and also the seeds of <s>ahaskara</s>: all these are regulators in every operation.

children.text: etāḥ samastā vyastā vā deyā hyaṣṭādaśādhikāḥ
children.translated_text: All of these, or each separately, may be applied; indeed more than eighteen may be used.
These should be employed in the killing, stupefying, and binding of <s>rasa</s>.
Having ground the preceding regulators with the urine of cows that have not calved,
one should rub <s>sūta</s> with their liquids in the sequence stated before.
Thus the calcination process has been stated, and the killing has been described.

children.text: parīkṣā mārite sūte kartavyā ca yathoditā ||
children.translated_text: When <s>sūta</s> has been killed, the test should be performed as taught.
When, heated below by a chaff-fire, it remains undiminished,
then one should know it to be ash; one should inspect it for a <s>yāma</s> in the hearth.
Mercury killed by herbs should be used in all formulae.
This calcined <s>sūta</s> removes old age, poverty, and disease.
When stupefied it destroys illness; when bound it should be used everywhere.
Now, therefore, the method for stupefying purified <s>sūta</s> is stated.
One should rub the <s>rasa</s> with <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, and <s>śūraṇa</s>.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu tadgolaṃ hiṅgunā veṣṭayed bahiḥ
children.translated_text: When the paste has disappeared, that ball should be wrapped externally with <s>hiṅgu</s>.
One should cook it, placed in a salt apparatus, for one day with a fierce fire.
When what is attached above has risen, one should bind it tightly with cloth.

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ tulyaṃ dattvā saumyānale pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed equal sulfur above and below, one should cook it over a gentle fire.

children.text: jīrṇe gandhe punar deyaṃ ṣaḍbhir vāraiḥ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: When the sulfur is digested, more should be added again, in six repetitions, equal each time.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇe gandhake jīrṇe mūrchito rogahā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When six times its quantity of sulfur has been digested, the stupefied mercury becomes disease-destroying.

children.text: gandhakaṃ madhusāraṃ ca śuddhasūtaṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Sulfur, <s>madhusāra</s>, and purified <s>sūta</s> should be taken in equal quantities.
One should cook them for one <s>yāma</s> in a mortar and place them in a glass bottle.
After sealing it, one should cook that in a sand apparatus for twelve <s>yāmas</s>.
When it is cooled by itself, one should break it open and discard the sulfur above.
Taking the <s>rasa</s> situated below, one should use it in all diseases.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ sūtārddhaṃ saindhavaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: One should add twice as much sulfur to purified <s>sūta</s>, and rock salt equal to half the <s>sūta</s>.
It should be rubbed for three days with the juices of white <s>jayantī</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā golaṃ ca saṃśoṣya kṣiptvā mūṣāṃ nirundhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made it into a ball, dried it, and placed it in a crucible, one should seal it.

children.text: śoṣayitvā dhamet kiṃcit sutaptāṃ tāṃ jale kṣipet
children.translated_text: After drying it, one should heat it somewhat by blowing and throw that very hot crucible into water.
Having taken the <s>rasa</s> out from that, infused with <s>trikaṇṭa</s> juice,
one should use it in all diseases, or heat it by blowing and cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.

children.text: rasārdhaṃ gandhakaṃ mardyaṃ ghṛtairyuktaṃ tu golakam ||
children.translated_text: Sulfur equal to half the <s>rasa</s> should be rubbed, and the ball should be mixed with ghee.
Having made that into a ball, one should bind it in cloth and cook it in a swing apparatus.
It should be placed in cow urine for one <s>yāma</s> and in human urine for three days.
One should dry it again, bind it in cloth, and wrap it always very tightly.
When dry, it should be sealed in a crucible and then cooked with a chaff-fire.
Turning the upper part downward and the lower part upward,
by this sort of reversal one should steam it for three days.

children.text: paścād uddhṛtya taṃ sūtaṃ yogavāhaṃ rujāpaham ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards, taking out that <s>sūta</s>, it is a carrier of medicinal efficacy and a remover of pain.
The feces of a newborn infant, <s>palāśa</s> seed,

children.text: cāṇḍālī rudhiraṃ sūtaṃ sūtapādaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>cāṇḍālī</s>, blood, <s>sūta</s>, and borax equal to a quarter of the <s>sūta</s>:

children.text: jayantyā mardayed drāvair dinaikaṃ tattu golakam
children.translated_text: one should rub these with the juices of <s>jayantī</s> for one day; that ball
should then be ground with <s>sahadevī</s>, and a copper capsule should be smeared with it.
Having placed the ball inside it, one should gently steam it for two <s>yāmas</s>
within a sand apparatus; after taking it out, then again

children.text: citrakaiḥ sahadevyā ca gandhakair lepayed bahiḥ
children.translated_text: one should smear the outside with <s>citraka</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and sulfur.
One should bind the capsule in cloth, smear it with clay, and dry it.
Having sealed it in a closed crucible and heated it with blowing, one should take out the sealed capsule.
Reduced to a fine powder, the great <s>rasa</s>, a carrier of medicines, removes diseases.
The sealed capsule should be equal to the <s>sūta</s> (mercury), by the procedure seen in the treatise.
<s>Gandhaka</s> (sulfur), together with mercury, should be ground for a day with the juices of <s>dhattūra</s>.

children.text: andhamūṣe dinaṃ svedyaṃ bhūdhare mūrchito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: It should be steamed for a day in a closed crucible; in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus it becomes mūrchita, stupefied.

children.text: kṛtvā ṣaḍaṅgulāṃ mūṣāṃ supakvāṃ mṛnmayīṃ dṛḍhām
children.translated_text: Having made a six-aṅgula crucible, well fired, earthen, and firm,
one should then smear the womb of the crucible with the roots of <s>bahulapatraka</s>.

children.text: tanmadhye sūtakaṃ kṣiptvā mūṣāṃ pūryāttu taddravaiḥ
children.translated_text: Putting mercury in the middle of it, one should fill the crucible with those liquids.
Having sealed it with salt-containing fittings, one should cook it on the hearth with blazing fire.
At the end of seven days, having taken it out, a barley-measure is fever-dispelling.

children.text: kāśīśaṃ saindhavaṃ sūtaṃ tulyaṃ tulyaṃ vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: One should grind <s>kāśīśa</s>, rock salt, and mercury in equal amounts.
For one part of this <s>kāśīśa</s>, <s>phullatūrikā</s> should be added.

children.text: stokastokaṃ kṣipet khalve triyāmaṃ caiva mūrchayet ||
children.translated_text: One should cast it little by little into the mortar and stupefy it for three yāmas.
Each should be one hundred niṣkas; it should be neither less nor more.
By means of the pot-sealed apparatus, one should cook it for a day over fierce fire.
Then one should take the stupefied mercury that has adhered above in the hearth.
The <s>rasa</s> should be steeped in the juices of <s>kuraṇṭaka</s> and ground in the sun.
Or one should grind it with leaves of creeping <s>karañja</s>, using the tip of the thumb.
When properly stupefied for one day, it should be employed in all diseases.
Now this is the procedure for purified <s>sūta</s>, even when it has been stupefied.

children.text: sūtatulyaṃ ghṛtaṃ jīrṇaṃ dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ ca gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: Old ghee equal to the mercury, and <s>gandhaka</s> equal to the two, should be used.
It should be ground for a day with the milks of <s>arka</s>; after sealing it, in a <s>bhūdhara</s>,
through a <s>puṭa</s> heating, the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Hairaṇyagarbhaka</s> becomes perfected.
In a bulb produced from bitter gourd, in the milk-bulb of the barren plant,
having taken one unripe bulb, one should then place a pellet in its hollow.
There should be ten niṣkas of purified mercury and one niṣka of purified <s>gandhaka</s>.

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣiped gandhaṃ pāṣāṇe taṃ tu kuṭṭayet ||
children.translated_text: One should add the sulfur little by little and pound it on a stone.

children.text: yāmamātre bhavet piṇḍī rasaṃ kande vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: In the space of a yāma it becomes a pellet; one should place the <s>rasa</s> in the bulb.

children.text: adha ūrdhvaṃ bhasma vaikrāntaṃ dattvā niṣkārddhamātrakam ||
children.translated_text: Below and above, one should add ash of <s>vaikrānta</s> in the measure of half a niṣka.

children.text: tataḥ kandasya majjābhirmukhaṃ baddhvā mṛdā dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Then, with the pulp of the bulb, one should close its mouth firmly with clay.
The ball, smeared everywhere to the measure of an aṅgula, should be dried.

children.text: pācayed bhūdhare yantre tata uddhṛtya punaḥ pacet
children.translated_text: One should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; then, having taken it out, cook it again.
One should turn the upper part downward; in just this way it should be inverted.
Gradually one should move it upward and cook it outside with pairs of cow-dung cakes.
Then, when it has been broken open, it should be collected; when bound, it should resemble a pomegranate.
Known by the name <s>Vaikrāntabaddha</s>, this should be used in all diseases.

children.text: athavā gandhapīṭhīnāṃ vastre baddhvā tu gandhakam
children.translated_text: Or, having tied <s>gandhaka</s> in a cloth among the sulfur pastes,

children.text: tulyaṃ dattvā nirundhyātha sampuṭe lohaje dṛḍhe ||
children.translated_text: after adding an equal amount, one should seal it in a firm iron capsule.
One should heat it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> until the sulfur is digested.
Thus it should be given again and again until the sulfur is sixfold.
In this way, when bound in sulfur, <s>sūta</s> becomes a remover of all diseases.
The crucible should be the width of a citron and sixteen aṅgulas in length.
It should be unfired but very firm, placed in the middle of a vessel of sand.

children.text: tribhāgaṃ vālukā lagnā pādāṃśena bahiḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Three parts should be covered with sand, while a quarter part remains outside.
One pala of powdered sulfur should be placed in the middle of the crucible.
After that one should add an equal amount of purified mercury, then a pala of sulfur.
One should set the vessel on the hearth, carefully covering the crucible.
One should cook it over a gentle fire until it becomes free of smoke.
When the sulfur-smoke has passed away, that crucible should be filled with juices of <s>kākamācī</s>.
When the liquid is digested, it should again be filled with juices of <s>nāgavallī</s> leaves.
When that is digested, after filling it with <s>dhattūra</s> juices, one should cook it again.
Until that sulfur is digested, again with <s>kākamācī</s> and the rest,
adding them again and again, one should cook the <s>rasa</s> in that same way, in the order beginning with <s>dhattūra</s>.
Having broken the crucible, one should collect the <s>rasa</s>, which removes old age and disease.
This sulfur-bound one should be used everywhere among <s>yogavāhas</s>, carriers of medicines.
When the mercury has the appearance of lampblack, having abandoned its dense volatility,

children.text: mūrchitaḥ sa tadā jñeyo nānārasagataḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: then it should be known as stupefied, sometimes having entered various rasas.
Endowed with sweetness and heaviness, like the sun in brilliance,
when it stands in the midst of fire, then that is the characteristic of <s>vṛkṣa</s>.

children.text: sa jayati rasarājo mṛtyuśaṅkāpahārī sakalaguṇanidhānaḥ kāyakalpādhikārī
children.translated_text: Victorious is that king of <s>rasa</s>, remover of the fear of death, treasury of all virtues, entitled to rejuvenation of the body.

children.text: valipalitavināśaṃ sevanādvīryavṛddhiṃ sthiramapi kurute yaḥ kāminīnāṃ prasaṅge ||
children.translated_text: Through use it causes the destruction of wrinkles and gray hair, an increase of virility, and steadiness even in intercourse with women.

children.text: ityetā māritāḥ sūtā mūrchitā baddham āgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus these mercuries, killed, stupefied, and brought to a bound state,
each becomes a <s>yogavāha</s>; each should be applied in its corresponding formulation.
The killed form is for bodily perfection; the stupefied form is for the destruction of disease.
In some diseases one uses <s>rasa</s>-ash; for the body, in some cases, the stupefied form.
One should employ the bound form for both purposes, by the procedure seen in the treatise.
The prepared <s>rasa</s> should be kept in ivory, horn, or bamboo.
Mercury destroys worms and skin disease, gives strength, longevity, and sight.
By use it destroys all diseases; it is appetizing, heavy, and astringent.

children.text: sūte guṇānāṃ śatakoṭir vajre cābhre sahasraṃ kanake śataikam
children.translated_text: In <s>sūta</s> there are a hundred crores of virtues; in diamond and mica, a thousand; in gold, one hundred.

children.text: tāre guṇāśītis tadardhaṃ kānte tīkṣṇe catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ ravau tadardham ||
children.translated_text: In silver there are eighty virtues; in magnet, half of that; in sharp iron, sixty-four; in copper, half of that.

children.text: rasādibhiryā kriyate cikitsā daivīti sadbhiḥ parikīrtitā sā
children.translated_text: The treatment that is performed with <s>rasa</s> and the like is called divine by the good.

children.text: sā mānuṣī mantrakṛtā śiphādyaiḥ sā rākṣasī śastrakṛtādibhiryā ||
children.translated_text: That which is done by mantras and roots and the like is human; that which is done by knives and the like is demonic.
<s>Gandhaka</s>, <s>vajra</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>vajrābhra</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, <s>śilā</s>,
<s>kharpara</s>, <s>śikhituttha</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, and <s>hemamākṣika</s>,
<s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s>, <s>varāṭī</s>, then <s>hiṅgula</s>,
<s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, conch, <s>bhūnāga</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and <s>śilājatu</s>:

children.text: ete uparasāḥ śodhyāḥ māryā drāvyāḥ puṭe kvacit ||
children.translated_text: these secondary minerals are to be purified, killed, and liquefied, sometimes in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: apakvagandhaṃ kurute'ti kuṣṭhaṃ tāpaṃ bhramaṃ pittarujāṃ karoti
children.translated_text: Uncooked <s>gandhaka</s> produces severe skin disease, feverish heat, dizziness, and bilious pains.

children.text: rūpaṃ sukhaṃ vīryabalaṃ ca hanti tasmāt saṃśuddhaṃ vidhiyojanīyam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys beauty, comfort, vigor, and strength; therefore it should be used according to rule after being thoroughly purified.

children.text: sājyaṃ bhāṇḍe payaḥ kṣiptvā mukhaṃ vastreṇa bandhayet
children.translated_text: After putting milk with ghee into a vessel, one should tie its mouth with cloth.

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe cūrṇitaṃ gandhaṃ kṣiptvā srāveṇa rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: On the back of that cloth one should place powdered <s>gandhaka</s> and seal it with a coating.

children.text: bhāṇḍaṃ nikṣipya bhūmyante ūrdhve deyaṃ puṭaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: After placing the vessel in the ground, one should apply a light <s>puṭa</s> above it.

children.text: tataḥ kṣīre drutaṃ gandhaṃ śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>gandhaka</s>, melted into the milk, is pure and should be used in preparations.
Or else a cloth should be smeared seven times with the milks of <s>arka</s> and <s>snuhī</s>.
After grinding <s>gandhaka</s> with fresh butter, one should smear the cloth with it.
Having carried that to a place blazing with fire, it should indeed be held facing downward.
The oil falls into the lower vessel; it should be collected and used in preparations.
Purified <s>gandhaka</s> removes diseases such as skin disease, mortal illness, and fever.
It kindles digestion, is very hot, and increases virility.
<s>Vajra</s>, joined with <s>vyāghrīkanda</s> and cooked in a swinging apparatus,

children.text: saptāhāt kaudrave kvāthe kaulatthe vimalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: becomes stainless after a week in a decoction of <s>kodrava</s> and <s>kulattha</s>.
Having heated it twenty-one times, one should sprinkle it with donkey's urine.
After grinding <s>tālaka</s> in sixfold quantity, one should place the diamond in that ball.
Blown with the bellows and sprinkled with horse's urine according to the previously stated procedures,
that <s>vajra</s> becomes ash and makes the body diamond-like.

children.text: ūrṇāśṛṅgaṃ paripiṣya piṇḍam etasya madhye tu nidhāya vajram
children.translated_text: After thoroughly grinding <s>ūrṇāśṛṅga</s>, one should make a lump and place the diamond in its middle.

children.text: piṇḍe'thavādhāya ca vajravallyāḥ puṭatrayaṃ tasya rase vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, placing it in a lump of <s>vajravallī</s>, one should give it three <s>puṭas</s> with that plant's juice.
There is no doubt that this will be the death of that substance called <s>vajra</s>.

children.text: aśuddhavajram āyurghnaṃ pīḍāṃ kuṣṭhaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: Impure <s>vajra</s> destroys life and causes pain and skin disease.
It also causes pallor, burning heat, and heaviness; therefore one should have it purified.
White, red, yellow, and black are the diamond classes beginning with the Brahmin class.
In <s>rasāyana</s>, the white Brahmin type grants accomplishment.
The red Kṣatriya type conquers death and removes wrinkles, gray hair, and disease.
The yellow Vaiśya type causes liquefaction and makes the body firm.

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ śūdro rujāṃ hanti vayaḥsthairyaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: The black Śūdra type removes illnesses and gives stability to age.
These are to be recognized by their marks as male, female, and neuter.
Those that are round, fully faceted, brilliant, and large
are said to be male, free from lines and dots.
Those furnished with lines and dots and hexagonal are remembered as female.
Those that are triangular, elongated, and long are to be known as neuter.
Among these, each earlier class is praised; males are stronger.
Female diamonds produce bodily beauty and grant enjoyments.
Neuters have little potency, are lustful, and lack vital essence.

children.text: strī tu strīṇāṃ pradātavyā klībaṃ klībe tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: A female should be given to women, and likewise a neuter to a neuter.
Males, being stronger, are suitable for all people at all times.

children.text: gṛhītvā tu śubhaṃ vajraṃ vyāghrīkandodare kṣipet
children.translated_text: After taking an auspicious <s>vajra</s>, one should place it inside a <s>vyāghrīkanda</s> tuber.
It should be coated with buffalo dung and cooked in a fire of dung-cakes.
For four watches of the night, or at the end of the night, in horse's urine,
one should sprinkle each of them; in seven nights it is purified.
<s>Meghanādā</s>, <s>śamī</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, what is produced from <s>madanaka</s>,
<s>kulattha</s>, <s>vetasa</s>, then <s>agastya</s>, and <s>sindhuvāraka</s>:
with watery decoctions of these, <s>vajra</s> placed in the middle of a <s>jambīra</s> fruit
should be cooked for three days in a swinging apparatus; in this way one should purify <s>vajra</s>.
One should cook it in a swinging apparatus in a decoction of <s>kulattha</s> and <s>kodrava</s>.
<s>Vajra</s> placed in <s>vyāghrīkanda</s> obtains purification after a week.

children.text: vyāghrīṃ kandagataṃ vajraṃ mṛdā liptaṃ puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: One should cook <s>vajra</s> placed in a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber, coated with clay, in a <s>puṭa</s>.
After taking it out after a day and night, one should sprinkle it with horse's urine.

children.text: vajrīkṣīreṇa vā siñcedevaṃ śuddhaṃ ca mārayet ||
children.translated_text: Or one may sprinkle it with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>; when purified in this way, it should be killed.
Now the killing of the Brahmin and other classes of <s>vajra</s> is again described.
<s>Aśvattha</s>, <s>badarī</s>, <s>jhiṇṭī</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and crab bone

children.text: tulyaṃ snuhīpayaḥ piṣṭvā vajraṃ tadgolake kṣipet
children.translated_text: should be ground in equal amounts with <s>snuhī</s> milk, and the <s>vajra</s> should be placed in that ball.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; the Brahmin class becomes dead.

children.text: karavīraṃ meṣaśṛṅgaṃ ca badaraṃ ca udumbaram
children.translated_text: <s>Karavīra</s>, ram's horn, <s>badara</s>, and <s>udumbara</s>,
ground with an equal amount of <s>arka</s> milk, should kill the royal type just as the Brahmin type.
One should grind <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>gandhaka</s>, and tortoise bone.
With these, or with the milk of <s>vāruṇī</s>, the Vaiśya also dies just like the Brahmin type.

children.text: sūraṇaṃ lasunaṃ śaṅkhaṃ samaṃ peṣyaṃ manaḥśilām
children.translated_text: <s>Sūraṇa</s>, garlic, conch, and <s>manaḥśilā</s> should be ground in equal amounts
with banyan milk inside a crucible; the Śūdra is killed just like the Brahmin type.
The female types among them are killed by the corresponding medicinal recipes.
The death of the neuter types among the four is effected with the medicines of all four together.
With the root of a cotton plant grown for two years, together with <s>kāntamukha</s>,

children.text: nārīstanyena sampiṣya piṣṭvā dhmātaṃ mṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: ground with a woman's breast milk and then heated after grinding, it becomes dead.
With ram's horn, snake bone, turtle shell, and sour <s>vetasa</s>,
ground in a quantity equal to elephant tusk, one should make a ball with the latex of <s>vajrī</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā tanmadhyagaṃ vajraṃ mriyate dhamanena tu
children.translated_text: Having placed <s>vajra</s> (diamond) inside it, it is killed by blowing with fire.
Then the root of a cotton plant, barren of <s>nāga</s> for three years,

children.text: piṣṭvā tanmadhyagaṃ vajraṃ kṛtvā mūṣāṃ nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground; placing <s>vajra</s> inside it, one should make and seal a crucible.

children.text: pacedgajapuṭe taṃ ca mriyate saptadhā puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; it is killed by seven firings.
With the blood of bedbugs, dried by seven heats,
the <s>kuliśa</s> (diamond) should be treated; likewise powdered <s>manaḥśilā</s>.

children.text: liptvā ca badarīpatraiḥ veṣṭayitvā pure pacet
children.translated_text: After smearing it and wrapping it in leaves of <s>badarī</s>, one should cook it in an enclosure.

children.text: punarlepyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ saptadhā mriyate'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: It should be smeared again and cooked again; after seven times it is killed.
<s>Vajra</s> placed in a shell from a great river should be repeatedly treated
for a day with two or one of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>unmatta</s>, and <s>kanyā</s>.
Ground with the flesh of a black crab, it should be wrapped on the outside
with the clay of <s>bhūnāga</s>; when properly blown, it attains the state of ash.
With roots of red lotus and buds of <s>meghanāda</s>,
made into lumps and wrapped around it, blown <s>vajra</s> readily becomes ash.
<s>Vajra</s> gives life, strength, beauty, and bodily comfort,

children.text: sevito hanti rogāṃśca mṛto vajro na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: and, when taken after being killed, it destroys diseases; there is no doubt.

children.text: vaikrāntaṃ vajravacchodhyaṃ nīlaṃ vā lohitaṃ ca vā
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, whether blue or red, should be purified like <s>vajra</s>.
It should be heated and heated again and sprinkled in horse urine twenty-one times.
Then one should put it into a ball made from the five parts of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a crucible-firing; having taken it out, again in a ball

children.text: kṣiptvā ruddhvā pacedevaṃ saptadhā bhasmatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: one should put it, seal it, and cook it thus seven times; it goes to the state of ash.
Once <s>vaikrānta</s> has become ash, it should be employed in place of <s>vajra</s>.
Unpurified <s>abhra</s> (mica) destroys life and increases <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
Unstruck and unprocessed, it cuts the body and produces weak digestion and worms.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ pītaṃ sitaṃ raktaṃ yojyaṃ yoge rasāyane
children.translated_text: The black, yellow, white, and red kinds are to be used in rasāyana preparations.

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajraṃ ceti caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: It is fourfold: <s>pināka</s>, <s>dardura</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>vajra</s>.
The three beginning with <s>pināka</s> are to be rejected; one should carefully obtain the <s>vajra</s> kind.
When thrown into fire, <s>pināka</s> releases a mass of layers.
Eating it through ignorance causes severe skin disease.
<s>Dardura</s>, when placed in fire, makes a frog-like sound.
And <s>nāga</s>, when it has entered fire, emits a sound and a hissing noise.

children.text: sa ca dehagato nityaṃ vyādhiṃ kuryādbhagandaram ||
children.translated_text: When that is in the body, it constantly produces the disease <s>bhagandara</s>.

children.text: vajrābhrakaṃ vahnisaṃsthaṃ na kiṃcid vikṛtiṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrābhraka</s> set in fire undergoes no alteration at all.
Therefore <s>vajrābhraka</s>, conquering disease, old age, and death, is to be used.
One should blow <s>vajrābhraka</s> in fire and then quench it in milk.
Knowing it to have split leaves, in the liquids and acids of <s>meghanāda</s>
one should treat it for eight watches; the wise man should make it into <s>dhānyābhra</s>.

children.text: athavābhrasya bhāgau dvau ṭaṅkaścaikaṃ jalaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: Or else, two parts of mica and one part of <s>ṭaṅka</s>, together with water,
should be kept in a vessel for two days; after making it fine, one should grind it thoroughly.
Tied in a cloth with grain, it should be rubbed together with <s>kāñjika</s>.

children.text: adho yadgālitaṃ sūkṣmaṃ śuddhaṃ dhānyābhrakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The fine material that filters downward becomes pure <s>dhānyābhraka</s>.
For one day <s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be triturated with the liquids of <s>punarnavā</s> and <s>meghanāda</s>.
One should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then again with tamarind and <s>sūraṇa</s>
liquids, and with liquids produced from <s>mustā</s>, it should be triturated separately; three firings should be given.

children.text: evaṃ markadalair veṣṭyaṃ deyaṃ vā mocasampuṭe ||
children.translated_text: In this way it may be wrapped with <s>markada</s> leaves, or placed in a plantain enclosure.

children.text: niścandraṃ jāyate hyabhraṃ yathā doṣeṣu yojayet
children.translated_text: Thus mica becomes lusterless, and one should employ it according to the doṣas.

children.text: goghṛtaistriphalāṃ kvāthaiḥ paktvā ca pūrvavat pacet ||
children.translated_text: With cow ghee and decoctions of <s>triphala</s>, having cooked it, one should cook it as before.
With twenty-five firings, one should cook it with the liquids of <s>kāsamardī</s>.

children.text: deyaṃ puṭatrayaṃ kṣīrair mardayecca puṭe puṭe ||
children.translated_text: Three firings should be given with milks, and it should be triturated at each firing.
Thus mica becomes lusterless and removes old age, death, and disease.

children.text: dhānyābhrakasya bhāgaikaṃ dvau bhāgau ṭaṃkaṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: One part of purified <s>dhānyābhraka</s> and two parts of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>
should be ground; after sealing them in a blind crucible, one should cook them with intense fire.
The powder, naturally cooled, should be employed in all diseases.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s>, ground with acid, should be acid-sprinkled in a heated firing.
Having ground that, one should keep it in a mortar; it is to be treated with sour <s>āranāla</s>.

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ cāranālaiḥ pācyaṃ śodhyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Heated and heated again with <s>āranāla</s>, it should be cooked and purified again and again.

children.text: puṭe vā dhamane pācyaṃ viṃśadvāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a firing or by blowing it should be cooked twenty times, again and again.
Heated repeatedly, it should be thrown into milk; then, after grinding it, one should dry it again.
One should cook a milk-heated firing and sprinkle it while hot with milk.

children.text: evaṃ trisaptavārāṇi śoṣyaṃ peṣyaṃ puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Thus, twenty-one times, it should be dried, ground, and cooked in a firing.
After grinding it, one should cook it in a pot and stir it with an iron ladle.

children.text: dugdhasthaṃ ca tato dugdhaiḥ puṭe pacyātpunaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, while it is in milk, it should be cooked again and again in a firing with milk.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaṃ pacyāddivā caikaṃ puṭe niśi ||
children.translated_text: In this way one should cook it for seven days, by day and with one firing at night.
<s>Taṇḍulī</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, <s>tālamūlī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: cāṅgerī maricaṃ caiva balāyāḥ payasā saha ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>cāṅgerī</s> and pepper, together with the milk of <s>balā</s>,

children.text: ebhiśca peṣayeccābhraṃ pratyekaṃ taṃ tryahaṃ tryaham
children.translated_text: with these one should grind the mica, each one separately, for three days each.

children.text: sthitvā tapte puṭe paścātpratyekena punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After it has stood in a heated firing, one should do this again and again with each separately.

children.text: piṣṭvā punaḥ puṭe ghṛṣṭaṃ kajjalābhaṃ mṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Ground again and rubbed in a firing, it becomes killed, resembling lampblack.
Into purified <s>dhānyābhraka</s> one should put pepper to the extent of one tenth.
One should grind it with the acid group, and it should be treated in acid for three days.

children.text: taṃ śuṣkaṃ sampuṭe dhāmyaṃ khadirāṅgārakair dṛḍham
children.translated_text: When dry, it should be blown firmly in a sealed vessel with charcoal of <s>khadira</s>.
Having set out the upper vessel, one should then moisten it with a sour liquid.
With the roots of <s>agastya</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>varṣābhū</s>, and with juices produced from their leaves,
one should grind the <s>abhra</s> (mica) and sprinkle it with that, or else with some other sour juice.
The mica should be ground with sugar, honey, ghee, cow's milk, and sour curd.

children.text: matsyākṣyāḥ karavīrāyāḥ dravaiḥ piṣṭvā tridhā pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having ground it with the liquids of <s>matsyākṣī</s> and <s>karavīra</s>, one should cook it three times.
Then it should be cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; the mica becomes free from shine.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s> should be rubbed with the liquids of <s>matsyākṣī</s> and <s>tulasī</s>,
with root-liquids of <s>kokilākṣa</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, and white <s>dūrvā</s>,
and with <s>vyāghrīkanda</s> and <s>punarnavā</s>; one should rub it for a day with these.

children.text: kuñjarākhyaiḥ puṭaiḥ sapta piṣṭvā piṣṭvā pacet punaḥ
children.translated_text: With seven heatings called <s>kuñjara</s>, one should cook it again and again, grinding it each time.

children.text: tadvatpañcāmṛtaiḥ pācyaṃ piṣṭvā piṣṭvā tu saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise it should be cooked seven times with the five nectars, after repeated grinding.
In this way it becomes free from shine; one should use it in all diseases.
Equal parts of <s>dhānyābhra</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should be prepared with cow's urine and <s>tulasī</s> leaves.

children.text: vākucyāḥ sūraṇair alpair dinaṃ piṣṭvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: After grinding it for a day with <s>vākucī</s> and a little <s>sūraṇa</s>, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: jayantyāśca dravaiḥ paścānmardyaṃ mardya tridhā puṭet
children.translated_text: Afterwards it should be rubbed with liquids of <s>jayantī</s>, and after repeated rubbing it should be given three <s>puṭa</s> heatings.
In this way, by the fourfold <s>gajapuṭa</s>, it becomes shine-free and conquers all diseases.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s> should be rubbed with the milks of <s>ravi</s>, or with liquids from <s>ravi</s> roots,

children.text: mardyaṃ mardyaṃ puṭe pacyātsaptadhā mriyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: and, after repeated rubbing, cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>; after seven times it is certainly killed.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s> should be kept for a day in the sun with sour liquids made from husk and other acids.

children.text: yāmaṃ mardyaṃ caturgolaṃ ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: It should be rubbed for a <s>yāma</s>, made into four balls, sealed, and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ gokṣīramadhyasthaṃ sthāpyaṃ mardya puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Thus, after being placed in cow's milk, it should be rubbed and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ kārpāsatoyena sthāpyaṃ peṣyaṃ puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after being placed in cotton-plant water, it should be ground and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: tato'mlaiścaiva kārpāsair gavāṃ kṣīraiḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, again and again with sour liquids, cotton-plant liquids, and cow's milk,

children.text: gharmapākaṃ mardanaṃ ca puṭaṃ caivam anukramāt ||
children.translated_text: there should be sun-cooking, rubbing, and <s>puṭa</s> heating in this sequence.

children.text: evaṃ viṃśatpuṭe prāpte mṛto bhavati niścitam ||
children.translated_text: In this way, when twenty <s>puṭa</s> heatings have been reached, it is certainly killed.
Hear the <s>amṛtīkaraṇa</s> (revivifying treatment) of all killed micas.
One should take sixteen <s>palas</s> of decoction produced from <s>triphalā</s>,
eight <s>palas</s> of cow's urine, and ten <s>palas</s> of killed mica.
Having combined them, one should cook them in an iron vessel over a gentle fire.

children.text: drave jīrṇe samādāya sarvaṃ rogeṣu yojayet
children.translated_text: When the liquid has been digested, one should take it all and employ it in diseases.
Even without a vehicle, mica removes old age, death, and disease.
Or one should administer it with vehicles; it immediately removes each corresponding disease.
Killed mica removes diseases, old age, and death in many ways.
When consumed, it increases bodily firmness, beauty, and virility.
Unpurified <s>tāla</s> destroys life and causes disorders of wind and urine.
It produces heat, swelling, and contraction of the limbs; therefore one should purify it.

children.text: tālakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā daśāṃśena ca ṭaṅkaṇam
children.translated_text: Having broken <s>tālaka</s> into small pieces, with one tenth part <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: jambīrāṇāṃ dravaiḥ kṣālyaṃ kāñjikaiḥ kṣālayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should wash it with citron juices, and then wash it again with sour gruel.
After binding it in cloths of fourfold thickness, one should cook it for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
Joined with <s>āranāla</s>, it should be cooked for a day with juices produced from <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s>.
One should cook it for a <s>yāma</s> with sesame oil and for a <s>yāma</s> with <s>triphalā</s> water.

children.text: trivāraṃ tālakaṃ bhāvyaṃ piṣṭvā mūtraiśca kāñjikaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tālaka</s> should be impregnated three times, ground with urine and sour gruel.

children.text: tatphalair daśabhir deyaṃ ruddhvā puṭaṃ ca peṣayet
children.translated_text: It should be supplied with ten of those fruits, sealed, given a <s>puṭa</s>, and ground.

children.text: evaṃ dvādaśadhā pācyaṃ śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Having been cooked twelve times in this way, it is purified and should be used in formulations.
<s>Tālaka</s>, tied in a bundle, should be cooked for a week in sour gruel.
Then, by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>, for one <s>yāma</s> with juices produced from <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s>,
it should be cooked for a <s>yāma</s> in sesame oil and for a <s>yāma</s> in <s>triphalā</s> water.

children.text: evaṃ yantre caturyāmaṃ pācyaṃ śudhyati tālakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus it should be cooked in the apparatus for four <s>yāmas</s>; the <s>tālaka</s> is purified.
<s>Tālaka</s> removes diseases, skin disease, death, and fever.
When purified, though cooling in potency, it causes an increase of wind.
Unpurified <s>śilā</s> causes stones, urinary disease, and heart disease.
It also causes weak digestion and constipation; when purified, it removes every pain.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> should be cooked for three days in goat's urine in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
For purification, it should be impregnated seven times in heat with those goat biles.
<s>Śilā</s>, with juices from <s>jayantī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, and red <s>agastya</s>,

children.text: dolāyantre dinaṃ pācyā yāmaṃ chāgasya mūtrake ||
children.translated_text: should be cooked for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s> and for a <s>yāma</s> in goat's urine.
One should wash it with <s>āranāla</s> and use it in all diseases.
One should cook <s>rasaka</s> for a week with human urine and cow's urine.
By means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>, it is properly purified and should be used in formulations.
In a mortar one should rub it with the excrement of a cat and a pigeon.
One should add one tenth part <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>; then it should be cooked over a gentle fire.
For the purification of <s>tuttha</s>, a <s>puṭa</s> with curd and a <s>puṭa</s> with honey should be given.
The three kinds of <s>vimalā</s> should be cooked together with plantain water.
One should grind them with sour <s>vetasa</s>, sour grain-ferment, and ewe's urine.
In a <s>dolāyantra</s> for four <s>yāmas</s>: this purification is most excellent.
With liquids arising from <s>karkaṭī</s> and <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and with citron juices,
one should impregnate <s>vimalā</s> in strong sunlight; it is certainly purified.
Unpurified <s>mākṣika</s> causes weak digestion, loss of strength, wounds, obstruction, and eye pain,

children.text: kurute mākṣiko mṛtyum aśuddho nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and death; there is no doubt about this.
One should boil <s>mākṣika</s> with human urine and with liquids of <s>kodrava</s>.
Together with <s>vetasa</s>, the sour group, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and the three pungents,
it should be cooked for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, placed in the middle of <s>sūraṇa</s>.
It should be cooked for a day with plantain liquids; after removing it, one should grind it with ghee.
Joined with castor oil, it should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> for purification.

children.text: mākṣikasya trayo bhāgā bhāgaikaṃ saindhavasya ca ||
children.translated_text: There are three parts of <s>mākṣika</s> and one part of <s>saindhava</s>.
One should cook it with the liquids of <s>mātuluṅga</s>, or else with liquids produced from <s>jambīra</s>.
One should cook it in an iron vessel until the vessel is very red.
As long as it comes to have a coppery color, so long the <s>mākṣika</s> is purified.
With the exudates of <s>agastya</s> flowers one should rub <s>śigru</s> root.
With the liquids of <s>pāṣāṇabhedī</s> also one should cook the <s>mākṣika</s> together with these.
One should make it into a pill and cook it in a blind crucible with twenty cow-dung cakes.
Then, after grinding it again, one should seal it; by six firings it becomes purified.

children.text: meghanādapāṣāṇabhedī piṣṭvā tatpiṇḍamadhye mākṣikaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā nikṣipet
children.translated_text: After grinding <s>meghanāda</s> and <s>pāṣāṇabhedī</s>, one should make the <s>mākṣika</s> into small particles and place it in the middle of that lump.

children.text: tadgolakaṃ vastre baddhvā dolāyantre kulatthakvāthe dinamekaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: One should tie that ball in cloth and cook it for one day in a <s>dolāyantra</s> in a decoction of <s>kulattha</s>.
This should be applied, in the proper place, for the calcination of purified metals.
When broken it resembles gold; inside it is black, while outside it has luster.

children.text: bṛhadvarṇaṃ iti khyāto mākṣikaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Known as <s>bṛhadvarṇa</s>, that <s>mākṣika</s> is called the best.
It pervades the body, limb by limb, like a drop of oil in water.

children.text: na vinā śodhanaṃ sarve dhātavaḥ prabalādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without purification, all metals and the powerful substances beginning with them
do not act to pacify diseases; therefore their purification will be described.

children.text: pravālānāṃ strīdugdhena bhāvanā paścāddhaṇḍikāmadhye sthāpayitvā nirudhyopari śarāvakaṃ dattvā lepayet
children.translated_text: For corals there is trituration with woman's milk; afterward, placing them inside a small pot, sealing it, putting a small saucer above, one should coat it.
Having kindled the fire, in two watches the coral is killed.
The wise man should cook <s>kulattha</s> in a droṇa with a droṇa of water.
In that decoction, when one quarter remains, there should be eight <s>maṇa</s>s of stone.

children.text: ātape tridinaṃ śuṣkaṃ kvāthasiktaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Dried in the sun for three days, it should be sprinkled again and again with the decoction.
Taking powdered pearl, prepared with hail-water,

children.text: ātape tridinaṃ bhāvyaṃ cūrṇitaṃ mṛtyum āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: it should be infused in the sun for three days; when powdered, it attains calcination.
Conch and <s>nīlāñjana</s> too should be purified for a day as before.
With cow urine, decoctions of <s>triphala</s>, and the liquids of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, one should treat <s>jatu</s>.
One should rub it in an iron vessel; in a day there is purification of <s>śilājatu</s>.
<s>Darada</s>, infused with ewe's milk and with the acid group,
certainly attains purification when this is done carefully seven times.
<s>Sūryāvarta</s>, <s>vajrakanda</s>, plantain, <s>devadālikā</s>,

children.text: śigru kośātakī vandhyā kākamācī ca vāyasī
children.translated_text: <s>śigru</s>, <s>kośātakī</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>vāyasī</s>:
with the juice of any one of these, joined with the three alkalis and salts,
one should infuse it carefully for one day with the acid group.
<s>Sauvīra</s>, <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s>, purified earthworm-earth,
conch, <s>nīlāñjana</s>, and all the secondary minerals, whatever they are,

children.text: pṛthagbhāvyaṃ vidhānena śuddhiṃ yānti dine dine ||
children.translated_text: when each is infused separately according to the rule, attain purification day by day.
After that, with those liquids, the wise man should place them for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.

children.text: śudhyante nātra sandehaḥ sarveṣu paramā amī ||
children.translated_text: They are purified; there is no doubt here. All these are excellent in every case.
They also release liquefied <s>sattva</s>; this is remembered as the common opinion.

children.text: gugguluṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ lākṣā majjā sarjarasaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Guggulu</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, lac, marrow, and again <s>sarja</s> resin,

children.text: ūrṇā guñjā kṣetramīnam asthīni śaśakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: wool, <s>guñjā</s>, <s>kṣetramīna</s>, and the bones of a hare,
jaggery, honey, ghee, oil-cake, and <s>tuttha</s> are to be ground with goat's fluids.

children.text: sarvaṃ tulyaṃ ca dhānyābhraṃ bhūnāgaṃ mṛttikāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: All of it is equal in measure, as are <s>dhānyābhra</s>, <s>bhūnāga</s>, and clay.
It is equal to <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> also, and to whatever secondary minerals are hard.
One should combine them and cook them with buffalo products, ending with curds and cow-dung and the like.

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ mardyaṃ vaṭīṃ kuryātkarṣamātraṃ tu śoṣayet
children.translated_text: It should be rubbed firmly; one should make pills of a karṣa each and dry them.
In a <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s> one should blow strongly with well-aged charcoal.

children.text: trivāraṃ dhamanād eva sattvaṃ patati nirmalam
children.translated_text: By blowing three times, pure <s>sattva</s> falls down.

children.text: asādhyān mocayet sattvān mṛttikādeśca kā kathā ||
children.translated_text: It releases <s>sattva</s> from substances thought impossible to process; what need be said of clay and the rest?

children.text: lākṣā ājyaṃ tilāḥ śigruḥ ṭaṃkaṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ guḍam
children.translated_text: Lac, ghee, sesame, <s>śigru</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, salt, and jaggery,
combined with half as much <s>tālaka</s>, should be sealed in a perforated crucible.
In a firing, by means of the <s>pātālayantra</s>, the <s>sattva</s> certainly falls.
<s>Cāṅgerī</s>, sour chickpea preparation, <s>mātuluṅga</s>, sour <s>vetasa</s>,

children.text: ciñcā nāraṅgaṃ jambīranamṇa varga iti smṛtam
children.translated_text: tamarind, orange, and <s>jambīra</s>: this is remembered as the acid group.
Having powdered <s>tālaka</s>, one should infuse it with goat's milk.

children.text: vāratrayaṃ tato viddhimūlaṃ piṣṭvā tu miśritam
children.translated_text: After three times, then, having ground and mixed in the root called <s>viddhi</s>,

children.text: kṛtvā ca guḍakaṃ śuṣkaṃ satvaṃ grāhyaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: one should make a ball and dry it; the <s>sattva</s> should be obtained as before.
One should rub <s>tālaka</s> with milks, or with <s>sarpākṣī</s> or radishes.
As before, one should obtain the <s>sattva</s>, sealing the perforated crucible.
As with <s>tālaka</s>, the <s>sattva</s> of <s>śilā</s> should be obtained with those very herbs.
When blown with an equal amount of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, the <s>sattva</s> is a fourth part.
It should be infused with cow's milk, with <s>tuttha</s>-milk, and with castor oils.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, rubbed for one day and made into pellets,
yields <s>sattva</s> when blown as in the case of mica; this is the proper method for it too.
<s>Jayantī</s>, powdered <s>triphala</s>, turmeric, jaggery, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
this being one quarter part of the <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>: after grinding it, one should coat the crucible.
Having bound a tube in a closed crucible, one should dry it in the fierce sun.

children.text: grāhyaṃ pātālayantre ca satvaṃ dhmātaṃ puṭena ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s>, blown and fired, should be obtained in a <s>pātālayantra</s>.

children.text: svarṇaṃ tāraṃ tāmraṃ nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ kāntaṃ ca tīkṣṇakam
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇaka</s>,
up to <s>muṇḍa</s>, are the eightfold metals; bronze, <s>āra</s>, and <s>ghoṣaka</s> are threefold.
The secondary metals are said to be <s>maṇḍūra</s> and iron slag.

children.text: ete dvādaśadhā śodhyā māryā drāvyāḥ puṭādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: These, twelvefold, are to be purified, calcined, and melted in firings and the like.

children.text: taile takre gavāṃ mūtre hyāranāle kulatthake
children.translated_text: In oil, buttermilk, cow urine, <s>āranāla</s>, and <s>kulattha</s>...

children.text: kramātprāptaṃ tathā taptaṃ drāve drāve tu saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: Having been obtained in sequence and heated likewise, it is to be melted seven times, in each melting.
This is declared to be the purification of leaves of gold and the other metals.

children.text: hemnaḥ pādaṃ mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭamamlena kenacit ||
children.translated_text: For gold, one quarter as much incinerated <s>sūta</s> (mercury), ground with some acid,
should be smeared on the leaf and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>; by eight firings it is certainly incinerated.
For the incineration of all purified metals, the procedure is such as this.

children.text: saukhyaṃ vīryaṃ balaṃ hanti nānārogaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: An unpurified substance destroys comfort, virility, and strength, and produces many diseases.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ sūtaṃ ca tasmācchuddhaṃ tu mārayet ||
children.translated_text: Unpurified gold and <s>sūta</s> do this; therefore one should incinerate them only after purification.
Ant-hill earth, soot, red ochre, and brick-earth from a brick firing,
these and similar five earths, with citron juice and sour <s>āranāla</s>,

children.text: piṣṭvā lepyaṃ svarṇapatraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ puṭena śudhyati
children.translated_text: should be ground and smeared on gold leaf; the excellent gold is purified by a firing.
One should treat the five earths for three days with the acids of <s>mātuluṅga</s>.
With rock salt and earth-ash also, gold is purified as before.

children.text: nāgaiḥ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ ca tāpyairgandhena tāmraṃ śilayā ca nāgam
children.translated_text: Gold is treated with <s>nāga</s> (lead), silver with <s>tāpya</s>, copper with <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), and lead with <s>śilā</s>,

children.text: tālena vaṅgaṃ trividhaṃ ca lauhaṃ nārīpayo hanti ca hiṃgulena ||
children.translated_text: tin with <s>tāla</s>, and the three kinds of iron are killed with woman's milk and <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar).
<s>Mākṣika</s> and lead-powder, ground with the juice of <s>arka</s>,
incinerate gold leaf by a firing in only a moment.
Having added mercury equal to half the gold, one should carefully make a paste,
and, after placing lead-powder above and below, by firing it is certainly incinerated.
Lead-powder and <s>śilā</s>, sprinkled with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>,
are smeared on gold; that paste is incinerated by a firing.
Incinerated lead should be ground with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, or else with some acid,

children.text: piṣṭvā lepyaṃ suvarṇapatraṃ ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: smeared on gold leaf, sealed, and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Taking it up, one should grind it with acids, together with clay and one eighth part lead,
bind it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, combined with the previously mentioned lead.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ pacyādaṣṭadhā mriyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: Thus one should cook it again and again; by eight times it is certainly incinerated.
Sulfur equal to purified <s>sūta</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>, with strong acids,
by eight firings cause gold to be incinerated, performing the operation as before.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ samaṃ svarṇaṃ khalve kuryācca golakam ||
children.translated_text: One should make purified <s>sūta</s> and an equal amount of gold into a ball in a mortar.

children.text: adho vai gandhakaṃ dattvā sarvaṃ tulyaṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Putting <s>gandhaka</s> below, all in equal quantity, and sealing it,
one should give a firing with thirty forest cow-dung cakes; in this way there are fourteen firings.

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma gandhaṃ deyaṃ puṭe puṭe
children.translated_text: A non-rising ash is produced; <s>gandhaka</s> should be added at each firing.
One should triturate <s>sūta</s>, twice the quantity of gold, with acid for one watch.

children.text: adhaḥ ūrdhvaṃ mākṣikaṃ piṣṭvā mūṣāyāṃ svarṇatulyakam
children.translated_text: Below and above, ground <s>mākṣika</s> equal to the gold should be placed in a crucible.
On top of that goes the triturated gold, and on top of that gold-<s>mākṣika</s>.

children.text: deyaṃ svarṇaṃ samaṃ tacca pṛṣṭhe gandhaṃ ca tatsamam
children.translated_text: Gold equal to that should be added, and on its surface <s>gandhaka</s> equal to it.

children.text: ṣaḍvāraṃ cūrṇitaṃ dattvā ruddhvā mūṣāṃ dhameddṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: Having added it powdered six times, one should seal the crucible and blow it strongly.
When naturally cooled, that ash should be taken, five parts of it.

children.text: ṭaṃkaṇaṃ śvetakācaṃ ca bhāgaikaṃ ca prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: One part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) and white glass should also be used.
The three, mixed with honey and ghee, should be made into a ball.
One part of <s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be put below and above.
After sealing it, one should blow it intensely in a crucible for two <s>ghaṭikā</s>s.
A non-rising ash is produced; it should be applied in the respective formulations.
One part purified <s>mākṣika</s> and one part <s>avoṭa-mākṣika</s>,
with three parts <s>sūtaka</s> added, the three should be triturated with acid.
That ball should be cooked in a <s>pātāla-yantra</s> for three watches.

children.text: ityevaṃ mriyate svarṇaṃ nirutthaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In just this way gold is incinerated into a non-rising state; there is no doubt here.
Likewise, with <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, <s>bhallāta</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: liptvā svarṇasya patrāṇi ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: one should smear gold leaves, seal them, and cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: taiḥ dravaiśca punaḥ piṣṭvā mriyate saptadhā puṭe
children.translated_text: After grinding again with those liquids, it is incinerated by seven firings.
Beginning with one <s>tola</s> of gold and one <s>māṣa</s> of purified lead,

children.text: liptvā deyaṃ tu taṃ cūrṇaṃ tacchuddhairgandhamākṣikaiḥ
children.translated_text: after smearing, that powder should be added with purified <s>gandhaka</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>.
One should triturate it with acid for one watch, seal it, and cook it in a light firing.

children.text: gandhaṃ punaḥ punardeyaṃ mriyate daśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhaka</s> should be added again and again; it is incinerated by ten firings.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ ca bhavecchītaṃ tiktaṃ snigdhaṃ himaṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: Gold becomes cooling, bitter, unctuous, cold in potency, and heavy.
It produces intellect, learning, and memory; it is antitoxic and a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: āyuḥ śukraṃ balaṃ hanti rogavegaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: Unpurified silver destroys life, semen, and strength, and sets the force of disease in motion.
Therefore the wise should purify and incinerate <s>tāra</s> (silver), though it is nectar-like.
Melted with lead and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, it attains purification.
<s>Mākṣika</s> and <s>gandhaka</s> likewise should be triturated with the milk of <s>arka</s>.

children.text: tena liptaṃ rūpyapatraṃ puṭena mriyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: Silver leaf smeared with that is certainly incinerated by a firing.

children.text: tāraṃ trivāraṃ nikṣiptaṃ taile jyotiṣmatī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> should be plunged three times into the oil of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>.
One should grind copper with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> and smear the silver leaves.
Having sealed them, one should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then grind again with the substances previously stated.
Earth-<s>dhātrī</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>, in equal amount, with long pepper, rock salt, and acids,

children.text: liptvā tārasya patrāṇi ruddhvā saptapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: should be smeared on silver leaves, sealed, and cooked in seven firings.

children.text: dravaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ piṣṭvā mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
