children.translated_text: After grinding again and again with liquids, it is incinerated; there is no doubt here.
With three parts silver leaves and one part purified <s>mākṣika</s>,
one should triturate with liquids born from citron and smear the silver leaves.
One should dry it, seal it blindly, and cook it with thirty forest cow-dung cakes.
In this way, by fourteen firings, it is certainly incinerated into a non-rising state.
Four parts silver leaf and one part incinerated tin,
or else sulfur and <s>tāla</s>, should be smeared on, ground with citron.
Having sealed it, one should cook it in three firings with twenty-five forest cow-dung cakes.

children.text: mriyate nātra saṃdeho gandho deyaḥ puṭe puṭe
children.translated_text: It is killed, no doubt; <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) should be added in each firing.
Having made <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and <s>gandha</s> equal, [one should take] the root of <s>kākatuṇḍa</s>.
One should triturate it with buffalo milk; after grinding it, one should wash it with water.
Having put the ball into a ball of turmeric, and then into horse dung,
and having kept it there for twenty-one days, one should remove that ball again.
After grinding it, sheets of <s>tāra</s> (silver) are to be smeared with some acid.
With twenty firings, ash is produced; there is no doubt about this.
With the ash, ground with acid, one should combine <s>tālaka</s> through firings.
By that procedure it becomes a preparation that removes all diseases.
Uncooked copper destroys life, destroys complexion, and ruins all the bodily constituents.
It causes dizziness, fainting, confusion, hair loss, various pains, skin disease, and colic.
Having smeared a copper sheet with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, with salt and sour gruel,
it should be heated, and sprinkled again and again with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
This burning should be done twelve times through smearing the copper and quenching it.
Chalk and salt should be ground with buttermilk and sour <s>āranāla</s>.

children.text: tena liptvā tāmrapatraṃ taptaṃ taptaṃ niṣecayet
children.translated_text: With that, one should smear a copper sheet and quench it each time when hot.
For purification, this should be done six times with the acid-ground paste of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
One should cook the copper sheet in cow urine for one <s>yāma</s> with a strong fire.
It is purified, no doubt; now the killing of it is stated.
One should smear it with <s>gandha</s> equal to the copper, ground with acid.
The sheet should be pierced with thorns; after preparing it, one should cook it in a firing.

children.text: uddhṛtya cūrṇayet tasmin pādāṃśaṃ gandhakaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Having removed it, one should powder it; into it one should put a quarter part of <s>gandhaka</s>.
With limes, or with <s>āranāla</s>, and likewise with the liquids of <s>mṛgadūrvā</s>,

children.text: piṣṭvā piṣṭvā pacettadvat sagandhaṃ ca catuṣpuṭe
children.translated_text: grinding it again and again, one should cook it in the same way, together with sulfur, in four firings.
Having ground it with the juices of <s>mātulaṅga</s>, one should give one firing.
By this very procedure, copper ash certainly comes into being.
Mercury twice the amount of the copper should be triturated with lemon acid.
Likewise with white sugar, in three firings it becomes killed.
With the liquids of <s>pāṣāṇabhedī</s> and <s>matsyākṣī</s>, and with twice as much sulfur,
one should smear the copper sheet; after sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Again, when it has been burned with a seventh part, one should add liquids and grind it.
Thus, cooked in seven firings, copper ash certainly results.
Copper, <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), and mercury should be ground with lemon acid.

children.text: ādau mūṣāntare kṣiptvā dhattūrasya tu patrakam
children.translated_text: First, having placed a <s>dhattūra</s> leaf inside a crucible,

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe tāmratulyaṃ tu gandhakaṃ cūrṇitaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: on its back one should put powdered sulfur equal to the copper.

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe marditaṃ tāmraṃ pūrvatulyaṃ tu gandhakam
children.translated_text: On top of that, [one should put] the triturated copper, and sulfur equal to the previous measure.
Having covered it in <s>dhattūra</s> leaves, one should seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
The powder, once naturally cooled, certainly becomes ash.
One should wash the copper sheet with a little sulfur and acid.
With that sulfur and mercury, one should smear the copper sheet.
After being fired with sulfur, it is killed; there is no doubt about this.
Again, with sulfur twice the amount of copper, ground with acid,
having placed half the portion below, the wise man should add acid-ground material.

children.text: tatpiṇḍaṃ bhāṇḍagarbhe tu ruddhvā culyāṃ vipācayet
children.translated_text: That lump should be sealed inside a vessel and cooked on a stove.
With intense cooking for one <s>yāma</s>, it certainly becomes ash.

children.text: sūtamekaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ yāmaṃ kṛtvā vimarditam
children.translated_text: One part mercury and two parts sulfur should be triturated for one <s>yāma</s>.
A copper sheet equal to the two should be placed inside a pot.
When it is properly set in a salt apparatus, one should place ash at the side.
One should cook it on a stove for four <s>yāmas</s>, with cow dung on the back of the vessel.
Water should be added again and again; when it has naturally cooled, one should powder it.
It is killed, no doubt; one should employ it in all diseases.
Copper is regarded as having many kinds; for its purification, [take] five parts.
And one part white glass, and one part <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
having mixed them in a crucible, [one should add] one part copper sheet.
Having placed it above and sealed it, it should be blown, and taken when fully cooled.
The copper becomes faultless and removes all diseases.
Or else, killed copper should be triturated with a single acid.
That ball should be placed inside <s>sūraṇa</s>, sealed above, and smeared over.
When dry, it should be cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; it removes all defects.

children.text: vāntiṃ bhrāntiṃ virekaṃ ca na karoti kadācana
children.translated_text: It never causes vomiting, dizziness, or purgation.
Copper is sharp, hot, sweet, astringent, cooling, and fluid-moving.
It reduces <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, destroys wasting, anemia, and skin disease, and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It destroys post-digestive colic, hemorrhoids, and weak digestive fire.
Improperly cooked lead and tin cause skin disease, abdominal tumors, and pain.
They are said to bring urinary disease, anemia, abdominal disease, <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and death.
One should smear a sheet of <s>nāga</s> (lead) with powder of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> root and with <s>mārka</s> milk.

children.text: nāgapatraṃ tu taṃ śuṣkaṃ drāvayitvā niṣecayet ||
children.translated_text: When that lead sheet is dry, one should melt it and quench it.

children.text: nirguṇḍīdravamadhye tu tataḥ patraṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: Then one should make the sheet in the midst of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> liquid.

children.text: liptvā bhāvyaṃ punaḥ secyaṃ saptavāraṃ viśuddhaye ||
children.translated_text: It should be smeared, treated again, and quenched seven times for purification.
Turmeric, <s>tumburu</s> seeds, <s>kokilākṣa</s>, and <s>kuṭhārikā</s>,
<s>gaurīphalā</s>, <s>amlikā</s>, <s>caṇḍī</s>, <s>kṣudrā</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, together with cumin,
according to availability, one should treat the ash with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>.

children.text: tanmadhye bhāvitaṃ nāgaṃ śuddhaṃ sekaṃ tu saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: Within that, the treated lead is purified by seven quenchings.
Ash of the bark of <s>aśvattha</s> and tamarind, amounting to a fourth part of the <s>nāga</s> (lead),
should be thrown into the stove, cooked in a vessel, and stirred with an iron ladle.

children.text: yāvadbhasma bhaved etacca bhasma tulyaṃ manaḥśilām
children.translated_text: Until this becomes ash, and with <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) equal to that ash,
one should grind it with citron juice or <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel), seal it, and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> firing.
When it has cooled by itself, one should grind it again with twentieth parts of <s>śilāmlaka</s>,

children.text: evaṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ puṭe pāko nāgasyāpi nirutthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by cooking in six such <s>puṭas</s>, even <s>nāga</s> becomes dead and non-revivable.
Or else, lead sheets, smeared with powder on a potsherd,
should be cooked for one watch over very strong fire; then that ash, with juices of <s>citraka</s>,
should be fried in an iron vessel, being stirred with sticks of <s>arjuna</s>.
Up to sixteen watches, the liquid should be given again and again.
One should rub it with the stick while it is being boiled; after removing it, with juices of <s>citraka</s>,
one should make it into balls, seal it, and then kill it quickly in six <s>puṭas</s>.
With ashes produced from tamarind, <s>akṣa</s>, sugarcane, <s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>balā</s>, and <s>vajralatā</s>,
and with ashes of <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, and <s>aśvattha</s>, one should fry it firmly.

children.text: lohapātraṃ tu saptāhaṃ tulyaṃ bhasmāni cāśu ca
children.translated_text: In an iron vessel for seven days, with equal quantities of ashes, quickly,
and with a stick of <s>palāśa</s>, it dies; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: piṣṭvāgastiṃ ca bhūnāgaṃ liptvā pātraṃ viśoṣayet
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>agasti</s> and <s>bhūnāga</s>, one should smear the vessel and dry it.
In that vessel one should melt it for one watch and place it in a strong vessel.
In the alkali of <s>vāsā</s> and <s>circiṭa</s>, on leaves of <s>vāsā</s>, one should rub it.
One should cook it on the stove for one watch, remove it, and mix it thoroughly.
That powder, together with <s>śilā</s> and <s>tāpya</s>, should be joined with alkali of <s>vāsaka</s>.
With the previous lead equal to that, one should cook it in twenty-one <s>puṭas</s>.
Two <s>puṭas</s> should be given with alkalis of <s>circiṭa</s>, together with juices of <s>vāsā</s>.
The <s>nāga</s>, resembling the color of vermilion, dies and becomes effective for every operation.

children.text: kunaṭī mākṣikaṃ caiva samabhāgaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: One should make <s>kunaṭī</s> and <s>mākṣika</s> in equal parts,
grind that with a leaf of <s>arka</s>, and kill the lead sheets.
The dead <s>nāga</s> becomes slightly bitter and sweet, reduced to ash.
When used constantly, it produces longevity, fame, and increase of virility.
<s>Mākṣika</s> and <s>haritāla</s>, with the fresh juice of <s>palāśa</s>,
should be made into a paste; having smeared tin sheets with it, one should kill them.
One should purify <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) like <s>nāga</s>; likewise with <s>aśvattha</s> and tamarind.
That ash and <s>haritāla</s>, in equal amount, should be mixed with some acid,
or with liquids arising from <s>palāśa</s>; after making balls, one should seal it in a closed <s>puṭa</s>.
After removing it, one should triturate it with <s>tāla</s> amounting to one tenth.
Having mixed it with the previous liquids, one should seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ viṃśatpuṭe paktvā mṛtaṃ bhavati bhasmasāt ||
children.translated_text: After cooking it in twenty <s>puṭas</s> in this way, it becomes dead and reduced to ash.
One should coat tin sheets with mercury amounting to one quarter of the tin,
and, having collected material from the tamarind tree, it should also be covered within with rice.
Having ground that, one should place the tin sheets inside that lump and smear them.
With powders of <s>śirīṣa</s> and <s>rajanī</s>, one should make a good ball with <s>kumārī</s>.
The mercury-smeared tin sheet, well coated, is placed in the ball.

children.text: ruddhvā gajapuṭe pakvaṃ pūrvasaṃkhyā mṛto bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Sealed and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, it becomes killed according to the previous number of firings.
Having ground <s>akṣa</s> and <s>bhallātaka</s> with water, one should smear those sheets.

children.text: tatastilakhalī madhye kṣiptvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having placed them inside sesame oilcake, one should seal them and cook them in a <s>puṭa</s>.
In the firing called <s>gaja</s>, tin becomes ash through forty firings.
Tin, slightly bitter and salty, overcomes anemia, worms, and urinary disease.
It is scraping, somewhat yellow, and removes every disease of the body.
Unpurified iron is poison; it diminishes life and causes illness.

children.text: hṛtpīḍāṃ ca tṛṣāṃ jāḍyaṃ tasmācchuddhaṃ ca mārayet ||
children.translated_text: It also causes heart pain, thirst, and dullness; therefore one should purify and kill it.
In a vessel in which a dropped drop of oil does not spread,

children.text: hiṅgur gandhaṃ prasarati nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbukaśca
children.translated_text: where asafoetida diffuses its own smell and neem its bitterness,

children.text: pāke dagdhaṃ bhavati śikharākāratā naiva bhūmau
children.translated_text: where, when cooked, the burned material becomes peak-shaped and not flat upon the ground,

children.text: kāntaṃ lauhaṃ tadidamuditaṃ lakṣaṇoktaṃ na cānyat ||
children.translated_text: that is declared to be <s>kānta</s> iron, marked by these signs, and no other.

children.text: kāntaṃ mṛdutaraṃ tāraṃ rukmābhaṃ timiraṃ karam
children.translated_text: The <s>kānta</s> iron that is softer, bright, golden in appearance, and darkening,
and because of which neem paste kept overnight becomes sweet,
that <s>kānta</s> is excellent; and when smelted with silver, it combines.
This removes all diseases and is supreme in removing all skin diseases.
Smeared with the blood of a hare and a goat and heated in fire three times,
all iron, from <s>kānta</s> down to <s>muṇḍa</s>, becomes supreme in removing all diseases.
With water eight times the <s>triphala</s>, and with sixteen <s>palas</s> of <s>triphala</s>,
in that decoction, reduced to one quarter, five sheets of iron,
made into plates and heated, should be quenched seven times.
Thus the defect born from mountain-origin iron is dissolved away.

children.text: trividhaṃ lauhacūrṇaṃ vā gomūtraiḥ ṣaḍguṇaiḥ pacet
children.translated_text: Or the threefold iron powder should be cooked with sixfold cow urine,
washed in <s>āranāla</s>, and dried; it obtains purification.
<s>Raktamālā</s>, <s>haṃsapāda</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>,
<s>gopālī</s>, <s>tumburu</s>, and <s>dantī</s>, ground with an equal amount of cow urine:
into this, iron sheets, heated again and again fourteen times,
should be quenched, from <s>kānta</s> to <s>muṇḍa</s>, for the removal of all defects.
Among all medicinal preparations, an iron preparation is praised.
Therefore, with every effort, one should first kill all iron.
For iron above five <s>palas</s> and up to thirteen <s>palas</s>,
first the mantra and then the procedure are stated as they are to be performed.
One should grind five <s>palas</s> of <s>hiṅgula</s> with woman's breast milk.
With that, one should smear five <s>palas</s> of iron sheets.
Having sealed them, one should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, and then again with decoctions of <s>triphala</s>.
With <s>jambīra</s> fruits or sour gruels, [one should use] <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) in a twentieth part.
Having ground it, sealed it, and fired it in a <s>puṭa</s>, one should cook the metal again in just the same way.

children.text: catvāriṃśatpuṭair evaṃ kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca muṇḍakam ||
children.translated_text: By forty <s>puṭas</s> in this manner, <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍaka</s> iron [are treated].

children.text: ho mriyate trālasande dattvā dattvā ca hiṅgulam
children.translated_text: Iron is killed in the obscure <s>trālasanda</s> process, by adding <s>hiṅgula</s> again and again.
The bark of <s>arjuna</s>, very red, should be ground with <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel).
Into that one should place iron powder in a bronze vessel.

children.text: dinaikaṃ bhāvayedgharme dravaiḥ pūryaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one day he should soak it in the heat, filling it again and again with liquids.
With <s>arjuna</s> or with sour gruels, the threefold iron may be killed.
One should stir iron powder with the liquid from <s>dantī</s> leaves, whatever liquid there is.

children.text: dinaikaṃ bhāvayed gharme dravaṃ deyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: He should soak it for one day in the heat, adding the liquid again and again.

children.text: ruddhvā rātrau puṭaiḥ pacyād ebhirdrāvaiśca bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed it, he should cook it at night with <s>puṭas</s>, and should soak it with these liquids.
He should do this for eight days; the threefold iron is indeed killed.
One should make the threefold iron plate like a tamarind leaf.

children.text: mṛtpātrasthaṃ kṣiped gharme dantyā drāvaiḥ prapūrayet
children.translated_text: Placed in an earthen vessel in the heat, it should be filled with liquids of <s>dantī</s>.
The plate should be treated again and again, until the iron becomes heated through.
It is killed by fierce heat; after powdering it, one should put it to use.

children.text: kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tathā muṇḍacūrṇaṃ matsyākṣajair dravaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The powders of <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s> iron [should be treated] with liquids produced from <s>matsyākṣa</s>.
They should be soaked in the sun for three days, and for two days with liquids of <s>citraka</s>.
For three days [soak them] with liquids of <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>, and for three days with liquids of <s>sahadevī</s>.
With cow urine and a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>, one should soak them for three days each.

children.text: dhātakyāśca tato mardyaṃ kramāddeyaṃ puṭaṃ puṭam ||
children.translated_text: Then it should be ground with <s>dhātakī</s>; a <s>puṭa</s> should be given in sequence, one after another.
Having sealed it and fired it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, one should employ the killed product in formulations.
One should triturate iron powder with liquids arising from <s>kuraṇṭa</s> leaves.
For one day in strong sunlight it should be ground with liquids of <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>.
Again for a day [it should be treated] with <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>, and with cow urine.
With cow urine and with <s>triphalā</s> decocted, one should soak it in that decoction.
For three weeks, carefully, one should treat it; after that he should grind it for one day.
Having sealed it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, he should grind it with a decoction called <s>pañcādi</s>.
It should be ground by day and fired at night for twenty-one days.
In just twenty-one days the threefold iron is indeed killed.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ ca śilā hyamlair haridrā maricāni ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and <s>śilā</s> with sour liquids, along with turmeric and black pepper,

children.text: piṣṭvā mardyaṃ lohapatraṃ taptaṃ taptaṃ niṣecayet
children.translated_text: should be ground; the heated iron sheet should be quenched again and again in the paste.
Seven times in a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>; then it should be washed with water.
It should be beaten with an iron rod and ground with waters of <s>triphalā</s>.
<s>Mākṣika</s> and <s>śilā</s> should be added in a sixteenth part of the iron.
Stirred with sour liquid, sealed, it should be cooked in a <s>gajāndhaka-puṭa</s>.
The ash becomes <s>niruttha</s> (non-revivifiable): <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and also <s>muṇḍaka</s> iron.
Having smeared it with the pulp of <s>tindū</s> fruit, one should set it in the hot sun.
He should keep it in a bronze vessel; in one day it receives enough firing.

children.text: lepyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kuryāt dināntāntaṃ pralepayet
children.translated_text: The smearing should be done again and again; it should be anointed until the end of the day.
Combined with a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>, it becomes killed in one day.

children.text: sthālyāṃ vā lohapātre vā lauhadarvyā viloḍayet
children.translated_text: In an earthen pot or an iron vessel, one should stir it with an iron ladle.
He should cook the iron powder for one day in a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.

children.text: tatpiṇḍaṃ triphalātoyaiḥ piṣṭvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Having ground that lump with waters of <s>triphalā</s>, he should seal it and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
In a crucible, with a sixteenth part, he should cook it day and night in a windless place.
Thus it should be done three times: pot-cooking and then the intervening <s>puṭa</s>.
The liquid of <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>tālamūlī</s>, and the root of <s>hastikarṇa</s>,
root-decoctions of <s>śatāvarī</s> and <s>vidārī</s>, and also <s>triphalā</s>,

children.text: piṣṭvā tatpūrvavat sthālyāṃ pācyaṃ peṣyaṃ puṭe tridhā ||
children.translated_text: having ground it with these, as before it should be cooked in the pot, ground, and fired three times in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Then with waters of <s>punarnavā</s> and decoctions of <s>daśamūla</s>,
or with decoctions of <s>bṛhatī</s>, or with water of <s>bījapūra</s>,
likewise with <s>brahmabīja</s>, in a decoction of <s>śigru</s>, or even with cow's milk,
with each one separately, having first ground it, he should cook it in the former enclosing <s>puṭa</s>.
After the <s>puṭa</s>, he should soak it with the liquid alone for just one <s>yāma</s>.
With each one successively in this way, having ground it, he should treat it with <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: mriyate nātra saṃdehaḥ kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca muṇḍakam
children.translated_text: There is no doubt: <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍaka</s> iron are killed.
All this killed iron should be blown or smelted with the five <s>mitras</s>.
If in this way it has no rising again, it is fit to be used and becomes <s>vāritara</s> (floating on water).

children.text: madhvājyaṃ mṛtaṃ lauhaṃ ca sarūpyaṃ saṃpuṭe kṣipet
children.translated_text: Honey, ghee, killed iron, and an equal amount of silver should be placed in a sealed capsule.

children.text: ruddhvā dabhāyaṃ tu saṃgrāhyaṃ rūpyaṃ ca pūrvamānakam ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed it, it should be collected after the obscure <s>dabhāya</s> treatment, and the silver should be in the former measure.

children.text: tadā lauhaṃ mṛtaṃ vidyādamṛtaṃ mārayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should know the iron to be killed; if it is not killed, he should kill it again.

children.text: gandhakaṃ tu mṛtaṃ lauhaṃ tulyaṃ khalve vimardayet
children.translated_text: Sulfur and killed iron, in equal amounts, should be triturated in a mortar.
For one day with liquids of <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe), it should be sealed and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
In this way this <s>niruttha</s> process should be performed for all metals.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ kṛtvā khalve tu kajjalīm
children.translated_text: Having made purified mercury and twice as much sulfur into <s>kajjalī</s> in a mortar,
one should triturate iron powder equal to the two with liquids of <s>kanyakā</s>.
After two <s>yāmas</s>, having taken it out, [place] that ball in a copper vessel.
Covering it with castor leaves, it will become hot in half a <s>yāma</s>.
Afterwards one should place it in a heap of grain; after three days he should take it out.

children.text: sampiṣya gālayed vastre sadyo vāritaraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having ground it well, he should strain it through cloth; at once it becomes <s>vāritara</s>.

children.text: kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tathā muṇḍaṃ nirutthaṃ jāyate mṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s> iron become killed and <s>niruttha</s>.
In this way he should kill gold and the other metals too, after powdering them, just like iron.
This perfected procedure is famous, received face to face from the <s>siddhas</s>.
The iron preparation, made fit to be food, removes all diseases and fevers.
Mixed with the juice of <s>triphala</s>, it should be applied in all diseases.
Dead, calcined irons come under control,
and, when used with proper method, they destroy all ailments.
Through repeated use, made firm and perfected in its procedure,
they bring about the destruction of disease, death, and old age.
With water reduced until one eighth remains, and with five <s>palas</s> of <s>triphala</s>,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ kvāthasya tulyaṃ syāccūrṇaṃ tulyaṃ mṛtāyasam ||
children.translated_text: the ghee should be equal to the decoction, and the powder should be an equal amount of dead iron.
One should cook it in a copper vessel and stir it with an iron ladle.
It should be cooked over a gentle fire until the sulphur is digested.
<s>Śivā</s> equal to the iron should be added, and when it is well cooked one should take it down.
This is known as a <s>yogavāha</s> (carrier of a formulation); dead iron is a great elixir.

children.text: evaṃ kāntasya tīkṣṇasya muṇḍasyāpi vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus too the procedure is remembered for <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and even <s>muṇḍa</s> iron.
Iron ash, with one <s>pala</s> added, should be cooked in a <s>kuḍava</s> of molasses.
In diseases it should be administered in a dose the size of a jujube, according to the particular preparation.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tulyaṃ mṛtaṃ lohaṃ lohapātragataṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: One should cook an equal amount of ghee and dead iron placed in an iron vessel.
When the ghee has been digested, one should take it up and use it in carrier preparations.

children.text: oṃ amṛtena bhakṣyāya namaḥ anena manunā lauhaṃ bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: With the mantra, "oṃ, homage to the one to be eaten with nectar," one should consume the iron.
Iron gives life, virility, and strength, and removes anemia, urinary disease, and skin disease and the like.
It removes <s>āmavāta</s> and destroys wrinkles and grey hair.
The three alkalis and the five salts should be triturated seven times with an acidic liquid.
Sheets of <s>kāṃsya</s>, <s>āra</s>, and <s>ghoṣa</s> should be smeared with sesame paste.
Having sealed them, one should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; they attain purification and not otherwise.
One should kill them like copper; after preparing them, one should use them everywhere.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ kaṣāyamuṣṇaṃ ca laghu rūkṣaṃ ca tiktakam
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṃsya</s> is astringent and hot, light, dry, and bitter.
It destroys disorders of phlegm and bile and increases welfare of the heart, body, and life.

children.text: rītikā ca galaṃ rūkṣam atiktalavaṇaṃ saram
children.translated_text: <s>Rītikā</s> is drying to the throat, dry, not bitter, salty, and mobile.
It is purifying, destroys all diseases, and increases strength, virility, and life.

children.text: alpāṅgāre dhamet kiṭṭaṃ lauhajaṃ ca gavāṃ jalaiḥ
children.translated_text: One should heat iron-born slag over a small bed of coals and sprinkle it with cow urine,
and also with leaves of <s>akṣa</s>, seven times again and again.
This is called <s>maṇḍūra</s>; when purified and finely powdered, it should be applied.
<s>Muṇḍa</s> iron is a hundred times better than slag, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is a hundred times better than <s>muṇḍa</s>.
<s>Kānta</s> iron produces by ingestion a quality a hundred thousand times greater than <s>tīkṣṇa</s>.

children.text: tasmāt kāntaṃ sadā sevyaṃ jarāmṛtyuharaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>kānta</s> should always be used; it is supreme in removing old age and death.
I shall describe the extraction of oils, by cooking in the sun or else in fire.
Whatever oil is obtained by the use of an apparatus should be used in preparations.
One should prepare powders of <s>dhattūra</s> seeds, sifted through cloth.
Having smeared a bronze vessel with them, one should keep it in fierce sunlight.
When it is thoroughly heated and filtered through cloth, one should make the oil fall and collect it.
From the seeds of <s>śigru</s>, <s>puṣkara</s>, and <s>mārkava</s> also,
the oil of each separately should be taken in the same way as with <s>dhattūra</s>.

children.text: yathā dhattūrajaṃ tailaṃ kvāthād gharme samuddhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Just as oil from <s>dhattūra</s> is extracted from a decoction by heat,
so everywhere oils should be collected from other medicinal substances.
There should also be oil of <s>aṅkoṭa</s>, with <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> together with its root.
And oil should be made from <s>vākucī</s> and <s>devadālī</s>, and from the root of <s>karkoṭī</s>.
By means of a decoction of <s>apāmārga</s>, oil from <s>viṣatuṇḍa</s> may be obtained.
With root-decoctions of <s>kumārī</s>, oil from <s>jaipāla</s> may be obtained.
With a decoction of <s>raktamārga</s>, one should extract <s>vākucī</s> oil.
And with a decoction of <s>indravāruṇī</s>, <s>āragvadha</s> oil may be obtained.
From a decoction produced from <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> and <s>apāmārga</s>, one should collect the oil.
One should stir the seeds of bitter gourd with cow dung.
When dry, one should pound them in a mortar together with rice husks.
Then, after removing the husks and powdering them, together with the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>,
one should triturate them and, in the sun, take the oil when pressing is applied.
One should make powders from the seeds of <s>kṛṣṇā</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>.
Combining them with powdered <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s>, one should seal the mixture.
Having cooked it placed in a heap of grain, when it is removed one should collect the oil.
The seed-and-stone powder should be impregnated with juices of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit.

children.text: dinaikaṃ ca tato yantre tailaṃ grāhyaṃ ca tailake
children.translated_text: After one day, the oil should be taken in the oil-apparatus.
<s>Guñjā</s> and <s>karañja</s> fruit should be impregnated with human urine.
After seven times, one should smear a bronze vessel in the heat.

children.text: uddhṛtya dhārayed gharme tailaṃ patati pīḍanāt ||
children.translated_text: Having removed it, one should keep it in heat; the oil falls out under pressing.
Having ground the powder with increasingly strong <s>āranāla</s>, one should impregnate it.
In the sun, one should collect the oil arising from seeds of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>.
Powder of <s>putrajīva</s> seeds and that born from <s>agastya</s> seeds
should be prepared like <s>āmrātaka</s>; then the oils are obtained separately.
The powder of <s>bilva</s> seeds should be impregnated with coconut water.
After one day, one should extract the oil with an oil-apparatus and use it.
One should lightly rub husked <s>aṅkola</s> seeds a little.
After grinding them with a chickpea coating, one should smear them on a bronze vessel.

children.text: tanmukhe ṭaṃkaṇaṃ cūrṇaṃ kiṃcit kiṃcit pralepayet
children.translated_text: At its mouth, one should sprinkle powdered <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> little by little.
One should keep it in fierce sunlight and collect the oil from the mouth.
Having ground it with an equal amount of <s>śamī</s> powder, one should place it in a perforated pot.

children.text: chidrādhaḥ sthāpayed bhāṇḍaṃ chidre keśaṃ ca dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Beneath the hole one should place a vessel, and one should put a hair into the hole.
One should sprinkle the substance with water and collect it below the hole.
Into its middle one should insert a hair soaked in ghee, and gently place a firing above.
At once it becomes in the form of a fluid; this is the hair-oil.
Having taken the juice of unripe <s>bhānupatra</s> leaves, one should triturate it.
The whole powder of seeds, both those mentioned and those not mentioned, should be treated separately, one by one.

children.text: ātape mucyate tailaṃ sādhyāsādhyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the sunlight oil is released; there is no doubt about what can and cannot be prepared.
In the same way, one should collect it with a decoction of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>.
One should cause the oil of all seeds to be taken up in fierce sunlight.
The dried material of all seeds, bones, and flesh should indeed be ground in many ways.
Or, from all seeds, the oil should be taken in a <s>pātālayantra</s> (subterranean apparatus).
From bamboo and every kind of wood, from coconut shell,
and from husks, grains, and seeds, the little oil is obtained by means of a <s>garbhayantra</s> (enclosed apparatus).
One should extract it from all seeds, and then employ it in the medicinal formulas.
<s>Vatsanābha</s> is a poison, sweet in taste, kindling digestion and conquering phlegm and wind.
When joined with the proper formula, it becomes nectar-like and pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>.
It nourishes strength and virility and is like a hundred submarine fires.
In counteracting <s>sannipāta</s> (combined humoral disorder), its efficacy is indeed powerful.

children.text: uddhṛtaṃ phalapākānte navaṃ snigdhaṃ ghanaṃ guru
children.translated_text: Taken up at the time when the fruit ripens, fresh, oily, dense, and heavy,
not spreading, poison-destroying, and dried by wind and sunlight,
it should be smeared with red mustard oil and kept in cloth.
Or else, as obtained, the poison should be combined with cow urine.

children.text: ātape tridinaṃ śuṣkaṃ nihitaṃ vīryadhṛk bhavet
children.translated_text: Dried in the sun for three days and stored away, it becomes retaining its potency.

children.text: mṛtaṃ sūtābhrakaṃ lauhaṃ viṣaṃ ca tulyavīryakam ||
children.translated_text: Killed mercury, mica, iron, and poison are equal in potency.
Therefore poison should be used as a <s>yogavāhin</s> (carrier) in a rasāyana preparation.

children.text: tāni caiva tu mānāni aṣṭau ṣaḍvā caturthakam ||
children.translated_text: And those measures are eight, six, or a quarter part.
Three doses are taught: superior, inferior, and middling.
It should be given in all diseases to one who eats ghee and wholesome food.
It should be given to a man observing rasāyana practice who lives on milk.

children.text: na krodhine na pittāḍhye na klībe rājayakṣmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: It should not be given to one who is angry, rich in bile, impotent, or suffering from royal consumption.
Nor to one dried up by hunger, thirst, exertion, work, or travel, or to a patient with wasting disease.
Poison is not to be given among pregnant women, children, or the aged, nor in a royal palace.

children.text: na dātavyaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ visaṃvāde kadācana
children.translated_text: It is not to be given or eaten at any time when there is disagreement.
But it should be consumed by the teacher, as something that creates confidence in the pupil.
One should grind it with this mantra and should not place it on the ground.
One should say, 'It is nectar'; this is the procedure.
Om. Homage to the accomplished gurus.
Homage to the supreme gurus.
Homage to the gurus beyond the highest.
Homage to the supreme-standing gurus.
<s>Saktuka</s>, <s>mustaka</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>vālaka</s>, and what is called mustard,
together with <s>vatsanābha</s>, <s>kūrma</s>, and white <s>śṛṅgī</s> as the eighth:
these eight should be used in a formula, while <s>kālakūṭa</s> and the others are to be avoided.
<s>Kālakūṭa</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>hālāhala</s>, and <s>dardura</s>,
<s>karkaṭa</s>, <s>markaṭa</s>, <s>granthi</s>, <s>hāridra</s>, and red <s>śṛṅgaka</s>,
and <s>keśava</s> as the tenth: these are to be avoided by the best physicians.
One should use those beginning with <s>saktuka</s> in rasāyana for all diseases.

children.text: etadviṣaṃ jāticatuṣṭayaṃ ca vicārya yojyaṃ bhiṣaguttamena ||
children.translated_text: This poison and the four classes should be examined and used by the best physician.

children.text: vipro rakṣati yauvanaṃ narapatistadbhūtale pālatāṃ vaiśyaḥ kuṣṭhavināśane ca kuśalaḥ śūdro harejjīvanam
children.translated_text: The brahmin protects youth; the king protects sovereignty on that earth; the merchant is skilled in destroying skin disease; the śūdra removes life.

children.text: tasmāccāpi bhiṣagvareṇa nipuṇaistadvedinā bhāvayet kuryādeva tato viṣaṃ nṛpavaro mṛtyuṃjayāya kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the excellent physician, skilled and knowing that, should process the poison; then the excellent king should act on earth for victory over death.

children.text: śvetā vā yadi vā piṅgā madhurā ūṣarāpi vā
children.translated_text: Whether white, tawny, sweet, or even saline,
if it is hairy, it is of the brahmin class; the kṣatriya class is red.

children.text: pītā vā madhurā kiṃcid vaiśyajātistu dhūsarā
children.translated_text: If yellow or slightly sweet, it is of the vaiśya class; if grayish,

children.text: kṛṣṇā śūdrasya dṛśyeta eteṣāṃ ca bhiṣagvaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and black, it is seen as the śūdra's; these are to be recognized by the best physicians.
Having placed poison in a vessel filled with milk, one should examine it.

children.text: jāyate'pi yadā varṇaṃ tadā jātiṃ vinirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: When a color appears, then one should determine its class.

children.text: śuklaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ceti caturvidham
children.translated_text: White, red, yellow, and black: thus it is fourfold.
The determination of class for brahmin, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra should be known.

children.text: kṣiptaṃ dugdhe viṣaṃ vaidyo jānīyāt kramaśo yadi
children.translated_text: If a physician throws poison into milk, he should know it in order,

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ coṣṇalameva ca ||
children.translated_text: as white, red, yellow, black, and also hot and saline.
By grinding with <s>tuttha</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, poison is killed.
Among poisons called mobile, poison born from <s>nāga</s> is beneficial.
This alone is supremely excellent, destroying the three <s>doṣas</s> in an instant.
It immediately kindles digestion, like a hundred submarine fires.
In counteracting <s>sannipāta</s>, its efficacy is indeed powerful.
Poison arising from <s>nāga</s>, obtained as available, should be combined with cow urine.

children.text: ātape tridinaṃ śuṣkaṃ nihitaṃ vīryadhṛg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Dried in the sun for three days and stored away, it becomes retaining its potency.

children.text: atimātraṃ yadā bhuṅkte tadārjya ṭaṅkaṇaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: When someone consumes an excessive dose, he should then drink clarified butter with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.

children.text: rajanī meghanādā vā sarpākṣī vā ghṛtānvitā ||
children.translated_text: Or he should take <s>rajanī</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, or <s>sarpākṣī</s> together with ghee.
Or he should lick powdered bark of <s>arjuna</s> with honey and ghee.
Or he should drink the pith of <s>putrajīvaka</s>, or the two kinds of <s>nimbaka</s>.

children.text: evaṃ viṣavidhiḥ khyātaḥ prayogaṃ ca vadāmyaham
children.translated_text: Thus the rule concerning poison has been stated; now I shall tell the application.
Poison, the three pungents, <s>musta</s>, turmeric, and neem leaf,

children.text: viḍaṅgam aṣṭamaṃ cūrṇaṃ chāgamūtraiḥ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: with <s>viḍaṅga</s> as the eighth powder, should be mixed in equal parts with goat urine.
A pill the size of a chickpea is taught; it is victorious and serves as a <s>yogavāhikā</s> (carrier).
Poison, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>balā</s>, and <s>tālīsapattra</s>,
black pepper, long pepper, and neem should be mixed equally with goat urine.
The pill should be made as before; the pill is a <s>yogavāhikā</s> (carrier).

children.text: nidrāṃ tandrāṃ klamaṃ dāhaṃ saphenaṃ lomaharṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Mobile poison causes sleep, torpor, fatigue, burning, frothing, horripilation,

children.text: śoṣaṃ caivātisāraṃ ca kurute jaṅgamaṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: drying up, and diarrhea.

children.text: sthāvaraṃ tu jvaraṃ hikkāṃ dantaharṣaṃ galagraham ||
children.translated_text: But immobile poison causes fever, hiccup, tooth sensitivity, and constriction of the throat.
Poison causes foaming, vomiting, loss of appetite, difficult breathing, and fainting.

children.text: na jānāti yadā mantrī viṣaṃ bhakṣeccikitsitam ||
children.translated_text: When the practitioner does not understand poison, he may consume poison as though it had been treated.
Then that very poison takes hold of him and sinks him as if in the ocean.
Therefore the king should carefully protect himself from a poison-physician.

children.text: prathamaṃ vahnikharparikāyāṃ manāgbhṛṣṭvā vakṣyamāṇamantreṇa nirviṣaṃ vidhāya gṛhṇīyāditi
children.translated_text: First, after slightly roasting it in a heated potsherd, one should make it free of poison by the mantra to be stated and then take it.

children.text: nimbudrave pittaṃ vāratrayaṃ vibhāvya prakṣālya saṃśoṣya gṛhṇīyāditi
children.translated_text: One should soak the bile three times in lemon juice, wash it, dry it thoroughly, and then take it.
Mountain minerals such as gold, heated by the sun, exude.
The exudation that resembles lac, is soft, and resembles earth is <s>śilājatu</s>.

children.text: anaghaṃ cālpakaṣāyaṃ ca kaṭu pāke śilājatu
children.translated_text: Good <s>śilājatu</s> is flawless, slightly astringent, and pungent in post-digestive effect.
It is neither too hot nor too cold, and it arises from four metals.
It comes from gold, then from silver, from copper, and best of all from black iron.

children.text: madhuraṃ ca satiktaṃ ca japāpuṣpanibhaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: That which is sweet, slightly bitter, and like a hibiscus flower in appearance,

children.text: vipāke kaṭu śītaṃ ca tatsuvarṇasya nisṛtam
children.translated_text: pungent in post-digestive effect and cold, is what has flowed from gold.

children.text: rājataṃ kaṭukaṃ śvetaṃ śītaṃ svādu vipacyate ||
children.translated_text: The silver-derived kind is pungent, white, cold, and becomes sweet in digestion.
That from copper resembles a peacock's neck, is sharp and hot, and digests pungently.
That which resembles <s>guggulu</s>, is somewhat bitter, and is joined with saltiness,

children.text: vipāke kaṭu śītaṃ ca sarvaśreṣṭhaṃ tadāyasam
children.translated_text: pungent in post-digestive effect and cold, is the iron-derived kind; it is the best of all.
All have the smell of cow urine and are suitable in all procedures.
In rasāyana applications, however, the last is especially distinguished.
In order, for vāta-pitta, phlegm-pitta, kapha, and the three doṣas together,
the exudates born from gold and the other metals are especially praised.
The iron type becomes like slag in fire and burns without smoke in water.

children.text: tṛṇādyagre kṛtaṃ śreṣṭham adho galati tantuvat
children.translated_text: When placed on the tip of grass and the like, the best kind melts downward like a thread.
For removing defects from bites, fangs, medicines, and the like, one should fumigate ram's horn with birch bark.

children.text: kvāthyadravyaṃ śilājatusamaṃ caturguṇena jalaṃ dattvā caturbhāgāvaśeṣeṇa bhāvayed ityekaḥ pakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: One view is that the decoction-drug should be equal to the <s>śilājatu</s>; after adding four times as much water and reducing it to one quarter, one should use it for levigation.
<s>Vāgbhaṭa</s>, however, teaches adding eight times as much water and reducing it to one eighth; in practice both methods are used as before.
Good <s>śilājatu</s> should be placed in a hot filtered decoction of <s>triphala</s> and <s>daśamūla</s>,

children.text: kevaloṣṇodake vā sthite ūrdhvaṃ vībhūte paddhapatravat sarvaṃ grāhyam
children.translated_text: or in hot water alone; when it has settled and separated above like a lotus leaf, all of it should be taken.

children.text: tataḥ śivāguḍikoktakrameṇa bhāvanāṃ dattvā viśodhya sālasārādinā bhāvayedyathā
children.translated_text: Then, following the procedure stated for <s>Śivā-guḍikā</s>, one should give it levigations, purify it, and levigate it with the group beginning with <s>sālasāra</s>, as follows.
The two <s>sāla</s> trees, the two <s>karañja</s> trees, <s>khadira</s>, and the two <s>candana</s> types,
<s>gardabhāṇḍa</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, and here the pair of <s>lodhra</s> and <s>dhavāsana</s>,
<s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>aguru</s>, <s>kālīyaka</s>, <s>pūga</s>, <s>pūtika</s>, and <s>karkaṭa</s>:
this group also, beginning with <s>sālasāra</s>, removes phlegmatic diseases.
It removes urinary disorders, abdominal tumors, hemorrhoids, skin diseases, excess fat, and the pains of anemia.

children.text: ebhirdivātape śoṣyaṃ rātrau rātrau ca bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: With these, it should be dried in the daytime sun and levigated night after night.
The required amount of liquid is that by which the substance becomes unified and reaches moistness.
This is the measure prescribed by physicians in the rule for levigation.
The drug to be decocted should be equal in amount, and the decoction should be reduced to one eighth.
With that, the substance, made equally moist, should be dried in strong sunlight.

children.text: dagdhahīrakaṃ yojyaṃ nikṣipyāgnau dhmāpayitvā nirguṇḍīrasena saptavārān nirvāpya prakṣālya ca gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Calcined diamond should be added; after placing it in fire and blowing on it, one should quench it seven times in the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, wash it, and then take it.
They arise in the <s>Vāmaruka</s> region in summer, oppressed by the heat of the sun,

children.text: śītoṣaṇe śiśire ca guggulurasaṃ muñcanti te pañcadhā ||
children.translated_text: and in cold, heat, and winter they release <s>guggulu</s> resin in five forms.

children.text: hemābhaṃ mahiṣākṣatulyamaparaṃ tatpadmarāgopamaṃ bhṛṅgābhaṃ kumudadyutiṃ ca vidhinā grāhyā parīkṣyā tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: One is gold-colored, another like a buffalo's eye, another like ruby, another like a bee, and another shining like a white lotus; after examining them, they should be taken according to rule.

children.text: vahnau jvalanti tapane vilayaṃ prayānti klidyanti koṣṇasalile payasā samānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They blaze in fire, melt in the sun, and become moist in lukewarm water, resembling milk.
The auspicious good ones should be taken; one should avoid those long aged, visibly cracked in body, and like <s>kharpara-gandhika</s> in color.

children.text: svāde svāduḥ kaṣāyatiktakaṭuko vīrye vipāke kaṭuḥ
children.translated_text: In taste it is sweet, astringent, bitter, and pungent; in potency and post-digestive effect it is pungent.
It is aphrodisiac, exceedingly clear in cleansing the channels, sharp, diffusive, and flowing.
It promotes long life, gives voice, pacifies the three doṣas, and produces intelligence, memory, and beauty.
It is auspicious, destroys sin, kindles the digestive fire, and again purifies the heart and throat.

children.text: daśamūlakvāthe uṣṇe pūte gugguluṃ parikṣipyāloḍya ca vastrapūtaṃ vidhāya caṇḍātape viśoṣya ghṛtaṃ dattvā piṇḍitavyam ||
children.translated_text: One should put <s>guggulu</s> into a hot, filtered decoction of <s>daśamūla</s>, stir it, filter it through cloth, dry it in fierce sunlight, add ghee, and form it into a lump.
Likewise one should levigate <s>śaṅkhanābhi</s> with an acid liquid seven times.
In the sun, after discarding the impurities and so forth, one should wash it and take it.
One should put the cowry into the fine juices of buttermilk, <s>cāṅgerī</s>, and lemon,
and levigate it until it is no longer seen as white.
Afterwards one should take it out and use the cowry that has reached purification.

children.text: bhaumikaṃ jalam ādāya muktāṃ ca vyuṣitāmapi
children.translated_text: Taking mineral water and also a pearl, even one that has been left overnight,

children.text: tyaktvā malādikāṃ tāṃ ca prakṣālya grāhayediti ||
children.translated_text: one should discard its impurities and so forth, wash it, and take it.

children.text: kaliṅgakāravallyamlatailakūṣmāṇḍarājikāḥ jayati sa rasarājo mṛtyuśaṅkāpahārī sakalaguṇanidhānaṃ kāyakalpādhikārī
children.translated_text: <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>kāravallī</s>, acid oil, <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, and <s>rājikā</s>: victorious is that king of rasas, remover of the fear of death, treasure-house of all virtues, and master of bodily transformation.

children.text: valipalitavināśaṃ sevito vīryavṛddhiṃ sthiram api kurute yaḥ kāminīnāṃ prasaṅgam ||
children.translated_text: When used, it destroys wrinkles and gray hair, increases virility, and makes intercourse with women firm.
Now then I shall proclaim the excellent perfection of the body.
When it is accomplished, all accomplishments arise for human beings.

children.text: na dehena vinā kiṃcid iṣṭam asti jagattraye
children.translated_text: Without the body, there is nothing desired in the three worlds.
Therefore, by every effort, effort should be directed toward that.
On an auspicious lunar-station day, after emesis and purgation have been performed,
then, for special purification, one should use the liquid produced from the <s>ketakī</s>-stana.
For three days one should drink one <s>kuḍava</s> each day; it removes the defect of salt.
<s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, combined with <s>ketakī</s>-stana,
when boiled and drunk for three days, are supreme for removing the defect of acidity.
<s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>vahni</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, the three pungents, <s>triphala</s>, and <s>vṛṣa</s>,

children.text: saindhavaṃ devadāruś ca mustā caitat samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: rock salt, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>mustā</s>: all these should be in equal amounts.

children.text: ghṛtair lehyaṃ tu karṣaikaṃ saptāhāt sarvadoṣajit ||
children.translated_text: One <s>karṣa</s> should be licked with ghee; within a week it conquers all the doṣas.

children.text: evaṃ viśuddhadehas tu pūjayed devatāṃ gurum
children.translated_text: Thus, with the body purified, one should worship the deity and the guru,
the maiden and the circle of <s>yoginīs</s>; then one should perform the rasāyana.
In a windless place, or in an underground chamber, free from external anxieties,
with the senses mastered and anger mastered, he should eat food of milk and <s>śāli</s> rice.
He may eat <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, barley food, wheat, and mung-bean soup,

children.text: jāṅgalaṃ bhakṣayen māṃsaṃ kevalaṃ kṣīram eva vā ||
children.translated_text: or meat from wild animals, or only milk.
Or he should eat strengthening food, free from greens and salt.

children.text: abhyaṅgaṃ mastunā kuryāt snānaṃ caiva sukhāmbunā ||
children.translated_text: He should perform oiling of the body with whey, and bathe with pleasant water.

children.text: kākinīṃ strīṃ bhajen nityaṃ svānukūlāṃ suyauvanām
children.translated_text: He should regularly enjoy a <s>kākinī</s> woman, favorable to him and in good youth.

children.text: rasendre bhakṣyamāṇe tu kāmāndho jāyate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when <s>rasendra</s> is being consumed, a man becomes blinded by desire.

children.text: maithunena vinā tasya hy ajīrṇo jāyate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Without sexual intercourse, his mercury becomes undigested.
When it is undigested, tremor, burning, pains, hiccup, fainting, fever, and aversion arise,
as do cough, shortness of breath, loss of appetite, vomiting, dizziness, and delusion.
Therefore he should resort to a fortunate woman and avoid an unfortunate one.
He should avoid body-oiling with pungent oil, sour gruel, liquor, curds,
<s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>kāravallī</s>, sour oil, <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, and <s>rājikā</s>,
<s>bilva</s>, mushrooms, <s>arka</s>, eggplant, <s>vidala</s>, and <s>kākamācikā</s>,

children.text: mūlakaṃ laśunaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ śītam uṣṇaṃ ca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: radish, garlic, and whatever is sharp, cold, or hot.

children.text: rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ tyājyaṃ divāsvāpaṃ ca maithunam
children.translated_text: Wakefulness at night, sleeping by day, and sexual intercourse should be abandoned.
Quarrels, agitation, anxieties, and grief too should be avoided.
From transgression there may arise colic, sleepiness, lassitude, fever, and aversion.
To pacify that, for three days he should drink cucumber fruit with water,
or lick powder of dry ginger and rock salt with the sour juices of citron.

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ gavāṃ mūtraiḥ pibed vā tatpraśāntaye ||
children.translated_text: Or he should drink <s>sauvarcala</s> salt with cow urine in order to pacify it.
He should boil <s>vandhyākarkoṭakī</s>, <s>puṅkhā</s>, and <s>pātālagaruḍī</s> with water,
using eight times as much water, reduced to one eighth, together with rock salt.
For three days he should drink it; it destroys all disorders and was spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: mūlaṃ vā kāravallyutthaṃ saindhavaṃ vā gavāṃ jalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or he should take the root produced from <s>kāravallī</s>, or rock salt, with cow's liquid.
For three days he should drink a <s>karṣa</s>-measure; it conquers all disorders.
This has been taught for consumers of mercury who follow an improper regimen.

children.text: amum eva vidhiṃ kuryād rasāyanavidhau kila
children.translated_text: Indeed, in the procedure of rasāyana one should perform this very rule.

children.text: amṛtaṃ vidhisaṃyuktaṃ vidhihīnaṃ tu tad viṣam ||
children.translated_text: With the proper procedure it is nectar; without the procedure, however, it is poison.
The four aromatics, camphor, <s>kaṅkola</s>, and <s>kaṭukī</s> fruit
should be eaten together with betel; this is beneficial for the transmission of mercury.
Now here the killing of mercury at the beginning will be taught properly.
Of <s>rasendra</s> that has a mouth, or that has had its mouth opened by preparation,

children.text: krameṇa jārayet svarṇaṃ samāṃśaṃ pūrvavat tataḥ
children.translated_text: one should gradually digest an equal portion of gold, as before; then,
after adding to it an equal amount of sulfur, with the liquids of divine herbs

children.text: mardayet tridinaṃ khalve mūṣāyāṃ cāndhitaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: one should grind it for three days in a mortar; then, sealed in a crucible,
it should be heated in a cow-dung fire for a day and night, or for three nights with husk-fire.
When it has been heated, one should grind it again with seeds produced from divine herbs.
Grinding it in the mortar for four <s>yāmas</s>, sealed in a diamond-crucible, one should blow it.
It then becomes calcined mercury; that is to be employed in every rasāyana.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ samaṃ svarṇaṃ yāmam amlair vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: Purified mercury and an equal amount of gold should be ground for a <s>yāma</s> with acids.
After washing, one should take the paste; purified sulfur should be half the amount of the paste.
After adding borax equal to half the sulfur, and turmeric equal to the whole,
all that should be ground with <s>strīpuṣpa</s> (menstrual fluid), together with plantain juice.
At the end of the day, making it into a pellet, one should cook it in a sand apparatus.

children.text: dinaṃ mandāgninā taṃ vai samuddhṛtya vicūrṇayet
children.translated_text: For one day over a gentle fire, one should take it out and pulverize it.

children.text: cūrṇāṃśaṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā garbhayantre tryahaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: After adding sulfur equal to the amount of the powder, one should cook it for three days in a womb-apparatus.
By husk-fire, because of its lightness, it becomes calcined mercury.
Purified mercury should be three parts, and copper powder one part.

children.text: dinaikaṃ mardayed amlaiḥ kṣālitaṃ piṣṭim āharet
children.translated_text: One should grind it for one day with acids; after it is washed, one should take the paste.
And purified essence from <s>mākṣika</s> should be prepared equal to the paste.
All that should be ground for three days with the juices of <s>cakramarda</s> leaves.
That pellet, placed in a womb-apparatus, should be cooked for three days with husk-fire,

children.text: karīṣāgnau divārātraṃ paced vā bhasmatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: or cooked in a cow-dung fire for a day and night; it will become ash.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ vyomasattvaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, essence of mica, and gold should each be in equal amounts.

children.text: sarvatulyaṃ viḍaṃ dattvā mardyaṃ rambhādravair dinam
children.translated_text: After adding <s>viḍa</s> equal to all of them, it should be ground for a day with plantain juices.

children.text: bījair divyauṣadhīnāṃ ca tulyair mardyaṃ dinadvayam ||
children.translated_text: And with equal seeds of divine herbs it should be ground for two days.
Placed in a womb-apparatus, it should be cooked; it is killed in a sealed heating, as before.
It should be four finger-breadths long and three finger-breadths wide.

children.text: mṛnmayaṃ sampuṭaṃ kṛtvā chāyāśuṣkaṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: Having made an earthen sealed vessel, one should cause it to dry in the shade.

children.text: lavaṇaṃ viṃśabhāgaṃ syād bhāgam ekaṃ tu guggulum ||
children.translated_text: Salt should be twenty parts, while <s>guggulu</s> should be one part.
Then grind everything with water; with that same paste, smear the inside of the sealed capsule.

children.text: liptvā tatra rasaṃ rundhyād garbhayantram idaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared it, one should enclose the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) there; this is the <s>garbhayantra</s> apparatus.
Take <s>vimalā</s> and purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury) in equal measure, with the juices of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>.

children.text: mardayet tridinaṃ taṃ vai kācakūpyāṃ niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: One should levigate it for three days and place it in a glass bottle.
But if there is no glass bottle, one should seal it in a covered pair of earthen saucers.
One should cook it in a sand-bath apparatus for four <s>yāmas</s>; it becomes killed.
Take the washed essence from <s>mākṣika</s>, and purified sulfur equal to that.
Add purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury) equal to the two together, and use the juices of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s> for a day.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ marditaṃ golaṃ vajramūṣāndhitaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: All that, levigated and made into a ball, should be sealed in a diamond crucible and cooked.
After one day in the sand-bath apparatus it becomes killed, reddish in color.
Sulfur in equal quantity should be placed above and below purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
It is to be put in the belly of a baked crucible; then add juice of <s>kākamācī</s>.

children.text: dvābhyāṃ caturguṇaṃ dattvā tām ācchādya pacec chanaiḥ
children.translated_text: After adding four times as much as the two substances, cover it and cook it slowly.
With gradual fire in a sand-bath apparatus, for four <s>yāmas</s>, it becomes killed.

children.text: snuhyā vā hemavallyā vā kṣīraiḥ śuddharasaṃ dinam
children.translated_text: With the milks of <s>snuhī</s> or <s>hemavallī</s>, one should levigate purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury) for a day.
One should levigate it with an equal amount of sulfur, place it in the <s>garbhayantra</s>, and roast it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Killed by the previous sequential method, it should be applied in the formulas.
Take <s>guñjā</s>, lac, wool, honey, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), equal to purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury).

children.text: tat sarvaṃ bhṛṅgajair drāvair dinam ekaṃ vimardayet
children.translated_text: One should levigate all that for one day with juices produced from <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
Sealed in a diamond crucible and heated by blowing, it dies and becomes moon-like.

children.text: dravais tu kīṭamāriṇyā hy ajamodādravaiś ca vā
children.translated_text: With juices of <s>kīṭamāriṇī</s>, or with juices of <s>ajamodā</s>,
or else with juices of <s>ahimārī</s>, or perhaps with the juices of white <s>aṅkula</s>,
one should levigate purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury), together with an equal amount of sulfur, for three days.
After sealing it in an earthen capsule, one should cook it in a dung-fire by day and night.

children.text: pacet tuṣāgninā vātha tridinān mriyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: Or one should cook it with a chaff-fire; in three days it is certainly killed.
Purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and killed diamond, in equal parts, are placed in a heated mortar.
They should be levigated with juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s>; at the end of three days one should remove them.
One should smear a diamond crucible with the seeds of divine herbs.
Having sealed the former <s>rasa</s> (mercury) in it, one should cook it for three days with a chaff-fire.
After cooking it and removing it, add purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury) equal to it.

children.text: ekīkṛtya tryahaṃ mardyaṃ haṃsapādyā dravair dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Combining them, one should levigate them firmly for three days with juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s>.

children.text: tadgolaṃ pūrvavat pacyān mṛtaṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: That ball should be cooked as before; it becomes well killed.
For diamond, mica, and the other eight metals, as stated in the <s>Rasakhaṇḍa</s>,

children.text: māraṇaṃ vādikhaṇḍe vā tathā jñeyaṃ rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: the killing should likewise be understood in the <s>Vādikhaṇḍa</s>, and similarly in rasāyana practice.

children.text: evaṃ mṛto rasavaraḥ paramāmūtaḥ syāt tatsevakāḥ satatam asya dṛḍhaṃ tu teṣām
children.translated_text: Thus the best <s>rasa</s> (mercury), when killed, becomes supreme nectar; for those who always consume it, it makes their body firm.

children.text: dehaṃ karoti sahasā surasundarīṇāṃ krīḍākṣamaṃ paramasundaram eva nityam ||
children.translated_text: It quickly makes the body fit for the sport of heavenly women, and always exceedingly beautiful.

children.text: dharmajñaiḥ śivavatsalair nirjarair bhūpair mahāsādhakaiḥ samyagdivyarasāyanena satataṃ kalpāntasīmāvadhi
children.translated_text: By knowers of <s>dharma</s>, devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, deathless kings, and great adepts, through proper divine rasāyana, constantly up to the limit of the end of an aeon,

children.text: rakṣyaṃ gātram anantapuṇyanicaye muktiś ca yasmād bhavet tad vakṣye paramādbhutaṃ sukhakaraṃ sāmrājyadaṃ dhīmatām ||
children.translated_text: the body should be protected amid an accumulation of endless merit, since liberation arises from it; I shall teach that supremely wondrous, pleasure-giving thing that grants sovereignty to the wise.
At first one should consume mica that has been killed and made into nectar.
For one month, by the <s>niṣka</s> measure, this is for the sake of preparing the field.

children.text: yasmād abhraṃ rasakṣetraṃ tataḥ kuryād rasāyanam
children.translated_text: Since mica is the field for <s>rasa</s> (mercury), therefore one should undertake the rasāyana.

children.text: akṣetrīkaraṇe sūto hy amṛto viṣatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: If the field has not been prepared, <s>sūta</s> (mercury), though deathless, turns into poison.
How could there be success in its fruit, just as with good seed in saline barren soil?
One should prepare ash of diamond and <s>pārada</s> (mercury) in equal portions.

children.text: sūtapādaṃ mṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ sarvaṃ mardyaṃ dināvadhi
children.translated_text: With a quarter part of killed gold, all of it should be levigated for a day.

children.text: haṃsapādyā dravair eva tadgolaṃ cāndhitaṃ puṭet ||
children.translated_text: With juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s> alone, that ball should be sealed and roasted in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: arkakṣīraiḥ punar mardyaṃ tadvad gajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Again it should be levigated with the milk of <s>arka</s>; in the same way it should be cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
One should consume it, increasing by mustard-seed increments, until one has increased it to a <s>māṣa</s>.
This <s>rasa</s> called <s>Vajrapañjara</s> is the refuge of practitioners.
<s>Citraka</s>, fresh ginger, rock salt, calcined <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, and <s>suvarcala</s> salt,

children.text: samaṃ sarvaṃ sadā cānu bhakṣyaṃ syāt krāmaṇe hitam
children.translated_text: all in equal parts, should always be eaten afterward; it is beneficial for <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrative activation).
By using it for six months, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
One is freed from wrinkles and gray hair, with a divine body and great strength.
One should prepare killed diamond in a twelfth part of killed <s>sūta</s> (mercury).

children.text: dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ mṛtaṃ kāntaṃ kāntatulyaṃ mṛtābhrakam
children.translated_text: Killed <s>kānta</s> should be equal to the two, and killed mica equal to the <s>kānta</s>.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ bhṛṅgajair drāvair marditaṃ bhāvayet tryaham ||
children.translated_text: All that, levigated with juices from <s>bhṛṅga</s>, should be impregnated for three days.

children.text: tryahaṃ gokṣurakadrāvaiḥ kṣaudrair māṣaṃ tato lihet
children.translated_text: For three days it should be treated with juices of <s>gokṣuraka</s>; then one should lick a <s>māṣa</s> with honey.
This <s>rasa</s>, named <s>Vajreśvara</s>, makes a diamond-like body for men.

children.text: caturmāsair jarāṃ hanti jīved brahmadinaṃ kila
children.translated_text: In four months it destroys old age; one is said to live for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
One should powder the five parts of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, together with an equal amount of <s>triphala</s>.

children.text: palaikaṃ madhunā lehyaṃ krāmakaṃ paramaṃ rase
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> should be licked with honey; it is the supreme <s>krāmaka</s> in <s>rasa</s> practice.

children.text: vajrasūtābhrahemnāṃ tu bhasma śuddhaṃ tu mākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: The pure ash of diamond, <s>sūta</s> (mercury), mica, and gold, together with purified <s>mākṣika</s>,
in equal parts, should be levigated firmly for seven days with juices of divine herbs.

children.text: ruddhvā taṃ tridinaṃ pacyād vālukāyantragaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, one should cook it for three days, again placed in a sand-bath apparatus.
After removing it, it should be impregnated for three days with juices from <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>sarpākṣī</s>.
One should lick one <s>māṣa</s> of <s>Vajradhārā-rasa</s> with honey and ghee.
By using it for six months, a man becomes equal to <s>Rudra</s>.
He is freed from wrinkles and gray hair, swift as the wind, and very strong.
<s>Punarnavā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, sesame, and <s>vājigandhā</s> are to be taken in equal parts.

children.text: sarvatulyā sitā yojyā cūrṇitaṃ bhakṣayet palam ||
children.translated_text: Sugar equal to all the ingredients should be added; after powdering it, one should eat a pala.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ pāradaṃ kāntaṃ mṛtaṃ sarvaṃ samaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Gold, mercury, and <s>kānta</s>, all calcined, should be in equal parts.
One should levigate it for three days with the juices of <s>śatāvarī</s> roots.
For three days with decoctions of <s>triphala</s>, and for three days with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s>,
when it has been so infused, one should eat the <s>Bhairava</s> rasa with honey and ghee.
Taking one māṣa at a time for the course of a year, one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
The root powder of <s>śatāvarī</s>, joined with the milk of a black goat,

children.text: palaikaikaṃ pibec cānu krāmakaṃ paramaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: one should drink one pala at a time afterwards; it is a supreme and beneficial <s>krāmaka</s> regimen.
Ash of rasa, an equal amount of sulfur, <s>śilājatu</s>, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
one should grind all together for one yāma and lick it mixed with honey and ghee.
One niṣka at a time for the course of a year: this is <s>Śilāvīra</s>, a great rasa.
It quickly destroys the time of old age, and one lives for three hundred years.
One should drink half a pala of <s>musalī</s> powder with juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>,
or else with juices of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit; this is indeed the auxiliary drink in the <s>krāmaka</s> course.
Purified mercury should be ground for three days with juices of <s>meghanāda</s>.

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ dviniśaṃ vyoṣaṃ samaṃ cūrṇaṃ prakalpayet
children.translated_text: One should prepare an equal powder of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, the two <s>niśā</s> drugs, and <s>vyoṣa</s>.

children.text: āragvadhasya mūlaṃ tu cūrṇasya dviguṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The root of <s>āragvadha</s> should be twice the amount of the powder.

children.text: cūrṇasya dviguṇaṃ cājyaṃ kṣaudraṃ caiva caturguṇam
children.translated_text: Ghee should be twice the amount of the powder, and honey four times as much.

children.text: sarvaṃ pūrvarase kṣiptvā mṛdvagnau cālayat pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having put everything into the preceding rasa, one should cook it over a gentle fire while stirring.
One should eat that lump, one karṣa at a time; it is <s>Amṛtārṇava</s>.
In the course of a year it destroys old age, and one lives for three hundred years.
One should drink one karṣa of <s>vākucī</s> powder with juices of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit.

children.text: pāradād dviguṇaṃ gandhaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvaṃ vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: One should thoroughly grind purified sulfur in twice the amount of mercury, all together.
In a mortar, again and again for three weeks, with the juices of <s>muṇḍī</s> and fresh ginger.

children.text: etat tulyaṃ śuddhatāmraṃ sampuṭe tan nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Pure copper equal to that should be confined in a covered crucible.
One should wrap it with a piece of cloth and, outside, with diamond-clay.

children.text: liptvā viśoṣayet taṃ vai samyag gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: After coating it, one should dry it and cook it properly in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> fire.

children.text: uddhṛtya sampuṭaṃ cūrṇyaṃ devadālyā dravais tryaham
children.translated_text: After taking out the covered crucible, it is to be powdered and treated for three days with juices of <s>devadālī</s>.
It should be separately infused with juices of hemp and <s>punarnavā</s>, three days with each.
Having added powder of dry ginger equal to that, mixed with honey and ghee,
one should lick two māṣas daily until the completion of a year.
This rasa is <s>Udayāditya</s>, supreme remover of old age and death.
Powders of <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, and <s>bhṛṅga</s>, each in equal quantity,

children.text: madhvājyābhyāṃ lihet karṣam anu syāt krāmaṇaṃ param
children.translated_text: one should lick one karṣa with honey and ghee; afterwards there should be the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s> regimen.

children.text: pārado gaganaṃ kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca māritaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Mercury, <s>gagana</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and sharp iron, calcined, in equal parts,
one should infuse for three days in the shade with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>dhātrī</s> fruit.
Together with sugar, honey, and ghee in equal amount, one should confine everything in a vessel.

children.text: dhānyarāśau sthitaṃ māsaṃ tato niṣkatrayaṃ samam
children.translated_text: It should remain for a month in a heap of grain; then three niṣkas should be taken in equal measure.

children.text: bhakṣayec ca pibet kṣīraṃ karṣaikaṃ triphalām anu ||
children.translated_text: One should eat it, drink milk, and afterwards take one karṣa of <s>triphala</s>.

children.text: rātrau śuṇṭhīṃ kaṇāṃ khāded varṣaikād amaro bhavet
children.translated_text: At night one should eat dry ginger and <s>kaṇā</s>; after one year one becomes deathless.

children.text: jīved brahmadinaṃ vīraḥ syād raso gaganeśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hero lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>; this rasa is <s>Gaganeśvara</s>.

children.text: vaṭakṣīrais tryahaṃ mardyaṃ gandhaṃ śuddharasaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Sulfur and purified rasa in equal parts should be ground for three days with the milk of the banyan.
One should cook it with a fire of banyan wood in an earthen vessel for five yāmas.
Repeatedly adding the milk of the banyan, one should stir it with that very wood.
After taking it out, it should be infused for three days with juices of <s>devadālī</s> leaves.
In the hot season, one guñjā, together with a betel leaf,
should always be eaten with the increase of the moon until the dose reaches sixteen guñjās.
Powder made from <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>, <s>vākucī</s>, and <s>devadālī</s>,

children.text: madhvājyābhyāṃ lihet karṣaṃ krāmakaṃ hy anupānakam ||
children.translated_text: one should lick one karṣa with honey and ghee; the auxiliary drink is indeed the <s>krāmaka</s> regimen.
In the course of a year it destroys old age, and one lives for three hundred years.
This rasa, named <s>Vaṭeśvara</s>, makes men's bodies adamantine.

children.text: mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ śuddhagandhaṃ triphalāṃ gugguluṃ samam
children.translated_text: Calcined mercury, purified sulfur, <s>triphala</s>, and <s>guggulu</s> in equal parts,

children.text: sarvaṃ vātāritailena miśraṃ karṣaṃ lihet sadā ||
children.translated_text: all mixed with <s>vātāri</s> oil, one should always lick in a dose of one karṣa.
In six months it destroys old age, and one lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.

children.text: ajasya vṛṣaṇaṃ pācyaṃ gavāṃ kṣīreṇa taṃ niśi
children.translated_text: The testicle of a goat should be cooked with cow's milk at night.
One should drink it afterwards with sugar; this rasa is <s>Acaleśvara</s>.

children.text: rasaṃ vajraṃ svarṇakānte muṇḍaṃ ca māritaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Rasa, diamond, gold, <s>kānta</s>, and iron, calcined, in equal parts,

children.text: mākṣikaṃ gandhakaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvaṃ jambīrajair dravaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: purified <s>mākṣika</s> and sulfur, all with liquids produced from lemons,

children.text: saptāhaṃ mardayet khalve tadgolaṃ cāndhitaṃ puṭet
children.translated_text: one should grind in a mortar for seven days, make it into a ball, seal it, and heat it in a covered firing.

children.text: bhūdhare dinam ekaṃ tu khyātaḥ siddharasaḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a mountain-like furnace for one day: it is renowned as the supreme perfected rasa.
One māṣa should be licked with honey; within a year it removes death and old age.
A man becomes divine-bodied and perfected, with the valor of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
One should always drink the root of white <s>punarnavā</s>, ground with milk.

children.text: bhakṣayed vā sitā sārdhaṃ krāmakaṃ parame rase ||
children.translated_text: Or one may eat it together with sugar as a <s>krāmaka</s> in the supreme rasa.
One should mix purified sulfur in twice the amount of calcined mercury.
After grinding it for one day with the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>, one should confine it.

children.text: dinaikaṃ madhunā pacyān niṣkaikaṃ madhunā lihet
children.translated_text: One should cook it for one day with honey and lick one niṣka with honey.

children.text: gandhāmṛto raso nāma vatsarān mṛtyujid bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The rasa named <s>Gandhāmṛta</s> becomes conqueror of death within a year.
One should powder whole <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, roots and all, dried in the shade.
There should be an equal amount of <s>triphala</s> powder, and sugar equal to everything.
After combining them, one should eat one pala at a time as the auxiliary drink.

children.text: pāradābhraṃ mṛtaṃ tulyaṃ dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ tu gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: Calcined <s>pārada</s> (mercury) and mica are to be in equal amounts, and the sulfur is equal to the two.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ bhṛṅgajair drāvair mardayed dinasaptakam
children.translated_text: All that should be ground for seven days with the liquids of <s>bhṛṅgaja</s> plants.
After giving it six levigations with <s>cāṅkulī</s> oils, one should then eat it.
The dose is one <s>māṣa</s> for one year; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Kālakaṇṭaka</s>.

children.text: piṣṭvā karañjapatrāṇi gavāṃ kṣīraiḥ pibed anu ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards one should grind <s>karañja</s> leaves and drink them with cow's milk.
Freed from old age and death, a man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Calcined mercury and mica, <s>kānta</s>, poison, <s>tāpya</s>, and <s>śilājatu</s>,
in equal parts, should always be licked in a dose of three <s>guñjās</s> with honey and ghee.

children.text: ṣaṇmāsena jarāṃ hanti jīved brahmadinaṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In six months it destroys old age, and a man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Powder of <s>aśvagandhā</s> root is to be combined with seven parts of ghee.

children.text: bhāgāṣṭakaṃ guḍaṃ tasmin kṣiped bhāgaṃ ca pippalīm ||
children.translated_text: Into it one should put eight parts of jaggery and one part of <s>pippalī</s>.

children.text: mṛdvagninā ca tat sarvaṃ piṇḍitaṃ bhakṣayet palam
children.translated_text: All that, made into a lump over a gentle fire, should be eaten in a dose of one <s>pala</s>.
This is indeed the supreme <s>krāmaka</s> for accomplishing <s>Amṛteśa</s>, the king of rasas.
One should add purified sulfur in three times the amount of purified mercury.
Powder of iron <s>parpaṭikā</s> should be added in an amount equal to the mercury.
All that should be ground for three days with the latex of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>.

children.text: tac chuṣkaṃ cāndhitaṃ pacyāt karīṣāgnau divāniśam ||
children.translated_text: When dry, it should be sealed and cooked in a cow-dung fire for a day and night.

children.text: tataś ca ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā ruddhvā dhamed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Then, after adding borax and glass, one should seal it and smelt it strongly.
One should eat one <s>guñjā</s> with honey; this is <s>Rasavīra Mahārasa</s>.
In one year it destroys old age, and one lives as long as the moon and stars.
One should drink powder of <s>musalī</s> root with the liquids of <s>guñjā</s> leaves,

children.text: chāgīmūtreṇa vā taṃ vai karṣaikaṃ krāmakaṃ param
children.translated_text: or with goat's urine, one <s>karṣa</s> of it; this is the supreme <s>krāmaka</s>.
Sulfur equal to calcined mercury should be ground for a day with the liquids of <s>kākamācī</s>.
After it has been ground and sealed, it should be cooked in a cow-dung fire for a day and night.
It should be ground for a day with the juices of leaves of divine herbs, and then sealed.

children.text: dhmātaṃ tasmāt samuddhṛtya tattulyaṃ hāṭakaṃ mṛtam
children.translated_text: After smelting it, one should take it out; calcined gold equal to that is then used.
Having combined them, one should lick one <s>māṣa</s> with ghee for the duration of a year.

children.text: jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ nihanty āśu satyaṃ kāñcāyano rasaḥ
children.translated_text: It quickly destroys old age and death; truly, this is the <s>Kāñcāyana Rasa</s>.
Powder produced from <s>dhātrī</s> fruit should be impregnated with the liquids of <s>kākamācī</s>.

children.text: madhunā bhakṣayet karṣam anu syāt krāmakaṃ param
children.translated_text: One should eat one <s>karṣa</s> with honey; afterwards there should be the supreme <s>krāmaka</s>.
Calcined mercury and mica, together with sulfur in equal amount, for seven days,
should be ground with the liquid of <s>śigru</s> root; that ball is placed inside a vessel.
After sealing it, one should cook it gently with <s>śāka</s> wood for a day.

children.text: parānando raso nāma ghṛtair niṣkaṃ sadā lihet
children.translated_text: This is the <s>rasa</s> named <s>Parānanda</s>; one should always lick one <s>niṣka</s> with ghee.
One should cook <s>kuṣṭha</s> well for one day with decoctions of <s>triphala</s>.

children.text: tac chuṣkaṃ cūrṇitaṃ karṣaṃ madhvājyābhyāṃ lihed anu
children.translated_text: When it is dry and powdered, one should then lick one <s>karṣa</s> with honey and ghee.
Through use for a year, one lives as long as the moon and stars.
Calcined mercury and mica are equal, and calcined iron is equal to those two.
Purified sulfur, in the portion of the iron, should be impregnated for seven days.
All that should be impregnated with decoctions of <s>triphala</s> and with the liquids of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: dravaiḥ pṛthak pṛthag bhāvyaṃ saptadhā saptadhā kramāt ||
children.translated_text: each separately, seven times and seven times in order.
