After it has been impregnated seven times with decoctions of <s>kaṭukī</s>, one should powder it again.
Powder of <s>kaṇā</s> equal to the powder, and old jaggery in equal amount,
should all be combined; one should eat one <s>niṣka</s> for the duration of a year.
This <s>rasa</s> is named <s>Mahākāla</s>, terrifying to old age and to time.
Afterwards one should eat sesame and <s>koraṇṭa</s> leaves with jaggery.
Iron <s>parpaṭaka</s> should be equal to the calcined mercury.
Sulfur should be three times the mercury; all of it is to be treated with the liquids of divine herbs.

children.text: marditaṃ taddinaṃ ruddhvā dhmāto baddho bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After being ground that day, sealed, and smelted, the <s>rasa</s> becomes fixed.

children.text: tasmin pādaṃ mṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ kṣiptvā vahnyārdrakadravaiḥ
children.translated_text: Into it one should add one quarter-part of calcined gold and grind it with the liquids of <s>vahni</s> and fresh ginger.
It should be ground for one <s>yāma</s>; then, having powdered it, with <s>vyoṣa</s>, cumin, and rock salt,

children.text: tulyaṃ pūrvarasaṃ tulyaṃ niṣkaikaikaṃ ca bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: one should eat equal amounts: an equal amount of the previous <s>rasa</s> and one <s>niṣka</s> of each.
This <s>Hemaparpaṭaka Rasa</s> quickly destroys old age and death.
<s>Yaṣṭi</s> equal to <s>aśvagandhā</s> should be impregnated for a day with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit.
Once impregnated, one should lick one <s>pala</s> with honey; this is the supreme <s>krāmaka</s>.

children.text: svarṇatārārkakāntaṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ vā māritaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, <s>kānta</s>, and sharp iron, or else these calcined, are equal.
Black mica essence and <s>mākṣīka</s>, each separately, are in an amount equal to the gold.
All that should be sealed and smelted; that ingot and calcined mercury

children.text: samaṃ sūtānmṛtaṃ vajraṃ pādāṃśaṃ tatra yojayet ||
children.translated_text: equal to the mercury, with calcined diamond as a quarter part, should be added there.
All of it should be thoroughly ground in a heated mortar with the juices of lemons.

children.text: dinaikaṃ taṃ nirudhyātha bhūdhare pāvayed dinam ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it for one day, one should heat it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus for a day.

children.text: uddhṛtya gandhakaṃ tulyaṃ dattvā ruddhvā dhamed drutam
children.translated_text: After taking it out, one should add equal sulfur, seal it, and smelt it quickly.
One should always lick that powder with honey and ghee in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>.
This <s>rasa</s>, named <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, grants <s>khecaratva</s> (the power of moving through the sky).
Through use for a year, one lives until the very end of the aeon.
By his urine and feces all metals become gold.

children.text: palaikaṃ gandhakaṃ kṣīraiḥ krāmakaṃ cānu pāyayet ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards one should make him drink one <s>pala</s> of sulfur with milk as the <s>krāmaka</s>.
One part of purified copper and twelve parts of purified mercury,
and three parts of the essence of <s>bhūnāga</s> should be combined together in one place.
All of it should be ground for a day in a heated mortar with the juices of lemons.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ kacchape yantre kṣiptvā tatraiva gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: All that should be placed in the <s>kacchapa</s> apparatus; there, sulfur itself,

children.text: kāsamardarasaiḥ piṣṭaṃ tulyaṃ dattvā nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: ground with the juices of <s>kāsamarda</s>, should be added in equal amount and sealed.

children.text: yāvaj jīrṇaṃ puṭe pacyād evaṃ ṣaḍguṇagandhakam ||
children.translated_text: One should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> until it is digested; in this way the <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) should be made sixfold.
One should digest it by the proper sequence; then, after taking it out, one should triturate it
for one <s>yāma</s> with liquids from lemons; then the <s>abhraka</s> (mica) is without its shining flakes.
Levigated with an equal amount of <s>amlavetasa</s>, it should be added to the <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
In a heated mortar, one should add a sixteenth part, sour <s>caṇaka</s>, and <s>tālaka</s>,

children.text: kāsīsaṃ ca daśāṃśena dattvā mardyaṃ dināvadhi
children.translated_text: and also <s>kāsīsa</s> in a tenth part; after adding them, it should be ground for a whole day.
All of that should be placed in a fired crucible and bound with cloth.
In a <s>dolāyantra</s>, with a <s>sāranāla</s>, one should cook it for three days over a gentle fire.
After taking it out, one should wash it with warm <s>kāñjika</s>; if it has been digested, so much the better.
If it is undigested, one should cook it in the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s>, together with <s>viḍa</s>.
Thus the <s>gagana</s> (mica) should be digested again and again until it equals the <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
Gold leaves smeared with peacock bile
should be added in the proportion of one sixty-fourth and thoroughly rubbed in the mortar.
One should sweat it in the apparatus as before; when it is digested, gold should again be added.

children.text: ityevaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ tu svarṇaṃ jāryaṃ rasasya vai ||
children.translated_text: In just this way, gold amounting to a sixteenth part should be digested into the <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: tato jāryaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ ca hemavat
children.translated_text: Then calcined diamond should be digested, one sixteenth part, just as with the gold.
After that it should be ground with <s>tālaka</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and lemon.
Then one should triturate that <s>sūta</s> (mercury) for three days with the liquids of divine herbs.
Enclosed in a diamond crucible, it should be heated by blowing; when it has become bound, one should powder it again.
One should eat a <s>guñjā</s>-measure of it together with honey and sugar.
This <s>rasa</s>, bound as <s>khecara</s>, becomes a conqueror of death in six months.
He becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair, endowed with great strength and valor.
For seven days, with liquids from <s>bhṛṅga</s>, three fruits of <s>nīlamuṇḍī</s>
should be impregnated; afterwards one should lick a <s>karṣa</s>-measure with honey and ghee.
With purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and twice as much <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), one should make <s>kajjalī</s> in a mortar.

children.text: tayostulyaṃ kāntacūrṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ vā muṇḍameva vā
children.translated_text: To those one should add an equal amount of powdered <s>kānta</s>, or else <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron or <s>muṇḍa</s> iron.
Having combined everything in a mortar, one should triturate it with the liquids of <s>kanyā</s>.
After one day, one should make it into a ball and place it in a copper vessel.
When it is covered with castor leaves, it becomes very hot within half a <s>yāma</s>.
One should place it in a heap of grain, and after two days take it out.
<s>Kanyā</s>, <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
<s>koraṇṭa</s>, <s>vākucī</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>śālmalī</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, and <s>dhūrta</s>: with the liquids of these, each separately,
it should be impregnated seven times each, and seven times with decoctions produced from <s>triphala</s>.
When it has been impregnated, it should be powdered; nutmeg and clove,

children.text: trikaṭu triphalā cailā cūrṇayen navakaṃ samam
children.translated_text: <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and <s>elā</s>: one should powder these nine in equal quantity.

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ pūrvacūrṇaṃ ca samaṃ kṣaudreṇa karṣakam ||
children.translated_text: That powder and the former powder should be taken in equal quantity; with honey, one <s>karṣa</s>
should be licked every day for one year, in order to pacify the time of old age.
This is the <s>Svayamagnirasa</s>, which has come well from the mouths of the <s>siddhas</s>.
One should lick half a <s>pala</s> of the powders of sesame and <s>aśvagandhā</s> with honey.
<s>Nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>nīlikā</s>, <s>vajrī</s>, <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, and <s>tridaṇḍikā</s>,
<s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>mudgaparṇī</s>, white <s>arka</s>, <s>vānarī</s>, and <s>jayā</s>,
<s>peṭārī</s>, black <s>dhattūra</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, and <s>kṣīrakandaka</s>:
with these substances, either all together or separately, it should be ground for three days.
Purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should be ground in a heated mortar; that paste, in <s>kṣīrakandaka</s>
or else in <s>vajrakanda</s>, should be enclosed; again with clay made from their piths,

children.text: taṃ kandaṃ vajramūṣāyāṃ ruddhvā laghupuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: one should seal that tuber in a diamond crucible and cook it in a light <s>puṭa</s>.
It should be ground again and cooked again; in this way, in order, seven times.

children.text: rasaḥ kakṣapuṭo nāma guñjaikaṃ madhunā lihet ||
children.translated_text: This <s>rasa</s> is called <s>Kakṣapuṭa</s>; one should lick one <s>guñjā</s> with honey.
He lives for one day of <s>Brahmā</s>, free from wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: varṣaikena na saṃdeho rasakāyo bhaven naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Within one year, without doubt, a man becomes possessed of a body transformed by <s>rasa</s>.
Powder of <s>bhallātaka</s> seed, with <s>hayagandhā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and ghee,

children.text: palaikaṃ bhakṣayec cānu krāmakaṃ paramaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: he should eat in the amount of one <s>pala</s>; afterwards the gradual after-regimen is supremely beneficial.
Calcined <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>abhraka</s> (mica), diamond, <s>kānta</s>, silver, copper, and gold,

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ ca tulyatulyāṃśaṃ sarveṣāṃ gandhakaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, each in equal parts, with sulfur equal to them all,
should all be levigated with oil of <s>palāśa</s> for seven days.
This is called <s>Mahāśaktirasa</s>; one should always lick a <s>māṣa</s> of it with honey.
In six months it destroys old age; he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
After a year he lives for seven aeons; there is no doubt at all.
Moving at will, a great <s>siddha</s>, he becomes equal to the supreme <s>śakti</s>.
By his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
Oil produced from <s>palāśa</s> seeds, eight <s>palas</s>, is to be licked with honey.

children.text: krāmakaṃ hy anupānaṃ syāt samyakchaktyā prakāśitam ||
children.translated_text: It is the <s>krāmaka</s> after-drink, properly revealed by <s>Śakti</s>.

children.text: lohitaṃ vātha vā kṛṣṇaṃ vaikrāntaṃ māritaṃ palam
children.translated_text: Red or else black <s>vaikrānta</s>, calcined, one <s>pala</s>,
one <s>pala</s> of gold powder, and two <s>palas</s> of purified mercury:
one should grind all that for a day with young castor juice and goat's urine.
<s>Śarapuṅkhā</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>kaṭutumbikā</s>,
and <s>indravāruṇikā</s>: with the liquids of these it should be ground for three days.

children.text: tadgolaṃ garbhayantre tu ruddhvā pacyād dinatrayam ||
children.translated_text: That ball should be sealed in a <s>garbhayantra</s> and cooked for three days.
With husk-fire, gently, it should be taken out and powdered.
After being impregnated seven times with liquids from <s>bhṛṅga</s>, it should be powdered again.
One should mix the powder equally with <s>triphala</s>, <s>tryūṣa</s>, honey, and ghee.
One should always eat one <s>māṣa</s> at a time; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Nāṭakeśvara</s>.
Within a year it fully destroys all disease, old age, and death.
With divine radiance and a mighty body, he lives as long as the moon and stars.
The root-bark from the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>, dried in the shade and powdered,

children.text: piben niṣkadvayāṃ takraiḥ krāmakaṃ paramaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: one should drink in a dose of two <s>niṣkas</s> with buttermilk; it is a supreme, auspicious <s>krāmaka</s>.
Well-purified white <s>vaikrānta</s> should be impregnated in the sun for seven days;
ground with <s>amlavetasa</s>, by that very means it will attain liquefaction.
This liquefied substance and purified mercury, in equal amount, with honey for three days,
having been ground, should be licked in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>; in a month a man becomes young.
In a year he becomes equal to <s>Brahmā</s>; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Bālasundara</s>.
Afterwards he should lick one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>vākucī</s> seed with honey and ghee.
Four <s>palas</s> of purified mercury and one <s>pala</s> of calcined gold,
with the juices of <s>palāśa</s> buds and with their oils, for three days,
one should grind in a heated mortar; and sulfur, equal to the gold,
purified, should be put into it, and one should grind it for a day with the substances mentioned before.
One should eat a pill measuring one <s>māṣa</s>; after a year he will become a conqueror of death.
The heroic man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Brahmapañjara</s>.
Powder from seeds produced by <s>vānarī</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, in equal amounts,
should be impregnated for three days with the juices of bark and leaves of <s>śālmalī</s>.
Then, impregnated for three days with liquids from <s>bhṛṅga</s>, one should powder it.
With old jaggery equal to it, one should afterwards eat one <s>karṣa</s>.
On red ground, having collected <s>bhūnāgas</s>, one should test them;

children.text: chede niryāti raktaṃ cet tān svīkuryāt prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: if blood comes out when they are cut, one should carefully accept them.
With black-colored cow's ghee, equal in amount, one should cook them
in an iron vessel, stirring, until it has the color of vermilion.
All that becomes ash; calcined mercury equal to that,
all stirred with honey, should be increased by half and half of a <s>guñjā</s>.
Afterwards one should always eat a <s>guñjā</s> for the duration of a year.
The <s>rasa</s> named <s>Śivāmṛta</s> removes old age and death for men,
and grants a lifespan of a day of <s>Brahmā</s>; afterwards one should make him drink <s>śivāmbu</s>.

children.text: evaṃ divyarasāyanaiḥ samucitaiḥ sārātisāraiḥ śubhaiḥ siddhaṃ dehamanekasādhanabalād yeṣāṃ tu dṛṣṭaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Thus, by these suitable divine <s>rasāyanas</s>, auspicious essences surpassing essences, I have seen the perfected body of those who achieved it through the power of many practices.

children.text: tānārādhya ca teṣu sāramakhilaṃ saṃgṛhya śāstrādapi bhūpānāṃ viduṣāṃ mahāmatimatāṃ proktaṃ hitārthāya vai ||
children.translated_text: Having honored them and gathered from them, and also from the śāstra, all the essence, it has been taught for the welfare of kings, learned men, and those of great intelligence.
The <s>rasāyana</s> of the divine-yoga pill does not succeed when it is without <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
It should be used precisely because it brings quick accomplishment; here this is the accompanying drink for the sake of <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
<s>Kākatumbī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>kumārikā</s>,

children.text: gojihvā saindhavaṃ guñjā hy ārdrakaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: <s>gojihvā</s>, rock salt, <s>guñjā</s>, and fresh ginger, all in equal amounts,
having ground them, every part of the crucible should be smeared with it to the measure of a finger.

children.text: pāradaṃ vyomasattvaṃ ca kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca muṇḍakam ||
children.translated_text: Mercury, mica essence, <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, and <s>muṇḍaka</s> iron,

children.text: tāpyasattvaṃ ca tulyāṃśaṃ sarvaṃ saṃcūrṇya mardayet
children.translated_text: and <s>tāpya</s> essence, in equal portions: one should powder everything and grind it
for a day with liquids from lemons, and put it into that crucible.
Having covered it, smeared it with paste, sealed it, and dried it,
one should cook it in a cow-dung fire, in a <s>puṭa</s>, for a day and night, and take it out.

children.text: punaḥ praliptamūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā ruddhvā puṭet tataḥ
children.translated_text: Again, after putting it into a smeared crucible and sealing it, one should heat it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
In just this way one should cook it in ten crucibles that have been smeared.
A divine pill arises, the supreme <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s>.

children.text: vaktre śirasi kaṇṭhe vā karṇe vā dhāritā kare ||
children.translated_text: Worn at the mouth, on the head, at the throat, at the ear, or in the hand,
properly encased in gold, it is supreme for arresting age.
It destroys wrinkles, gray hair, the fire of time, and fear of death.
After only a year, without doubt, one lives for three hundred years.
One should always drink one purified <s>pala</s> of it with cow's milk.

children.text: anena tv anupānena dehe saṃkramate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: By this accompanying drink the <s>rasa</s> passes into the body.
Activated mercury, <s>kānta</s>, <s>muṇḍa</s> iron, and mica essence,

children.text: tattvaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ sarvaṃ jambīrajair dravaiḥ
children.translated_text: the essence and calcined diamond, all with liquids from lemons,

children.text: saptāhaṃ mardayet tulyaṃ kṛtvā golaṃ samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: one should grind for seven days; having made an equal ball, one should take it out.
<s>Nirguṇḍī</s>, rock salt, honey, <s>gojihvā</s>, and <s>kākatuṇḍikā</s>,
having ground them, one should smear the ball all around to a thickness of one finger.

children.text: taṃ ruddhvā vajramūṣāyāṃ pacedyāmaṃ tu bhūdhare
children.translated_text: Having sealed it in a diamond crucible, one should cook it for one <s>yāma</s> in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
It should be smeared, sealed again, and cooked again; in this way for the duration of a fortnight.
With seeds from barley, tamarind, and <s>palāśa</s>, together with mustard and cotton seeds,
well ground, one should smear a crucible, with the former ball in its middle.

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ śvetakācaṃ ca dattvā pṛṣṭhe nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Having put borax and white glass on the back and sealed it,
one should blow with <s>khadira</s> charcoal until it becomes molten.
Then one should place it in a crucible smeared with <s>viḍa</s>.
One should add gold equal to it and bring it under control by blowing again and again.
When the gold has been digested, one should take it out and grind it in a heated mortar.
For three days, with liquids of divine herbs, one should blow it enclosed in a diamond crucible.

children.text: jāyate guṭikā divyā nāmnā vajreśvarī parā
children.translated_text: A divine pill arises, supreme, named <s>Vajreśvarī</s>.

children.text: vaktrasthā sā jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ hanti saṃvatsarātkila ||
children.translated_text: Kept in the mouth, it surely destroys old age and death in a year.

children.text: śastrastambhaṃ ca kurute brahmāyur yacchati dhruvam
children.translated_text: It also causes the arresting of weapons and certainly grants the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
On the black eighth lunar day, having gathered <s>sahadevī</s>, one should powder it well.

children.text: karṣaikāṃ bhakṣayed ājyairanu syāt krāmeṇa hitam
children.translated_text: One should eat one <s>karṣa</s> with ghee; afterwards, through the proper sequence, it will be beneficial.
Red <s>meghanāda</s> and likewise <s>pāṣāṇabhedaka</s>,
having ground them together with woman's breast milk, one should smear the crucible with that.
Putting into it one part of calcined diamond and sixteen parts of gold powder,

children.text: kṣiptvā tasyāṃ nirudhyātha yāmamātraṃ dṛḍhaṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: then, after sealing it, one should blow strongly for the measure of one <s>yāma</s>.
Having taken it out, one should place purified mercury equal to it in a mortar.
One should grind it with fresh ginger juices until it becomes a ball.
Taking the bulb of <s>caṇḍālī</s>, one should grind it well with women's breast milk.
Having coated the ball with this, one should seal it in a diamond crucible.
After cooking it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> fire, the pill called <s>Vajrasundarī</s> is to be taken.
One should hold it in the mouth for one year; he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
One should drink daily one <s>pala</s> of powder of the bark of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> with milk.
It is the <s>krāmaṇa</s> and the accompanying drink, exceedingly productive of success for the practitioner.

children.text: tadudbhavamalair liptaṃ tāmraṃ tu dhamanena hi ||
children.translated_text: Copper smeared with the impurities produced from that, by blowing in the furnace,
becomes divine gold. This is true, spoken by <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
As before, one should digest gold equal in amount to the opened <s>rasendra</s>.
Afterwards, by the application of <s>viḍa</s>, it should be ground for three days.
With divine herbs and cow urine, one should heat it after closing it in a diamond crucible.
Having taken it out, one should hold in the mouth the pill called <s>Hemasundarī</s>.
Then one should lick half a <s>pala</s> of sulfur with twice as much ghee.
In one year it destroys old age, and one lives as long as the moon and stars.
Purified mercury, calcined diamond, mica essence, and gold
should all be ground equally with the acidic group for three days.
Having made that ball firm, one should then dry it in the shade.
<s>Brahmakārpāsa</s> seeds, <s>rājikā</s>, <s>yavaciñcikā</s>,

children.text: vandhyā sarvaṃ samaṃ piṣṭvā pūrvagolaṃ pralepayet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>vandhyā</s>: having ground all these equally, one should coat the previous ball.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; having taken it out, he should then coat it again.
After sealing it in a crucible, one should heat it strongly; the pill called <s>Vajrakhecarī</s> results.
When held in the mouth for a year, it destroys death.
One <s>pala</s> of powder of <s>bhūtāravaṭa</s>, mixed with sugar,
should be eaten for the sake of <s>krāmaṇa</s>; a man obtains the life span of <s>Brahmā</s>.
With the leaf juices of cotton, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>kanyā</s>,

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ dinaṃ mardyaṃ kṣālyam amlaiḥ samuddharet
children.translated_text: purified mercury should be ground for a day, washed with sour liquids, and taken out.
Of that mercury, four <s>niṣkas</s>; of copper powder, half a <s>niṣka</s>;
mica-derived essence, one quarter less than a <s>niṣka</s>; and gold, one quarter <s>niṣka</s>.
Powder of iron equal to the gold should all be thoroughly ground with sour liquids.
At the end of the day, having made a ball, one should place it inside a lemon.
For three days one should cook it in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus with a good tube.
Having taken it out, one should hold in the mouth the pill called <s>Vyomasundarī</s>.
After only a year it destroys old age, and the man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Powder of <s>citramūla</s>, with honey, in a magnetic vessel,
should be stirred and eaten in a <s>karṣa</s> dose; afterwards it is beneficial for <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
One <s>niṣka</s> of gold leaf and three <s>niṣkas</s> of purified mercury
should be ground for a day with juices produced from lemon and <s>śarapuṅkha</s>.
That ball should be tied in a cloth and cooked in cow's milk
in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus for a day and night; the pill called <s>Hāṭakeśvarī</s> results.
When held in the mouth, it destroys old age and death.
In only a year, without doubt, a man lives for ten thousand years.
For one day, powder of <s>triphala</s> should be impregnated with decoctions of acacia seeds.
With honey and ghee, one should lick one <s>pala</s> as a <s>krāmaka</s> preparation.
Three <s>niṣkas</s> of purified mercury and one <s>niṣka</s> of copper powder
should be ground for a day in a mortar with sour buttermilk made acidic by tamarind fruit.
That ball should be tied in cloths and placed in buttermilk and tamarind sour liquid.
One should cook it for a day in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus; the pill called <s>Arkaprabhāvatī</s> results.
One should hold it in the mouth for one year, and the man becomes equal to the sun.
Oil from <s>palāśa</s> seeds, in a <s>karṣa</s> measure, with cow's milk,

children.text: krāmakaṃ hy anupānaṃ syāj jarāmṛtyuharaṃ param
children.translated_text: is the <s>krāmaka</s> accompanying drink, supreme in removing old age and death.
Gold one part, <s>kānta</s> one part, five parts silver, and mercury two parts;
mica essence should be three parts, and copper powder six parts.
All this, made fine, should be ground for three days in a heated mortar
with the acidic group, in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus together with sour gruel.
That ball should be cooked for three days; the pill called <s>Surasundarī</s> results.
When held in the mouth, after a year it removes death and old age.
Afterwards one should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>bhūtāravaṭa</s> root with milk.
Gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, lead, and mica essence
should all be powdered in equal amounts, with calcined diamond in an amount equal to the powder.
Purified mercury equal to all of them should be ground with the liquids of divine herbs
for one day; then, after closing it in a diamond crucible, one should heat it.
This pill called <s>Vajratuṇḍā</s> results, to be held in the mouth.
After a year it is said to destroy old age, death, and a mass of weapons.
With a diamond body and great heroism, one lives for three hundred years.

children.text: kumāryāḥ svarasaṃ grāhyaṃ guḍena saha loḍayet ||
children.translated_text: The fresh juice of <s>kumārī</s> should be taken and rolled together with jaggery.
One <s>pala</s> should always be licked as the <s>krāmaka</s> accompanying preparation.
Gold powder is one part, and purified mercury three parts.
Calcined diamond is a quarter part; all that, with liquids born from <s>kṣīrakanda</s>
and produced from <s>devadālī</s>, should be ground for a day in a heated mortar.

children.text: mardayet kāntacūrṇaṃ ca vajratulyaṃ kṣipec ca vai
children.translated_text: One should also add magnetic powder equal to the diamond.
It should be heated after being closed in a diamond crucible; the pill called <s>Kāmasundarī</s> results.
When held in the mouth, after a year it removes death and old age.
Three <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>brahmataila</s> and two <s>palas</s> of cow's milk
Mixed, one should make the man drink it afterwards; he becomes one whose lifespan is a hundred thousand years.

children.text: lohapātre drute gandhe pādāṃśaṃ pāradaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: In an iron vessel, when the sulfur has melted, one should add mercury in a quarter portion.

children.text: kiṃcic cālyaṃ tu kāṣṭhena muhūrtād avatārayet
children.translated_text: It should be stirred a little with a piece of wood, and after a <s>muhūrta</s> one should take it down.
<s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, and <s>indravāruṇī</s>,
<s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>ciñcā</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>suradālikā</s>:
with the cloth-filtered liquids of these, it should be ground for three days.
In that vessel, with an iron pestle, it should be dried in the shade and made into pills.
Having put it into an iron capsule and sealed it, one should make the joint firm with clay and salt.
One should smelt it over <s>khadira</s> charcoal until it is red, and then take it out.
Digging and digging it out again, one should extract that <s>rasa</s> from its middle.
Mixed with glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), it should be closed in a crucible and cooked.

children.text: gāndhārīguṭikā siddhā varṣaṃ vaktre sthitā sadā ||
children.translated_text: The pill called <s>Gāndhārī</s> is accomplished; it should remain constantly in the mouth for a year.
One should administer as nasal medicine one <s>karṣa</s> of oil from <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> seed.
This should be the <s>krāmaka</s> as an after-drink; one lives for a thousand years.
Sulfur equal to purified mercury, when ground, is made into <s>kajjalī</s>.

children.text: tat tāmrasampuṭe ruddhvā lavaṇena mṛdā dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: That should be sealed in a copper capsule, made firm with salt and clay.
When dry, it should be cooked by lamp-flame for one <s>yāma</s> in the ash-apparatus.
Then one should remove what has adhered to the upper part of the capsule and grind it.
Joined with an equal amount of mercury, it should be cooked in a capsule as before.
Having taken it out, joined it with an equal amount of mercury, and ground it, one should cook it.
Thus one should do this seven times; then again mercury and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>

children.text: tulyaṃ tulyaṃ kṣipet tasmin dinaṃ sarvaṃ vimardayet
children.translated_text: should be added to it in equal and equal amounts, and it should be ground for the whole day.
Sealed inside a diamond-crucible, when smelted, the <s>rasa</s> becomes a fixed ingot.

children.text: mārtaṇḍī guṭikā hy eṣā varṣaikaṃ yasya vaktragā
children.translated_text: This indeed is the pill <s>Mārtaṇḍī</s>; for the one in whose mouth it stays for a year,
he is freed from wrinkles and gray hair, and lives as long as the moon and stars.
Oil produced from <s>palāśa</s> seed, one <s>pala</s>, equal with milk,

children.text: krāmaṇaṃ prapiben nityaṃ tatkṣaṇān mūrchito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one should drink daily as the <s>krāmaṇa</s>; immediately he becomes unconscious.

children.text: tasya vaktre gavāṃ kṣīraṃ stokaṃ stokaṃ niṣecayet
children.translated_text: Into his mouth one should pour cow's milk little by little.
When he has awakened, milk-rice is the supremely beneficial food for his meal.
By his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
He has the speed of wind, is greatly accomplished, and sees openings in the earth.
With the liquids of <s>kākamācī</s> and <s>amṛtā</s>, mercury and <s>tālaka</s> in equal amounts

children.text: mardayed dinamekaṃ tu kṛtvā golaṃ viśoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground for one day; after making a ball, one should dry it.
One should place it in a diamond-crucible, covering it with flakes of iron.
Having sealed the joint, one should smelt it intensely; the <s>rasa</s> becomes fixed as an ingot.

children.text: lohaparpaṭakaṃ dattvā tadvad dhāmyaṃ tridhā punaḥ
children.translated_text: After adding iron flakes, it should again be smelted in that same way three times.
One should hold the pill <s>Tārakeśvarī</s> in the mouth for one year.
Afterwards one should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>vākucī</s> seed with cow's milk.
Essence of <s>vyoma</s> (mica), calcined diamond, gold, silver, copper, and <s>muṇḍaka</s>,

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ kāntaṃ tālakaṃ ca śuddhaṃ kṛtvā vimiśrayet
children.translated_text: sharp iron, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>tālaka</s> should be purified and mixed.
All should be a fine powder in equal amounts, with purified mercury equal to the amount of the powder.
Ground for three days with the sour group, it should be closed and smelted.
The pill known as <s>Vidyāvāgīśvarī</s>, for the span of a year,

children.text: yasya vaktre sthitā tasya jarā mṛtyurna vidyate
children.translated_text: when it stays in a man's mouth, for him there is no old age and no death.
For the purpose of <s>krāmaṇa</s>, one should constantly drink one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> oil.
He becomes eloquent, a lord of speech, and wise; he lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
Lodestone, <s>mākṣīka</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and crab bone,
the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and <s>bhūnāga</s>: all this should be equal.

children.text: strīstanyena dinaṃ mardyaṃ tena mūṣāṃ pralepayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be ground for a day with women's milk; with it one should coat a crucible.

children.text: tanmadhye drutasūtaṃ tu vajrabhasma samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: In the middle of that, melted mercury and calcined diamond, each in equal amount,
should be placed and sealed; it should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> called <s>gaja</s> for only one <s>yāma</s>.
Then, having placed it in a coated crucible and sealed it, one should smelt it forcefully.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kāryaṃ vajrasūtaṃ milatyalam ||
children.translated_text: This should be done again and again; diamond and mercury combine thoroughly.
Then to that very substance one should add an equal amount of glass together with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ mūṣāśate deyaṃ tulyaṃ tulyaṃ dhaman dhaman ||
children.translated_text: Thus it should be put through a hundred crucibles, equal amount after equal amount, smelting again and again.
That lord of <s>rasa</s> becomes a mass of brilliance, resembling the sun.
This pill <s>Vajratuṇḍī</s>, kept in the mouth, destroys death.

children.text: varṣamātrān na saṃdeho rudratulyo bhaven naraḥ
children.translated_text: After only a year, without doubt, a man becomes equal to <s>Rudra</s>.
By his urine and feces, as before, gold is produced.
He should eat one <s>karṣa</s> of the five-part plant of <s>rudantī</s> with honey and ghee.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, crab bones, wool, and <s>śilājatu</s>,
excrement produced from the ears and eyes of a buffalo cow, together with an equal amount of women's milk,
should be ground; in a crucible coated with that, one should place mica essence and smelt it.
There one should add melted mercury, as before, equal to the essence.

children.text: dravaṃ divyauṣadhīnāṃ ca dattvā tatraiva taddhamet ||
children.translated_text: Having also added the liquid of divine herbs there, one should smelt it right there.
Having combined, it becomes fixed; as before, with glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
this <s>rasa</s>, smelted through a hundred crucibles, becomes a mass of brilliance.
One should hold it in the mouth for one year; a man becomes equal to <s>Śiva</s>.
This pill <s>Gaganeśvarī</s> brings freedom from old age and death.
Afterwards one should drink a <s>niṣka</s> measure of oil produced from <s>bilva</s> seed.

children.text: udare jāyate vahniḥ pibetkṣīraṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A fire arises in the belly; he should drink milk again and again.
Directly there arise recollection of previous births, poetic power, and retention of what has been heard,
the power of moving through the sky and invisibility; there is no doubt about this.
<s>Agnimantha</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s>, and wild <s>sūraṇa</s>
And <s>citraka</s>, with the liquids of these, should be ground with purified mercury for a day.
One should grind that <s>rasa</s> in the heated mortar, in the amount of one <s>pala</s>.
One <s>pala</s> each of <s>tāla</s> and tin, and all that, with sour <s>vetasa</s> juice,

children.text: mardayed dinamekaṃ tu kṛtvā taṃ golakaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: should be ground for one day. Then, having made it into a ball again,

children.text: catuḥpalāṃ nāgamūṣāṃ kṛtvā tasyāṃ tu tatkṣipet ||
children.translated_text: one should make a lead crucible of four <s>palas</s> and place that in it.
One should enclose it in a purified copper capsule of four <s>palas</s>.

children.text: mṛṇmūṣāyāṃ tu tāṃ ruddhvā āraṇyotpalakaiḥ puṭet ||
children.translated_text: After sealing that in an earthen crucible, one should heat it with forest cow-dung cakes.
With two hundred as the measure, when it has cooled of itself, one should take it out.
All of it should be ground for three days with the liquids of divine herbs.
Pills of four <s>niṣkas</s> should be made; then one should dry them.
Having sealed each one in a diamond crucible, one should smelt it with intense fire.
This is the <s>Ānandaguṭikā</s>; when kept in the mouth it destroys death.
There is no doubt: after a year one would live for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Oil produced from the seeds of <s>vātāri</s>, in a <s>niṣka</s> measure, with cow's milk,
should be drunk daily for <s>krāmaṇa</s> (assimilation); it is supreme and quickly brings accomplishment.
Mercury equal to diamond ash, for three days with the liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s>,
should be ground, placed in a crucible smeared with <s>dvaṃdva</s>, sealed, and heated.
In the apparatus called <s>Bhūdhara</s>, for a day and night, and then, after taking it out,
one should add mercury in the former proportion, and for three days with the liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s>,
it should be ground, placed in a crucible smeared with <s>dvaṃdva</s>, sealed, and smelted.
That ingot should be purified by smelting in combination with glass and borax.
Until it becomes star-like in appearance, it should be smelted again and again.

children.text: tadrasaṃ vyomasattvaṃ ca kāñcanaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s>, mica essence, and gold, in equal amounts,
should be fused together; then a pill should be made to be kept in the middle of the mouth.
It is named <s>Vajrakhecarikā</s>, destroying death for years.
A man becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair and obtains a divine body.
Afterwards he should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> and <s>muni</s> powder with ghee.

children.text: kāntaṃ śulbaṃ samaṃ cūrṇaṃ vajramūṣāndhitaṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: Magnetite and copper, powdered equally, should be smelted sealed in a diamond crucible.
The powder made from that perfected ingot should be ground with sulfur and an acid.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a proper heating; then, after taking it out, one should grind it.
By the same procedure as before, one should heat it fourteen times.
With this, one should color gold alloyed with diamond.

children.text: mūṣāmadhye dhamann evaṃ saptavāraṃ samaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Smelting it in the middle of a crucible in this way, one should add an equal amount seven times.
That ingot, powdered, should be impregnated for a day with menstrual blood.

children.text: tattulyaṃ drutasūtaṃ tu sarvaṃ yāmaṃ vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: One should add molten mercury equal to that and grind everything thoroughly for one <s>yāma</s>.

children.text: veṣṭayed bhūrjapattreṇa vastre baddhvā pacet tryaham
children.translated_text: It should be wrapped in birch bark, bound in cloth, and cooked for three days.
In a swinging apparatus with a tube of pith, one should take out the ball that has formed.
<s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>jīvanī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>indravāruṇī</s>,
with a lump paste of these, one should wrap the previous ball.
After sealing it, one should cook it for a day in the <s>Bhūdhara</s> apparatus and take it out.
It should be smeared again and cooked again, for fourteen days.

children.text: guṭikā jāyate divyā nāmnā ratneśvarī tathā
children.translated_text: A divine pill is produced, likewise named <s>Ratneśvarī</s>.

children.text: vaktrasthā varṣamātraṃ tu nanditulyo bhaven naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it is kept in the mouth for only a year, a man becomes equal to <s>Nandi</s>.
He lives for thousands of years, with divine brilliance and great strength.

children.text: varṣadvādaśaparyantaṃ yasya vaktre sthitā tu sā ||
children.translated_text: When that pill remains in his mouth for twelve years,
from contact with his sweat the eight metals become gold.
There is no doubt: this is true, spoken by <s>Īśvara</s>.
Afterwards one should lick powder of the five parts of the <s>rudantī</s> plant with honey and ghee.

children.text: svarṇaṃ kṛṣṇābhrasattvaṃ ca tāraṃ tāmraṃ sucūrṇitam ||
children.translated_text: Gold, the essence of black mica, silver, and copper, well powdered,
in equal parts, should be sealed in a crucible smeared with <s>dvaṃdva</s> and smelted.
Four parts of that ingot, and one part of calcined diamond,
<s>mākṣika</s>, sharp iron, and magnetite, each one part and well powdered,
all together should be sealed in a crucible smeared with <s>dvaṃdva</s> and smelted.
That ingot, made into fine powder, and molten mercury equal to the powder,
should be ground for three days in a heated mortar with the liquids of divine herbs.
After sealing it, one should cook it in the <s>Bhūdhara</s> apparatus and take it out after a day and night.
Again, after adding an equal amount of molten mercury, it should be ground and heated in the same way.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptavārāṃstu drutaṃ sūtaṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Thus, seven times, molten mercury in equal amount each time

children.text: dattvā mardyaṃ puṭe pacyāj jāyate bhasmasūtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be added, ground, and cooked in a heating; calcined mercury is produced.

children.text: bhasmasūtasamaṃ gandhaṃ dattvā ruddhvā dhamed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Having added sulfur equal to the calcined mercury, one should seal it and smelt it firmly.
A divine pill is produced, famous as <s>Divyakhecarī</s>.
One should hold it in the mouth for one year; one lives for a thousand aeons.
By smearing all metal with his urine and feces,

children.text: jāyate kanakaṃ divyaṃ samāvarte na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: divine gold is produced in the fusion; there is no doubt.
He should always drink after it two <s>palas</s> of the liquid of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>.

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ bhasmasūtaṃ vā guñjāmātraṃ sadā lihet
children.translated_text: Or he should always lick the previously described calcined mercury in the measure of a <s>guñjā</s>.
For one year, with honey and ghee, a man attains a life of one hundred thousand years.
He is freed from wrinkles and gray hair, and has great strength and valor.
Gold and the essence of <s>vaikrānta</s>, alloyed together, should be digested in mercury.
Until they become equal in parts, then with that very substance one should cause penetration.

children.text: samena jāyate baddho dhārayettaṃ mukhe sadā ||
children.translated_text: With an equal amount it becomes fixed; one should always keep it in the mouth.
By a year's use, he conquers old age, time, and untimely death.
Afterwards he should drink the juice born from the leaves of <s>kumārī</s>, mixed with sugar.
This gold-and-<s>vaikrānta</s>-fixed preparation grants people the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
One should triturate purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) with an equal portion of <s>vaikrānta</s>-essence.
For a day, with the liquids of divine herbs, that ball should then be smeared with <s>nigaḍa</s>.
It should be sealed inside a diamond crucible placed in the belly of salt.
One should dry the joint in the shade and heat it gently for three days with husk-fire.
Or one should sweat it in a dung-fire by day and night, and then take it out.

children.text: tadgolaṃ nigaḍenaiva liptvā tadvan nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: That same ball should again be smeared with <s>nigaḍa</s> and sealed in the same way.
When it has dried in the shade, one should blow it strongly; it certainly comes to fixation.
If one keeps it in the mouth for a year, one lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
This is the <s>Vaikrānta</s> pill, bestowing the fruit of every desire.
Afterwards one should lick one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>triphala</s> powder with honey and ghee.
Diamond that has been combined with gold should be made into a fine powder.
This should be placed with secret <s>sūta</s> in a crucible, below and above.
With care, after sealing the joint to the extent of a quarter part, one should dry it out.
It should be cooked for a day in the apparatus called <s>Bhūdhara</s>; after taking it out, one should grind it.
For one day, in a heated mortar, it should be triturated with the juices of divine herbs and fruits.

children.text: ruddhvātha bhūdhare pacyād dinaṃ laghupuṭaiḥ puṭet
children.translated_text: Then, after sealing it, one should cook it in the <s>Bhūdhara</s>, and heat it with light <s>puṭas</s> for a day.
Having taken it out, one should again grind it in the same way and seal it for three days.
It should be gently sweated with husk-fire, turning it above and below.
This calcined <s>sūta</s> is produced; one should use it in all preparations.
One part of molten <s>sūta</s> and one part of the previous ash,
together with one part of purified <s>nāga</s> (lead), should all be ground with sour liquid.
Placed in a sealed crucible, it should be blown; that <s>rasa</s> becomes a lump.
One should blow it in an open crucible until the <s>nāga</s> is destroyed.
After liquefying this <s>rasa</s> according to the method for molten <s>sūta</s>,
one should place it in a <s>kacchapa</s> apparatus, adding <s>viḍa</s> in a tenth part.
All the metals, beginning with gold, should then be digested in order.

children.text: pratyekaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ paścād vajradvaṃdvaṃ ca jārayet ||
children.translated_text: Each should be digested sixfold, and afterwards the diamond-pair should also be digested.

children.text: triguṇaṃ tu bhavedyāvattato ratnāni vai kramāt
children.translated_text: When it has become threefold, then the gems, in order,

children.text: jārayed drāvitāny eva pratyekaṃ triguṇaṃ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be digested only after being liquefied, each threefold and slowly.
Then, after taking it out from the apparatus, it should be ground for a day with the liquids of divine herbs.

children.text: mardyaṃ ruddhvā dhamedgāḍhaṃ jāyate guṭikā śubhā ||
children.translated_text: After it is ground and sealed, one should blow it strongly; an auspicious pill is produced.
One should worship it with <s>Aṅkuśī</s> mantras; by name it is the divine <s>Khecarī</s>.

children.text: yasya vaktre sthitā hy eṣā sa bhavedbhairavopamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever has this situated in his mouth becomes comparable to <s>Bhairava</s>.
With divine brilliance and a great body, he moves with the state of a sky-goer.

children.text: yatrecchā tatra tatraiva krīḍate hy aṅganādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wherever he wishes, there and there he sports with women and the like.
He remains until the end of a great aeon; there is no doubt.
By his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
Powder of <s>palāśa</s> flowers, black sesame seeds, and sugar,

children.text: sarvaṃ palatrayaṃ khāden nityaṃ syāt krāmaṇe hitam ||
children.translated_text: three <s>palas</s> of all this, should be eaten daily; it is beneficial for the gradual regimen.
Powder of a horse's hoof should be added in equal quantity to secret <s>sūta</s>.
All that should be ground firmly for three days with the sour juice of <s>mātuluṅga</s>.

children.text: sūtatulyaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ tasmin kṣiptvātha mardayet
children.translated_text: Then calcined diamond equal to the <s>sūta</s> should be put into it and ground.
For a day, in a heated mortar, it should be ground with sour liquids; that ball, sealed in a closed crucible, should be roasted.
For one day in the <s>Bhūdhara</s> apparatus, one part of the former mercury
should be placed in it and ground firmly for a day with <s>mātuluṅga</s> juice.
Then, after sealing it, one should cook it as before, and mercury should again be added.

children.text: mardyaṃ pācyaṃ yathāpūrvamevaṃ kuryāc ca saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: It should be ground and cooked just as before; one should do this seven times.
By adding the <s>rasa</s> again and again, calcined <s>sūta</s> is thus produced.
One should use it in all preparations; it destroys old age and death.
One part of powdered <s>nāga</s> and one part of the previous ash,

children.text: drutasūtasya bhāgaikaṃ khoṭaṃ kuryāc ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: with one part of molten <s>sūta</s>, should be made into a lump as before.
It should be blown in the same way; when the <s>nāga</s> has gone, the liquefied substance should again be digested.

children.text: pūrvaval loharatnāntaṃ jīrṇe baddhā sthitā mukhe ||
children.translated_text: As before, up through the metals and gems, when it has been digested and bound, it is kept in the mouth.
The pill named <s>Pracaṇḍakhecarī</s> grants motion in the sky.
As before, the heroic practitioner obtains a result exceedingly hard to attain.
One should drink a <s>karṣa</s> of powdered <s>nirguṇḍī</s> root with buttermilk afterwards.
For purified <s>sūta</s>, calcined diamond should be added in a one-sixteenth portion.
All that should be ground for three days in a heated mortar with the class of sour liquids.
After grinding it, one should then coat, in equal parts,
the leaves of <s>pakvabīja</s>; those, again, wrapped in <s>bhānu</s> leaves,
should be sealed and then buried in the cavity of a hearth.
After covering it, one should kindle a wood fire there for three days.
Having taken it out, one should seal it in a crucible smeared with the compound pair.
It should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> with dung-fire and taken out after a day and night.
An equal amount of this should be placed in <s>sūta</s> whose mouth has been opened by <s>vāsanā</s>.
One should grind it with sour liquid for a <s>yāma</s>, and take out the ball that has formed.

children.text: kṣipejjambīragarbhe taṃ vastre baddhvā tryahaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: One should put it inside a <s>jambīra</s> fruit, tie it in cloth, and cook it for three days.
In a swing apparatus, in a <s>sāranāla</s>, an auspicious pill is produced.
Named <s>Kaṅkālakhecarī</s>, it destroys death when held in the mouth.
Whoever keeps it for a year lives for one day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Afterwards one should lick one <s>karṣa</s> of sulfur and <s>guggulu</s> in equal quantity with ghee.
The essence of black <s>abhraka</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>mākṣīka</s>, and gold,

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ sauvīracūrṇaṃ ca tulyaṃ ruddhvā dhamed dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron and powdered <s>sauvīra</s>, all in equal quantity, should be sealed and blown strongly.
That lump, finely powdered, should be equal in quantity to molten <s>sūta</s>.
One should grind calcined diamond, half the amount of the <s>sūta</s> (mercury), all together with acid.

children.text: dinaikaṃ taptakhalve tu taṃ ruddhvā bhūdhare pacet
children.translated_text: For one day in a heated mortar; then, after sealing it, one should cook it in the <s>Bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
After a day and night, one should take it out and add the same amount of the previous mercury.
Having added it, one should grind everything with liquids of divine herbs for the length of a day.
One should cook it in the <s>Bhūdhara</s> apparatus as before, and again add an equal amount of molten mercury.
Having added it, one should grind and cook it again; thus, in this very way, seven times.

children.text: etadbhasmasamaṃ gandhaṃ dattvā cāndhyaṃ dhamed dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: Having added <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) equal to this ash, one should seal it and smelt it firmly.
A divine <s>guṭikā</s> (pill) is produced, supreme, destructive of time.

children.text: yasya vaktre sthitā hy eṣā tasya kālaḥ karoti kim ||
children.translated_text: When this is placed in a person's mouth, what can time do to him?
By using it for six years, he lives for a thousand <s>kalpas</s>.
By the mere sweat of his body, all metals become gold.

children.text: jāyante nātra saṃdehaḥ śivāmbu krāmakaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: They become so; there is no doubt. He should drink <s>śivāmbu</s> as the accelerator.
Gold, silver, copper, magnetite, and sharp iron powder, each in equal quantity,
should be smelted sealed in a crucible smeared with <s>dvaṃdva</s>.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ cūrṇitaṃ kṛtvā cābhiṣiktaṃ tu pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Having powdered that ingot and impregnated it as before,
one should digest it in mercury in the <s>samukha</s> procedure, gradually, until it is fivefold.
One should grind it for three days with liquids of divine herbs.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, it becomes an auspicious <s>guṭikā</s>.
Named <s>Pañcānanā</s>, it should be held in the mouth for the length of a year.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
<s>Hastikarṇī</s>, together with its root, should be powdered and mixed with honey and ghee.

children.text: snigdhabhāṇḍe tu tāṃ ruddhvā dhānyarāśau niveśayet
children.translated_text: After sealing it in a greased vessel, one should place it in a heap of grain.
After three weeks, one should take it out and then eat one <s>pala</s>.
The varied binding of mercury that was taught in the <s>Ṛddhikhaṇḍa</s>,
of that very thing I shall here explain the procedure for body-penetration, as follows.

children.text: jāritair bandhitais tais tai rasarājaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak
children.translated_text: With those various kings of mercury, digested and bound separately,
one should make a divine <s>guṭikā</s>, the size of a jujube fruit.
It is to be held in the mouth for a year, giving a result corresponding to itself.
The hundred-penetrating <s>guṭikā</s> gives men the lifespan of a <s>yuga</s>.
The thousand-penetrating <s>guṭikā</s> protects through eight <s>kalpas</s>.

children.text: lakṣavedhakarī yā tu sā datte viṣṇuvadbalam ||
children.translated_text: The one that produces a hundred-thousand-fold penetration gives strength like <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The penetrative one of ten hundred-thousands grants the rank of <s>Rudra</s>.
The one that produces ten-million-fold penetration makes men into an <s>Īśvara</s>.
The penetrative one of one hundred million grants the state called <s>Sadākhya</s>.
The <s>guṭikā</s> that penetrates an <s>arbuda</s> grants the rank of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>.
The conch-number penetrative <s>guṭikā</s> grants the state of <s>Samyagbhava</s>.

children.text: dhūmravedhī tu yā siddhā sā śaktipadadāyinī ||
children.translated_text: The perfected smoke-penetrating one grants the rank of <s>Śakti</s>.
The one that produces touch-penetration grants the rank of <s>Parāśakti</s>.

children.text: śabdavedhakarā yā tu sā yasya vatsarāvadhi ||
children.translated_text: And the one that produces sound-penetration, when it remains for a year

children.text: vaktre sthitā sa vai siddho nityaṃ nityapadaṃ labhet
children.translated_text: in a person's mouth: he is indeed a siddha and always attains the eternal state.
Moving according to his own will, with a diamond body, he is not split by thunderbolts.
Through his urine and feces all metals become gold.
They become so from contact with his sweat, and even from contact with his body.
For all the procedures that have been taught, purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) should be the adjunct.
He should eat half a <s>pala</s> daily; it is useful for the transmission of rasa.
O <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Mahākālī</s>, eater of flesh and blood,
O goddess with red-and-black face, grant me accomplishment in mercury.
Svāhā. With this accomplished mantra one should worship the circle of <s>Śakti</s>.

children.text: kālikāṃ bhairavaṃ siddhān kumārīṃ sādhitaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: One should worship <s>Kālikā</s>, <s>Bhairava</s>, the siddhas, the maiden, and the consecrated mercury.
Then he should consume the divine <s>rasāyana</s> and attain accomplishment.
He should hold the <s>guṭikā</s> in his mouth and always recite the previous mantra.
Through the application of the rasa-mantra, he quickly attains accomplishment.
For the later accomplishment of mercury that was taught in the <s>Manthānabhairava</s>,

children.text: tadarthaṃ pañca tattvāni ṣaṣṭhaṃ jīvaṃ ca sādhayet
children.translated_text: for that purpose one should prepare the five tattvas and, as the sixth, the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: kākinyāḥ puṣpakāle tu saṅgaṃ kṛtvā samāharet ||
children.translated_text: At the time of <s>Kākinī</s>'s flower, having had intercourse, one should collect it.
The menstrual seed situated in her yoni: the wise know that as ether.
The fresh feces of the son born from <s>Kākinī</s> is called air.
Fire is <s>Kākinī</s>'s flower; water is the blood of her son.
The whole body of <s>Kākinī</s>'s son is called the earth element.
The semen arisen from the body of the consumer of mercury is called the <s>jīva</s>.
Each of these, having ten-million-fold penetration, one <s>karṣa</s> each, should be combined with mercury.
Having prepared them, one should preserve them separately, well ground and made into balls.
As high as a man in height, and half of that in breadth,
one should make a copper cauldron, thick to the measure of six fingers.

children.text: caturmukhasya koṣṭhasya pṛṣṭhe dhāryaṃ dṛḍhaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: It should be set firmly on the back of a four-mouthed furnace.
One should mix cow's ghee and human oil in equal parts.
Having filled that cauldron with it, one should then worship the perfected circle.
The maiden, the guru, the gods, the fires, and <s>Bhairava</s> together with <s>Bhairavī</s>,
one should satiate with bali-meat, and one should worship the field-protector.

children.text: dhamanaṃ tatra kurvīta caturdikṣu śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: There one should perform the blowing from the four directions, slowly, slowly,
with four bent tubes and with the use of <s>khadira</s> charcoal.

children.text: sutaptaṃ phenanirmuktaṃ nirdhūmaṃ ca yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: When it is well heated, free from foam, and smokeless,
then, having bowed to the deities and worlds of the moon, sun, planets, and stars,

children.text: namaskṛtya guruṃ devaṃ dehaṃ tatra vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: and to the guru and the god, one should place the body there.
When he knows it to be well melted, he should add the earthy mercury.

children.text: dhamann atraiva yatnena yāvat tat kalkatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Blowing carefully right there, one should continue until it becomes a paste.

children.text: aptattvākhyaṃ rasaṃ tasmin kṣiped raktaṃ bhavet tu tat ||
children.translated_text: One should add to it mercury called <s>ap-tattva</s>; then it becomes red.
When mercury combined with <s>vāyu</s> is added, it becomes white in color.

children.text: tejoyuktaṃ rasaṃ kṣipyād ghanībhūtaṃ bhavettu tat ||
children.translated_text: One should add mercury combined with fire; it becomes solidified.
Then one should cast into it mercury combined with ether.
When repeatedly heated it becomes gold-like; one should add it there.
Then, with the divine mercury united with life, he should utter the <s>huṃkāra</s>.
Making there a great roar, together with three utterances of <s>huṃ</s>.

children.text: tataś cottiṣṭhate siddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe bhāskaro yathā
children.translated_text: Then the perfected adept rises up, like the sun in the forenoon.
He has divine radiance, a great body, and great strength and valor.
His strength becomes greater than that of nine thousand <s>nāgas</s>.

children.text: jīvate vajradehaḥ san satyaṃ satyaṃ śivoditam ||
children.translated_text: He lives, having a diamond body. This is true, true, spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.
For those whose limbs are broken down by old age, for the blind, the lame, and leprous,
for those whose speech is lost, the dull, the impotent, the hunchbacked, and those with leprous bodies,
for those afflicted by many diseases, confused, insane, or demon-possessed,
how much more so for kings with pure bodies who make use of mercury?
It grants divine accomplishment to heroes and to practitioners.
Therefore whoever here is more heroic is that <s>Bhairava</s>; there is no doubt.
The perfected adept becomes diamond-bodied, intelligent, and possessed of divine form.
An aerial car half a <s>yojana</s> wide, attended by <s>apsarases</s>,
comes before that perfected adept; there is no doubt about this.
Mounted on it, he sports in the world of <s>Rudra</s> like <s>Bhairava</s>.
Freed from hunger and thirst, he is not destroyed at the destruction of the world.

children.text: bhuñjānaḥ sarvabhogāṃśca yogināṃ sa priyo bhavet
children.translated_text: Enjoying all enjoyments, he becomes dear to the yogins.
Accomplished at will and a great hero, he becomes filled with eternal bliss.
Having seen everything and experienced, among rasāyanas, the essence beyond essence, easier for men to accomplish happily,

children.text: dehasya dārḍhyakaraṇe guṭikāprayogāḥ proktāḥ paraṃ śivakarāḥ satataṃ susiddhyai ||
children.translated_text: the pill procedures for strengthening the body have been declared, supremely auspicious and always leading to complete success.
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury), <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), <s>gagana</s> (mica), iron, and copper, calcined and made supremely nectar-like,
and even one desired group of herbs, when used, quickly bring perfection of the body.
Calcined magnetite and mica, <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>,
and <s>bilva</s> seed with the rind removed: each should be sixteen <s>palas</s>.
There should also be thirty <s>palas</s> of the three pungents, and thirty each of ghee and honey.
There should be ten <s>palas</s> of <s>citraka</s> root; all this should be powdered and mixed.
Of <s>triphalā</s> there should be four hundred preceded by twenty <s>palas</s>.
It should be decocted with eight times as much water, and taken when one eighth remains.
With that decoction one should impregnate the mixture previously stirred for one month.

children.text: lohapātre khare gharme tatpalārdhaṃ sadā pibet ||
children.translated_text: In an iron vessel in strong heat, one should always drink half a <s>pala</s> of it.
With milk at bedtime, for years, it removes death and old age.
He becomes young, with firm joints, and lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
It is a great divine rasāyana, satisfying a hundred women.
One should put black mica, heated by fire and fire-colored, into milk.
Then, after making it split into flakes, one should cast it into water.
With care there should be thirty <s>palas</s> of it, and five <s>palas</s> of pepper.
Powdered pepper should be placed in it; at the end of three days one should take it out.
One should grind all that finely and bind it in a white cloth.
In a jar filled with water, in heat, one should hold it by means of a swinging apparatus.

children.text: śuṣke toye punastoyaṃ dadyād yāvaj jale gatam ||
children.translated_text: When the water has dried up, one should add water again, until it has passed into the water.

children.text: tadabhrakaṃ tato vastraṃ saṃtyajed rakṣayej jalam
children.translated_text: Then one should discard that mica and the cloth, and preserve the water.

children.text: triṃśadbhāgaṃ tataḥ kuryāt taj jalaṃ sābhrakaṃ sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the wise man should divide that mica-infused water into thirty parts.
With one part of that, after mixing one <s>pala</s> of white rice,

children.text: triṃśatpale gavāṃ kṣīre tat pacec cātha śītalam ||
children.translated_text: he should cook it in thirty <s>palas</s> of cow's milk, and then let it cool.
Mixed with two <s>palas</s> each of honey and ghee, and with pepper in <s>niṣka</s> measures,
the practitioner should eat it daily for months; it removes death and old age.

children.text: keśā dantā nakhāstasya patanti hy udbhavanti ca
children.translated_text: His hair, teeth, and nails fall out and then grow again.
He becomes a diamond-bodied perfected adept, swift as the wind and very strong.
This is the immortal mica preparation, formerly taught by <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: mṛtābhraṃ gandhakaṃ śuddhaṃ kaṇā sarvaṃ samaṃ ghṛtaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Calcined mica, purified sulfur, and <s>kaṇā</s>, all in equal measure, are to be taken with ghee.
One should eat one <s>karṣa</s> daily for years; it removes death and old age.
Leaves of <s>koraṇṭaka</s>, calcined mica, and sulfur should be equal.
All that should be impregnated in the sun for seven days with the juices of <s>nīlikā</s>.
One should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of that with milk for years; it removes death and old age.

children.text: mṛtābhrakasya karṣaikaṃ gavāṃ kṣīraṃ palaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: One <s>karṣa</s> of calcined mica, and likewise one <s>pala</s> of cow's milk,

children.text: samūlapattrāṃ sarpākṣīṃ sārdrāṃ piṣṭvā ca gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: and fresh <s>sarpākṣī</s>, with root and leaves, and sulfur should be ground together.
Combining them, one should drink it all; in one year he conquers old age.
Diamond-bodied and sky-moving, he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: mṛtābhraṃ kāntalohaṃ ca triphalā māgadhī samam
children.translated_text: Calcined mica, magnetite, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>māgadhī</s> should be equal.
One should add powder of the five parts of <s>badarī</s>, equal to the mica.
Joined with sugar, honey, and ghee, one should always eat half a <s>pala</s>.

children.text: hanti varṣāj jarāṃ mṛtyumāyuḥ syādbrahmaṇo dinam ||
children.translated_text: In a year it destroys old age and death; his lifespan becomes a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Amṛtakrīḍe</s>, <s>Viṣṇusaṃvaraṇi</s>, svāhā.

children.text: anena mantreṇa sarve abhrakayogā abhimantrya bhakṣaṇīyāḥ
children.translated_text: With this mantra all mica preparations should be consecrated and eaten.
Calcined magnetite, black sesame seeds, and powder of <s>badarī</s> fruit,
and powder of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> seeds: one should prepare all in equal measure.
It should be impregnated for three days with the juices of <s>śālmalī</s> and <s>mallī</s> leaves.
For three days it should be impregnated with juices produced from <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and then dried again.

children.text: tasmin tulyaṃ guḍaṃ kṣiptvā vaṭikāḥ karṣamātrakāḥ
children.translated_text: After putting an equal amount of jaggery into it, one should make pills measuring one <s>karṣa</s> each.

children.text: rudanty utthadravaiḥ kṣīrair madhvājyābhyāṃ pibet sadā ||
children.translated_text: One should always drink them with the fresh liquids of <s>rudantī</s>, with milk, honey, and ghee.

children.text: varṣaikena jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ hanti satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: In one year it destroys old age and death. This is true; there is no doubt.
Calcined <s>kānta</s>, black sesame seeds, and <s>triphalā</s> should be powdered in equal amounts.
It should be stirred with the liquids of <s>śālmalī</s> and <s>ketakī</s> in a <s>kānta</s> vessel.
Kept overnight, half a <s>pala</s> should be drunk in the morning; it destroys death.
In one year it destroys old age; one lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Calcined <s>kānta</s>, powder of <s>kaṇā</s>, and the exudation of <s>nimba</s>,
together with <s>triphalā</s>, each in equal parts: half a <s>pala</s> should be taken with honey and ghee.
A man should lick it daily for eight months; he lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Having cooked pieces of <s>kuṣṭha</s> in an equal decoction of <s>triphalā</s>,

children.text: śoṣayitvā vicūrṇyātha tāni kāntaṃ mṛtaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: then, after drying and powdering them, one should mix those with an equal amount of calcined <s>kānta</s>.
With honey and ghee one should lick one <s>karṣa</s> for a year; it removes death and old age.
Powder of <s>koraṇṭa</s> leaves, calcined <s>kānta</s>, sesame seeds, and jaggery

children.text: tulyaṃ bhakṣyaṃ palārdhaṃ tad varṣān mṛtyujarāpaham
children.translated_text: should be eaten in equal parts, half a <s>pala</s>; for a year it removes death and old age.
Calcined <s>kānta</s> and an equal amount of <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), with oils produced from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>,
one should lick daily in a measure of four <s>niṣkas</s>; a man obtains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
After a year he surely becomes equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> in speech.
Calcined <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (sharp iron), three parts, and purified <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), eight parts,
should be impregnated in heat for three weeks with all the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>.
He should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of that with cow's milk; he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
After only a year, without doubt, he is divinely radiant and very strong.

children.text: mṛtaṃ kāntaṃ śilā śuddhā tulyaṃ madhvājyakairlihet
children.translated_text: Calcined <s>kānta</s> and purified <s>śilā</s>, in equal amount, one should lick with honey and ghee.
One <s>niṣka</s> after another, for one year, he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: triniṣkaṃ mṛtatīkṣṇaṃ tu muṇḍaṃ vā kāntameva vā
children.translated_text: Three <s>niṣkas</s> of calcined <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, or else <s>muṇḍa</s> or <s>kānta</s>,
one should drink with milk warm straight from the udder; it arrests age for men.
By use for two years he lives as long as the moon and stars.
In a vessel properly made of <s>kānta</s>, powder of <s>dhātrī</s> with <s>śivāmbu</s>
should be smeared in the measure of one <s>pala</s> at night; rising in the morning, one should eat it.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, after a year he becomes a conqueror of death.
One should smear the inside of a <s>kānta</s> vessel with one <s>pala</s> of <s>triphalā</s> and honey.

children.text: divārātraṃ sthitaṃ peyaṃ tannityaṃ tu śivāmbunā
children.translated_text: After it has stood for a day and night, that should be drunk daily with <s>śivāmbu</s>.
In a year it destroys death and old age; he lives for three hundred years.

children.text: oṃ haḥ amṛte amṛtaśakti amṛtagandhopajīvi niṣpannaṃ candrāmṛtam ājñāpitaṃkuru kurusvāhā he he haṃ haḥ gaṃ iti gandhakalohayorbhakṣaṇamantraḥ
children.translated_text: This is the mantra for consuming <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) and metal: "oṃ haḥ amṛte amṛtaśakti amṛtagandhopajīvi niṣpannaṃ candrāmṛtam ājñāpitaṃ kuru kuru svāhā he he haṃ haḥ gaṃ."
After all metal preparations, there should be drinking of milk.
One should taste the fresh juice of sweet <s>mustā</s> plants, pressed with the teeth.
One should eat their roots to calm unpleasant taste in the mouth.

children.text: baddhe koṣṭhe tu dīptāgnau taptaṃ kṣīraṃ pibetsadā ||
children.translated_text: When the bowels are bound and the digestive fire is kindled, one should always drink hot milk.
If there is obstruction, one should avoid bathing, massage, and sharply hot things.
One should chew betel constantly, with camphor, again and again.

children.text: samyagjīrṇe tu dīptāgnau pibet paścād bubhukṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: When digestion is complete and the digestive fire is bright, afterwards, when hungry, one should drink

children.text: śṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ tato'nnaṃ ca sevyaṃ lauharasāyane ||
children.translated_text: boiled milk; then food should be taken in a metal-rasāyana regimen.
The five parts of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>, shade-dried and finely powdered,
one should lick in a measure of one <s>karṣa</s> with honey and ghee; in one year he conquers old age.
He lives a thousand years, divinely radiant and very strong.
The flowers of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> should be shade-dried.
Thirty <s>palas</s> of that powder and twenty-four <s>palas</s> of ghee
should be combined, placed in a vessel, sealed, and put into a heap of grain.
After a month, having taken it out, one should make fourteen portions.
He should eat one portion daily and take his meal from a <s>kānta</s> vessel.
Doing this for three months, a man becomes diamond-bodied.
Through his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
The seeds of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>, powdered together with ghee,
should be placed in the middle of grain as before and taken out after a month.
He should always eat one <s>pala</s> at a time; after a year he becomes a conqueror of death.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Oil produced from <s>brahma</s> seeds, together with two <s>palas</s> of cow's milk,
should be drunk in equal measure; fainting occurs, and milk should be sprinkled into his mouth.
When he awakens, milk-rice should be given; after a month a man becomes wise.
In the second month he becomes equal to <s>Śukra</s>; in the third he becomes like diamond.
In the fourth he hears from afar; in the fifth his movement is through the sky.
In the sixth month he becomes self-empowered, with valor equal to <s>Śiva</s>.
By use for one year he lives until the end of the great aeon.
A very thick <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> should be cut at its upper part.

children.text: adho rakṣyaṃ trihastaṃ syāttasya mūrdhni bilaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Three <s>hastas</s> below should be preserved, and a cavity should be made in its top.
It should be filled with ripe <s>dhātrī</s> fruits and closed with that wood.
One should wrap it all with <s>kuśa</s> grass and then smear it with clay and cow dung.
After wrapping it with a piece of cloth, one should then smear it with clay and cow dung.
When it is dry, a <s>gajapuṭa</s> heating should be given all around with forest dung-cakes.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take out the fruits together with their liquids.
One should put those very things into a vessel mixed with honey and ghee and eat them.
Living underground and subsisting on milk, he conquers old age as he wishes.
In two months he certainly sees the earth as full of holes.
He lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s> and sheds his slough like a snake.
The five parts of white <s>palāśa</s>, powdered, together with honey,
one should eat one <s>karṣa</s> daily; in months it removes death and old age.
The perfected man gains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s> in only a year; there is no doubt.
With goat's ghee he should always eat one seed of it at a time.
The body should be rubbed with its ash; in months he conquers death and old age.
The man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s> and becomes divine-bodied.

children.text: anye yogā yathā rakte brahmavṛkṣe ca ye guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever other procedures and qualities there are in the red <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>,
those same qualities will indeed occur for the practitioner in white <s>palāśa</s>.
'Make nectar, make nectar; homage to <s>Amṛtamālinī</s>.'
With this mantra, all the procedures, enchanted seven times, are to be eaten.

children.text: śuklapakṣe'tha pūrṇāyāṃ puṣye vā śravaṇe tathā
children.translated_text: In the bright fortnight, on the full-moon day, or under <s>Puṣya</s> or <s>Śravaṇa</s>,
or under <s>Revatī</s>, after worshiping, one should dig up the five parts of <s>muṇḍī</s>.

children.text: chāyāśuṣkaṃ tu taccūrṇaṃ karṣaṃ gopayasā saha
children.translated_text: Its powder, dried in the shade, one <s>karṣa</s>, together with cow's milk,
destroys old age in one year, and he lives for three hundred years.
Through his urine and feces, copper becomes golden.
That powder should be licked with ghee; likewise, wondrous strength will arise.

children.text: oṃ namo'mṛtodbhavāya amṛtaṃ kuru kuru svāhā oṃ hrāṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: The mantra is: 'Oṃ, homage to the nectar-born one; make nectar, make nectar, svāhā; oṃ hrāṃ saḥ.'
Thus is the mantra for eating the medicine.
One should then powder the five parts of <s>devadālī</s>, dried in the shade.
He should lick one <s>karṣa</s> with honey and ghee; in a year he conquers death and old age.
A man lives for a thousand aeons and becomes equal to <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ karṣamātraṃ tu nityaṃ peyaṃ śivāmbunā ||
children.translated_text: One <s>karṣa</s> of that powder should be drunk daily with <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine).
Perfection arises as before in a year; of this there is no doubt.
That powder should be in equal parts with <s>vākucī</s>, <s>vahni</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>.

children.text: cūrṇitaṃ karṣamātraṃ tu nityaṃ peyaṃ śivāmbunā
children.translated_text: Powdered, one <s>karṣa</s> should be drunk daily with <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine).

children.text: varṣānmṛtyuṃ jarāṃ hanti chidrāṃ paśyati medinīm ||
children.translated_text: In a year it destroys death and old age, and he sees the earth as full of holes.
A man should drink daily the juices of <s>punarnavā</s> and <s>devadālī</s>.
Or he should drink one <s>pala</s> of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>sarpākṣī</s> with <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine).
The perfection will be as before in a year; of this there is no doubt.
He should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> with <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine).
In one year it destroys old age, and he lives as long as the moon and stars.
The mantra is: 'Oṃ, nectar-host, Rudra-host waters, svāhā.'
And this is the mantra for taking hold of it.

children.text: namo bhagavate rudrāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: 'Homage to the blessed <s>Rudra</s>; huṃ phaṭ svāhā.'
This is the practitioner's mantra for tying the topknot.
'Oṃ cara ra ra.'
This is the mantra for eating.
Under <s>Puṣya</s>, the root of white <s>arka</s> should be taken and dried in the shade.
One should drink a <s>karṣa</s> of the powder with cow's milk, mixed with two <s>palas</s> of <s>dvaṃdva</s>.
After six months it destroys old age, and he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
The liquid of white <s>arka</s> leaves, equal to the liquid of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>,
should be combined, dried in the sun, and the powder mixed with four times as much milk.
He should cook it over a gentle fire until it has become a lump.
One <s>karṣa</s> of that should be licked with ghee; in a year the result will be as before.
The mantra is: 'Oṃ āṃ haṃ, to <s>Vāsaramālin</s>, svāhā.'
This is the mantra for eating.
On <s>Somatrayodaśī</s> one should take the leaf of <s>hastikarṇa</s>.

children.text: chāyāśuṣkaṃ tu taccūrṇaṃ gavāṃ kṣīraiḥ pibetpalam ||
children.translated_text: Its powder, dried in the shade, should be drunk, one <s>pala</s>, with cow's milk.
In only a year it destroys old age, and a man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
The five parts of <s>hastikarṇa</s>, dried in the shade and finely powdered,
one should drink daily in the measure of a <s>karṣa</s> for one month with water.
Then it is to be taken successively with sour gruel, buttermilk, curds, milk, ghee, and honey,
each one separately, for one month; it removes old age.
He lives for a day and a half of <s>Brahmā</s>, with an adamantine body and great strength.
The mantra is: 'Oṃ, I seize the poison and venom in sight, svāhā.'
This is the mantra for taking <s>hastikarṇa</s>.

children.text: oṃ amṛtakuṭījātānām amṛtaṃ kuru kuru svāhā
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ, for those born in the nectar-hut, make nectar, make nectar, svāhā.'
With this one should worship.

children.text: oṃ amṛtodbhavāya amṛtaṃ kuru kuru nityaṃ namo namaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ, to the nectar-born one, make nectar, make nectar always; homage, homage.'
This is the mantra for eating.
One should finely powder the five parts of <s>rudantī</s>, dried in the shade.
Half as much powder of <s>musalī</s>, and half as much of <s>musalī</s> of the three fruits,
and oil from roots arising from <s>kataka</s> should be obtained in a subterranean apparatus,
or in a womb-apparatus; that oil should be washed with water.
Or it should be washed with coconut water five times.
Mixed with this oil, the previous powder should be licked in due order.
The dose should be increased from a <s>karṣa</s> onward, and then increased up to a <s>pala</s>.
In this way, after a year it destroys old age, and the lifespan becomes a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: siddhayogo hy ayaṃ khyāto vajrakāyakaro nṛṇām
children.translated_text: This is indeed a famous perfected procedure, producing an adamantine body for men.
When <s>Puṣya</s> falls on a Sunday, one should take in the morning the bark from the root of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
After drying it in the shade and powdering it, he should always drink one <s>karṣa</s>,
with one <s>pala</s> of goat's urine; in six months he becomes immortal.
By a year-long application, a man becomes equal to <s>Śiva</s>.
That powder, stirred with milk, honey, and ghee in a greased vessel,
should be sealed and placed in a heap of grain; after one month he should take it out and eat it.
Taking two <s>palas</s> for a full year, he lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
One should lick half a <s>pala</s> of that powder with ghee; the result will be as before.

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ triphalā muṇḍī bhṛṅgī nimbo guḍūcikā ||
children.translated_text: That powder consists of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>guḍūcikā</s>,

children.text: vacā caiṣāṃ samaṃ cūrṇaṃ madhvājyābhyāṃ lihetpalam
children.translated_text: and <s>vacā</s>; one should lick a <s>pala</s> of the powder of these, in equal parts, with honey and ghee.
After a year it destroys death and old age; he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
The liquid produced from <s>nirguṇḍī</s> leaves should be cooked in a vessel over a gentle fire.
When it has reached a jaggery-like consistency, if drunk it causes vomiting and purging.
His worms come out through the mouth, nose, eyes, and ears.
And diseases beginning with royal consumption are destroyed in seven days.
