After three months it destroys old age; he lives for three hundred years.

children.text: oṃ namo māya gaṇapataye bhūpataye kuberāya svāhā iti bhakṣaṇamantraḥ
children.translated_text: This is the mantra for eating: "Oṃ, homage to <s>Māyā</s>, to <s>Gaṇapati</s>, to <s>Bhūpati</s>, to <s>Kubera</s>, svāhā."
<s>Bhallātaka</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, the fruit of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
<s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>nimba</s> leaves, and <s>sahadevī</s>, each in equal amount:
from these the oil should be carefully obtained by means of a <s>pātālayantra</s> apparatus.
One should drink half a <s>pala</s> of that oil combined with the root of <s>nīlikā</s>.
After a year it destroys gray hair; one's lifespan becomes a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
When nasal treatment is performed with half a <s>niṣka</s> of that oil, the result is as before.
One <s>prastha</s> of black cumin and an equal amount of juice from <s>bhṛṅga</s>,
and <s>yaṣṭī</s> and <s>nīlotpala</s>, one should take half a <s>prastha</s> of each.
A quarter <s>prastha</s> of oil from sesame should be cooked together with all of it.
When only the oil remains, it should be taken, and nasal treatment should be carried out with that very oil.
One should perform nasal treatment with <s>aṅkolla</s> oil, which removes death and old age.
With a dose of half a <s>niṣka</s> or a <s>niṣka</s> for one year, he lives for three hundred years.
Having ground the fruit of <s>kākamācī</s>, one should drink one <s>karṣa</s> with water.
After a year it destroys gray hair; one's lifespan becomes a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: guḍūcī musalī muṇḍī nirguṇḍī ca śatāvarī
children.translated_text: <s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
and <s>vijayā</s>, made into a powder in equal parts and combined with sugar, honey, and ghee:
one should eat two <s>karṣas</s> daily; after a year he conquers gray hair.
This was taught by <s>Gorakṣanātha</s>; he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
On the dark eighth lunar day, with black threads, the tree of <s>śunakaśālmalī</s>
should be wrapped with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, and at night a black goat should be given as an offering.
Having given it, one should recite <s>Aghora</s> there up to eight thousand times.
Its root-bark should be taken, dried in the shade, and powdered.
One should always eat one <s>pala</s> with honey and ghee for the period of a year.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, a man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tasya puṣpāṇi saṃgṛhya gavāṃ kṣīraiḥ sadā pacet
children.translated_text: One should gather its flowers and always cook them with cow's milk.
The milk should be drunk with the flowers removed; after a month it removes death and old age.

children.text: phalaikaṃ tasya vṛkṣasya gavāṃ kṣīreṇa pācayet
children.translated_text: One fruit of that tree should be cooked in cow's milk.
The milk should be drunk with the fruit removed; the wise man should drink milk in this way.
By four months' use, a man becomes diamond-bodied.
He lives until the end of the aeon, swift as the wind and very strong.
Through his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
<s>Kākamācī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>sahadevikā</s>,
with the whole plant of <s>devadālī</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>vākucī</s> seed,
the fruits of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, and the roots of <s>brahmā</s> and <s>aśvagandhā</s>,
the leaves of <s>nīlakoraṇṭa</s>, and <s>triphalā</s>, all in equal amounts:
that powder should be steeped for seven days in the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>.
Dried in the shade, it should be prepared with sugar, honey, and ghee.
One should eat two <s>karṣas</s> daily; after only a year he conquers old age.
He lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars, great-bodied and very strong.

children.text: oṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ saḥ saḥ saḥ amṛte amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtasaṃjīvani sarvakāmaprade bhagavān somarāja ājñāpayati svāhā iti bhakṣaṇamantraḥ
children.translated_text: This is the mantra for eating: "Oṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ saḥ saḥ saḥ, O immortal one, O showerer of immortality, O reviver with immortality, O giver of all desires, the blessed <s>Somarāja</s> commands, svāhā."
<s>Triphalā</s>, <s>vākucī</s> seed, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>aśvagandhikā</s>:

children.text: sarvaṃ tulyaṃ kṛtaṃ cūrṇaṃ madhvājyābhyāṃ lihetpalam
children.translated_text: all made into an equal powder, one should lick one <s>pala</s> with honey and ghee.
After a year it destroys death and old age; he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ saḥ svāhā anena mantreṇa bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: By this mantra he should eat: "Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ saḥ svāhā."
In applications of root-preparations, one <s>guñjā</s> of killed mercury
should be eaten together with each preparation; the result becomes a hundredfold.
By the power of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), he quickly obtains accomplishment.
The mantra practitioner, wearing a bone seal, should recite one hundred thousand times in a cremation ground.
It destroys great fear and grants accomplishment in <s>rasāyana</s>.
By merely eating it, he lives as long as the moon and stars.
Unconquerable by gods and demons, he can even move mountains.
"Oṃ hrīṃ mahābhayerum."

children.text: prātaḥ puṣyārkamukhye vividhaśubhadine mantrapūjāvidhānair grāhyaṃ divyauṣadhīnāṃ phaladalakusumaṃ mūlapattraṃ rasaṃ vā
children.translated_text: In the morning, on a foremost auspicious day such as <s>Puṣyārka</s>, through the rites of mantra and worship, one should collect the fruit, leaf, flower, root, leaf, or sap of divine herbs for accomplishment.

children.text: sarvāṅgaṃ vātha siddhyai sakalamabhinavaṃ sevayed brahmacārī kṣīrānnaṃ codakānnaṃ hitamaśanamidaṃ sarvamanyad vivarjyam ||
children.translated_text: Or one should use the whole fresh plant in its entirety; the celibate practitioner should take milk-rice and water-rice as wholesome food and avoid everything else.

children.text: udvartanaṃ palitahāri paraṃ narāṇāṃ śobhāvahaṃ sukhakaraṃ kacarañjanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: I shall describe a supreme anointing for men, removing gray hair, bringing beauty and comfort, and dyeing the hair.
It is useful for the old, easy to accomplish by many methods, well-proven, and seen on the path of experience.
Mercury and sulfur, in equal amounts, should be ground with a woman's breast milk.
<s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>munimuṇḍikā</s>:
with the juices of these, it should be ground in a mortar for a day, and then taken out.
Barley flour and sesame, each equal in amount to the mercury, should also be used.
One should throw it into that, with ghee and honey, mix everything thoroughly, and preserve it.
With this, rubbing the body properly destroys wrinkles and gray hair.
After a year he becomes divine-bodied and lives for a thousand years.
The root of <s>vajrakāpālinī</s> and mercury should be taken in equal parts.
They should be ground for three days with <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine); by rubbing, the result is as before.

children.text: utpalāni samūlāni pāradaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Whole <s>utpala</s> lotuses with their roots and mercury should be taken in equal parts.
One should grind them for seven days in a mortar with one's own <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine).
With that very preparation one should rub the body; the result is as before.
A root of <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, in an amount equal to the mercury,
should be added and ground for seven days with one's own <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine).
With this one should rub the body; the result is as before.
Sulfur should be steeped in pungent oil in the heat for the length of a day.
One should always eat half a <s>pala</s> of that; it produces a divine body in men.
After a year the body becomes like gold and free from wrinkles.

children.text: kuṣṭhacūrṇaṃ samadhvājyaṃ nityaṃ karṣaṃ lihettu yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever daily licks one <s>karṣa</s> of powdered <s>kuṣṭha</s> with honey and ghee,
after a year becomes divine-bodied, with a fragrance like <s>śatapuṣpā</s>.
Powder of <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> should be combined with oil, honey, and ghee,
and all the fruit of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>; all this should be prepared in equal measure.
Having sealed it in a vessel, one should put it for a month in a heap of grain and then take it out.
With this one should smear the head, and indeed make a nasal preparation from this.
After three days the hairs become like bees, for half a year.
One <s>pala</s> of powdered <s>nāga</s> (lead) and two <s>palas</s> of powdered conch,
and one <s>niṣka</s> of powdered <s>pathyā</s> should all be ground for a day.
Mixed carefully with sour curd, after bathing it should first be put on the head.
One should rub for half a <s>ghaṭikā</s>, and it should be wrapped with castor leaves.

children.text: śiraḥ saṃveṣṭya vastreṇa prātaḥ snānaṃ samācaret ||
children.translated_text: After wrapping the head with cloth, in the morning one should perform bathing.
Doing just this carefully for three days, one should dye the hair.
The five parts of <s>nīlikā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and iron powder,
all made equal and fine, should be ground with <s>iḍā</s>-urine.
For half a day, with that paste, hair-dyeing is as before.
<s>Guñjā</s> seeds with their husk removed, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, cardamom, and <s>devadāru</s>,
as equal powder, should be steeped for a day with liquids produced from <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>.
One should cook everything in four times as much oil over a gentle fire.
By anointing the hair with that, there is dyeing like a bee.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> should be added in equal amount to burnt elephant tusk.
After grinding that with goat's milk, the smearing dyes the hair.
<s>Triphalā</s>, iron powder, black earth, liquid from <s>bhṛṅga</s>,
and juice of sugarcane stalk should be confined in a vessel for a month.
By smearing that, one dyes the hair; it lasts for as much as five months.
Iron dross, hibiscus flower, and <s>dhātrī</s> fruit in equal amount should be ground.
When the locks are smeared with that for three days, they become like bees.
A <s>prastha</s> of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> juice and oil produced from black sesame,

children.text: tulyaṃ ca nīlikādrāvaṃ sarvaṃ yāmaṃ vimardayet
children.translated_text: together with an equal amount of <s>nīlikā</s> liquid, should all be thoroughly ground for one watch.
That smearing should be done for three days; it becomes a dyeing of the hair.

children.text: sindūrasya samaṃ cūrṇaṃ sābuṇaṃ ca tayoḥ samam
children.translated_text: An equal powder of vermilion and soap, and an equal amount of the two,
ground in water, should be applied; it dyes the locks immediately.
<s>Śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, black sesame seeds, and <s>rocana</s>,
all should be ground for a day with <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine) in an iron vessel.
One should apply that smear for three days; hair-dyeing takes place.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ sarjī yavakṣāraṃ siddhārthaṃ kāñjikaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: Powdered alkali, barley-alkali, and white mustard, together with sour gruel,
should be ground with liquids from <s>nāgapuṣpā</s>; by its smearing, dyeing takes place.
<s>Nīlī</s> leaves, green vitriol, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> juice, and curd,
with iron powder, should be ground equally; that smearing is a hair-dye.
Powder, vermilion, and charcoal, combined with plantain rhizome,
should be ground in an iron vessel with an iron pestle and with liquids from citron.

children.text: dinaikaṃ ca tato lepyaṃ keśānāṃ rañjanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For one day, and then it should be applied; hair-dyeing takes place.
The leaves of <s>kuraṇṭaka</s> should be thoroughly ground with a lead pestle.
One should apply that smear for three days; hair-dyeing arises.
Mango stone, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and citron,

children.text: niśā nīlī mṛṇālāni nāgaṃ lohaṃ ca cūrṇitam ||
children.translated_text: turmeric, <s>nīlī</s>, lotus fibers, lead, and iron, powdered,
should be made into an equal paste in a <s>kānta</s> vessel and steeped with neem oil.
For just a month; after that, by smearing with it, dyeing occurs.
Seeds of <s>kākamācī</s>, and likewise an equal amount of black sesame seeds,
one should extract their oil in an apparatus; that nasal application dyes the hair.
Cow ghee, liquid from <s>bhṛṅga</s>, together with peacock crest,
should be cooked over a gentle fire; with that, a nasal preparation dyes the hair.
One should make a nasal application of hibiscus-flower juice and one <s>karṣa</s> of honey.
After seven days it dyes the hair; this is the rule for all nasal applications.
<s>Triphalā</s> and iron powder should be ground equally with water,
and with an equal amount of oil and <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> juice.
One should cook it until only the oil remains, and confine it in a greasy vessel.
One should keep it underground for one month, and with it smear the head.
Having wrapped it with leaves of bitter gourd, one should then bind it with cloth.
Remaining out of the wind, subsisting on milk as food, one should wash it with <s>triphalā</s> water.
This smearing should be performed daily for seven days.
It is renowned as <s>kapālarañjana</s> (scalp-dye), lasting for life, without doubt.
The seeds of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, together with <s>siryālī</s> seeds,
should be powdered and infused for four days with the liquids of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
For the same length of time it should be infused with the juices of hibiscus flowers; then, in a <s>pātāla-yantra</s>,

children.text: tailaṃ prāhyaṃ tu tallepātkeśānāṃ rañjanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the oil should be extracted. From applying that oil there will be dyeing of the hair.
It should be wrapped with castor leaves; one should stay out of the wind and take milk as food.
One should bathe with sour gruel daily; when seven days have been completed,

children.text: yāvajjīvaṃ na saṃdehaḥ keśāḥ syur bhramaropamāḥ
children.translated_text: the hairs become like black bees for life, without doubt.
<s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>kācamācī</s>, and <s>jalamaṇḍavī</s>, in equal parts,
should be ground, made into a cake, and cooked in oil.
When that has been cooked, one should grind it with oils; the paste will be a dye for the hair.
By the same sequence of procedure as before, its result comes about in a week.
At night, in a vessel made of <s>ayaskānta</s> (magnetite), the three fruits should be smeared,
together with the liquids of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>; in the morning one should smear the hair.
One should do this for three weeks; the result is produced as before.
One should put black cumin into a buffalo horn and seal it.

children.text: gṛhāgre kardame kṣiptvā ṣaṇmāsāt tat samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed it in mud in front of the house, one should take it out after six months.

children.text: taddrutaṃ jāyate kṛṣṇaṃ karṣaikaṃ śirasi kṣipet
children.translated_text: It becomes black when liquefied; one should place one <s>karṣa</s> on the head.
One should wrap it by the previous method; it becomes a <s>kapālarañjana</s> (scalp-dye).
It is like black bee-collyrium and lasts for life, without doubt.
Indigo leaf, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and black iron,

children.text: madanasya ca bījāni puṣpaṃ koraṇṭakasya ca
children.translated_text: the seeds of <s>madana</s>, and the flower of <s>koraṇṭaka</s>,
powdered bark of <s>arjuna</s>, and mud from the lotus root:
one should put all these in equal measure into an iron vessel and seal it.
One should bury it in the ground for a fortnight and take the paste out from the vessel.
To the paste should be added four times as much oil, and to the oil four times as much liquid.
The liquid made from <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>triphalā</s> should be added, and it should be cooked until only oil remains.
For testing, one should put in a feather of a heron; when it becomes

children.text: kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ tadā siddhaṃ pātre kṛṣṇāyase kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: black in color, then it is perfected, and one should place it in a black iron vessel.
One should keep it in that for one month; then one should apply it to the hairs.
They remain for six months resembling swarms of black bees.
With strong sticks made from <s>vāsā</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>ciñcā</s>, or <s>aśvattha</s>,
<s>nāga</s> (lead), placed in a vessel, should be stirred until it becomes processed.
Taking one <s>pala</s> of that, and two <s>palas</s> of iron powder,
three <s>palas</s> of <s>triphalā</s> powder, and the rind of pomegranate fruit,

children.text: śuṣkaṃ cūrṇaṃ palaikaṃ tatsarveṣāṃ kāñjikaṃ samam
children.translated_text: one <s>pala</s> of that dried powder, and sour gruel equal to all of them,
one should cook everything a little in a vessel and then put it into an iron container.
Having added liquid produced from <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> and <s>kuraṇṭa</s>, one should place it in the sun.

children.text: trisaptāhaṃ prayatnena dravo deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For three weeks, carefully, the liquid should be added again and again.
Then one should preserve it. By application with it there will be dyeing of the hair.
In the stated and unstated pastes, the head should be wrapped with castor leaves

children.text: śiro rātrau divā snānaṃ yuktireṣā praśasyate
children.translated_text: at night, and bathed during the day; this procedure is recommended.
For seven days one should infuse the fruit of <s>abhayā</s> with <s>vajrī</s> milk.
By applying oil mixed with that powder, they indeed become white.
The head hairs and all body hairs become conch-colored.
For seven days one should infuse very white sesame seeds with <s>vajra</s> milk.
Having obtained oil from them, by applying that oil they indeed become white.
White <s>āmalaka</s> powder should be infused seven times with <s>vajrī</s> milk.
By that paste the hairs of the head become white.

children.text: sindūraṃ sphaṭikāṃ śvetāṃ jalena saha lepayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sindūra</s> and white crystal should be applied together with water.

children.text: tallepena tu romāṇi suśuklāni bhavanti hi
children.translated_text: By that application the body hairs indeed become very white.
For one month, <s>māgadhī</s> powder should be infused with <s>vajrī</s> milk.
It is the best whitener for men, horses, elephants, and steeds.
<s>Indragopa</s>, <s>tailinī</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, the two <s>rajanī</s>s,

children.text: manaḥśilā ca tulyāṃśaṃ cūrṇaṃ snukpayasā tryaham
children.translated_text: and <s>manaḥśilā</s>, in equal parts, should be powdered with the milk of <s>snuk</s> for three days.
For three days it should be infused with the milks of <s>arka</s> plants in harsh sunlight.
Then it should be infused with the liquids of <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s> for seven days.
Then, having placed it inside a <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s> gourd, one should take it out after a month.
With oil, one should apply it to all body hairs and to the hair for three days.
One should wrap them with <s>arka</s> leaves, and they become white in color.

children.text: snāne kṛte śuṣkakaceṣu rātrau lepe kṛte pūrvadalaistu veṣṭyam
children.translated_text: After bathing, when the hair is dry and the paste has been applied at night, it should be wrapped with the previously mentioned leaves.

children.text: dadhnā tilaiḥ snānamataḥ prabhāte kuryāttryahaṃ lepanamitthameva ||
children.translated_text: Then in the morning one should bathe with curds and sesame; one should perform the application in just this way for three days.

children.text: yeṣāṃ rāmā ramaṇakuśalā rāgasaktāḥ pragalbhāḥ kāmāsaktā hariṇanayanāścandrabimbānanāśca
children.translated_text: For those whose women are skilled in lovemaking, attached to passion, bold, devoted to desire, deer-eyed, and moon-faced,

children.text: teṣāṃ vakṣye madanasukhadāṃ vīryavṛddhiṃ prabhūtāṃ mattāḥ siddhāḥ śatamapi dṛḍhāstādṛśāstoṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: I shall declare an abundant increase of virility that gives the pleasure of love; intoxicated and perfected, they satisfy even a hundred such women firmly.
Calcined powders of diamond, gold, <s>arka</s>, mercury, mica, and iron, in successive order,
should all be rubbed with the fluids of a maiden and with the liquids of <s>śālmalī</s> for three days.
Having sealed that inside a glass bottle, one should cook it in sand for three days.
That paste, with decoctions of <s>musalī</s> and joined with the milks of <s>vajra</s> and <s>arka</s>,
should be ground for one day in a mortar, sealed, and heated in an underground <s>puṭa</s> furnace.
After taking it out after a watch of the day and pulverizing it, with sugar, black pepper, and <s>trijāta</s>,
one should mix it with an equal quantity of those; then one should always eat one <s>māṣa</s>.
<s>Māgadhī</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, and <s>vānarī</s> seed, in equal amount,
Afterward he should administer half a <s>pala</s> of the powder with sugar, ghee, and cow's milk.
Even while making love to a thousand women, he is not overcome.
Through its use he becomes firm-bodied; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Makaradhvaja</s>.
Purified mercury and an equal amount of sulfur should be treated with the juices of red-lotus petals.

children.text: yāmaṃ mardyaṃ punargandhaṃ sārdhaṃ tatra vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: It should be ground for one <s>yāma</s>; then additional sulfur, one and a half parts, should be added there.
It should be ground for a day with the previous liquids, and again sulfur amounting to half the mercury should be added.
After grinding it for a day in the same way, he should seal it in a glass bottle.
After cooking it for one day in a sand apparatus, he should remove it and powder it.
He should impregnate it for seven days with a decoction of <s>bhūkuṣmāṇḍī</s>.
After drying it in the shade, he should always eat one <s>niṣka</s> of it, mixed with an equal amount of sugar.

children.text: śaṇamūlaṃ sabījaṃ ca musalī śarkarā samam ||
children.translated_text: The root of <s>śaṇa</s> together with its seed, <s>musalī</s>, and sugar should be in equal amounts.

children.text: gavāṃ kṣīraiḥ palārdhaṃ tu anu rātrau sadā pibet
children.translated_text: At night he should always drink half a <s>pala</s> of that afterward with cow's milk.
His virility increases without limit; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Madanodaya</s>.
Purified mercury and an equal amount of sulfur should be treated with the juices of <s>badarī</s> and <s>citraka</s>.
It should be ground with liquids from <s>aṅkolla</s> for three days in a heated mortar.

children.text: sadyo hatājamāṃsasya piṇḍe nyastaṃ ca sīvayet
children.translated_text: It should be placed inside a lump of flesh from a freshly killed goat and sewn up.
That lump should be cooked slowly in sesame oil in an iron vessel.
When the flesh has become red in color, he should then remove the mercury.
After it has been impregnated for three days with decoctions of <s>musalī</s>, it should be mixed with sugar.
He should eat one <s>niṣka</s> daily; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Madaneśvara</s>.
He should drink one <s>pala</s> of powdered <s>vidārīkanda</s> with milk and ghee.
He may enjoy a hundred women daily; if he abandons it, he goes blind.

children.text: mṛtābhraṃ pāradaṃ svarṇaṃ tulyaṃ mardyaṃ dinatrayam ||
children.translated_text: Calcined mica, mercury, and gold, in equal amounts, should be ground for three days.
This should be done with decoctions of <s>musalī</s> and <s>triphala</s>, and with decoctions of <s>vājigandhā</s>.
With liquids from plantain tubers, that ball should be sealed and calcined in a <s>puṭa</s>.
It should remain in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace for one day only; then, after removing it, he should grind it.
For one day he should grind it with the previous liquids; likewise, after sealing it, he should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Again it should be ground, and again it should be cooked; in this way it should be cooked through eight <s>puṭas</s>.
With exudates produced from <s>śālmalī</s>, together with an equal amount of sugar,
he should eat two <s>niṣkas</s> daily, and he will arouse a hundred women.
Afterward he should administer half a <s>pala</s> of <s>markaṭī</s> seed with cow's milk.
He should perform a full-body rubbing with liquids of <s>śālmalī</s> together with barley.
This <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Kāmakalā</s>, produces great virility in men.

children.text: mṛtasūtaṃ trayo bhāgā bhāgaikaṃ hāṭakaṃ mṛtam
children.translated_text: Calcined mercury should be three parts, and calcined <s>hāṭaka</s> gold one part.
It should be treated for a day with liquids from plantain tubers and with liquids from <s>śālmalī</s>.
It should also be ground for a day with cow's milk, and cooked for a moment with ghee.

children.text: tanmadhye śarkarāṃ drākṣāṃ dhātrīṃ rambhāphalaṃ madhu ||
children.translated_text: Into it he should put sugar, grapes, <s>dhātrī</s>, plantain fruit, and honey,
as well as cow's milk, <s>musalī</s>, <s>māṣa</s> beans, and the seed of <s>kokilākṣa</s>.
After adding four times as much as the mercury, it should be ground with liquids from <s>śālmalī</s>.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ dinamekaṃ tu kāmadevo raso bhavet
children.translated_text: All that, after one day, becomes the <s>Kāmadeva</s> <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: niṣkamātraṃ sadā bhakṣyaṃ gavāṃ kṣīraṃ pibedanu ||
children.translated_text: One should always eat a measure of one <s>niṣka</s> and afterward drink cow's milk.
In intercourse his penis becomes firm, and he arouses a multitude of women.
He should grind calcined mercury with the first menstrual blood of women.

children.text: mṛtaṃ tāmraṃ ca tāraṃ ca gandhakaṃ ca samaṃ dinam
children.translated_text: Calcined copper, silver, and sulfur should also be ground in equal amounts for a day.
After eating one <s>niṣka</s> mixed with sugar, honey, and ghee, he should drink milk.
Named <s>Ratikāmarasa</s>, it is beneficial for the pleasure of women.
<s>Vānarī</s> root, wheat, and the seed of <s>kokilākṣa</s>,
together with <s>māṣa</s> beans, should all be mixed with sugarcane juice and cooked with ghee.

children.text: tenaiva vaṭakāḥ kāryā nityaṃ khādeddvayaṃ dvayam ||
children.translated_text: Pills should be made from that very mixture; he should eat two and two daily.
This adjunct is proven; through its use he may enjoy a hundred women.
Purified mercury and an equal amount of sulfur should be ground for three days with juices from <s>kahlāra</s>.
After it has been ground and sealed, it should be cooked for one <s>yāma</s> in a sand apparatus.
It should be impregnated for one day with liquids of red <s>agastya</s>, together with sugar.
He should always eat a measure of one <s>niṣka</s>; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Madavardhana</s>.
A goat's testicle should be cooked in milk, together with sesame and sugar.
He may eat it afterward as he wishes, and he may enjoy a hundred women.

children.text: paladvayaṃ dvayaṃ śuddhaṃ pāradaṃ gandhakaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Two <s>palas</s> each of purified mercury and good sulfur should be taken.
One <s>karṣa</s> of calcined gold and one <s>pala</s> of calcined copper should be added.
There should be four <s>niṣkas</s> of silver ash; all of it should be ground for a day with the five nectars.

children.text: mardyaṃ ruddhvā dinaṃ pacyādbhūdhare taṃ samuddharet
children.translated_text: After grinding it, he should seal it and cook it for a day in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace, then remove it.
After pounding it with the five nectars, he should eat a pill the size of a jujube.
It is known as <s>Anaṅgasundarī</s>; he delights with a hundred women.
Powdered root of <s>śālmalī</s> should be combined with honey and sugar.
He should eat one <s>pala</s>, and afterward he should drink sweetened milk.
Purified mercury should be ground for one fortnight with liquids arising from <s>śālmalī</s>.
Purified sulfur should be ground separately for three weeks with those liquids.
These two, in equal amounts, should then be ground again with ghee for four <s>yāmas</s>.
That ball should be tied in cloth and cooked with ghee for two <s>yāmas</s>.
Then it should be ground with liquids of <s>śālmalī</s> for three days.
He should place it inside a glass bottle and cook it in a sand apparatus.
He should pour liquid from <s>śālmalī</s> into the belly of the bottle for the duration of a day.
Removing it while still moist, he should mix it with an equal amount of sugar.
He should always eat a measure of one <s>niṣka</s>; this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Kāmanāyaka</s>.
Afterward he should administer one <s>pala</s> of <s>musalī</s> with sugar in milk.
It would arouse a thousand women within the blink of an eye.
There should be three parts of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and one part of copper powder.
Having made a paste, he should then enclose it again inside the tuber of a plantain.
Coated with clay and dried, it should be cooked for one day with a cow-dung fire.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaṃ pacyātkande kande dinaṃ dinam ||
children.translated_text: In this way he should cook it for seven days, in a fresh tuber day by day.
Taking it out, he should tie it in a firm cloth, indeed folded four times.
He should cook it, placed in goat's blood mixed with the flesh of small <s>śambūka</s> snails.

children.text: dolāyantre tryahaṃ yāvaddeyaṃ raktaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: In a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus), for three days, blood should be added again and again.
With <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>gajapippalī</s>, <s>kadalī</s>, and <s>kokilākṣa</s>,
and with the liquids of <s>gokṣurī</s>, <s>vānarī</s> root, and <s>jātī</s> root,
or with their decoctions, he should cook it in a <s>dolāyantra</s> for three days.
Then, in the same way, he should cook it in milk mixed with sugar for the length of a day.

children.text: aśvagandhā vacā kuṣṭhaṃ bṛhatī ca śatāvarī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvagandhā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>
should be cooked with sesame oil; with that he should massage it as before.
The penis becomes thick, firm, and long in the space of a month.
Oil produced from <s>jambū</s> and pig, <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>, and borax,
as this paste together with honey, makes the penis grow in a month.
Powder of <s>musalī</s> should be mixed with fresh buffalo butter.
That vessel, placed in a heap of grain, should be removed after seven days.
With that he should smear the penis; it grows in the space of a month.

children.text: pippalī maricaṃ kṣīraṃ sitā tulyaṃ vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: Long pepper, black pepper, milk, and sugar should be ground in equal amounts.
For one month it makes the penis grow; no deliberation is to be made about this.

children.text: māhiṣaṃ goghṛtaṃ tulyaṃ saindhavaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Buffalo ghee and cow ghee, and rock salt, all in equal amounts:
with this one should smear the penis; it becomes thick within a month.
<s>Aśvagandhā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>sārivā</s>, <s>akṣa</s> fruit, sesame,
mustard, and <s>indrayava</s>, in equal amounts, should be ground with goat's milk.
By massaging the penis with that for one month, it obtains growth.
<s>Māṃsī</s>, <s>akṣa</s> fruit, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>:
this paste, cooked in oil, makes the penis grow in a month.
Bile from a <s>rohīta</s> fish, leeches, and <s>lāṅgalī</s>, in equal amounts:
with this one should smear the penis; in a month it becomes like a pestle.
Turmeric, sugar, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and mercury should be ground in equal amounts.
With this one should massage the penis, and also the vulva, ears, and breasts.
They grow in the space of a month; no deliberation is to be made about this.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate uḍḍāmareśvarāya sara prasara 2 kuru ṭha ṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the blessed <s>Uḍḍāmareśvara</s>: flow, spread forth, spread forth, do it, ṭha ṭhaḥ.

children.text: anena mantreṇa sarve vardhanayogāḥ saptābhimantritāḥ siddhā bhavanti
children.translated_text: With this mantra, all the enlargement preparations, empowered by seven recitations, become effective.
He should smear on the bile of the <s>jambū</s> creature and the cat, kneaded with barley gruel.

children.text: māsaikādvardhate liṅgaṃ stanau karṇau ca mardanāt ||
children.translated_text: From one month the penis grows, and so do the breasts and ears, through massage.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate uḍḍāmareśvarāya sara prasara prasara nikala nikala nikālaya nikālaya svāhā ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the blessed <s>Uḍḍāmareśvara</s>: flow, spread forth, spread forth, come out, come out, bring out, bring out, svāhā, ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ.

children.text: gṛhagodhā śuno jihvā strījarāyuḥ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: A house-lizard, the tongue of a dog, and a woman's afterbirth, each in equal amount,

children.text: piṣṭvā dhāryaṃ tāmrapātre saptāhāttaṃ punaḥ pacet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground and kept in a copper vessel; after seven days, he should cook it again.
With sesame oil, by massaging with that oil, there is indeed growth.

children.text: liṅgaṃ stanau ca karṇau ca hastau pādau na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The penis, breasts, ears, hands, and feet grow; there is no doubt.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate uḍḍāmareśvarāya sara sara hili hili svāhā ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the blessed <s>Uḍḍāmareśvara</s>: flow, flow, hili hili, svāhā, ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ.

children.text: atitarasukhasādhyair yogarājaiḥ prasiddhaiḥ satatasuratayogyaṃ stambhanaṃ vardhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: By these renowned kingly preparations, extremely quick and easy to accomplish, there is fixation and enlargement fit for constant lovemaking.

children.text: nipuṇarasikarāmārañjakaṃ mohakaṃ syād gaditamiha samastaṃ bhogināṃ saukhyahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Everything has been stated here as a cause of pleasure for enjoyers: pleasing to skilled connoisseur women and able to enchant them.

children.text: śrīśaile dehasiddhiḥ prabhavati sahasā vṛkṣamṛtkandatoyais tacchāstraṃ śambhunoktaṃ pragahanam akhilaṃ vīkṣitaṃ yattu sāram
children.translated_text: At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, bodily perfection quickly arises from trees, earth, tubers, and waters; the essence of that profound teaching, entirely spoken by <s>Śambhu</s>, has been examined.

children.text: vyāhṛtyānekayuktyā sakalasukhakaraṃ dṛṣṭasiddhaṃ tu yadyattadvakṣye sādhakānāmanubhavapathagaṃ bhuktaye muktaye ca ||
children.translated_text: After explaining with many methods whatever is seen to be effective and productive of every happiness, I shall state what lies on the path of practitioners' experience, for enjoyment and liberation.
In front of the god <s>Mallikārjuna</s>, like an elephant,

children.text: śilā tiṣṭhati yā rātrau sravate gugguluṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: there stands a stone which at night always exudes guggulu resin.
It should be collected with a spoon of palāśa wood and put into a gourd vessel.
One should always eat one <s>niṣka</s> of sulphur equal in amount to that guggulu.
In a month it destroys death and old age; one lives as long as the moon and stars.
That guggulu should be combined with molten copper in the proportion of one part in ten million.
It becomes divine gold, equal in brilliance to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
To the left of <s>Mallinātha</s> stands <s>Ghaṇṭāsiddheśvara</s>.

children.text: taddvāre vidyate kuṇḍaṃ tatra ghaṇṭā vilambate
children.translated_text: At his doorway there is a pool, and there a bell hangs down.
On the night of the dark fourteenth lunar day, with three fasting men,
the rite should be performed there by men free from distraction and sleepless.
One should bathe the god; one should carry the water.
One should ring the bell continuously until the end of the night.
Then <s>Śambhu</s>, being pleased, grants sky-going power.
A <s>krośa</s> to the south of <s>Ghaṇṭāsiddheśvara</s>,
one should dig; there earth like yellow orpiment is seen.
One should drink a <s>karṣa</s> of it with milk and sugar; after seven days he becomes immortal.
The famous Moon-water is to the west of <s>Mallinātha</s>.
It is situated there; in the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, on the full-moon day, one should accomplish the rite well.
The practitioner, standing near it without distraction,
should perform recitation at night; when, at midnight, the moon goes to touch that water,

children.text: spraṣṭuṃ candro yadā gacchettadā kṣipraṃ karāñjalim ||
children.translated_text: then he should quickly make a hollow of his joined hands.
When that water comes, he should stand ready and drink it at once.
The hero becomes diamond-bodied and lives as long as the moon and stars.
At the eastern gate of <s>Śrīśaila</s> there is the god <s>Tripurāntaka</s>.
In the northern direction from the god, nearby, there is a tamarind tree.

children.text: vidyate tasya mūle tu bhairavo dṛśyate svayam
children.translated_text: At its root <s>Bhairava</s> himself is seen.
In front of him one should dig the ground to the measure of a man.
There is seen a hot pool, furnished with blue-colored water.
The leaves of the tamarind tree should be bound properly in a cloth.

children.text: tasmin kuṇḍe vinikṣipya tāni mīnā bhavanti vai
children.translated_text: Having thrown them into that pit, they indeed become fish.
Having gathered them, he should cook them with wood from that; he should remove from them

children.text: kaṇṭakāni śiraḥ pucchaṃ śeṣaṃ bhakṣeta sādhakaḥ
children.translated_text: the bones, head, and tail, and the <s>sādhaka</s> should eat what remains.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ mūrchā bhavettena prabuddho jāyate svayam ||
children.translated_text: Through that there is fainting for a moment; when awakened, he comes to by himself.
He sees an opening in the earth, and the man lives for ten thousand years.
Two <s>gavyūtis</s> west of <s>Tripurāntakadeva</s>,
there is a village called <s>Maṇipalli</s>; to its west is a mountain.
On the western side of that mountain an auspicious door is seen.
Facing east he should enter; then he should go south.
For a distance of ten <s>dhanvantaras</s>, fire-like lights are seen.
There are excellent stones shaped like mangoes; he should take them and bind them in cloth.
The cloth becomes red; then he should put them in milk.

children.text: tatkṣīraṃ jāyate raktaṃ tatkṣīraṃ sādhakaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: That milk becomes red like blood; the <s>sādhaka</s> should drink that milk.
In seven days he becomes vajra-bodied and lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
North of <s>Tripurāntakadeva</s> is <s>Kokilābila</s>,
renowned in all worlds; after performing emesis and purgation,
the <s>sādhaka</s> should enter there for a distance of ten <s>dhanvantaras</s>.
Stones shaped like cuckoos stand there, and he should take them.

children.text: teṣāṃ pṛṣṭhe tilāḥ kṣiptāḥ sphuṭantyeva hi tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Sesame seeds thrown on their backs burst apart at that very moment.

children.text: ityevaṃ pratyayaṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃś ca ghṛṣṭvā parasparam ||
children.translated_text: Having seen this proof, he should rub those stones against each other.

children.text: kṣīramadhye kṣipettān vai kṣīraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ prajāyate
children.translated_text: He should then put them into milk; the milk becomes black.
He should drink it up to his throat; the man becomes a divine poet.
Free from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
He sees an opening in the earth, has the speed of wind, and possesses great strength.
One <s>yojana</s> to the east of <s>Tripurāntakadeva</s>,

children.text: devaḥ svargapurī nāma vidyate tatra vai khanet ||
children.translated_text: there is a deity named <s>Svargapurī</s>; there he should dig.

children.text: devāgre bhūmikāṃ jānumātrāṃ tatra phalā iva
children.translated_text: Before the deity he should dig the ground knee-deep; there, like fruits,

children.text: nirgacchanti tu pāṣāṇāḥ kharasparśā bhavanti vai ||
children.translated_text: stones come out, and they are rough to the touch.
Half a <s>yojana</s> west of <s>Tripurāntakadeva</s>

children.text: vidyate hi biladvāraṃ tanmadhye dhanuṣāṃ trayam ||
children.translated_text: there is the mouth of a cave; inside it he should go three bow-lengths.
A date-palm tree, black in color, is seen there.

children.text: tatphalānāṃ rasaṃ pītvā mūrchā saṃjāyate kṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: After drinking the juice of its fruits, fainting arises for a moment.
Then he becomes a <s>siddha</s> and lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
At the southern gate of <s>Śrīśaila</s>, <s>Jāleśvara</s> and <s>Sureśvara</s>,
two renowned deities, are present; there he should dig the ground.
Stones shaped like <s>śrīphala</s> fruits come out, capable of transmutation by touch.
The deity <s>Rāmeśvara</s> is there; in his vicinity
there are stones shaped like <s>rudrākṣa</s> beads, rough to the touch.
At the <s>Jyotiḥsiddhavaṭa</s> tree he stands on one foot.
Nearby to the west is a deity named <s>Āvartadeva</s>.
There is a mountain there, with stones resembling <s>tālaka</s>.

children.text: ādāya tān dhamettīvraṃ divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Having taken them, he should blow them strongly in the fire; divine gold is produced.
There at the southern gate is the deity <s>Kuṇḍaleśvara</s>.
Near him he should dig the ground knee-deep, and then take them out.
The stones are shaped like <s>śrīphala</s> fruits, red, and transmuting by touch.
Near the deity <s>Puruṣeśvara</s> there is a tank.

children.text: guñjā ca riṭhṭhakaś caiva dvau vṛkṣau tatra tiṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>guñjā</s> and a <s>riṭṭhaka</s>, two trees, stand there.

children.text: tayoḥ pattrāṇi saṃbhakṣya tatkṣaṇād amaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having eaten the leaves of the two, he becomes immortal at that very moment.

children.text: tathā hastiśilā tatra tasyā dakṣiṇataḥ khanet
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>Hastiśilā</s> is there; to its south he should dig.
At the measure of a cubit, he will then see a stone shaped like a <s>jambū</s> fruit.
A stone is said to be there, to be carefully obtained by touch.

children.text: nāmnā hastiśiraḥ khyātaṃ saiva hastiśilā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Known by the name <s>Hastiśiraḥ</s>, that very one is <s>Hastiśilā</s>.
In the southern direction from it, at one <s>yojana</s>, there stands
the famous <s>Chāyāchattra</s>, a form of <s>Śiva</s>, taught by <s>Śiva</s>.
That sacred field is circular, measuring one hundred cubits.

children.text: yo 'sau gacchati tasyādho nāsau kenāpi dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Whoever goes beneath it is not seen by anyone.
He becomes a <s>siddha</s> equal to <s>Rudra</s> and sports in the three worlds.
Or else one should accomplish from afar the famous set of eight siddhis.
<s>Kāntābhra</s>, gold, and <s>sūta</s> should be ground in successively increasing proportions.

children.text: tadgolaṃ veṣṭayel lohais tribhir yatnāt krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: He should wrap that ball carefully with three metals in order.

children.text: vastre baddhvā tu tadvastraṃ vaṃśāgre bandhayeddṛḍham
children.translated_text: Having bound it in cloth, he should tie that cloth firmly to the tip of a bamboo.
He should empower it with the <s>Kālī</s> mantra and place it in <s>Chāyāchattra</s>.

children.text: tadvaṃśāgraṃ kṣaṇaikena jāyate guṭikā tu tām
children.translated_text: In a single moment, at the tip of that bamboo, it becomes a <s>guṭikā</s>; that
the <s>sādhaka</s> should hold in his mouth, and it grants sky-going power.
Likewise he should tie <s>tālaka</s> and <s>kunaṭī</s> to a bamboo and place them there.
Whoever has his eyes anointed with those two sees treasure hidden underground.
He should tie a sword to the bamboo and insert it, empowered with the previous mantra.
Holding that sword in his hand, he becomes conqueror of the three worlds.

children.text: vastre gorocanaṃ baddhvā vaṃśasthaṃ tatra veśayet
children.translated_text: Having bound <s>gorocanā</s> in cloth, mounted on a bamboo, he should insert it there.
With that he should make a forehead mark; on being seen, he enchants the world.

children.text: srotoñjanaṃ kajjalaṃ ca kṣiptvā tatraiva pūrvavat
children.translated_text: He should put <s>srotoñjana</s> and lampblack there in the same way as before.

children.text: tena cāñjitanetro yo devairapi na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Whoever has his eyes anointed with that is not seen even by the gods.

children.text: pādukāṃ tena yogena kṣiptvā padbhyāṃ tu dhārayet
children.translated_text: Having put sandals there by that same procedure, he should wear them on his feet.

children.text: yatrecchā tatra tatraiva gantā bhavati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Wherever he wishes, there and there he goes at that very moment.
Likewise the practitioner should throw a red cloth there and wrap it up.

children.text: adṛśyo jāyate samyakpaṭe mukte tu dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: He becomes properly invisible; but when the cloth is released, he is seen.

children.text: kāntābhraṃ kāñcanaṃ sūtaṃ kṛtvā golaṃ tu veśayet
children.translated_text: Having made a ball of <s>kāntābhra</s>, gold, and <s>sūta</s> (mercury), he should insert it.
Placed at the tip of a bamboo and joined with a mantra, it becomes <s>sparśavedhin</s> (transmuting by touch).
At the western gate of <s>Śrīśaila</s> there is <s>Brahmeśvareśvara</s> by name.
They call that liṅga <s>Sparśa</s>, and <s>Durgā</s> there is of the same kind.

children.text: navamaṃ yattu sopānaṃ nadyāṃ tattādṛśaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: The ninth step in the river also stands there with that same nature.
At the gate of the god he should look for one the color of green gram.
Southwest of <s>Brahmeśvara</s> there is a tamarind grove.

children.text: tasmin vane sthitaṃ kuṇḍaṃ tatra tiṣṭhati caṇḍikā ||
children.translated_text: In that grove there is a pool, and <s>Caṇḍikā</s> dwells there.
Standing on one foot beneath the tamarind, he should take a leaf from that tree.

children.text: baddhvā vastre kṣipetkuṇḍe snānaṃ tatra samācaret ||
children.translated_text: Having tied it in a cloth, he should throw it into the pool and perform bathing there.

children.text: snānānte poṭalī grāhyā sarve matsyā bhavanti te
children.translated_text: At the end of the bath the bundle should be taken up; all of them have become fish.
He should cook them with wood from that tree, discarding the throat, tail, and head.
He should dedicate one portion to the deity; the second should belong to a guest.

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ sādhako bhuktvā kṣaṇaṃ bhavati mūrchitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After eating the third, the practitioner becomes faint for a moment.
At that very moment he becomes a siddha and sees the earth with its openings.
He attains ageless immortality and is not harmed even by the thirty gods.
North of <s>Alampura</s> there is a village called <s>Bhīmapāduka</s>.

children.text: tasya grāmasya pārśve tu hastamātraṃ khanedbhuvam ||
children.translated_text: Beside that village he should dig the ground to the depth of a hand.

children.text: pāṣāṇāḥ sarpavadvakrā grāhyāḥ sparśā bhavanti te
children.translated_text: Stones curved like snakes should be taken; they become touch-stones.

children.text: yogeśvarīti vikhyātā devatā yā tv alampure ||
children.translated_text: The deity in <s>Alampura</s> is famed as <s>Yogeśvarī</s>.

children.text: devyā hy agre guhā ramyā tanmadhye nikhanedbhuvam
children.translated_text: In front of the goddess there is a lovely cave; in its middle he should dig the ground.
Stones resembling frogs should be taken together with cat dung.
After mixing them and putting them into tin, that tin turns into silver.
The wise man should eat those stones together with honey and ghee.
At the northern gate of <s>Śrīśaila</s> there is a deity named <s>Maheśa</s>.
There stands the <s>Bhramarāmra</s> mango tree; its ripe fruits indeed
should be split open there, and living bees come out.
Having recognized this proof, he should discard those bees.
He should cook the fruits with milk and drink the milk as much as he likes.
A slight fainting occurs from it; then, when consciousness returns, he should drink again.
Doing this for three weeks, a man becomes diamond-bodied.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives as long as the moon and stars.
A man becomes a knower of all literature and swift as the wind.
With that single mango fruit itself, after the bee has been removed,
he surely fixes a thousand <s>palas</s> of molten tin.
By casting it in, he obtains silver; this is true, spoken by Īśvara.

children.text: tatphalaṃ chidritaṃ kṛtvā utpātya bhramaraṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having pierced that fruit and then drawn out the bee,
he should put into it one <s>karṣa</s> of purified mercury and an equal amount of black mica.
After sealing its mouth, he should smear it with clay and cow dung.
When it has dried in the shade, he should cook it for a <s>yāma</s> with decoctions made from that mango.
When naturally cool, the pill in the middle of the fruit should be taken.
Held in the mouth, the powerful one grants sky-going and invisibility.
With the decoction he becomes equal to the lord of speech and lives as long as the moon and stars.

children.text: tāraṃ tāmraṃ bhujaṃgaṃ vā koṭibhāgena vedhayet
children.translated_text: It transmutes silver, copper, or <s>bhujaṅga</s> by a ten-millionth part.
Black mica and purified <s>sūta</s> should be put in that fruit as before.
He should smear it with clay and cow dung as before and heat it with wild dung-cakes.
When naturally cool, that <s>rasa</s> should be taken with honey and ghee.
He should always eat a <s>guñjā</s>-measure; in a month a man becomes young.
The hero lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, endowed with the strength of nine nāgas.
He is known and famed in the world, worthy of worship with the five offerings.
By practitioners free from wavering, with the mantra <s>oṃ huṃ phaṭkāra</s>.

children.text: vīkṣya paścimadigbhāge hy antarikṣe ca tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Looking toward the western quarter and into the sky at that very moment,
he sees divine aerial vehicles, and great conviction arises.
Then the wise man should go toward the western quarter and cross a river.
A cavern is seen there; he should enter it facing west.
He should go three <s>yojanas</s>, alone and without wavering.
A plantain grove five <s>yojanas</s> wide is seen.
In its middle there is a very broad lake filled with water.
And in its middle is a throne resembling pure crystal.
Seeing it, he should fall on the ground like a staff and recite the mantra.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ vidyāvāgīśvarādhipataye hrīṃ oṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ hrīṃ vidyāvāgīśvarādhipataye hrīṃ oṃ svāhā</s>.
Having bathed carefully, he should then recite it one hundred thousand times.
He should eat whatever food he desires, such as bulbs, roots, and fruits.
Then, above the throne, resembling pure crystal,
<s>Parameśvara</s> is seen, four-armed and three-eyed.
With hymns, mantras, and salutations, he should bow down again and again.

children.text: varaṃ datte yatheṣṭaṃ vai sādhakasya na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He grants whatever boon the practitioner desires; there is no doubt.

children.text: śatamāyatanaṃ tatra kūpānāṃ ca śataṃ nava
children.translated_text: There are one hundred shrines there, and nine hundred wells.
There are gardens in the same number, and forests named <s>Nandana</s>.
Likewise nine hundred tanks are found in the plantain grove.
There are just as many cave-doors and wish-granting trees.

children.text: tatraiva maukalī nāma yakṣiṇī prakaṭā sthitā
children.translated_text: There itself a yakṣiṇī named <s>Maukalī</s> stands manifest.

children.text: sā vakti bhojanaṃ dehi yadīcchasi samīhitam ||
children.translated_text: She says, "Give food, if you desire what you seek."
Then he should say to her, "I shall give it, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>."

children.text: kṣīrānnaṃ vā phalāhāraṃ tadagre dāpayet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should have milk-rice or a meal of fruits offered before her.

children.text: sā vakti mama putro'yaṃ kṣaṇaṃ vakṣasi dhāraya
children.translated_text: She says, "This is my son; hold him for a moment against your breast.

children.text: yadā na muñcase bhūmau tadā siddhyaṣṭakaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: When you do not let him fall to the ground, then the set of eight <s>siddhi</s>s is yours.
I shall give it; there is no doubt of this, either after the meal or again.
If he is dropped, I bring about destruction; therefore protect him carefully."
Acting in just this way, the heroic <s>sādhaka</s> should obtain the <s>siddhi</s>.
He should go to the northern side of that lake, half a <s>yojana</s> away.
There is a divine <s>Nandana</s> grove there, filled with flowers.
By merely smelling the flowers, hunger and thirst do not exist.
Or else he should eat one fruit from it, as he wishes.
By merely eating it, a man becomes diamond-bodied.
He should go to the southern side of the lake, a quarter <s>yojana</s> away.
There is seen a <s>Nandana</s> grove filled with pomegranates.
When the perfected one eats its fruit, he lives for a thousand ages.
On the eastern side of that lake he should go only half a <s>krośa</s>.

children.text: tatra dhātrīphalaiḥ pūrṇaṃ śyāmalaṃ nandanaṃ vanam
children.translated_text: There is a dark <s>Nandana</s> grove filled with fruits of the āmalakī tree.
If he eats those fruits, he lives for three hundred aeons.
On the western side of that lake he should go one <s>yojana</s>.

children.text: tatra bilvaphalaiḥ pūrṇaṃ dṛśyate nandanaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: There is seen a <s>Nandana</s> grove filled with bilva fruits.
The hero should eat its fruit, and he lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
In that lovely <s>Nandana</s> grove there is a blue-colored <s>liṅga</s>.
He should enter by the northern gate. There a serpent of great strength
is seen, fierce, seven-hooded in form, and exceedingly terrifying.
He should make obeisance to it, utter "hruṃ hruṃ," and raise it up.
Then it speaks this utterance: "I grant you invisibility.
Go to the western gate; there is a divine maiden there."
The great heroic <s>sādhaka</s> should go there while uttering the <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: hāraṃ dāsyati sā tuṣṭā na praveśaṃ prayacchati
children.translated_text: Pleased, she will give a necklace, but she will not grant entrance.
He should wear that necklace on his throat; he becomes <s>Vāgīśvara</s> in person.
Then he should go to the southern gate; there is a terrifying one there,
with loosened hair, crooked eyes, a mace in hand, and naked.
Seeing the blue-colored <s>kṣetrapāla</s>, he should utter the <s>mantra</s>:

children.text: ha hā he he haṃ hruṃkāraṃ phaṭ huṃ svāhāntameva ca ||
children.translated_text: "ha hā he he haṃ," the syllable "hruṃ," and then ending with "phaṭ huṃ svāhā."
By this recitation of the <s>mantra</s>, the <s>kṣetrapāla</s> is pleased.

children.text: dadāti khecarīṃ siddhiṃ na praveśaṃ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: He gives the <s>khecarī</s> <s>siddhi</s>, but never entrance.
Then on the eastern side is the gate; there is <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>.
The <s>sādhaka</s> should worship him, and then he should enter.

children.text: dṛśyate divyacāpaṃ tu tathā liṅgaṃ manoharam
children.translated_text: A divine bow is seen, and also a lovely <s>liṅga</s>.
He should worship with the <s>Śiva</s> <s>mantra</s>, only with the syllable ra and not otherwise.
Then there he should perform recitation, fasting for a day and night.

children.text: pratyakṣo jāyate rudro varaṃ datte yathepsitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> becomes manifest and gives the boon exactly as desired.
Such and similar <s>siddhi</s>s exist in the <s>Kadalīvana</s>.
At the gate it is written in letters: there is the cave of <s>Padmāvatī</s>.
It stands one <s>yojana</s> to the east of the lake.
After performing vomiting and purging, the <s>sādhaka</s> should enter there.
He should go there as far as a hundred bow-lengths; there is a <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drum.
Seeing it, the hero should beat it properly; then <s>Padmāvatī</s>,
having come, gives nectar, by drinking which one becomes immortal.
Then she entreats him: "Come to my dwelling.
Accept five hundred divine maidens along with their retinue.

children.text: ahaṃ patnī bhaviṣyāmi yāvadbrahmā ca jīvati ||
children.translated_text: I shall be your wife as long as <s>Brahmā</s> lives.

children.text: tadante paramaṃ sthānaṃ gacchāmo nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: At the end of that, we shall go to the supreme place; there is no doubt."
The deity <s>Kadambeśvara</s> is found in the southeastern direction.
Before his eastern tank there stands a kadamba tree.
Having gathered its leaves, he should smear them with pungent oil.
Or, with oil from that tree's seeds, the wise man should cook them with its wood.

children.text: matsyā bhavanti te sarve tāmrapātre vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: They all become fish; he should place them in a copper vessel.
Avoiding the throat, tail, and head, he should eat them with honey and ghee.
At that very moment he becomes a <s>siddha</s>, equal to <s>Rudra</s> and very strong.

children.text: nadīsthāne ca yo vṛkṣo vidyate kuṇḍaleśvare
children.translated_text: And the tree that exists at the river-place at <s>Kuṇḍaleśvara</s>:
by the same procedure as before, <s>siddhi</s> comes about; there is no doubt.
North of the deity <s>Kapoteśvara</s> lies <s>Puṣpagiri</s>.

children.text: tasya kuryāt prayatnena trivāraṃ tu pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: He should carefully circumambulate it three times.
Then, having climbed upon its summit, a man obtains the state of sky-going.
On its northeastern side is the entrance called <s>Chelikā</s>.
There, facing north, he should enter for three bow-lengths.
Mouse-shaped stones stand there; he should collect them.
Having ground one of them with buttermilk, he should drink it and will faint.
In a moment he rises as a <s>siddha</s> and lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
That same thing becomes an agent of touch-transmutation for all metals.
Having fasted for a day and night, he obtains <s>siddhi</s> before the deity.
To the south of the deity <s>Kapoteśvara</s> there are two deities.
Between them he should dig waist-deep; there are stones resembling <s>gorocanā</s>.
Having taken those stones, he should grind them with honey and ghee.
By drinking that, a mortal becomes one whose lifespan is an aeon; there is no doubt.
To the northwest of the deity <s>Kapoteśvara</s>, he should dig to the measure of a cubit.
Stones resembling pigeons, capable of transmutation by touch,
remain there; after worship of the deity has been performed, he should take one.
To the northeast of the deity <s>Mallikārjuna</s> there is <s>Bhṛgupātana</s>.
Near it is a tank; from that he should take earth.
He should mix it with the five products of the cow and blow it with khadira charcoal.
The metal becomes like a blue lotus; then he should quench it,
well heated with honey and ghee, seven times again and again.
Holding that ball in his mouth, a man becomes equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the eastern region from <s>Bhṛgupātana</s>, in the place more than a krośa away,
before it there is a mountain famous by the name <s>Acchataila</s>.
To its west is the entrance of a cave; within it, after going five bow-lengths,

children.text: gate tu dṛśyate kuṇḍaṃ raso lākṣārasaprabhaḥ
children.translated_text: a tank is seen, and the rasa is like lac resin in color.
Having collected it in a gourd vessel, it becomes capable of transmuting ten million times.
East of the deity <s>Mallikārjuna</s>, well known in the world,
there is the rampart of <s>Candragupta</s>; a temple stands there.
To its east is a caitya, and east of the caitya is a great rock.

children.text: mudgavarṇā ca sā khyātā sparśavedhakarā tu sā ||
children.translated_text: It is known as being mung-bean colored, and it is capable of transmutation by touch.
An elephant is famous there itself; having mounted it with concentration,

children.text: tasya pṛṣṭhāttṛṇaṃ grāhyaṃ tatsarvaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: grass should be taken from its back; all of that becomes gold.
On the northern side of the elephant he should dig the ground knee-deep.
There are stones shaped like jambū fruits, capable of transmutation by touch.
Or else he should dig beneath the elephant; when he has gone knee-deep, he then obtains
a perfected triangular pellet, supreme, capable of transmuting a hundred thousand times.

children.text: śrīśailasya tu vāyavye tīrthaṃ devahradaḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: To the northwest of <s>Śrīśaila</s> is a tīrtha called <s>Devahrada</s>.
In the tank there are mung-bean-colored stones, capable of transmutation by touch.
There is a tortoise-like liṅga there, supreme in producing transmutation by touch.
On the full-moon day of <s>Kṛttikā</s>, after performing worship, he should collect it.
Two gavyūtis from that is remembered a place named <s>Nīlavana</s>.

children.text: tatra liṅgaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ jalaṃ caiva tu tādṛśam ||
children.translated_text: There the liṅga is blue in color, and the water too is just the same.
There are stones resembling dark horse-mica and crows, capable of transmutation by touch.
They are inside the temple; he should dig to the knee and take them out.

children.text: śrīśailasya tu nairṛtye nāmnā guṇḍiprabhā sthitā
children.translated_text: To the southwest of <s>Śrīśaila</s> there is a place named <s>Guṇḍiprabhā</s>.
From in front of it yellow earth from a pit should be taken and burned in puṭa fires.
From that gold comes forth, of gleaming form; there is no doubt.
There too there are bhramaras, bestowing results as before.

children.text: tathā tambīpure nāmni tīrthe ca vipule śubham
children.translated_text: Likewise, at the auspicious and extensive tīrtha named <s>Tambīpura</s>,
the ever-fruitful substance is famous; the wise man should accomplish it as before.
Southwest of <s>Śrīśaila</s> is one named <s>Mahānandeśvara</s>.
On its northeastern side, one should go by the royal road.
There is a deity named <s>Kālavarṇeśvara</s>, and a small tank before him.
In its middle there is rasa resembling an indragopa insect.
The seven metals, when heated, become gold by sprinkling with that.
To the northeast of <s>Śrīśaila</s> there is the deity <s>Turaleśvara</s>.
To his north is the excellent and very famous <s>Umāparvata</s>.
On its summit stand beautiful darbha grasses shaped like tridents.

children.text: tasyādhaḥ kaṭimātraṃ tu khātvā nīlāṃ mṛdaṃ haret
children.translated_text: Beneath that, after digging waist-deep, he should take blue earth.
He should cook it with wood from akṣa trees and set aside a share for the deity.
Likewise he should assign one share for the guest and one share for the fire.
He should eat one share himself; a man lives for ten thousand kalpas.
There, near <s>Ileśvara</s>, <s>Koṭīśvara</s> is renowned.
Before it, even a flower-sized portion becomes capable of transmutation by touch.
<s>Acaleśa</s> too is there, supreme in producing transmutation by touch.
It is found one yojana to the south of <s>Ileśa</s>.
There is one called the deity <s>Amareśvara</s>; there is an auspicious gold-stone there.

children.text: tasya pṛṣṭhe ca gomāṃsaṃ mahāmāṃsaṃ ca vā kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: On its back he should throw cow flesh, or else mahāmāṃsa.

children.text: prajvālya badarīkāṣṭhaiḥ prātaḥ svarṇopamā tu sā
children.translated_text: Having kindled it with badarī wood, in the morning it is seen as gold-like.
A piece of cloth impregnated with the menstrual blood of women
should be rubbed on that stone and kept in a gourd vessel.
By mere contact with that, iron becomes hāṭaka gold.
At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, here and there, stones stand in the form of lumps of earth.
One should continually eat one karṣa of their powder together with half as much triphalā.
For half a month it destroys old age; one lives as long as the moon and stars.
Southwest of the king of mountains is <s>Paṭāhakarṇa Īśvara</s>.
In the northeastern direction from him, at twenty-five bow-lengths,
there is a raised stone two cubits high; there he should dig two cubits.
He should take thirty stones resembling śrāva-cases.
After making them fire-colored, he should sprinkle them with juices from kūṣmāṇḍa gourds.
From their midst he should take butter, with one share for the deity,
one share for the guest, and one share the wise man should eat.
Fainting occurs for a day and night; when he awakens, the man becomes
a hero who lives for ten thousand years, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
The second step of that deity is capable of transmutation by touch.

children.text: tasya devasya pārśve tu pāṣāṇāḥ śvetapītakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the side of that deity are stones, white and yellow.
All are touch-transmuting; there is no doubt. He should take just one.

children.text: tasya devasya pūrve tu kūpaḥ syānnātidūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: To the east of that deity is a well, not very far away.
Among them are stones resembling frogs, capable of transmutation by touch.
To the north of that deity is the famous <s>Liṅgaparvata</s>.
On its northern side there is a river flowing eastward.
On the western side of the river is a <s>liṅga</s> tawny in color.
There a tank, filled with mountain water, brings about transmutation in an instant.
On the southern side of <s>Maheśa</s>, two <s>yojanas</s> away, is <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
She is famous as <s>Piṇḍādevī</s>; from her northwestern corner
there stands a well, and within it are stones the color of green gram.
Likewise there are some resembling <s>pathyā</s> fruits; all of them are capable of transmutation by touch.
Here, through the touching of all these, the procedure for transmutation is prescribed.
If the substance is coarse, one should grind it fine, and with it make a crucible.
The eight metals should be melted together in it.
All of that becomes gold; thus one should act as desired.
If it is fine, one should put it wherever the eight metals are molten.

children.text: taṃ sarvaṃ nikṣipenmadhye sarvaṃ tatkāñcanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: He should cast all of it into the middle; all of that becomes gold.
Northwest of <s>Mallikārjuna</s> is the sacred ford <s>Sarveśvara</s>.
On its southern side, along the water route, after going half a <s>yojana</s>,

children.text: gate ḍāṅgarikaṃ tatra dṛśyate tasya mūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ḍāṅgarika</s> is seen there; upon its summit
there are black <s>dhātrī</s> fruits, and one should eat them.
For seven days, as much as he wishes, and a man becomes diamond-bodied.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives for three hundred <s>kalpas</s>.
From there, on the southern side, is <s>Kākalerīmahānava</s>.
There stands a plantain-pillar; the <s>sādhaka</s> should enter there.
He should go only half a <s>krośa</s>, and a tank of <s>rasa</s> is seen.
Taking it in a bottle-gourd vessel, the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of transmuting ten million times its quantity.
In that forest there is a peacock made of blue-colored stone.
At the tip of its beak is a tank, blue and twelve finger-breadths across.

children.text: tanmadhye śuṣkavaṃśaṃ tu kṣiptvā syānnūtanaḥ kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: If dry bamboo is thrown into it, it becomes fresh in an instant.

children.text: dine pattraṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ jāyate tasya nānyathā
children.translated_text: In a day leaf, fruit, and flower arise on it; it is not otherwise.
There one should put in one <s>prastha</s> of mercury and draw off the same amount of water.
He should drink that, honey-like; at that very moment he becomes unconscious.
After a <s>muhūrta</s> he obtains a kingdom and lives for a thousand <s>yugas</s>.
On the southeastern side of the mountain is <s>Guṭikāsiddhakeśvara</s>.
In front of him one should dig the ground to five cubits.
There are stones shaped like jujube fruits, granting the power of moving through the sky.
Having brought just one, those who travel through the sky should hold it in the mouth.
At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, the procedure for all the yogic practices that have been taught is now stated.
Having first performed the mantra-nyāsa, afterward he should repeat the <s>Aghora</s> mantra one hundred thousand times.
By that he quickly obtains each particular <s>siddhi</s>.
He should invoke the deity of the sacred field.

children.text: tatra svapne devatā pratyakṣībhūya varaṃ dadāti
children.translated_text: There, in a dream, the deity becomes manifest and grants a boon.

children.text: evaṃ mantraparaiḥ suniścalatarair bhaktaiśca tatsādhakaiḥ śambhoḥ pūjanatatparaiḥ pratidinaṃ pūjāvidheḥ pālakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the practice of <s>Śrīgiri</s> should be performed by those devoted to mantra, very steady, by devotees and practitioners of <s>Śambhu</s>, intent on worship and observing the rule of daily worship,

children.text: kāryaṃ śrīgirisādhanaṃ japaparair āmnāyapāraṃgatair no cetkleśakaraṃ parākṛtamaho vyarthaṃ bhavenniścitam ||
children.translated_text: by those devoted to recitation and versed in the tradition; otherwise, alas, when set aside, it will certainly become troublesome and fruitless.

children.text: yena sṛṣṭaṃ vidā cidātmasvamaruttejojalorvīgaṇāḥ satsaṃvicchivaśaktibhairavakalāḥ śrīkaṇṭhapañcānanaḥ
children.translated_text: He by whom were created, through knowledge, the groups of the conscious self, ether, wind, fire, water, and earth, and the powers of true consciousness, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> and <s>Pañcānana</s>,

children.text: īśo rudramurāridhātṛvibudhāś candrārkatārāgaṇāḥ so 'yaṃ pātu carācaraṃ jagadidaṃ nirnāmanāmādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Murāri</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the gods, and the hosts of moon, sun, and stars: may this lord beyond name and names protect this whole moving and unmoving world.

children.text: sūte sūtavaro varaṃ ca kanakaṃ śabdātparaṃ sparśanāddhūmādvidhyati tatkṣaṇād aghaharaṃ saṃkhyāṃ sakharvāṃśataḥ
children.translated_text: The excellent <s>sūta</s> produces excellent gold; beyond sound, by touch and by smoke, it pierces instantly, removing sin, in numbers of hundreds of <s>kharvas</s>.

children.text: saṃkhyām arbudakoṭilakṣamayutaṃ yuktyā sahasraṃ śataṃ datte khegatimakṣayaṃ śivapadaṃ tasmai parasmai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It grants, by method, numbers amounting to <s>arbuda</s>, <s>koṭi</s>, <s>lakṣa</s>, <s>ayuta</s>, thousands and hundreds, as well as imperishable sky-going power and the state of <s>Śiva</s>; homage to that supreme one.
Having bowed to the goddess <s>Śrī Pārvatī</s>, to <s>Bhairava</s>, and to the lineage of <s>siddhas</s>,
I shall teach the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>, auspicious for the body and for metals.
<s>Śivabīja</s>, king <s>sūta</s>, <s>pārada</s>, and <s>rasendra</s>:
these are names of <s>rasa</s>, and there are others as well, O <s>Śivā</s>.
It grants the state of <s>Śiva</s> and the highest <s>siddhi</s> to practitioners.
Therefore it is called <s>Śivabīja</s>, the giver of all <s>siddhis</s>.
Because <s>sūta</s> arose from supreme <s>Śiva</s>, for that reason it is called <s>sūta</s>.

children.text: saṃsārasya paraṃ pāraṃ datte'sau pāradaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it carries one to the far shore of worldly existence, it is remembered as <s>pārada</s>.
Metals, and even bodies, become assimilated to <s>rasa</s> through proper use.

children.text: rasendras tena vikhyāto dravatvācca rasaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason it is famous as <s>rasendra</s>, and because of its fluidity it is remembered as <s>rasa</s>.
In all the treatises on <s>rasa</s>, this <s>rasa</s> was formerly indicated by <s>Śambhu</s>.
It is the divine <s>rasāyana</s>; it is not understood merely from an indication.

children.text: siddhaiḥ śivamukhāt prāptaṃ teṣāṃ siddhistu sādhanāt
children.translated_text: It was received by the <s>siddhas</s> from the mouth of <s>Śiva</s>, and their attainment came through practice.
The sequence of the lineage and the method were concealed by them in their own treatises.
I too received it from their mouth and then practiced it in many ways.
Having examined all the treatises on <s>rasa</s> in due order,
it is now being made manifest for the benefit of practitioners.

children.text: na krameṇa vinā śāstraṃ na śāstreṇa vinā kramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no treatise without procedure, and no procedure without a treatise.

children.text: śāstraṃ kramayutaṃ jñātvā yaḥ karoti sa siddhibhāk
children.translated_text: The one who knows the treatise together with its procedure and acts accordingly shares in success.
The teacher should be knowledgeable, skillful, and expert in <s>rasaśāstra</s>,
accomplished in mantra, a great hero, steady, and dear to <s>Śiva</s>.
He should be a devotee of the Goddess, always steadfast, intent on approaching and worshipping the deity.
He should know the special doctrines of all the <s>āmnāyas</s> and be skilled in alchemical operations.
Endowed with such characteristics, he should be a guru of <s>rasavidyā</s>.
Disciples should be devoted to the guru, of good conduct, truthful, and firm in their vows.
They should be free from laziness, know their own <s>dharma</s>, and always obey commands.
They should be free from hypocrisy and envy and initiated in the practices of the <s>kula</s>.
They should be highly devoted practitioners, peaceful, and intent on mantra worship.
Endowed with these characteristics, disciples are fit for the attainment of rasa-siddhi.
All the assistants should be energetic; disciples should be even more so.
Those of good lineage and devoted to their master should be appointed in alchemical work.
But those who are unbelievers, of bad conduct, deceivers, or violators of the guru's bed,
who wish to obtain the science by theft, force, or deceit,
for them nothing succeeds, whether jewel, mantra, medicine, or the like.

children.text: kurvanti yadi mohena nāśayanti svakaṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: If they act out of delusion, they destroy their own wealth.

children.text: iha loke sukhaṃ nāsti paraloke tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: There is no happiness for them in this world, and likewise none in the next.
Therefore, only through the power of devotion does the guru become pleased.
In that way the disciple should receive that <s>rasavidyā</s> for the perfection of the self.
Having obtained the boon through the joining of hand and head, he should practice it well.
In a land free from disease, in a delightful kingdom governed by <s>dharma</s>,
in an auspicious, prosperous city endowed with <s>Umā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
there the wise man should perform the practice of <s>Rasarāja</s>.
In a very delightful grove, adorned with four gates,
a spacious and pleasing hall should be built there.
It should be furnished with proper windows and decorated with splendid paintings.
Near it, on level and elongated ground, a rasa pavilion should be made.
It should be very secluded, spacious, and adorned with door panels and bolts.
It should be rich with banners, parasols, and canopies, and hung with flower garlands.
It should resound with drums, kāhala horns, bells, and other horn sounds.

children.text: bhūḥ samā tatra kartavyā sudṛḍhā darpaṇopamā ||
children.translated_text: The ground there should be made level, very firm, and like a mirror.
In its middle a beautiful altar, furnished with the proper marks, should be made.
There should be a gold leaf of three <s>niṣkas</s> and <s>rasendra</s> of nine <s>niṣkas</s>.

children.text: amlena mardayedyāmaṃ tena liṅgaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: He should grind it with acid for a <s>yāma</s>, and from it he should make a <s>liṅga</s>.
He should cook it for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, in a tube, placed in citron juice.
There he should worship that <s>liṅga</s> with very auspicious offerings.
Whatever fruit comes from the proper worship of a thousand crores of <s>liṅgas</s>,
that fruit, multiplied ten million times, comes from worshipping the rasa-<s>liṅga</s>.
Thousands of <s>brahmahatyā</s> sins and even tens of thousands of cow-killings
vanish at that very moment from the sight of the rasa-<s>liṅga</s>.
By touching it, liberation is obtained; this is true, spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.
He should worship it with the mantra-king joined with <s>Vāṅmāyā</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, and the revered <s>Aghora</s>.
He should visualize the rasa-<s>liṅga</s> as auspicious, white, eighteen-armed, five-faced, and three-eyed,
mounted on a corpse and blue-throated.
On its lap he should visualize the great Goddess, one-faced and four-armed.
On the right she holds a rosary and goad; on the left, a noose and the auspicious gesture of fearlessness.
He should visualize her as having the luster of heated gold and wearing yellow garments.
<s>Vāṅmāyā</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, the <s>Kāmarāja</s> śakti, the seed, and <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s>,
together with <s>yai namaḥ</s>: these twelve make up the <s>Kāmavidyā</s> called <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s>.
With this he should worship the Goddess with scents, flowers, unbroken grains, and the like.
He should worship <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgin</s>, and <s>Mahākāla</s> in order, beginning from the eastern direction.
He should worship them with name-mantras beginning with the <s>praṇava</s> and ending with <s>namaḥ</s>.
In this way daily worship should be performed there for rasa-siddhi.
The rasa-initiation taught by <s>Śiva</s> should indeed be given to the practitioner
by the guru, with a joyful mind, according to the prescribed procedure.
At a good moment and under a good constellation, when the moon and stars are strong,
he should set up a pot filled with water and furnished with gold, jewels, and fruits.
It should be placed before the rasa-<s>liṅga</s>, wrapped in divine cloth.
He should worship it with scents, flowers, unbroken grains, incense, lamps, and food offering.
At the end of the worship he should perform a fire offering in a well-marked <s>yoni</s>-fire pit.
With sesame, ghee, milk-rice, and flowers he should offer one hundred and eight oblations of each.
With <s>Aghora</s> and <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>, at the end of the oblation he should bring in the disciple.
The disciple should be joined with the <s>Kākinī</s> śakti and devoted to rasa-siddhi.

children.text: yasyāḥ saṃkucitāḥ keśāḥ śyāmā yā padmalocanā
children.translated_text: She whose hair is curled, who is dark and lotus-eyed,
beautiful, young, variegated, with broad hips and auspicious,
with close-set teeth, bent by the weight of full breasts,
soft in kissing, embracing, and touching, and gentle in speech,
adorned with a genital region like an aśvattha leaf,

children.text: kṛṣṇapakṣe puṣpavatī sā nārī kākinī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: and menstruating in the dark fortnight, that woman is known as a <s>Kākinī</s>.
For binding <s>rasa</s> and for practical operation, she is the best in rasa practice.

children.text: tadabhāve surūpā tu yā kācit taruṇāṅganā ||
children.translated_text: If she is absent, then any beautiful young woman
should be given sulfur mixed with ghee for three weeks.
One <s>karṣa</s> each morning should be given; she then becomes equal to a <s>Kākinī</s>.
The best guru, joined with such a śakti, should initiate him.
After he has bathed well, the guru should consecrate him with pure waters from the pots.
The true guru should give the <s>Aghorāṅkuśī</s> vidyā to the disciple.
Then the disciple should give guru-dakṣiṇā according to his ability.
Thereafter, with the guru's permission, he should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times for each part.
He should offer one tenth of that in a triangular fire pit measuring one hand.
It should be a lotus and a square, well adorned with four gates.
At the completion he should perform maiden worship with jasmine flowers smeared with the three sweet substances.
Having done this, he should then enter an auspicious hall, plastered and provided with a good altar.
