There, with vermilion, he should draw a six-cornered maṇḍala two cubits across,
properly on the altar, and outside it an eight-petalled form.
There should be a lotus and a square, adorned with four doors.
In the pericarp he should place an iron mortar marked with lines of gold.
In its center he should place the king of <s>rasa</s>, in the measure of one hundred <s>palas</s>,
or fifty or twenty-five, and worship it like a <s>rasa-liṅga</s>.
Diamond, <s>vaikrānta</s>, diamond-mica, magnet-stone, and borax,
and <s>bhūnāga</s>: these powers should be worshipped in the six petals.
Sulfur, orpiment, green vitriol, realgar, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, and <s>bhūkhaga</s>,

children.text: rājāvarto gairikaṃ ca khyātā uparasā amī ||
children.translated_text: with lapis-like <s>rājāvarta</s> and red ochre: these are known as the secondary minerals.
These should be worshipped on the eight petals, going in order from the east to the northeast.
<s>Rasaka</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>capalā</s>, blue vitriol, and collyrium,

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ sasyakaṃ caiva khyātā ete mahārasāḥ
children.translated_text: cinnabar and <s>sasyaka</s>: these are known as the great minerals.
He should worship them on the tips of the petals, from the east through the northeast.
At the eastern door he should worship gold and silver; at the southern, copper and lead;
at the western, tin and magnet; and at the northern, sharp iron and wrought iron.
He should worship all this with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, accompanied by the goad.
Fluxes, sour gruel, apparatuses, alkalis, clays, and salts,
the furnace, crucible, bent tube, husks, charcoal, and forest cow-dung fuel,
the bellows, the tongs, a single stone, the mortar, and also the pestle,
the goldsmith's equipment and all the balances,
and various vessels made of clay, wood, copper, iron, and the like,
divine herbs and substance groups, coloring agents, and oils or unguents:
these he should worship outside the doors with the root mantra.

children.text: vāṅmāyāṃ heṃ tataḥ kṣmeṃ ca kṣmaśca pañcākṣaro manuḥ
children.translated_text: "Vāṅ," "māyāṃ," "heṃ," then "kṣmeṃ" and "kṣmaḥ": this is the five-syllabled mantra.
With this root mantra he should worship <s>Bhairava</s> there.
At that time he should recite the names of all the <s>rasa-siddhas</s>:
<s>Vyālācārya</s>, <s>Candrasena</s>, <s>Subuddhi</s>, and <s>Naravāhana</s>;
<s>Nāgārjuna</s>, <s>Ratnaghoṣa</s>, <s>Surānanda</s>, and <s>Yaśodhara</s>;
also <s>Indradyumna</s>, <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, <s>Carpaṭi</s>, and <s>Śūrasenaka</s>;
<s>Vāḍaba</s>, <s>Nāgabuddhi</s>, <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, <s>Kāpālika</s>, and <s>Hara</s>;
<s>Kāmalī</s>, <s>Tāttvika</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Loka</s>, <s>Lampaṭa</s>, and <s>Śārada</s>;
<s>Bāṇāsura</s>, the best of sages, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and <s>Bali</s>.

children.text: ete sarve tu bhūpendrā rasasiddhā mahābalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All these, O king, are mighty <s>rasa-siddhas</s>.
They move through all the worlds, forever free from old age and death.
Twenty-seven in number, they bestow success in <s>rasa</s>.
They should be carefully honored and worshipped; after that one should perform <s>rasāyana</s>.
He should gladden the brahmins and gods, and satisfy his chosen deity.
Maidens, <s>yoginīs</s>, yogins, sages, <s>māyikas</s>, and practitioners
he should satisfy and worship with devotion, according to his own capacity.
Thus he should perform the festival of <s>rasa</s>, furnished with all materials,
for the pacification of every obstacle and as a giver of all desired fruits.
But if a deluded person, without the sequence of mantra initiation,
wishes to carry out the practice of <s>sūta</s> without a guru,
he does not attain success, even with hundreds of crores of efforts.
Therefore, with every effort, he should have the rite performed as taught in the śāstra.

children.text: samyaksādhanasodyamā guruyutā rājājñayālaṃkṛtā nānākarmaṇi kovidā rasaparāstvāḍhyā janaiścārthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are properly engaged in practice, joined with a guru, honored by royal command, skilled in many operations, devoted to <s>rasa</s>, prosperous, and sought by people,

children.text: mātrāyantrasupākakarmakuśalāḥ sarvauṣadhīkovidāsteṣāṃ sidhyati nānyathā vidhibalāt śrī pāradaḥ pāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: skillful in measures, apparatuses, and well-cooked operations, and knowledgeable about all herbs: for them, by the force of rule, blessed mercury succeeds, not otherwise.

children.text: bhaktyā śāstravicāraṇādanudinaṃ pūjāvidheḥ pālanāt svātmānandanimajjanāt parahitāt kāryakriyāgopanāt
children.translated_text: Through devotion, daily reflection on the śāstra, observance of the worship procedure, immersion in the bliss of one's own self, helping others, and concealment of the operative rites,

children.text: nityaṃ sadgurusevanād anubhavāt sūtasya sadbhāvanād dāsyante nijaraśmayo varabalāt satsampradāyātsphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: through constant service to the true guru, experience, and right regard for <s>sūta</s>, its own rays will clearly be granted by the power of blessing and true lineage.
From <s>rasa</s> down to metals, various groups are declared useful in purification and incineration,
and sometimes also in impregnation treatments.

children.text: aṅge nokte bhavenmūlaṃ dravaḥ sarvāṅgato bhavet
children.translated_text: When a subsidiary part is not stated, the basic substance should be assumed; the liquid should apply to every part.
When no measure is specified, an equal measure should be understood in <s>rasa</s> work.
Sesame, <s>apāmārga</s>, plantain, <s>citraka</s>, fresh ginger, and radish,
<s>śigru</s>, <s>mokṣa</s>, and <s>palāśa</s>: all of these should be burned in a covered heating-pit.
After stirring them with water and binding them in cloth, the lower water should be collected.
He should purify that water and cook it over fire in an earthen vessel.
The alkali residue should be collected; this is remembered as plant alkali.
Lime, <s>kūrpa</s>, conch shell, oyster shell, and cowries make up the white group.
The dung of pigeons, <s>cāṣas</s>, vultures, peacocks, and cocks is another group.
<s>Cāṅgerī</s>, sour chick-pea gruel, citron, and sour <s>vetasa</s>,
tamarind, orange, and citron are remembered as the acid group.

children.text: sāmudraṃ saindhavaṃ kācaṃ cullikā ca suvarcalam ||
children.translated_text: Sea salt, rock salt, <s>kāca</s>, <s>cullikā</s>, and <s>suvarcala</s>,
with <s>cūlikā</s> as sal ammoniac: this is the fivefold group of salts.
<s>Sajjīkṣāra</s>, <s>yavakṣāra</s>, and borax as the third:
this is known as the triad of alkalis. Of goats, horses, buffaloes, and cows,
of women, sheep, donkeys, camels, and elephants, there is the urine group.
Honey, ghee, borax, <s>guñjā</s>, and jaggery are the five allies.
The bile of humans, horses, peacocks, cows, and fish belongs to the bile group.
The fat of fish, snakes, humans, sheep, and peacocks is considered fat.
Madder, saffron, lac, pomegranate, and red sandalwood

children.text: bandhūkaṃ karavīraṃ ca raktavargo hyayaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: <s>Bandhūka</s> and <s>karavīra</s>: this is the red group.
<s>Kusumbha</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, <s>rātri</s>, <s>pataṅga</s>, and <s>madayantikā</s>.
This is known as the yellow group; listen to the class of divine herbs.
<s>Ajakarṇī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>rudantī</s>, and <s>kākatuṇḍikā</s>;
<s>Haṃsapādī</s>, <s>vyāghranakhī</s>, <s>cāṇḍālī</s>, and <s>kṣīrakandaka</s>;
<s>Vandhyākarkoṭakī</s>, <s>rambhā</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, and <s>kokilākṣaka</s>;
the <s>śākavṛkṣa</s>, <s>hemavallī</s>, <s>pātālagaruḍī</s>, and <s>śamī</s>;
<s>Kaṭutumbī</s>, <s>vajralatā</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s>, and wild <s>sūraṇa</s>;
<s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>cakramarda</s>, <s>jalakumbhī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>;
<s>Guñjā</s>, <s>kośātakī</s>, <s>nīlī</s>, <s>ākhukarṇī</s>, and <s>triparṇikā</s>;
<s>Kukkuṭī</s>, black <s>tulasī</s>, <s>puṅkhā</s>, and white <s>aparājitā</s>;
<s>Garuḍī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>cāṅgerī</s>, and <s>padmacāriṇī</s>.
Then, having taken a good diamond, he should put it inside a tuber of <s>vyāghrī</s>.

children.text: mahiṣīviṣṭhayā liptvā tulāgnau ca puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: After smearing it with buffalo dung, he should cook it in a sealed heating with <s>tulāgni</s> fire.
After a day and night he should take it out and sprinkle it with horse urine.
Again putting it into a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber, he should place it inside a <s>vajrakanda</s> tuber.
He should moisten it with horse urine and, in the sealed heating, sprinkle it as before.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaiḥ śuddhaṃ vajraṃ syānnātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: In this way, after seven days, the diamond becomes purified; there is no doubt about this.
A decoction of <s>kulattha</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, horse urine, and the milk of <s>snuhī</s>:
having put these in a vessel, he should put into it the diamond placed in the <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber.
In a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus), after a day and night, he should take it out and put it in again.
Putting the <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber into a large tuber, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> firing.
When it is cooked, he should sprinkle it with the juices of <s>kāñcanī</s>; it attains purification.
<s>Ākhukarṇī</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>meṣaśṛṅgikā</s>;
<s>Amlavetasa</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>kulattha</s>, <s>kodrava</s>, <s>śamī</s>,
and <s>muni</s>: with horse urine he should make a good decoction.

children.text: jambīre sūraṇe vātha kṣiptvā vajraṃ dinaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: Putting the diamond into <s>jambīra</s> citron or into <s>sūraṇa</s>, he should cook it for a day.
In a <s>dolā</s> apparatus with the previous decoction it attains purification, and not otherwise.

children.text: śuddhaṃ vajraṃ matkuṇānāṃ raktairliptvā dhamettu tat ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared the purified diamond with the blood of bedbugs, he should heat it with the bellows.
When it has the color of fire, he should throw it repeatedly into urine produced by a donkey.
It should be smeared and heated in just that way; he should do this twenty-one times.

children.text: tālakaṃ matkuṇaiḥ piṣṭvā gole tasminkṣipettu tat
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>tālaka</s> with bedbugs, he should put that into a pellet.

children.text: ruddhvā mūṣāṃ dhamed dārḍhyāt hayamūtre vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: After sealing the crucible, he should heat it firmly with the bellows and cast it into horse urine.
Taking it out, he should repeat the same procedure; after seven times it becomes killed.
<s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, snake bone, tortoise shell, <s>śilājatu</s>,
sulfur, lodestone, <s>munipuṣpa</s>, and <s>tālaka</s>;
the three alkalis, the five salts, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and <s>indravāruṇī</s>;
<s>Vajravallī</s>, <s>mūṣakarṇī</s>, and jujube buds;
mouse dung, breast milk, the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and bedbugs;
the five parts of <s>śarapuṅkhā</s>, and the urines of elephant, human, and goat;
<s>Peṭārī</s> seed, women's menstrual fluid, pigeon dung, and stone;

children.text: puṣpāṇi caiva vākucyāḥ pañcāṅgaṃ nimbakasya ca
children.translated_text: the flowers of <s>vākucī</s> and also the five parts of <s>nimbaka</s>;
the five parts of the <s>dhātrī</s> tree, <s>gorambhā</s>, and goat urine;
<s>Haṃsapādī</s>, <s>vajrakanda</s>, and the fruits of <s>bṛhatī</s> and <s>sūraṇa</s>;

children.text: gojihvā karkaṭaṃ māṃsaṃ mūtravargaṃ ca miśrayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gojihvā</s>, crab, meat, and the class of urines: he should mix these.
All this, together or separately, according to what is available, should be well pounded.
In that lump he should place the diamond, put it into a sealed crucible, and heat it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Having ground <s>kulattha</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, he should stir them with horse urine.
Into the middle of that he should sprinkle the heated crucible taken out from the <s>puṭa</s>.
He should do this again and again, twenty-one times.
Taking the previously treated diamond, in <s>tālaka</s> ground with bedbugs,
he should put it into a pellet, seal it in a crucible, and heat it with the bellows in an intense fire.
Thus it should be heated seven times and sprinkled with horse urine.
By this ordered procedure it certainly becomes killed.
He should powder the killed substance in a mortar; this is called an accomplished procedure.
The mouth of the <s>bhrāmaka</s> should be heated with <s>peṭārī</s> seed and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
There should be alkali of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>, sulfur, <s>tālaka</s>, and <s>śamī</s>.
After it is set in the earth and subjected to one <s>puṭa</s>, he should remove it and grind it thoroughly.
As before, with the aforesaid liquids, he should likewise seal it and cook it.

children.text: punarmardyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ daśavāraṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Again it should be ground, and again cooked ten times as before.
He should distill it in a <s>pātanayantra</s> (distillation apparatus); the <s>rasa</s> becomes properly purified.

children.text: rasasya daśamāṃśaṃ tu gandhaṃ dattvā vimardayet
children.translated_text: Adding sulfur in a tenth part of the amount of <s>rasa</s>, he should triturate it.
With liquids derived from <s>jambīra</s> citron for one <s>yāma</s>, it should be distilled in a <s>pātanayantra</s>.
It should be ground again and distilled again seven times for purification.
Or mercury should be ground in a heated mortar for the length of a day.
With powders of <s>kumārī</s> and <s>rajanī</s>, it should be distilled in a <s>pātanayantra</s>.
With <s>kanyāgni</s> and <s>triphalā</s> as well, he should grind it again and distill it.
It should be ground again and distilled again seven times for purification.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā kuryāt samyak śuddho bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he does this sevenfold in this way, the <s>rasa</s> becomes properly purified.
Trituration in a heated mortar is suitable for all <s>sūta</s>.

children.text: śodhane cāraṇe caiva jāraṇe ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Especially in purification, <s>cāraṇa</s>, and <s>jāraṇa</s>,

children.text: mūrchane māraṇe caiva bandhane ca praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: and also in <s>mūrchana</s>, <s>māraṇa</s>, and <s>bandhana</s>, it is praised.
Goat dung, a chaff fire, and a pit in the ground: he should put the three together.
A mortar set over that is this heated mortar.

children.text: khalvaṃ lohamayaṃ śastaṃ mardakaṃ caiva lohajam
children.translated_text: An iron mortar is recommended, and the pestle too should be made of iron.

children.text: tadabhāve śilotthaṃ vā yogyaṃ khalvaṃ ca mardakam ||
children.translated_text: In its absence, one made of stone is suitable as both mortar and pestle.
Or else, it is now explained how one should obtain <s>sūta</s> (mercury) from cinnabar.
With cow urine, with buffalo urine, with sesame oil, and with sour fermented liquids,
one should cook the cinnabar for seven days in an iron vessel over a gradually increased fire.
One should stir it with an iron rod, adding liquid again and again.
Taking it together with its liquid, one should triturate it with peacock bile.
At the end of the day one should distill it in a distillation apparatus with a fierce fire.
Freed from the seven coverings, this is known as purified <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury).
Again it should be ground with kanyā and triphalā, and then distilled.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā kuryāt samyak śuddho bhaved rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Doing this seven times in just this way, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes properly purified.
Cinnabar should be ground for one day in a mortar with some acidic substance.
One should distill it in the distillation apparatus, and at the end of the day collect it.
Even without the eight operations, this <s>sūta</s> performs every task.
This doctrine of all the siddhas has been stated: it is supreme, marvelous, and purifies <s>sūta</s>.
With little ritual labor it grants abundant siddhi, and it is praised for work on the body and on metals.

children.text: ṣaṭkāṣṭakaṃ hyaṣṭakamaṣṭakaṃ ca śodhyaṃ vimardyaṃ ca yathoditaṃ tat
children.translated_text: The sixfold, the eightfold, and the octad are to be purified and ground as previously taught.
Beginning with diamond and the other substances down to metals and pearls, that will be taught for the accomplishment of excellent <s>sūta</s>.
White, red, yellow, and black are the diamond classes, beginning with the brahmin class.
They should also be recognized by their marks as male, female, and neuter.
Those that are round, complete in their facets, brilliant, and rather large
are called male; they are free of lines and spots.
Those joined with lines and spots and having six angles are remembered as female.
What is triangular, leaf-shaped in body, or elongated is neuter.
Among all of them the male diamonds are best; they pierce and bind <s>rasa</s>.
Female diamonds are for bodily siddhi; the neuter is for the krāmaka operation.
Ajāmārī, kākamācī, devadālī, indravāruṇī,
kākajaṅghā, śikhiśikhā, sarpākṣī, and nāgavallikā,
mīnākṣī, black dhattūra, balā, nāgavallī, and jayā,

children.text: muṇḍī mahābalā pūgī trividhaṃ citrakaṃ niśā ||
children.translated_text: muṇḍī, mahābalā, pūgī, the three kinds of citraka, and niśā,
mūrvā, kāñcānana, kanyā, peṭārī, and sūryavartaka,
viṣṇukrāntā, kāravallī, vākucī, and sinduvārikā,
svarṇapuṣpī, khaṇḍajārī, mañjiṣṭhā, pīluka, and vacā,

children.text: snuhī raktasnuhī bilvaṃ kārpāsaḥ kaṃguṇī ghanā ||
children.translated_text: snuhī, red snuhī, bilva, kārpāsa, kaṃguṇī, and ghanā,
palāśa, aṅkola, vijayā, meghanāda, arka, and mustard,
brahmadaṇḍī, mahārāṣṭrī, and both white and red punarnavā,
udumbara, somalatā, kumbhī, and puṣkaramūla,
tilaparṇī, black cumin, vṛścikālī, and kālikā,
karavīra, agnidamanī, bṛhatī, and bhūmipāṭalī,
yavaciñcī, candralatā, markaṭī, and vanarājaka,
badarī, lajjarī, lākṣā, caṇā, and vartulapatrakā,
apāmārga, bhūkadamba, viṣamuṣṭi, and ekavīraka,
gorambhā, kadalī, jātī, musalī, and sahadevikā,
eraṇḍa, rock salt, pathyā, dry ginger, and maṇḍūkaparṇikā,
marūvaka, asafoetida, vāla, lakṣmaṇā, and hastimūlikā,

children.text: kṣīravṛkṣāśca ye sarve tathā nānāvidhaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: and all the milk-exuding trees, as well as many kinds of poison:
this is known as the group of divine herbs for accomplishing the king of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: vyastaṃ vātha samastaṃ vā yathālābhaṃ niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: One should employ them separately or all together, according to what is available.
By means of various forest products that are sharp in smell, taste, and touch,
through grinding and steaming, <s>sūta</s> is killed and also bound.
Raktaśṛṅgī, kālakūṭa, hāridra, and saktūka,
as well as maustika, are the poison group; the making of a <s>mūṣā</s> (crucible) is now described.

children.text: tuṣaṃ vastraṃ samaṃ dagdhaṃ tatpādāṃśā ca mṛttikā
children.translated_text: Burnt husks and burnt cloth in equal amount, and clay equal to one quarter of that,
together with a quarter part of kūpī-stone, should be ground for a day with the liquids of vajravallī.
One should make from it a crucible called vajra, capable of binding <s>rasa</s>.
Ant-hill clay, charcoal, and old iron slag,

children.text: śvetapāṣāṇakaṃ caitat sarvaṃ cūrṇyaṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: and white stone: all this should be powdered in equal measure.

children.text: sarvatulyaṃ tuṣaṃ dagdhaṃ sarvaṃ toyaiśca mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Burnt husks equal to the whole should be added, and everything should be ground with water.

children.text: mūṣāsaṃpuṭakaṃ kuryāt sandhiṃ lipyācca tena vai
children.translated_text: One should make a closed crucible, and should smear its joint with that very mixture.
This powerful vajra-crucible accomplishes every operation.
Burnt gravel, burnt husks, and burnt ant-hill clay,

children.text: gajāśvānāṃ malaṃ dagdhaṃ yāvattat kṛṣṇatāṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: and the dung of elephants and horses, burnt until it has become black,

children.text: pāṣāṇabhedīpatrāṇi kṛṣṇā mṛc ca samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: with leaves of pāṣāṇabhedī and black earth, each in equal amount,

children.text: vajravallyā dravairmardyaṃ dinaṃ vā śoṣayed dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: should be ground with the juices of vajravallī for a day, or else dried until firm.

children.text: tena koṣṭhaṃ vaṅkanālaṃ vajramūṣāṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: With that one should make a furnace, a bent tube, and a vajra-crucible.
Round and shaped like a cow's udder, it is called a vajra-crucible.
It is useful for mūrchana, killing, binding, and the union of pairs.
That same crucible, provided with a hole and deep in the middle, is suitable for sāraṇa.
Open and shaped like a saucer, it is useful for quenching the seed.
Equal parts of <s>sūta</s> and dhānyābhraka, ground for a day with the juices of punarnavā,
should be cooked in a heated mortar, enclosed in a vajra-crucible.
Tamarind seed, meṣaśṛṅgī, woman's menstrual blood, and amlavetasa,
the five parts of śarapuṅkhā, hare's teeth, and śilājatu:
all these together, or separately, according to availability, should be well powdered.
They should be ground with the milks of snuhī, arka, unmatta, and vāruṇī, and with breast milk.

children.text: tadgolake kṣipedvajraṃ ruddhvā mūṣāṃ dhamed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: One should place the diamond in that pellet, seal the crucible, and blow strongly.
Guḍūcī, rock salt, asafoetida, together with musta and uttaravāruṇī...
After grinding it with decoctions of horse gram, he should quench it in that liquid.
Having put that <s>vajra</s> into a pellet as before, sealed it, he should heat it by blowing in the same way.
He should again carry out the procedure up to quenching twenty-one times.
Then, with a combination of <s>tāla</s> and <s>matkuṇa</s>, he should heat it again seven times.
He should quench that <s>vajra</s> in horse urine; it is certainly killed.
Taking the root of a cotton plant grown for three years, he should grind it.
Or he should grind it thoroughly with the own juices of a three-year-old <s>nāgavallī</s>.
He should put the <s>vajra</s> into that pellet, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ saptapuṭaiḥ pakva ekaikena mṛto bhavet
children.translated_text: When cooked in this way with seven <s>puṭas</s>, it becomes killed by each one.
There are <s>tāla</s>, green vitriol, alum, and the ash of <s>apāmārga</s>.
After grinding them with decoctions of horse gram, he should put into them the <s>vajra</s> that has been well heated.
After twenty-one times it is killed; there is no doubt about this.
He should grind sour <s>vetasa</s> together with ash of <s>vaikrānta</s>.
He should put the <s>vajra</s> into that pellet and heat it, placed in a blind crucible.
He should quench it in horse urine and again put it into the previous pellet.
After sealing, it should be heated and again quenched; he should do this twenty-one times.
It is killed; there is no doubt. He should employ it in all operations.
With the milks of <s>uttarāvāruṇī</s>, the mouth made from lodestone

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ piṣṭvā tu tadgole vajraṃ kṣiptvā pacedanu
children.translated_text: should be ground for a moment; then, putting the <s>vajra</s> into that pellet, he should cook it.

children.text: nṛtaile gandhataile vā mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In human oil or sulfur oil it is killed; there is no doubt about this.
He should grind earthworm, or else sulfur, with a woman's breast milk.
He should cook the <s>vajra</s> in that pellet; in the previous oil it becomes killed.
After grinding <s>vimalā</s> with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, he should place it in that pellet.

children.text: vajraṃ nirudhya mūṣāṃ tāṃ śuṣkāṃ tīvrāgninā dhamet ||
children.translated_text: Having enclosed the <s>vajra</s> and sealed that crucible, when it is dry he should heat it with an intense fire.

children.text: taptamaśvasya mūtre tu kṣiptvā vajraṃ samāharet
children.translated_text: Having thrown the heated <s>vajra</s> into horse urine, he should gather it up.
This should be done seven times. Then <s>tālaka</s> and <s>matkuṇa</s>
are to be made into a pellet; he should put the <s>vajra</s> into it and seal the crucible.
After heating it, it should be quenched as before; by seven times it becomes killed.
He should place <s>vajra</s> in the blood of bedbugs, smear it, and put it in the sun.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ lepyaṃ punaḥ śoṣyaṃ yāvat saptadināvadhi ||
children.translated_text: When dry, it should be smeared again and dried again, until a period of seven days has passed.
He should sprinkle it again and again with the liquids of <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s> and <s>peṭakārī</s>.

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ tu tadvajraṃ śatavārānmṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When that <s>vajra</s> is heated again and again, after one hundred times it becomes killed.

children.text: gandhakaṃ cūrṇitaṃ bhāvyaṃ strīpuṣpeṇa tu saptadhā
children.translated_text: Powdered sulfur should be impregnated seven times with menstrual blood.
Then, after mixing it again with menstrual blood, he should quench in it the <s>vajra</s> that has been well heated.
He should quench and heat it in this way; after twenty-one times it becomes killed.

children.text: mātuluṅgagataṃ vajraṃ ruddhvā bāhye mṛdā lipet
children.translated_text: He should seal <s>vajra</s> placed inside a citron and smear the outside with clay.
He should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>, take it out, and cook it in the same way through one hundred <s>puṭas</s>.
Smeared with the juices of <s>nāgavallī</s> and wrapped in its leaves alone,
that <s>vajra</s>, kept between the knees for a <s>yāma</s>, becomes soft.
He should place <s>vajra</s> in the middle of the living creature called <s>mātṛvāhaka</s>,
or inside a citron, and cook it for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
With decoctions of horse gram and kodo millet, or in a decoction of the three myrobalans,

children.text: ahorātrāt samuddhṛtya jambīre tu punaḥ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: after a day and night he should take it out and put it again into a citron.

children.text: mātṛvāhakajīve vā kṣiptvā paktvā ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Or, having put it into a living <s>mātṛvāhaka</s> and cooked it as before,

children.text: punaḥ kṣepyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ tridinānte samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: it should be inserted again and cooked again; at the end of three days he should take it out.
He should gather the shoots of jujube, banyan, and neem.
After grinding them, he should put the previously cooked <s>vajra</s> into that pellet.
That pellet should be wrapped with aśvattha leaves and placed between the knees.

children.text: dinaṃ vā dhārayet kakṣe mṛdurbhavati niścitam ||
children.translated_text: Or he should keep it in the armpit for a day; it certainly becomes soft.
He should rub mercury and powdered iron with acid for a day.
He should put <s>vajra</s> into that pellet and wrap it outside with thread.
It is to be wrapped with the liquids of <s>nāgavallī</s> and placed in a heap of grain.
At the end of a month, having taken it out, he should smear it with the juices of <s>nāgavallī</s>.
Wrapped in its leaves and kept between the knees, it becomes soft.
Either lodestone <s>vajra</s>, or powder produced from magnetic iron,
should be rubbed for one day with mercury and an acidic mixture.
He should put <s>vajra</s> into that pellet, with leaves produced from neem, cotton, and jujube
that have been ground; then it should be wrapped with leaves of <s>nāgavallī</s>.
That should be wrapped and kept between the knees; at the end of the day it becomes soft.
He should put the thunderbolt-like <s>vajra</s> inside the castor tree, or into its fruit.
After a full month, he should take it out and place it between the knees as before.

children.text: komalaṃ jāyate vajraṃ dinānte nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: At the end of the day the <s>vajra</s> becomes tender; there is no doubt about this.
He should wrap <s>vajra</s> with partridge meat and place it in the mouth
of an extremely large frog; he should wrap its mouth with thread.
He should bury it in the ground at a depth of one hand and take it out after a month.
Having sealed it in a frog container, he should cook it properly in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
That <s>vajra</s>, placed in the previous pellet, should be kept between the knees for a day.
It becomes visibly <s>vajraudana</s>; afterwards it should be killed and then employed.
For all kinds of <s>vajraudana</s>, the killing should be as before.
With the three alkalis, the five salts, fat, urine, acids, and kodo millet,
with fish bile, oils, ghee, horse gram, and sour gruel added,
one should cook seven-colored <s>vaikrānta</s>, placed in tiger-plant tuber, for seven days in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
It certainly attains purification.
Immersed in the juice of citrons, one should keep it for a day in the sun.
<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, conch shell, cowrie shell, collyrium, and red ochre are purified.

children.text: kāsīsaṃ bhūkhagaṃ caiva śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: One should employ purified kāsīsa and bhūkhaga in formulations.
Sulfur should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> with the liquids of nimba and ajagandhā,
or with the liquids of śṛṅgī and dhattūra, or else with those of tilaparṇī.
Taking that, together with an equal amount of ghee, he should cook it for a moment in an iron vessel.
With a gentle fire, when it has melted, he should quickly pour it into goat's milk.
Doing just this seven times, the sulfur becomes purified.
Karañja oil, castor oil, and goat's milk should be put into a vessel.

children.text: kṣiptvā tasya mukhaṃ ruddhvā svacchavastreṇa buddhimān
children.translated_text: Having put them in and sealed its mouth with a clean cloth, the wise man
should steep the sulfur for a day in dhattūra-born liquids and dry it.
That powder should be placed on the cloth over the earlier vessel.

children.text: ācchādya ca śarāveṇa pṛṣṭhe deyaṃ puṭaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: Covering it with a saucer, he should apply a light <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating) on the back.
Taking the melted sulfur, it should be steeped in liquids produced from dhattūra.
In the same way it should again be made liquid, steeped again, and then melted once more.
Taking it, he should steep it seven times in fish bile in the sun.
Then he should grind it together with powder of kośātakī seeds.
He should steep it in liquids produced from bhṛṅga for seven days in harsh sunlight.

children.text: toyena kṣālitaṃ śoṣyaṃ tato mṛdvagninā kṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: It should be washed with water, dried, and then heated for a moment with a gentle fire.
Then, melted in an iron vessel smeared with ghee, he should pour it out.
When it is placed in bhṛṅgarāja liquid, it becomes properly purified.
Now the extraction of oil from purified sulfur is explained.
Amlaparṇī, devadālī, pomegranate, and citron,
or orange, according to availability: he should obtain the liquid of one of these.
One fourth part of borax, relative to the sulfur, should be combined with the liquid.

children.text: etābhyāṃ gandhakaṃ bhāvyaṃ gharme vāratrayaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: With these two the sulfur should be steeped in the heat, again and again, three times.
Dhattūra, tulasī, kṛṣṇā, garlic, devadālikā,
śigru root, kākamācī, camphor, and śaṅkhapuṣpikā,
black agaru, musk, and vandhyākarkoṭakī, in equal parts,
should be ground with citron juice and put into castor oil.
With this he should treat the previous sulfur placed in an iron vessel.
After three times, it becomes like honey and free from sulfurous odor.
This is sulfur oil; it should be used in the various appropriate formulations.
Orpiment, together with powder and sour gruel, should be cooked for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus).
After powdering it, it should be steeped in liquids produced from kūṣmāṇḍa.
It should be dried, ground, and again steeped one hundred times for purification.
Having made the orpiment into small particles, one should add borax equal to one fourth of the orpiment.
The two should be washed with liquids from jambīra and also with sour gruels.
When that has dried, tied in a packet, it should be cooked in sour gruel together with powder.
For two days in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, and in the same way with liquids from kūṣmāṇḍa,
when cooked, the orpiment becomes purified and should be used everywhere.

children.text: suvarṇavarṇaṃ vimalaṃ tāpyaṃ vā kaṇaśaḥ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Golden-colored vimala, or tāpya, should be made into small particles.
Placed in a paste of punarnavā, it should be steamed in horse-gram water.
Or, combined with rock salt wetted with citron and made into a packet,
it should be steamed for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>; it certainly becomes purified.
Rasaka should be steeped for a day with the menstrual discharge and urine of a menstruating woman.
With those same substances it should be ground for one day; it obtains purification.
With punarnavā, meghanāda, kapi, jambīra, tinduka,
agasti flower, kumuda, tamarind, and amlavetasa,
with barley, sūraṇa, bhūdhātrī, māṇḍūkī, and karavīra,
with kāravallī, kṣīrakanda, red lotus, śamī, and vana plants,
with meṣaśṛṅgī, camel fat, śakravāruṇī, and borax,
and with oil, fish fat, and the three pungents, with these liquids together with sour gruel,
using all of these together or separately, in a <s>dolāyantra</s> for three days,
one should cook mica sheets and the other secondary minerals for the sake of purification.
Sūryāvarta, vajrakanda, kadalī, devadālikā,

children.text: śigruḥ kośātakī vandhyā kākamācī ca vālukam ||
children.translated_text: śigru, kośātakī, vandhyā, kākamācī, and sand,
with the juice of any one of these, along with the three alkalis and the group of five salts,
should be steeped with the acid group in intense heat for the span of a day.
With this paste mica, vajramākṣika,
vaikrānta, sasyaka, orpiment, lodestone, and añjana should be smeared,
as well as vimala, realgar, tuttha, and other secondary minerals.
In a <s>dolāyantra</s>, in sour gruel, combined with the preceding paste, he should cook them.
With a fierce fire, in one day, they indeed become purified.
Having taken purified mica and split it into sheets, together with rice in a strong
cloth, he should tie it and rub it inside a vessel filled with sour gruel.
He should rub it with his own hands until it passes by itself into the sour liquid.

children.text: dravaṃ tyaktvā tu tacchoṣyaṃ dinaṃ dhānyābhrakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Discarding the liquid, he should dry that for a day; it becomes <s>dhānyābhraka</s> (rice-processed mica).
This <s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be ground with bhānu milk for the span of a day.
Making it into a cake, wrapped in bhānu leaves, he should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ daśadhā pācyaṃ dugdhairbhāvyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus it should be cooked ten times, again and again steeped with the milks.
Then it should be ground with decoctions of banyan aerial roots and cooked with ten <s>puṭas</s>.
It should be ground with ghee and buffalo milk, and three <s>puṭas</s> should be applied.
The mica becomes free from shine and should be used in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative alchemy).
The herbs beginning with punarnavā are well known for the purification of mica.

children.text: dhānyābhrakaṃ tu taireva tridinaṃ tu puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: But <s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be cooked with those very substances for three days in a <s>puṭa</s>.
By the procedure of the preceding method, it is killed with five <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: taile takre gavāṃ mūtre kāñjike ravidugdhake
children.translated_text: In oil, buttermilk, cow urine, sour gruel, and the latex called <s>ravidugdhaka</s>,

children.text: kulatthānāṃ kaṣāye ca jambīrāṇāṃ drave tathā ||
children.translated_text: and also in a decoction of horse gram and in citron juice,
one should heat them again and again and quench them seven times in each one.
Sheets of gold and the other metals certainly attain purification.
For the purification of molten <s>nāga</s> (lead) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), one should cook them in the same way,
with the three alkalis and the five salts, seven times with citron acid.
They should be impregnated in strong sunlight; and after smearing with that paste,
one should cook sheets of <s>ghoṣāra</s> and copper in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> for their purification.
One should cook <s>nāga</s> in an iron vessel until it becomes completely molten,
stir it with a stick of <s>palāśa</s>, and take it up when it has turned to ash.
Having put into it <s>śilā</s> equal to the ash, together with some acid,
one should grind it for one <s>yāma</s>, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, it should be ground again, mixed with a twentieth part of <s>śilā</s>,

children.text: amlena yāmamātraṃ ca ruddhvā pacecca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: and with acid for one <s>yāma</s>; then it should be sealed and cooked as before.

children.text: evaṃ ṣaṣṭipuṭaiḥ pakvo mṛto bhavati pannagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cooked in this way with sixty <s>puṭas</s>, <s>pannaga</s> (lead) becomes incinerated.
Five <s>palas</s> of <s>hiṅgūla</s> should be ground with woman's breast milk.
With that, one should smear five <s>palas</s> of iron sheets.
After sealing them, one should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, and again with decoctions of the three myrobalans.
With citrons or with sour gruel, and with a twentieth part of <s>darada</s>,

children.text: piṣṭvā ruddhvā puṭellohaṃ tadvatpācyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should grind, seal, and fire the iron in a <s>puṭa</s>; it should be cooked in that same way again and again.
By exactly forty <s>puṭas</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>muṇḍaka</s> iron

children.text: mriyate nātra saṃdeho dattvā dattvaiva hiṅgulam ||
children.translated_text: are incinerated; there is no doubt here, if <s>hiṅgula</s> is added each time.

children.text: lohapātre drute vaṅge pādāṃśaṃ tālakaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: When <s>vaṅga</s> is molten in an iron vessel, one should add a quarter part of <s>tālaka</s>.
It should be stirred with a stick of <s>aśvattha</s>; when ash has formed, one should take it up.
That ash and <s>haritāla</s>, in equal measure, should be rubbed with acid,
or else with liquids of <s>palāśaka</s>; at the end of a <s>yāma</s> it should be taken out and fired in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Having taken it out, one should rub it with one tenth part of <s>tāla</s>,
with the previous liquids for one <s>yāma</s>; then, after sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Cooked in this way with exactly forty <s>puṭas</s>, the <s>vaṅga</s> becomes incinerated.
A copper sheet pierced with holes should be treated with equal parts of sulfur,
ground with acid; after smearing it, one should seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Having taken it out, one should powder it and add to it a quarter part of sulfur.
After grinding it with citrons or with sour gruel, one should seal it and fire it again in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ catuḥpuṭaiḥ pacyādgandho deyaḥ puṭe puṭe ||
children.translated_text: In this way one should cook it with four <s>puṭas</s>; sulfur should be added at every <s>puṭa</s>.
With citron juice, one further <s>puṭa</s> should be given in this way.
With white sugar, five <s>puṭas</s> should be given; it becomes incinerated.
A sheet of <s>tāra</s> (silver), equal in amount to <s>mākṣika</s> ground with acid,

children.text: liptvā ruddhvā puṭe paktvā samuddhṛtya vicūrṇayet ||
children.translated_text: should be smeared, sealed, cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>, taken out, and powdered.
<s>Kaṇā</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, sea-born salt, and <s>bhūdhātrī</s> should each be equal in amount.
This, in an amount equal to the previous powder, should be rubbed with acid.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; with those same substances one should rub it and fire it again.
Cooked in this way with seven <s>puṭas</s>, <s>tāra</s> (silver) reaches the state of ash.
Incinerated <s>nāga</s> (lead), ground with the latex of <s>snuhī</s> or else with some acid,
should be used in equal measure to smear sheets of gold.
After sealing and cooking them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, one should take them out and powder them.
Then, in that very material, one should smear on incinerated <s>nāga</s> in an eighth part.

children.text: yāmaikaṃ mardayed amlai ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: One should rub it for one <s>yāma</s> with acids, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Cooked in this way with eight <s>puṭas</s>, <s>hāṭaka</s> (gold) becomes incinerated.
For <s>āra</s> and <s>ghoṣa</s>, the superior incineration should be carried out as for copper.

children.text: vividhaparamayogair yuktiryuktaiḥ prasiddhairanubhavapathadṛṣṭaiḥ śodhanaṃ māraṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: By various excellent operations, joined with established procedures and seen on the path of experience, purification and incineration

children.text: pavibaligaganānāṃ sarvalohe viśeṣād gaditamiha hitārthaṃ vārtikānāṃ vibhūtyai ||
children.translated_text: of <s>pavi</s>, <s>bali</s>, and <s>gagana</s>, and especially of all metals, has been taught here for the welfare and prosperity of alchemical practitioners.

children.text: samyak siddhamatāntaraiḥ samucitaiḥ satsaṃpradāyaiḥ śubhaiḥ khyātair gandhakajāraṇādivividhairyogaiḥ susiddhaiḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: What has been fully perfected through other doctrines, through suitable and auspicious true traditions, and through renowned procedures beginning with sulfur digestion,
what has been seen as an easy making of gold by coloring <s>tāra</s> (silver),
that truth is being set forth, out of eagerness to protect good people.
Ten <s>niṣkas</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and one <s>niṣka</s> of purified sulfur

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣipetkhalve mardakena śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be added little by little into a mortar and slowly worked with the pestle.
From pounding, a paste is produced; this is the sulfur paste.
Three parts of purified <s>sūta</s> and one part of purified <s>hāṭaka</s> (gold)
should be rubbed with acid for one <s>yāma</s>; this is known as the gold paste.
The sulfur paste should be wrapped around the outside of the gold paste in equal measure.
It should be wrapped tightly with cloth and placed in an iron capsule called <s>sūta</s>.
Having placed the bundle inside, one should add sulfur equal in amount to the whole.
The joint should be sealed and stopped up with clay mixed with salt.

children.text: bhūdharākhye puṭe paktvā jīrṇe gandhaṃ punaḥ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: After cooking it in the <s>puṭa</s> called <s>bhūdhara</s>, when the sulfur has been digested, one should add sulfur again.
When sixfold sulfur has been digested, one should gradually remove the cloth.

children.text: punaḥ punaḥ samaṃ gandhaṃ dattvā jāryaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again and again, adding an equal amount of sulfur, it should be digested slowly.
It must not be completely exhausted; through negligence the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) escapes.
When one hundredfold has been digested in this way, one should take the paste out of the apparatus.

children.text: tattulye saṃpuṭe hemni ruddhvā bāhye ca veṣṭayet
children.translated_text: It should be sealed in an equal gold capsule, and the outside should be wrapped.
With glass ground in <s>kumārī</s> juice, a coating one finger thick should be made.
Outside that, with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and then with salt-clay,
it should be wrapped, oiled to a finger's thickness, and dried by the heat of the sun.
Placed in a <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s>, it should be blown in a <s>vaṅkanāla</s> with a strong fire;
its <s>khoṭa</s> becomes excellent, resembling vermilion red.
With that, the <s>vedha</s> should be applied to molten <s>tāra</s> (silver) at a hundredth part;
it becomes gold. This is stated to be a successful procedure.
Purified sulfur, powdered, should be impregnated seven times with <s>kanaka</s> liquids;
likewise in the sun, and again with the menstrual blood of women.

children.text: tad gandhaṃ karṣamekaṃ tu narapittena lolitam
children.translated_text: One karṣa of that sulfur, stirred with human bile,

children.text: palaikaṃ pāradaṃ śuddham ātape kharpare kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: and one pala of purified mercury should be placed on a potsherd in the sun.
Having put the stirred sulfur on its surface, he should rub it with the thumb;
a splendid piṣṭikā forms, granting the fruit of every desire.
Purified sulfur should be impregnated seven times with the juice of <s>tilaparṇī</s> alone;
he should grind it and dry it in the shade, again and again.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ palaikaṃ ca mūṣāyāṃ hi nidhāpayet
children.translated_text: He should place one pala of purified mercury in a crucible,
and put in a pellet of purified gold measuring one niṣka.
He should set that crucible in a sand-bath apparatus; the earlier sulfur
should be added in tiny portions, and cooked on the hearth with gentle fire.
When a quarter part of the sulfur has been digested, a <s>gandhapiṣṭikā</s> forms;
the sulfur paste should be collected separately, without the pellet of gold.
Sulfur should be impregnated in the shade a hundred times with the liquids of <s>markaṭī</s>;

children.text: gharme mṛtkharpare sūtaṃ kṣipet kiṃcic ca gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: in the heat he should put mercury on an earthen potsherd, together with a little sulfur.
When the sulfur, combined with <s>markaṭī</s> liquid, has been digested, liquid should again
be added, and sulfur with liquid should be given gradually up to a quarter portion.
A splendid piṣṭikā forms, granting the fruit of every desire.
Fine powdered sulfur should be washed three times with sour gruel;
three times with citron juices, and seven times with the juice of <s>haṃsapādī</s>.
Camphor too should be separately impregnated with liquids of <s>śvetādrikarṇikā</s>;
three times in the sun. Then he should begin the <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion).
He should smear the interior of the apparatus with camphor measuring two <s>guñjās</s>;
into that cavity he should add prepared sulfur measuring one and a half <s>niṣkas</s>,
half a pala of purified mercury, and camphor equal to the previous amount.
Then sulfur equal to the previous amount should likewise be added in sequence.
The root of <s>śvetādrikarṇikā</s> should be ground with cow urine;

children.text: ācchādya tena kalkena śarāveṇa nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: having covered it with that paste and sealed it with a dish,
he should cook it in a <s>nālikāyantra</s> and take it out at the end of the day.
Camphor and the rest should again be added; it should likewise be digested for a day.
Doing just this again, a <s>gandhapiṣṭikā</s> forms.
One pala of mercury and one karṣa of purified sulfur,
in a smooth mortar, moistened with <s>devadālī</s> liquid, with the fingers,
should be rubbed in intense sunlight; a <s>gandhapiṣṭikā</s> forms.
One pala of purified mercury and half a karṣa of purified sulfur

children.text: nidhāya tāmrakhalve tu tadadho'gniṃ mṛduṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: should be placed in a copper mortar, and a gentle fire set beneath it.
Rubbing with the thumb, in one <s>yāma</s> it becomes a piṣṭikā.
Bitter <s>kośātakī</s> seed and <s>cāṇḍālī</s> tuber,
ground with woman's breast milk, should be smeared on the <s>gandhapiṣṭikā</s>.
He should place it in a <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber and likewise in the inside of a <s>kṣīrakanda</s>,
or in <s>vandhyākarkoṭakī</s>, <s>vajrakanda</s>, or <s>kuḍuhuñjikā</s>.

children.text: mukhaṃ kandasya majjābhī ruddhvā kandaṃ mṛdā lipet
children.translated_text: After closing the mouth of the tuber with its pulp, he should smear the tuber with clay.
He should heat it for a day in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus over a dung-cake fire,

children.text: ūrdhvādhaḥ parivartena yathā kando na dahyate
children.translated_text: turning it top and bottom so that the tuber is not burned.

children.text: tataḥ piṣṭīṃ samuddhṛtya stambhitā jāyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Then, taking out the piṣṭī, it certainly becomes fixed.
Now its <s>jāraṇa</s> should be performed in an iron capsule called <s>stana</s>;

children.text: nidhāya jārayedgandhaṃ tulyaṃ tulyaṃ tu bhūdhare ||
children.translated_text: having placed it there, he should digest equal portions of sulfur in the <s>bhūdhara</s>.

children.text: jīrṇe gandhe punardeyaṃ yantre jāryaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: When the sulfur has been digested, more should be added; it should be digested in the apparatus as before.
Thus it should be digested one hundredfold; when digested, he should take it out of the apparatus.
For all <s>gandhapiṣṭīs</s>, coloring occurs through <s>jāraṇa</s>.
He should rub the piṣṭi in a mortar with liquids of the group of divine herbs;
at the end of the day, having made a ball, with seeds produced from the divine group
he should smear a <s>vajramūṣā</s> and seal the ball inside it.
He should cook it for one day in the <s>bhūdhara</s>, turning it top and bottom.
After taking it out, it should again be rubbed with the previous liquids as before.

children.text: puṭāntaṃ kārayed evaṃ daśavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should bring it through the end of a <s>puṭa</s> in this way ten times again and again.

children.text: mriyate nātra saṃdeho gandhapiṣṭyās tataḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: It is killed, of this there is no doubt. Then again, from the <s>gandhapiṣṭī</s>,
one pala of the killed paste should be ground with liquids of <s>vāsaka</s>.
With that paste, having smeared eight palas of lead sheet,
dried in the shade, he should place it in a ball made from <s>vāsā</s> leaves.
Having sealed that ball in a capsule, he should heat it with forest cow-dung cakes.
After taking it out, one pala of killed paste should again be added.
It should be rubbed for a day with <s>vāsā</s> liquids; that ball should again be wrapped
with a lump made from <s>vāsā</s> leaves, sealed, and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kuryādraktavarṇaṃ mṛtaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: He should do this again and again; it becomes killed and red in color.
That lead, one pala, for one <s>yāma</s> with <s>vāsaka</s> liquids,
having been rubbed, with it he should smear eight palas of copper sheet.
He should cook it for one day in a cooking apparatus; it is certainly killed.
With a sixteenth part of that same substance, he should administer <s>vedha</s> to <s>tāra</s> (silver);
that silver becomes gold, with a brilliance equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.

children.text: yayā kayā gandhapiṣṭyā stambhanaṃ jāraṇaṃ vinā
children.translated_text: By means of any <s>gandhapiṣṭī</s> (sulfur paste) whatsoever, without <s>stambhana</s> (fixing) or <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion),
through the sequence of procedure as before, it becomes excellent gold.

children.text: arjunasya tvaco bhasma vāsābhasma samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Ash of <s>arjuna</s> bark and ash of <s>vāsā</s> should be taken in equal measure.
They should be ground for one day with the juices of <s>gṛhakanyā</s>; with that he should smear it.
A sheet of <s>nāga</s> (lead), pierced so as to be thin, should be sealed and cooked in a light <s>puṭa</s>.
Having taken it out, he should grind it for a <s>yāma</s> with the previous liquids together with the ashes.
After sealing it and cooking it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, he should remove it when it has cooled by itself.

children.text: evaṃ śatapuṭaiḥ pācyaṃ bhasma drāvaiśca mardayet ||
children.translated_text: In this way it should be cooked through one hundred <s>puṭas</s>, and the ash should be ground with the liquids.
With that same material he should smear sheets of <s>tāra</s> (silver) that have been coated with honey.

children.text: ruddhvā gajapuṭe paktvā punarliptvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: After sealing them and cooking them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, he should smear them again and cook them in a <s>puṭa</s>.
When he has done this three times in just this way, the silver becomes gold.

children.text: lohapātre drute nāge cūrṇitaṃ rasakaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: In an iron vessel, into melted <s>nāga</s> (lead), he should put an equal amount of powdered <s>rasaka</s>.
He should cook it on a hearth for a <s>yāma</s>, stirring it with a stone pestle.
At the end of the <s>yāma</s>, powdered <s>hiṅgula</s>, equal in amount to the lead, should be added.
He should grind it very finely for that long with a firm stone pestle.
And he should cook it with a fierce fire for twenty-one days.

children.text: jāyate kuṅkumābhaṃ tu tāraṃ tenaiva vedhayet
children.translated_text: It becomes saffron-colored; with that very material he should pierce <s>tāra</s> (silver).
At a sixty-fourth part, it becomes excellent gold.
He should melt <s>nāga</s> (lead) in a potsherd and add one quarter part there.
He should rub in the alkali from the bark of tamarind and <s>aśvattha</s> with an iron ladle.
At the end of a <s>yāma</s>, having taken it out, he should grind it in a mortar for a day with the latex of <s>vajrī</s>.
Having taken it out, he should confine it inside an earthen vessel.
At night he should cook it for four <s>yāmas</s> on a hearth, again with a fierce fire.
Having taken it out, he should grind it in a mortar for a day with the latex of <s>vajrī</s>.

children.text: rātrau pācyaṃ divā mardyaṃ yāvat ṣaṇmāsameva ca
children.translated_text: It should be cooked at night and ground by day until six months have passed.

children.text: yathā na patate tasmiñjalaṃ dhūlistu rakṣayet
children.translated_text: He should protect it so that neither water nor dust falls into it.

children.text: sahasrāṃśe dhṛte śare vedhe datte sukāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: When it is applied in a thousandth part to <s>śara</s> and the piercing is made, it gives good gold.
He should grind equal parts of <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, camphor, and saffron.
For a <s>yāma</s> with the juices produced from citron, and an equal quantity of lead sheet,

children.text: liptvā liptvā puṭaiḥ pacyād yāvacchaṣṭipuṭī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: he should smear it again and again and cook it with <s>puṭas</s> until it has received sixty <s>puṭas</s>.
That lead becomes shining like lightning; with that he should perform the piercing.
At a sixty-fourth part, <s>tāra</s> (silver) becomes gold.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ śulbaṃ nāgavaṅgau drutaṃ nāgaṃ tu tutthakam
children.translated_text: <s>Tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), <s>śulba</s> (copper), <s>nāga</s> (lead), <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), melted lead, and <s>tuttha</s>,
each powdered in one part, and two parts of <s>hemamākṣika</s>,
should be sealed in a diamond crucible and blown; the resulting ingot should be well powdered.
Joined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, it makes <s>tāra</s> (silver) become gold.

children.text: śulbacūrṇaṃ tīkṣṇacūrṇaṃ tulyaṃ ruddhvā dhamet haṭhāt
children.translated_text: Equal amounts of copper powder and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> powder should be sealed and forcefully blown.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ siddhacūrṇaṃ ca mardyaṃ pācyaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: That ingot and <s>siddhacūrṇa</s> should be ground and cooked as before.
With that very material, mixed with honey, he should smear sheets of <s>tāra</s> (silver).
After sealing them, he should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; when this has been done three times,
it becomes yellow in color, and this is called <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.
Equal <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) and <s>nāga</s> (lead) with <s>kānta</s>, or else copper with lead,
<s>mākṣika</s> with copper and <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, or copper and lead together with tin:

children.text: ete yogāstu catvāraḥ pṛthak cūrṇāni kārayet ||
children.translated_text: these are four formulas; he should make the powders separately.
The ingots, separately smelted and joined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>,
when carried through grinding and the final <s>puṭa</s>, indeed produce <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.
Each one should be prepared by the smearing procedure as before.
The gold-making of that same <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> is now stated.
One part of purified <s>vaikrānta</s>, or else essence of <s>vaikrānta</s>,
and one part of lead powder should be placed in a closed crucible and blown.
Joined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, it should be brought through the sequence ending in grinding and <s>puṭa</s>-cooking.
The wise should do this as before, then take it up and rub it well.

children.text: madhunā yāmamātraṃ tu tena lepaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: For just a <s>yāma</s> with honey; with that he should make a coating.
He should carefully apply it, as one hundredth part, to sheets of <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.

children.text: ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacyād divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam
children.translated_text: After sealing them, he should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; excellent gold results.
The root, leaf, and fruit from <s>bilva</s>, and those three from the <s>śāka</s> tree,
together with <s>śigru</s> root: this juice he should grind with the liquids of <s>kiṃśuka</s>.

children.text: anena nāgacūrṇaṃ tu mardyaṃ mardyaṃ puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: With this, lead powder should be ground and ground, and then cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Cooked through one hundred <s>puṭas</s> in this way, it becomes like a ruby.
With that same material he should smear sheets of <s>tāra</s> (silver) that have been coated with honey.
After sealing them, he should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; when this has been done three times,
that silver becomes excellent, with a brilliance like <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
<s>Rājāvarta</s>, <s>hiṅgulaka</s>, <s>kaṃkuṣṭha</s>, and coral
should each be one <s>karṣa</s>, and <s>rasaka</s> should be one <s>pala</s>.
All this should be made into a fine powder and joined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>.
Placed in a closed crucible and blown, it should be brought through grinding and the final <s>puṭa</s>.
He should prepare it as before; afterwards he should mix it with honey.
Having smeared sheets of <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>, he should cook them in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ vāratrayaṃ kuryād divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: He should do this three times; excellent gold results.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, <s>darada</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, <s>rājāvarta</s>, and coral
are to be in equal parts, while <s>rasaka</s> should be two parts.
He should grind all of that for one day with ewe's milk.
Having dried it in the shade, he should add an equal portion of <s>mitrapañcaka</s>.

children.text: dattvā tu mardayet khalve tārāriṣṭaṃ tu lepayet
children.translated_text: Then he should grind it in a mortar and smear the <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.
First, with an equal amount of paste, he should seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Then it is to be smeared with half the paste, or again with a quarter paste.

children.text: evaṃ puṭatrayaṃ deyaṃ divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Thus three <s>puṭas</s> should be given; the gold becomes excellent.
Having sealed <s>rasaka</s> in an amount equal to <s>nāga</s>, he should make it into a <s>khoṭa</s>.
Joined with the <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, it is subjected to a <s>puṭa</s> as before.
With that same honey mentioned above, he should smear the <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.

children.text: ruddhvā ruddhvā puṭe pacyāt tridhā bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Sealing it again and again, he should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>; after three times it becomes gold.
Sulfur, <s>tālaka</s>, and copper are ground with an equal amount of <s>hiṅgula</s>.
Together with citron juices, with that indeed he should smear leaves of <s>nāga</s>.
After smearing and sealing them, he should cook them in a <s>puṭa</s>; then he should again triturate them with the same substance.
Cooked in this way with sixty <s>puṭas</s>, <s>nāga</s> becomes saffron-colored.
With that, he should smear leaves of <s>tāra</s> that have been coated with honey.
Having sealed them, he should heat them with intense fire; when this has been done three times,
that <s>tāra</s> becomes excellent, with a brilliance like <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>girikarṇī</s>, <s>agni</s>, and the root of <s>karavīra</s>,

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ stanyaiḥ piṣṭvā piṇḍaṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>sauvīra</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, should be ground with breast milk and made into a pellet.
Purified <s>vimalā</s>, prepared in four parts, one of them measuring a <s>pala</s>,
two <s>palas</s> of purified mercury, and three <s>palas</s> of purified gold should be taken.
He should grind everything for one <s>yāma</s> and place it in the interior of the preceding pellet.
That pellet should be sealed in a diamond-crucible and blown with a forceful fire.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ śatamāṃśena drutaṃ nāgaṃ tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, in a hundredth part, should transmute molten <s>nāga</s>.

children.text: tannāgena śatāṃśena drutaṃ śulbaṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: With that <s>nāga</s>, in a hundredth part, molten copper should be transmuted.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ śatamāṃśena drutaṃ nāgaṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, in a hundredth part, should transmute molten <s>nāga</s>.
Excellent divine gold is produced, fit as an ornament for the gods.
Mercury, saffron, and sulfur, with menstrual blood, for the period of a day,
should be ground in equal portions; with that paste he should process them.
Having smeared purified leaves of <s>tāra</s>, he should seal them and heat them vigorously.

children.text: patraṃ kṛtvā punarlepyaṃ ruddhvā dhāmyaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: After making a leaf, it should again be smeared, sealed, and heated as before.
In this way he should perform smearing and melting successively seven times.
Then he should smear its leaves with that same paste.
Opening it, he should melt it, and when it is molten he should throw it into ghee.
He should keep it there for seven days; it becomes excellent gold.

children.text: kuṅkumaṃ gandhakaṃ sūtaṃ mañjiṣṭhā tatsamaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Saffron, sulfur, mercury, and <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, each equal in amount,
should be triturated for a day with well-ripened juices of the fruits of the <s>śāka</s> tree.
With that he should smear leaves of <s>tāra</s> and dry them.
After melting, he should cast it there, impregnated with that paste.
He should do this again and again twenty-one times.
That <s>tāra</s> becomes gold, properly of twelve-<s>varṇa</s> quality.
Mercury, lodestone, sulfur, and red sandalwood,
mixed with the juice of <s>rudantī</s>, should be thoroughly triturated for one day.
With that he should smear leaves of <s>tāra</s> well and dry them.
He should heat them in a closed crucible; he should do this twenty-one times.
The root of the <s>śāka</s> tree should be impregnated with juices from its leaves,
and also separately with juices from red <s>aśvamāra</s>, three times each.
With this, an admixture should be made for the previously molten <s>tāra</s>.
He should have it given seven times; it becomes excellent gold.
Sulfur and <s>gandhamūlī</s> should be triturated with the latex of <s>ravi</s>.

children.text: mṛṇmaye saṃpuṭe ruddhvā māsaṃ bhūmau vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed it in an earthen covered vessel, he should bury it in the ground for a month.

children.text: uddhṛtya tena tārasya patralepaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: After taking it out, he should have a leaf-smearing of <s>tāra</s> made with it.

children.text: pūrvatāre drute deyaḥ prativāpaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The admixture should be put again and again into the previously molten <s>tāra</s>.
At the twenty-seventh admixture, that <s>tāra</s> becomes gold.
Sulfur equal to purified mercury should be ground in a mortar for a day.
An excellent <s>kajjalī</s> is produced, auspicious and effective for every operation.
<s>Kajjalī</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and <s>tāpya</s>, each measuring one <s>karṣa</s>,
and two <s>karṣas</s> of purified sulfur should all be powdered for one <s>yāma</s>.
This is known as <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>; its measure may be from a quarter up to a <s>pala</s>.

children.text: yatra yatra milatyetattatra cūrṇaṃ palaṃ palam
children.translated_text: Wherever this is mixed, in each case a <s>pala</s> of the powder should be added.
He should employ it in metal operations; that is now being explained.
Of copper, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>āra</s>, or <s>kānta</s>, he should take the powder of any one,

children.text: yathā lohe palaikaṃ tu siddhacūrṇena saṃyutam ||
children.translated_text: so that one <s>pala</s> of the metal is combined with the <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>.

children.text: vajramūṣāgataṃ ruddhvā dhmātaṃ khoṭaṃ bhavettu tat
children.translated_text: Placed in a diamond-crucible, sealed, and heated, it becomes that <s>khoṭa</s>.
With equal <s>bhūnāga</s> and <s>jīva</s>, or with an equal amount of sulfur,
he should triturate the preceding <s>khoṭa</s> with acidic citron juice for a day.
That pellet, sealed in a baked crucible, should be cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
In this way he should give fourteen <s>puṭas</s> with forest fuel-cakes.
It becomes like an <s>indragopaka</s>; he should worship <s>Śiva</s>.
With that same substance mixed with honey, he should smear leaves of <s>tāra</s>.
Having sealed them, he should heat them, or else in a <s>puṭa</s>; when this has been done three times,
excellent gold is produced. This is the successful coloring agent for <s>tāra</s>.
Thus, for all the procedures given here, each one separately,
it should be done by the wise according to rule, combined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>.

children.text: śulbaṃ nāgaṃ samaṃ dhāmyaṃ samaṃ vā śulvavaṅgakam ||
children.translated_text: Copper and <s>nāga</s> should be heated in equal amount, or copper and <s>vaṅga</s> in equal amount.
That powder is melted with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s> as before.
Copper, <s>nāga</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, or bell-metal: he should powder any one desired.
Also an equal powder of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> should be heated in a closed crucible.
Then, having powdered this <s>khoṭa</s>, he should combine it with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>.
By the sequential procedure as before, <s>tāra</s> comes to the state of gold.
There should be three parts of copper, and one part each of lead and tin.
After melting them together and then pulverizing them, combine them with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s> (perfected powder) as before.
Take one part lead and two parts copper; with that very copper, treat the lead.

children.text: ruddhvā dhmātaṃ ca taccūrṇya siddhacūrṇena pūrvavat
children.translated_text: When it has been sealed and smelted, powder it and combine it with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s> as before.
There are three parts of <s>siddhacūrṇa</s> and one part red ochre.
Seal and smelt it; then powder it again with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s> as before.

children.text: gandhakena hataṃ śulvaṃ mākṣikaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Copper killed with sulfur, and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), should be in equal quantities.
One should grind them for one day with the juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s> and <s>citraka</s>.

children.text: tenaiva tārapatrāṇi liptvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: With that same paste, smear silver sheets; seal them and cook them in a <s>puṭa</s> furnace.
Taking it out, one should afterward smelt it, make sheets, and smear them.
Seal them with the previous paste, then give a <s>puṭa</s> heating and take them out.
Doing this ten times, the silver becomes gold.
Take two parts <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), three parts <s>ghoṣamāra</s>, and four parts as prescribed.
Add nine parts copper powder and likewise nine parts lead.
When it has been smelted in a blind crucible, that ingot should be finely powdered.
Mixed with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, it serves for coloring silver as before.

children.text: mṛtanāgasamaṃ tutthaṃ dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ ca mākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tuttha</s> equal to dead lead, and <s>mākṣika</s> equal to those two, may be used.
Or use simply dead lead with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, as before.
Or lead with mica, or tin with mica, placed in a blind crucible, should be smelted forcefully.
That ingot, reduced to fine powder and joined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>,
by the sequential procedure as before, makes silver become gold.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ śulbaṃ nāgavaṅgaṃ mṛtaṃ nāgaṃ tu tutthakam
children.translated_text: Iron, copper, lead, tin, dead lead, and <s>tuttha</s>
should each be powdered in one part, with two parts <s>hemamākṣika</s> (golden pyrite).
Sealed in a diamond crucible and smelted, the ingot should be well pulverized.
When mixed with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, it makes silver become gold.
Seal equal parts of copper powder and iron powder, and smelt them forcefully.

children.text: tat khoṭaṃ siddhacūrṇaṃ tu mardyaṃ pācyaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: That ingot, with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, should be ground and cooked as before.
With that very substance mixed with honey, one should smear silver sheets.
Having sealed them, one should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; when this has been done three times,
it becomes yellow in color, and that is called <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.
Tin, lead, and lodestone in equal parts, or else copper and lead;

children.text: mākṣikaṃ śulbatīkṣṇaṃ ca śulvaṃ nāgaṃ savaṅgakam
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s>, copper, and iron; or copper, lead, and tin:

children.text: ete yogāstu catvāraḥ pṛthak cūrṇāni kārayet ||
children.translated_text: these are four formulations, and their powders should be prepared separately.
Their separately smelted ingots, together with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>,
when processed through grinding and up to the <s>puṭa</s> heating, indeed produce <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.
Each one should be prepared by the smearing procedure as before.
The conversion into gold of that very <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> is now taught.
Take one part purified <s>vaikrānta</s>, or else extract of <s>vaikrānta</s>,
and one part lead powder; it should be placed in a blind crucible and smelted.
Combined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, it should undergo grinding and the <s>puṭa</s> procedure,
as before, by the wise; taking it, one should grind it

children.text: madhunā yāmamātraṃ tu tena lepaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: with honey for one <s>yāma</s>. With it one should make a coating
on the sheets of <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>, carefully, in the proportion of one hundredth.

children.text: ruddhvā gajapuṭe paktvā divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam
children.translated_text: Having sealed it and cooked it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, it becomes divine gold.
<s>Rājāvarta</s>, <s>hiṅgula</s>, <s>kaṃkuṣṭha</s>, and coral
should each be one <s>karṣa</s>, and <s>rasaka</s> likewise one <s>pala</s>.
All of it should be made into a fine powder and combined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>.
Placed in a blind crucible and smelted, it should proceed through grinding and the <s>puṭa</s> procedure.
One should perform it as before; afterward it should be mixed with honey.
After smearing sheets of <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>, one should cook them in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Doing this three times, it becomes divine gold.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, <s>darada</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, <s>rājāvarta</s>, and coral:
these are in equal parts, while <s>rasaka</s> should be two parts.
All of that should be ground for one day with ewe’s milk.
After drying it in the shade, one should add an equal portion of <s>mitrapañcaka</s>.

children.text: dattvā tu mardayet khalve tārāriṣṭaṃ tu lepayet
children.translated_text: After grinding it in a mortar, one should smear the <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.
First, with an equal amount of paste, it should be sealed and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Then it should be smeared with half the paste, and again with a quarter of the paste.

children.text: evaṃ puṭatraye datte divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: When three <s>puṭas</s> have thus been given, it becomes divine gold.
<s>Rasaka</s> equal to lead should be sealed and made into an ingot.
Combined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, and after the <s>puṭa</s> procedure has been done as before,
with that very substance mixed with honey, he should smear the <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.

children.text: ruddhvā ruddhvā puṭaiḥ pacyāttridhā bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Sealing it again and again, he should cook it with <s>puṭas</s>; in three times it becomes gold.
He should heat sheets of copper and drop them into sour gruel.

children.text: punaḥ pācyaṃ punaḥ kṣepyaṃ yāvattatraiva śīryate ||
children.translated_text: They should be cooked again and dropped in again, until they crumble there.
Those sheets, while in sour gruel, should be washed with sour gruels.
Adding borax in a quarter portion, he should grind it with acid for one <s>yāma</s>.
Having sealed it, he should cook it with light <s>puṭas</s>; thus he should cook it with one hundred <s>puṭas</s>.
Honey, ghee, and then borax are added; after cooking it sealed, he should smelt it forcefully.
That copper becomes free from blackness and like a parrot’s beak.

children.text: tacchulbaṃ triguṇaṃ tāre nirvāpyaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: That copper, in triple quantity, should be quenched in silver; it will become gold.
With leaves equal to <s>śigru</s> leaves and roots resembling coral,

children.text: jñeyā divyauṣadhī siddhā nāmnā sā kīṭamāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: the accomplished divine herb should be known by the name <s>kīṭamāriṇī</s>.
Mercury should be ground with its juices for a period of seven days.
With that very substance he should smear leaves of <s>tāra</s> and dry them.
Having sealed them, he should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; in this way he should do it twenty-one times.
Divine gold is produced, as was formerly stated by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
There should be <s>rājī</s> equal to purified mercury, and sulfur measuring a quarter of the mercury.
He should cook it in an earthen vessel on a stove, mixed with the juice of <s>dhattūra</s>.

children.text: vāsākāṣṭhena tanmardyaṃ dravo deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: That should be triturated with wood of <s>vāsā</s>; liquid should be added again and again.
He should do this for three days; calcined mercury is produced.
That should be triturated with acidic citron juice for one day; then with that substance
he should smear leaves of <s>tāra</s> using a sixty-fourth part.
Having sealed them, he should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; when this has been done three times,
that <s>tāra</s> becomes gold, as declared by <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: tārasya rañjanamidaṃ sukhabhogahetuṃ kṛtvā vivekamatibhirbhuvane janānām
children.translated_text: This coloring of <s>tāra</s>, a cause of happy enjoyment, should be carried out for people in the world by those of discerning mind.

children.text: deyaṃ sadā sakalakīrtiśubhāptisiddhyai no cedvane vasatireva parā hi dhanyā ||
children.translated_text: It should always be given for the attainment of all fame, auspiciousness, and success; otherwise, dwelling in the forest alone is supremely blessed.

children.text: mahārasaiścoparasaiḥ sasūtair hemno dalaṃ rañjanamatra yuktyā
children.translated_text: Here, by method, the coloring of gold leaf with <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and mercury
and the various kinds of color enhancement are explained as suitable for practical use and enjoyment.
One part of the essence of <s>vaikrānta</s>, or purified <s>vaikrānta</s> itself,

children.text: kāṃsyākhyā vimalā vāpi hemākhyā vimalāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: or <s>vimalā</s> called bronze, or <s>vimalā</s> called gold,
should be blown in a closed crucible with an equal amount of lead powder.
Combined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>, it should be brought through trituration and the rest up to the final <s>puṭa</s> heating.
Taking it, he should carefully grind it with honey for the space of one <s>yāma</s>.

children.text: svarṇaṃ tāraṃ samaṃ drāvyaṃ tena patrāṇi kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should melt equal amounts of gold and <s>tāra</s>, and make leaves from them.
This is known as white gold; he should smear it with the preceding paste.
Having sealed it, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; when this has been done three times,
divine gold is produced. He should sprinkle it with salt water,
or sprinkle it with the juice of <s>brāhmī</s> for the purpose of removing transferred iron.
Thus a separate procedure with <s>vimalā</s> and lead has been stated.
By the procedure with lead and <s>vaikrānta</s>, he should smear it with beeswax.

children.text: sahasrāṃśe site heme divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam
children.translated_text: At a thousandth part in white gold, divine gold is produced.
Cinnabar should be heat-impregnated with ewe's milk and the acidic group.

children.text: śatadhā tatprayatnena śoṣyaṃ peṣyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: This should be dried and ground again and again, carefully, one hundred times.

children.text: anena sitasvarṇasya patraṃ liptvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: With this he should smear a leaf of white gold and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
He should do this twenty-one times; divine gold is produced.
Lead powder, <s>tāpya</s> powder, or lead with <s>vaikrānta</s>
should become a <s>khoṭa</s> in a closed crucible, combined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>.

children.text: mardanaṃ puṭapākaṃ ca pūrvavat kārayet kramāt ||
children.translated_text: He should perform trituration and <s>puṭa</s> cooking in sequence as before.
With that same substance, moistened with honey, he should smear a purified leaf of gold,
and after smearing it repeatedly, he should cook it with <s>puṭas</s> until it resembles saffron.
With a hundredth part of this gold, he should penetrate white gold.
Divine gold is produced; he should sprinkle it after it has been cast with the red group.
<s>Vaikrānta</s> and lead powder, brought through the <s>puṭa</s> process as before,
should effect penetration with a hundredth part into white gold, as before.
Through smearing and <s>puṭa</s> cooking, divine gold is produced.
He should triturate <s>rājāvarta</s> with an equal portion of <s>mākṣika</s> for three days
with citron juices; with that he should smear the leaves
of the previously mentioned white gold, seal them, and cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: punarlepyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ saptadhā kāṃcanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: It should be smeared again and cooked again; after seven repetitions it becomes gold.
<s>Rājāvarta</s>, vermilion, and pigeon droppings, in equal amounts,

children.text: aśītyaṃśena kurute svarṇaṃ raupyaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: make gold and silver by an eightieth part, as before.
With equal juices of <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers and ginger,
he should impregnate finely powdered <s>rājāvarta</s> seven times.
With that same substance as a hundredth part, he should penetrate molten equal gold and <s>tāra</s>,
completed as before; divine gold is produced.

children.text: kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ vimalā tāpyaṃ rasakaṃ daradaṃ śilā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, cinnabar, and realgar,
<s>rājāvarta</s>, coral, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, ochre, and borax,
and rock salt should be powdered equally; he should cast an eightieth part.

children.text: drute same svarṇatāre pūrvavat secayet kramāt
children.translated_text: Into molten equal gold and <s>tāra</s>, he should sprinkle it successively as before.
He should cast it three times in this way; divine gold is produced.

children.text: gairikaṃ ca pravālaṃ ca kākamācyā dravaiḥ samam
children.translated_text: Ochre and coral, with equal liquids of <s>kākamācī</s>,

children.text: yāmaṃ mardyaṃ tu tadruddhvā āraṇyotpalakaiḥ puṭet ||
children.translated_text: should be triturated for a <s>yāma</s>; then, after sealing that, he should heat it with forest fuel-cakes.
