Thus he should perform the trituration and <s>puṭa</s> cooking three times.
Having added purified <s>hiṅgula</s> equal to half of that, he should triturate it into the mixture.
With sour gruel, for the space of one <s>yāma</s>, he should cook it with a single <s>puṭa</s>.
One part of this paste and four parts of gold
should be blown in a closed crucible; taking it out, he should powder it.

children.text: pūrvavat pūrvakalkena ruddhvā deyaṃ puṭaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As before, after sealing it with the previous paste, another <s>puṭa</s> should be given.

children.text: evaṃ catuḥpuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ svarṇaṃ guñjānibhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Cooked with four <s>puṭas</s> in this way, the gold becomes like a <s>guñjā</s> seed.
This cooked seed is perfected; he should apply it in each appropriate operation.
With a sixteenth part of this, he should penetrate white gold.
He should quench it in <s>kuṅkuṇī</s> oil after it has been cast with the red group.
The wise man should penetrate it again and quench it again with a sixteenth part.

children.text: evaṃ vāratrayaṃ vedhyaṃ divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: In this way it should be penetrated three times; divine gold is produced.
With the cooked seed described earlier, he should penetrate the eight-grade material.

children.text: tatsvarṇaṃ daśavarṇaṃ syātpuṭe datte na hīyate ||
children.translated_text: That gold will be of ten-grade quality; when a <s>puṭa</s> is given, it does not diminish.
Sixteen <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>tuttha</s>, mercury, <s>hiṅgula</s>, and sulfur...
And likewise <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), each one separately, should be added in the amount of four <s>niṣkas</s>.
All this should be ground for a day, mixed with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> in three pourings.

children.text: niṣkamātrāṃ vaṭīṃ kṛtvā śreṣṭhe svarṇe drute kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: After making a pill of one <s>niṣka</s>, he should throw it into excellent molten gold.

children.text: ekaikaṃ niṣkamātraṃ tu mūṣāmadhye dinaṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: Each one, just one <s>niṣka</s> in measure, should be blown for a day in the crucible.

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe punardeyā evaṃ sarvāḥ pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: When each has been digested, another should again be supplied; in this way he should cause all of them to be added.
The gold becomes the color of <s>guñjā</s>; this is the famous <s>hemaraktikā</s>.
Into melted gold of eight <s>varṇas</s>, in the proportion of one tenth,
one should throw that; truly it becomes beautiful gold of ten <s>varṇas</s>.
With lead equal to the copper, one should purify it by blowing.
Having melted pure gold equal to the copper, he should make it into sheets.

children.text: iṣṭikā tuvarī caiva khaṭikā lavaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Brick, <s>tuvarī</s>, chalk, and likewise salt,
and red ocher in progressively increased portions should be ground with sour gruel.

children.text: tena liptvā pūrvapatraṃ ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared the former sheet with that, he should seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Thus it should be cooked again and again until only the gold remains.
That gold, joined with copper, should be melted and made into sheets.
By cooking in a <s>puṭa</s> as before, he should cook it until only the gold remains.

children.text: ityevaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ tāmraṃ svarṇe bāhyaṃ krameṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: In this way, six times as much copper is gradually carried externally into the gold.
All of that becomes divine, with a brilliance equal to a ruby.
With that very substance, in the proportion of one thirty-sixth, he should transmute gold of eight <s>varṇas</s>.

children.text: tatsvarṇaṃ jāyate divyaṃ daśavarṇaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: That gold becomes divine gold of ten <s>varṇas</s>; there is no doubt.
Equal parts of <s>tāpya</s> and copper powder, and iron powder half as much as the <s>tāpya</s>,

children.text: kanyādrāvaiḥ kṣaṇaṃ mardya gharme tenaiva bhāvayet
children.translated_text: should be ground for a moment with the juices of <s>kanyā</s> and then impregnated with that very substance in the heat.
After doing this sixty-four times, he should dry it and reduce it to powder.
With that very substance, in the proportion of one sixteenth, he should transmute gold of eight <s>varṇas</s>.

children.text: tatsvarṇaṃ jāyate divyaṃ daśavarṇaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That gold becomes divine gold of ten <s>varṇas</s>; there is no doubt.

children.text: rasakaṃ ghoṣatāmraṃ ca kācaṃ śvetaṃ nṛkeśakam
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s>, bell-metal copper, white glass, and human hair
should each be five <s>palas</s>, and each should be powdered separately.
Then sharp iron powder, three times the <s>rasaka</s>, should be added.
Sulfur, <s>rasaka</s>, bronze, and <s>mākṣika</s> should each be eight <s>niṣkas</s>.
<s>Dhūmasāra</s> should be twenty <s>niṣkas</s>; all this, for a day,
should be ground with juices from citron fruits and made into pellets of one <s>karṣa</s> each.
In a furnace apparatus it should be blown forcefully until only the copper remains.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇam tasya tāmrasya sīse vāhyaṃ dhamandhaman ||
children.translated_text: Six times as much of that copper should be carried into lead, by blowing again and again.
With that very substance, in the proportion of one thirty-sixth, he should transmute gold of eight <s>varṇas</s>.
It becomes gold of ten <s>varṇas</s>; no deliberation should be made about this.
Now he should prepare another copper, purified with lead.
With the juice of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>, it should be quenched fifty times.
With the juice of gourd, it should be quenched seven times.
With buttermilk mixed with turmeric, it should be quenched seven times.

children.text: evaṃ tāmraṃ drutaṃ ḍhālyaṃ kālikārahitaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When molten copper has thus been quenched, it becomes free from blackness.
This copper should be three parts, and the gold should be exactly five parts.
Pure silver should be two parts; then he should melt all of it together.
It becomes divine gold, as formerly taught by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
Having kindled wood of <s>aṅkolla</s>, and powdered wild cow-dung cakes,
he should throw powdered <s>aṅkolla</s> seed upon the burning wood.
Having taken those coals when they have cooled, he should blow them again.
He should add powdered <s>aṅkolla</s> seed and bind it with cloth.
With its smoke he should fumigate gold sheets of ten <s>varṇas</s>.
After melting them, he should again throw them into oil produced from <s>putrajīva</s>.
When they have been thrown in twice in this way, the color increases by two <s>varṇas</s>.
By small applications of procedures, by easily accomplished preparations, and by a method requiring little work but having many special details,
an instruction that produces gain, a tenth part of the capital, has truly been taught by me for the welfare of all people.
Taking its own essence from clusters of various red and very yellow flowers,
one should pour purified molten lead into that a hundred times.
Afterward, whatever coloring and transmutation of silver, gold, and copper is done according to rule,
all that is now being explained from the teacher's teaching, according to my own understanding.
A stabilized sulfur paste, not subjected to sulfur digestion,
should be taken in sixteen parts, and calcined diamond in one part.
It should be ground for three days with the juices of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>.
He should cook it in a tortoise apparatus and take it out after one <s>puṭa</s>.
Having ground it for one <s>yāma</s> with the previous juices, he should heat it in a <s>puṭa</s> as before.

children.text: evaṃ saptapuṭaiḥ pakvo yāmaṃ mardyaśca tairdravaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, cooked with seven <s>puṭas</s>, it should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> with those juices.
For one day he should cook it in a distillation apparatus over a gentle fire.

children.text: punarmardyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ yāvadūrdhvaṃ na gacchati ||
children.translated_text: It should be ground again and cooked again, until it no longer goes upward.
When it remains in the lower apparatus, then it is red mercury.
One part red mercury, two parts essence of black mica,

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇasya ca bhāgaikaṃ sarvaṃ mardyaṃ dināvadhi
children.translated_text: and one part <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should all be ground for a day.
With the milks of <s>vajrī</s> plants, that lump should be sealed and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
It should be ground again and cooked again, in this way fourteen times.

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṃśena nāgasya vedhe datte ca kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: When a transmutation dose of one sixteenth is given to lead, it becomes gold.
It becomes richly endowed with divine appearance, an excellent ornament for the gods.
With the juices of <s>śāka</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and <s>koraṇṭa</s>, and with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil,
he should grind lead powder for a day and cook it enclosed in a sealed container.
It should be ground and cooked again and again, precisely with a proper <s>gajapuṭa</s> firing.
When perfected by forty <s>puṭas</s>, it becomes divine gold.
<s>Rasaka</s>, saffron, <s>tuttha</s>, and the dung of a young calf,
yellow mica and poison in equal parts should be ground for a day with the juices of <s>mātuluṅga</s>.

children.text: marditaṃ chāyayā śuṣkaṃ madhunā saha kalkayet ||
children.translated_text: After it has dried in the shade, one should make it into a paste with honey.

children.text: tena nāgasya patrāṇi liptvā śoṣyāṇi chāyayā
children.translated_text: With that, sheets of <s>nāga</s> (lead) should be smeared and dried in the shade.
Placed in a blind crucible and smelted, it should then be quenched in the juice of <s>śāka</s> leaves.
One should take it out afterward, openly smelt it again,
quench it with the juices of <s>śāka</s> leaves, and again smelt and quench it.
Thus one should do it seven times, and then make sheets again.
One should smear them as before, dry them, seal them, and smelt them as before.
The quenching and the smelting should be carried out seven times.
Thus one should perform the whole process seven times, beginning with the coating and ending with smelting.
That <s>nāga</s> becomes divine, with a luster equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
Burnt limestone should be placed in sour gruel.
Having stirred it in an earthen vessel, one should carefully let it stand day and night.
One should collect that clear liquid, and with those liquids grind the buds of <s>śāka</s>.
With that paste one should thoroughly grind powder of <s>nāga</s>.
At the end of a <s>yāma</s>, one should dry it in the sun, then grind and dry it again.
Thus one should do it ten times; then that ball should be placed
inside a moist stem of <s>śāka</s>, and sealed with the same material.

children.text: mṛdā liptaṃ tu tacchuṣkaṃ samyaggajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: After it has been coated with clay and dried, one should cook it well in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: samuddhṛtya bhavet pītaṃ stambhanaṃ cāsya kathyate ||
children.translated_text: When taken out, it becomes yellow; its fixation is now described.
First one should wash <s>bhūnāgas</s>, together with living organisms, with cow urine.
Having added an equal amount of <s>sauvīrāñjana</s> to these, one should grind them thoroughly.
After one day with buffalo urine, one should take out the ball that has formed.
From that, oil should be carefully obtained by means of a <s>pātāla-yantra</s>.
Into that oil, the previous <s>nāga</s>, or else purified <s>nāga</s>,
should be thrown again and again after being melted, twenty-one times.
That <s>nāga</s> becomes divine, with a luster equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
Powder of purified <s>nāga</s> and an equal amount of <s>bhūnāga</s> powder
should be treated with the juices taken from the flowers of <s>śāka</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and <s>koraṇṭa</s>.
With whatever of those juices is available, one should grind it thoroughly for one day.
Placed in a blind crucible, it should be smelted, and then made into powder.
Ground and smelted as before, one should do this twenty-one times.
It becomes divine gold; that <s>nāga</s> is an ornament for the gods.
From one <s>pala</s> of purified <s>nāga</s>, a well-rounded crucible should be made.
One should put one <s>pala</s> of purified mercury into it, and two <s>palas</s> of sulfur.

children.text: tāṃ mūṣāṃ mṛṇmaye pātre dhārayedātape khare ||
children.translated_text: That crucible should be set in an earthen vessel under the fierce sun.
For one day with citron water, and for one day with the juices of <s>kākamācī</s>,
and also for one day with the juices of <s>kāsamarda</s>, and one day with fluids from <s>dhattūra</s>,
in this order one should subject it to these infusions in the heat for four days.
After removing everything from the earthen vessel so that nothing at all is lost,
one should grind <s>karañja</s> seed with fluids from <s>dhattūra</s>.
With that same material, one should smear the inside of the crucible to a thickness of one finger.

children.text: pūrve piṇḍaṃ kṣipettatra palaikaṃ cātha gandhakam
children.translated_text: One should place the earlier lump there, and then one <s>pala</s> of sulfur,
and put into it five <s>niṣkas</s> of the liquid of <s>bhūnāgas</s>.

children.text: vidhāya lepakalkena tato mūṣāṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: After applying the coating paste, one should then seal the crucible.
For one day in the ground, one should cook it with a fire of cow-dung cakes.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out and place it in the crucible as before.

children.text: lepaṃ gandhaṃ ca bhūnāgaṃ pūrvavacca puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: The coating, the sulfur, and the <s>bhūnāga</s> should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> as before.
In this way the sulfur, well prepared, should be digested until it is twentyfold.

children.text: sārdhaṃ paladvayaṃ tālaṃ rasakaṃ cāpi tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: Two and a half <s>palas</s> of <s>tāla</s>, and <s>rasaka</s> in the same amount,

children.text: palaikaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ piṣṭvā dvidhā kuryāttrayaṃ pṛthak
children.translated_text: and one <s>pala</s> of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should be ground; making the three separately into two portions,
one should place them inside a glass bottle, and then add half the <s>tālaka</s>.
Then <s>rasaka</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and afterward the previously perfected mercury, again

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ rasakaṃ tālaṃ kramād dadyāt punastrayam ||
children.translated_text: one should add <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, and <s>tāla</s>, the three in sequence.
The mouth of the glass bottle, heated by a lamp, should be wrapped with its own covering.
Or, having stopped it with a glass stopper and with clay mixed with salt,
one should coat the bottle with clay everywhere to a thickness of one finger.

children.text: tāṃ śuṣkāṃ bhūdhare yantre kṣiptvā pūrvaṃ ca kharparam ||
children.translated_text: When it is dry, one should place it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, and first place a potsherd there.

children.text: dattvā mṛdā lipetsaṃdhiṃ deyaṃ gajapuṭaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After sealing the joint with clay, one should again give it a <s>gajapuṭa</s> firing.

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ samuddhṛtya baliṃ pūjāṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out and perform an offering and worship.
With one sixty-fourth part, one should penetrate molten copper.
It becomes gold, rich in beauty; this is declared to be a perfected procedure.
Ten <s>palas</s> of sulfur and twenty-one of mercury,
and five <s>palas</s> of oil produced from the seeds of <s>mahākāla</s> should be taken.
Having sealed everything in an oily pot, one should cook it over a gentle fire,
with a coating of black-gram paste, so that no smoke escapes.

children.text: sa sūto jāyate khoṭaścandrārke drāvite kṣipet
children.translated_text: That mercury becomes a solid <s>khoṭa</s>; it should be thrown into molten silver or copper.
By means of that, in a thousandth part, divine gold is produced.
Mercury and sulfur in equal parts should be ground for one day with the juices of <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: marditaṃ tena tāmrasya patralepaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: With that, one should make a coating on sheets of copper.
After heating it in a blind crucible and taking it out, then again
one should extract the juice of the tender leaves of the <s>śāka</s> tree.

children.text: taddrave pūrvaśulbaṃ tu drāvitaṃ drāvitaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Into that liquid one should cast the earlier copper, melting it again and again.
Doing this one hundred times, the gold becomes divine.
Yellow sulfur powder should be steeped for three days in the juices of <s>nāgavallī</s>.

children.text: bhāvitaṃ tena tāmrasya patralepaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: With that, one should make a coating on sheets of copper.
When dry, one should seal it and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> with good forest cow-dung cakes.
It should be ground with bark of the <s>śāka</s> tree and the juices of red <s>aśvamāraka</s>.
The sheets of the earlier copper should be smeared with this paste.
Having sealed them, one should smelt them with intense fire; when this has been done one hundred times,
that copper becomes gold, with a brilliance equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
Powder of the root of <s>kāñcanī</s>, orpiment, realgar,
borax, and <s>mākṣika</s> in equal parts should be ground for three days with the juices of <s>vāsā</s> flowers.
With that one should smear a well-purified copper vessel.
It should be heated slowly over a gentle fire, and the dried coating should be applied.
It should be heated again and smeared again; in this way it should be done carefully seven times.
Then it should be smelted with intense fire, and it becomes good gold.
Orpiment, heated, <s>darada</s>, <s>kunaṭī</s>, and mercury in one and a half parts:
having placed them in a mortar, one should grind them for three days with the juice of <s>kākamācī</s>.
With that one should smear sheets of sun-metal and moon-metal, and cook them in fire in an earthen pan.
It becomes gold superior to copper, a strong substance for travelers.
One <s>pala</s> of purified mercury should be ground with the juices of <s>jvālāmukhī</s>.
At the end of the day one should put into it one quarter part of killed mica.
One quarter part of copper powder and one quarter part of <s>phullatorikā</s>
should all be ground with the juices of <s>jvālāmukhī</s> for seven days.
That ball should be sealed in a diamond crucible and smelted with intense fire.
Of that ingot take one part, and four parts of purified copper.
It should be placed in a blind crucible and smelted; after removing it, then again
it should be melted in an open crucible and quenched in oil produced from <s>putrajīva</s>.
Then it should again be melted; one should do this twenty-one times.

children.text: jāyate kanakaṃ divyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: It becomes divine gold; there is no need for doubt about this.
Sulfur should be thoroughly impregnated with the juices of white <s>palāśa</s> fruit.

children.text: śatavāraṃ prayatnena śoṣyaṃ peṣyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: For one hundred times, carefully, it should be dried and ground again and again.
For one hundred times, carefully, one should smear sheets with it,

children.text: samyak śuddhasya tāmrasya ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: sheets of thoroughly purified copper, and, after sealing them, cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
After removing them, one should smelt them again, and then make them into sheets.
They should be smeared again, cooked again, and repeated again in order.
Doing this twenty-one times, the gold becomes divine.
There should be twelve parts of silver and sixteen parts of copper.

children.text: āvartya kārayetpatraṃ liptvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: One should melt them together and make a sheet; after smearing and sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
This should be done sixteen times with extracts of <s>mahindī</s> leaves.
One should triturate mercury, sulfur, and realgar in parts increasing successively.
For one day with <s>aṅkola</s> oil, and in the same sequence as before,

children.text: liptvā ruddhvā dhamedgāḍhaṃ punaḥ patraṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: after smearing and sealing it, one should smelt it intensely and again make it into sheet.
It should be smeared again and cooked again, until the bronze comes to an end.
It becomes gold of eightfold color; there is no need for doubt about this.
There is an herb called <s>karuṇī</s>, which arises in the rainy season.
It has blue flowers and white leaves, and is very mucilaginous and full of sap.
Its juice should be poured into purified mercury while it is being smelted,
and while it is placed in a diamond crucible, for as long as seven days.

children.text: jāyate kanakaṃ divyaṃ rasa eva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The mercury itself becomes divine gold; there is no doubt.

children.text: palaṃ sūtaṃ palaṃ gandhaṃ kṛṣṇonmattadravais tryaham ||
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of mercury and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur should be ground for three days with the juices of black <s>unmatta</s>.

children.text: marditaṃ vajramūṣāyāṃ ruddhvā vaktraṃ pidhāya ca
children.translated_text: After placing it in a diamond crucible, sealing it, and closing its mouth,
at the end of the day one should remove it, grind it in the same way, and cook it.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaṃ kuryānmṛto bhavati vai rasaḥ
children.translated_text: One should do this for seven days; the mercury is indeed killed.

children.text: tadrasaṃ pannagaṃ svarṇaṃ candrārkair veṣṭayet kramāt ||
children.translated_text: That mercury, together with lead, gold, silver, and copper, should be wrapped in sequence.

children.text: samāṃśaṃ cāndhitaṃ dhāmyaṃ divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam
children.translated_text: Smelted in equal parts in a blind crucible, it becomes divine gold.
The mercury crucible is in the middle of a pit, and fire is everywhere in the outer trench.
This is called the wheel-apparatus by those who know the meaning of all the treatises.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ rasakaṃ tulyaṃ rasakārdhaṃ ca saindhavam
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> and <s>rasaka</s> are equal, and rock salt is half the <s>rasaka</s>.
They should be ground for one day with citron fruits and cooked for one day in an earthen vessel.
It should be cooked on the hearth until it becomes the color of saffron.
Mixed with sugar and honey, that paste should be ground for one day.
Then it should be cooked in an earthen pan, combined with cow's milk.
Stirring it for one day, one should take it down and smear
purified copper sheets, and after sealing them, smelt them with intense fire.
Then, made into sheets, it should be smeared and smelted in the same way with strong fire.

children.text: ityevaṃ ca punaḥ kuryātpītavarṇaṃ bhavettu tat
children.translated_text: Thus one should do it again; then it becomes yellow in color.
Very red realgar should be steeped for three days with <s>muni</s> flowers.

children.text: anayā pūrvaśulbaṃ tu patraṃ kṛtvā pralepayet
children.translated_text: With this, the earlier copper should be made into a sheet and smeared.
Smelted in a blind crucible, it should be thrown into <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil.

children.text: ityevaṃ tu tridhā kuryāddivyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam
children.translated_text: Doing this three times, it becomes divine gold.
By this very method one should color <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.
It becomes divine gold, with a brilliance equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
One <s>pala</s> of purified mercury and one <s>karṣa</s> of sulfur
should be placed in a greased mortar, soaked with the juice of <s>devadālī</s>.
It should be ground with the fingers of the hand; a sulfur paste is produced.
Take one part of <s>dhānyābhraka</s> and eight parts of purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury);
combined with <s>kuṇḍagolaka</s>, by grinding it becomes a <s>piṣṭikā</s> (paste).
These two pastes should be ground for one day with liquids produced from citron;
and for three days one should grind them with a decoction of <s>palāśa</s> root.

children.text: brahmamūlaṃ guḍaṃ guñjām ūrṇā ṭaṅkaṇakaṃ samam
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmamūla</s>, jaggery, <s>guñjā</s>, wool, and borax should be equal;
having ground them and mixed them with honey, one should smear the previous lump.

children.text: ruddhvā tīvrāgninā dhāmyaṃ khoṭo bhavati tadrasaḥ
children.translated_text: After sealing it, it should be smelted with intense fire; that <s>rasa</s> becomes an ingot.
It should be cooked in an open crucible; glass and borax should be added.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ śodhyaṃ yāvadbhavati nirmalam
children.translated_text: In this way it should be purified again and again until it becomes clear.

children.text: tataśca prakaṭaṃ dhāmyaṃ dattvā nāgaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then it should be smelted openly, adding lead again and again.
Thus one should make the serpent-metal, lead, enter the king of <s>rasa</s> in threefold quantity.
With black <s>abhraka</s> cooked in <s>puṭas</s>, one should color that ingot in sequence.
While it is being smelted in a crucible, again and again a hundred times,

children.text: dattvā dattvābhrakaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rañjito jāyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: by adding black <s>abhraka</s> repeatedly, it certainly becomes colored.
With one thousandth part of that very substance, the moon-metal and sun-metal become gold.
There is a stabilized sulphur paste that is free from sulphur digestion.
One should grind one <s>pala</s> of it for one day with the juices of citrons;
afterward, for three days, with decoctions of <s>brahma</s>; jaggery and borax equal to it
as well as wool and <s>guñjā</s> should be added to it, and everything should be ground together.
One should make a pill dried in the shade and smelt it after placing it in a great fire.
Then one should purify that ingot with white borax and glass;
one should purify it by smelting alone, and the ingot becomes clear.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ kuṭilaṃ gandhaṃ pratikarṣaṃ pralepayet
children.translated_text: One should smear that curved ingot with sulphur, one <s>karṣa</s> at a time.
Placed in a blind crucible, it should be smelted until only the ingot remains.
By this ordered procedure, after quenching tin, in sixfold quantity,

children.text: tato gandhaṃ ca nāgaṃ ca vāhayet ṣaḍguṇaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then one should again make sulphur and lead enter it, sixfold in quantity.
One <s>pala</s> of copper powder, combined with <s>siddhacūrṇa</s>,

children.text: ruddhvā taṃ ca dhamet khoṭaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ tena mardayet ||
children.translated_text: should be sealed and smelted into an ingot; with that one should grind sulphur.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; in this way, fourteen times.
With this, the ingot, melted as before, should be combined gradually.
As long as it has the color of saffron, so long it should be colored by adding again and again.

children.text: tataḥ svarṇaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca khoṭaṃ tulyaṃ pṛthakpṛthak ||
children.translated_text: Then gold, sulphur, and the ingot should each be equal, separately.
Then, after sealing, one should smelt it intensely until only the ingot remains.
In this way gold joined with sulphur should be made to enter in threefold quantity.

children.text: punaḥ svarṇena tulyena samāvartaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: Again one should make a fusion with an equal quantity of gold;
then again with twice as much gold, and afterward with three times as much.
Mercury that has thus been passed through three times pierces in a thousandth proportion.

children.text: drutaṃ śulbaṃ na saṃdeho divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Melted copper, without doubt, becomes divine gold.
The ingot that was previously purified should be fused with an equal amount of gold.
Then, after making it into fine powder, one should place it in three times as much purified mercury.
After putting it in and sealing it in a crucible, one should steam it with a gentle fire.
It melts within the womb of that very mercury; it should be steamed carefully for that long.
Alternatively, in a <s>dolikāyantra</s> one should steam the melted mercury.
With a hundredth part of this, one should smear white gold.
For three days in a <s>dolikāyantra</s>, wrapped with leaves of <s>arka</s>,
one should steam it with sour gruel; placed in a blind crucible, it should be smelted.
The gold becomes rich in appearance, the supreme raiser of the sixfold color-quality.
One should take one part of the purified mercury-ingot,
while the gold should be sixteen parts; placed in a blind crucible, it should be smelted.
By the ordered procedure as before, the <s>rasagarbhaka</s> preparation should pierce it.
By a hundredth part of that very substance, it becomes of sixfold quality as before.
One should grind <s>dhānyābhra</s> with the latex of <s>arka</s> for one <s>yāma</s> and then seal it.
It should be cooked in the <s>puṭa</s> called <s>kapota</s>; it should be ground again and cooked again.
When cooked in this way with twenty <s>puṭas</s>, that <s>abhraka</s>, in a sixteenth part,
should be added to purified mercury inside the belly of a fired crucible.
First, after sealing it with liquids from <s>arka</s> leaves, it should be steamed for three days.
With chaff-fire, carefully, one should then take it out and put it back.

children.text: tasminnabhraṃ dravaṃ caiva dattvā tadvatpacet tryaham ||
children.translated_text: Having added <s>abhraka</s> and liquid to it, one should cook it in the same way for three days.
Thus one should digest <s>abhraka</s> in mercury until the <s>abhraka</s> becomes equal to it.
With the juice of <s>tilaparṇī</s>, that mercury and <s>abhraka</s> again
should be ground in a heated mortar until it becomes a ball.
Separately, with an equal quantity of mercury, one should make a sulphur paste.
There is a stabilized sulphur paste that is free from sulphur digestion.

children.text: tatpiṣṭī svarṇapiṣṭī ca rasābhraṃ golakaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: That paste, the gold paste, and the mercury-mica ball likewise,
the three in equal parts, should be ground for one day with liquids from cotton.

children.text: tadgolaṃ vartulaṃ kṛtvā vastre baddhvātha śoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made that ball round, one should bind it in cloth and then dry it.
One should cook it with sulphur oil until it resembles saffron.
When it has formed, one should take it out, grind it with juices of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>,
and with an eighth part of that very substance one should smear sheets of lead.
Having ground cotton leaves, one should smear them with that paste.
Then, after sealing the lead sheets, one should cook them in the <s>puṭa</s> called <s>bhūdhara</s>.
After taking them out, they should again be smeared with an eighth part of that substance.
Having smeared them with cotton-leaf paste, sealed them, one should cook them in a <s>puṭa</s>.
By turning them above and below, one should take them out after a day and night.
Having again added an eighth part, he should grind the previous paste,
for a day with liquids from <s>nirguṇḍī</s>; he should smear that ball on the outside.
With a paste of cotton leaves he should seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
In this way, again and again, he should perform grinding and cooking in a <s>puṭa</s>.
That <s>nāga</s> (lead) is killed, saffron-colored, by ten <s>puṭas</s> in sequence.

children.text: anena cāṣṭamāṃśena drutaṃ śulbaṃ tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: With an eighth part of this he should quickly transmute <s>śulba</s> (copper).

children.text: tena śulbena tāraṃ tu aṣṭamāṃśena vedhayet
children.translated_text: With that copper, in turn, he should transmute <s>tāra</s> (silver) with an eighth part.
The copper becomes gold, an excellent ornament for the gods.
This is especially the coloring of <s>nāga</s>, the transmutation of copper, mercury, sun-metal, and moon-metal.
It should be accomplished by people who partake of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and happiness, for the protection of the whole world.
The procedure for <s>piṣṭikā</s> with metallic essences, stabilization, and coating with <s>nigaḍa</s>,
as well as the melting that produces bound <s>khoṭa</s> and the whole method of transmutation, is described.
It should be ground with divine herbal liquids in a heated mortar for three days.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ tato gharme śoṣyaṃ svacchaṃ samāharet ||
children.translated_text: Then the purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should be dried in the sun and collected when clean.

children.text: svarṇanāgārkakāntaṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca rūpyakam
children.translated_text: Gold, <s>nāga</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>kānta</s>, sharp iron, tin, and silver,
or else the essence of mica, any one desired, should first be powdered.
Equal to the previous mercury, it should be ground with an acidic liquid for one <s>yāma</s>.
One from the group of eight <s>mahārasas</s>, equal to the mercury, should be added.
With divine herbal liquids alone, after it has been sweated for a <s>yāma</s> in the fierce sun,
he should grind it firmly in a mortar; that ball is wrapped in cloth.
He should cook it for a day in sulfur oil; then he should take it out from the cloth.
This is known as the <s>piṣṭi</s>-ball. Now another opinion is stated.

children.text: pūrvaṃ yanmarditaṃ sūtaṃ tasya bhāgatrayaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: The mercury that was previously ground should be in three parts.
There should be two parts of <s>nāga</s>, or any single desired metal; into that he should add <s>nāga</s>.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kuṇḍagola</s>, and a divine herbal liquid

children.text: mardyaṃ yāmatrayaṃ khalve chāyāśuṣkaṃ tu golakam ||
children.translated_text: should be ground for three <s>yāmas</s> in a mortar; the ball should be dried in the shade.
Having made it, he should bind it in cloth and cook it for a day in sulfur oil.
After taking it out from inside the cloth, this becomes the <s>piṣṭi</s>-ball.
Now the auspicious <s>nigaḍa</s> for this <s>piṣṭi</s>-ball is described.
<s>Guggulu</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, and <s>saindhava</s> salt equal to them
should be ground with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>; this is a very excellent <s>nigaḍa</s>.
<s>Pālāśa</s>, seeds of <s>kokilākṣa</s>, and likewise <s>saindhava</s> salt,
ground with liquids from <s>unmatta</s> and <s>nīlī</s>, should be an excellent <s>nigaḍa</s>.
Mica, <s>saindhava</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, sand-clay, and iron dross,
ground with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, become a <s>nigaḍa</s> at the end of a <s>yāma</s>.
Seeds of <s>vākucī</s>, <s>brahma</s>, and <s>dhattūra</s>, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
crow-dung, plantain bulb, orpiment, sulfur, and realgar,
<s>guggulu</s>, the five salts, <s>gojihvā</s>, and <s>kokilākṣaka</s>,
bitter <s>kośātakī</s>, <s>nīlī</s>, poison-nut, and <s>indravāruṇī</s>,
the two kinds of cumin, crab bone, mixed with women's menstrual fluid and urine,
should be ground firmly for two <s>yāmas</s> with the milks and oils of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>.

children.text: vyastaṃ vātha samastaṃ vā nigaḍo'yaṃ mahottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Either separately or all together, this is a very excellent <s>nigaḍa</s>.
With one of these, that ball should be coated to the measure of a finger's breadth.
In a crucible of the size of a <s>bilva</s> fruit, he should put a little salt below.

children.text: liptaṃ golaṃ kṣipet tasyām ūrdhvaṃ loṇaṃ ca dāpayet
children.translated_text: He should place the coated ball in it and have salt put above it.
Having sealed the joint with clay and salts, and with burnt conches all around,
the coating of the crucible should be made, and he should have it dried in the shade.
In a cow-dung fire by day and night, or for three nights with a husk fire,
he should sweat it with gentle heat; afterward, having taken it out, he should coat it.
With proper <s>nigaḍa</s>-paste he should seal the previous crucible.

children.text: ūrdhvādho lavaṇaṃ dattvā ruddhvā lepyā ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Having put salt above and below, he should seal it and coat it as before.
When it is dried in the shade, he should blow it strongly; the <s>rasa</s> becomes <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā dhamed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Adding <s>sauvīra</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and glass again and again, he should blow it firmly.

children.text: tacchuddhaṃ jāyate khoṭam abhīkṣṇaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That becomes purified <s>khoṭa</s> repeatedly; there is no doubt about this.
Thus he should separately make <s>piṣṭikā</s> with all metallic essences.
By the methodical sequence stated before, that <s>rasa</s> becomes <s>khoṭa</s>.
There should be two parts of gold and three parts of mercury.
He should make the <s>piṣṭi</s> as before, and should purify the <s>khoṭa</s> in the same way.
Having thus made the <s>piṣṭi</s>-<s>khoṭas</s>, he should apply them everywhere.
That <s>khoṭa</s>, equal to gold, should be made to undergo <s>samāvarta</s>.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, magnetic stone, realgar, and sulfur should be in equal quantities.
He should grind them for a <s>yāma</s> with earthworms and make pills the size of chickpeas.

children.text: eṣā viḍavaṭī khyātā yojyā sarvatra jāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: This is known as the <s>viḍa</s>-pill, to be used everywhere in digestion.
He should drive each one into the mercury while it is being blown again and again.
In this way he should digest ten times as much gold by that sequence.
In the belly of an open crucible, the <s>vaḍavānala</s> fire swallows it.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, cinnabar, sulfur, <s>rājāvarta</s>, coral,

children.text: śilā tutthaṃ ca kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ samaṃ cūrṇaṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: realgar, blue vitriol, and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> should be prepared as an equal powder.
Together with the yellow and red groups and with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil,
he should soak it repeatedly for five days in the heat of the sun.
The digested mercury-<s>khoṭa</s>, joined with this paste,
should be placed in the middle of a sand-pot and inside a covered saucer-seal.

children.text: tridinaṃ pācayeccullyāṃ kalkaṃ deyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: He should cook it for three days on a stove; the paste should be applied again and again.

children.text: rañjito jāyate sūtaḥ śatavedhī na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mercury becomes colored and capable of hundredfold transmutation; there is no doubt.

children.text: tāre tāmre bhujaṅge vā candrārke vātha yojayet
children.translated_text: It should be applied to silver, copper, lead, or to <s>candrārka</s>.
Divine gold is produced, with the brilliance of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
The paste-mass and fine powder should be impregnated with woman's menstrual blood.

children.text: dinatrayaṃ khare gharme śuktau vā nālikeraje ||
children.translated_text: For three days, in fierce heat, it should be kept in a shell or in a coconut shell.
<s>Mīnākṣī</s>, banana corm, white and red <s>punarnavā</s>,
and <s>śilājatu</s> together with sea-salt should be ground with woman's menstrual blood.
The mass, impregnated as before, should be placed in that pellet.
The mass, impregnated as before, should be inserted as a pellet into that.

children.text: mukhaṃ tatpiṇḍakalkena ruddhvā piṇḍaṃ ca bandhayet
children.translated_text: Having closed its mouth with the paste of the pellet, he should bind up the pellet.
Wrapped in birch bark, he should cook it for three days in a <s>dolāyantra</s> with sour gruel.
The mercury at once becomes liquefied; then he should again add to it,
as before, an impregnated mass, a quarter part of the mass, again and again.
He should place it in the previous pellet and cook it in the same way for three days.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punardeyaṃ piṣṭiṃ khoṭaṃ subhāvitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the well-impregnated paste-mass should be added again and again.

children.text: āroṭasya samaṃ yāvattāvad deyaṃ drutaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Until it is equal to the <s>āroṭa</s>, it should be added; then it becomes liquefied.
Ginger, radish, dry ginger, garlic, asafoetida, <s>mākṣika</s>,
the three alkalis, the five salts, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and sulfur,

children.text: amlavargeṇa saṃyuktaṃ mardyaṃ piṇḍaṃ tu kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: mixed with the class of sour substances, should be ground, and a pellet should be prepared.

children.text: tasmin piṇḍe yathā pūrvaṃ drutaṃ sūtaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: In that pellet, as before, he should make the mercury liquefied.
<s>Mārjārī</s>, <s>ceśvarī</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, <s>kukkuṭī</s>, and <s>kṣīrakandaka</s>:
within a pellet made from these, he should impregnate the mercury as before.
This is known as liquefied mercury, and it should be used in all operations.
Two parts of liquefied mercury, one part of essence of black mica,
and one part of essence of <s>rasaka</s> should be ground for a day with the liquids of black <s>unmatta</s>.
He should make a ball; after adding calcined diamond, a quarter part of the ball,
he should grind the whole for one <s>yāma</s> with <s>unmatta</s> water.
Then, after sealing it, he should cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> with one <s>puṭa</s> and take it out.

children.text: pūrvāṃśaṃ drutasūtaṃ tu taṃ dattvā mardayetpunaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having added the previous portion of liquefied mercury, he should grind it again.
With liquids produced from <s>dhattūra</s>, he should grind it for one <s>yāma</s>, and cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> in the same way.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptavārāṇi sūtaṃ dattvā punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, after adding mercury again and again seven times,
he should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; that mercury becomes ash.
With one hundredth part of that very ash, he should grind it together with honey.
He should blow sheets made of <s>candrārka</s> in a sealed crucible.
They become gold, rich in appearance and with the brilliance of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
That ash, with an equal amount of sulfur, should be blown in a sealed crucible.

children.text: vedhyaṃ tena śatāṃśena nāgaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Lead is to be transmuted with one hundredth part of that; it becomes gold.

children.text: rasakābhrakayoḥ sattvaṃ drutaṃ sattvaṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: The essences of <s>rasaka</s> and mica, and the liquefied essence, each in equal parts,
one <s>pala</s> of the three together, should be combined with the perfected powder.
It should be ground for one day with <s>unmatta</s> liquids, enclosed, and blown.
That mass, powdered, should be ground with citron acid and sulfur.
After sealing it, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; in this way, thirteen times,
grinding and grinding it, he should cook it sealed, successively with forest cow-dung cakes.
With one hundredth part of <s>candrārka</s>, and with this substance smeared with honey,

children.text: liptvā ruddhvā dhamedgāḍhaṃ svarṇaṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: having coated it, sealed it, and blown it strongly, it becomes excellent gold.
Essence of <s>rasaka</s> and mica, liquefied mercury, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
all this in equal measure should be ground for a day with liquids of black <s>unmatta</s>.
Having made a pill dried in the shade, he should blow it when it has been put into a great fire.
Afterward he should purify that mass with white glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
Then, having melted it together with an equal amount of gold, he should digest it.

children.text: pūrvā viḍavaṭī yā tu tāmekaikāṃ pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: The previous flux pills, one by one, should then be added.
He should blow it in an open crucible until only mercury remains.
Then he should carry it three times with purified gold.

children.text: vedhyaṃ tena śatāṃśena śulvaṃ bhavati kāñcanam
children.translated_text: With one hundredth part of that, copper is to be transmuted; it becomes gold.
One part of liquefied mercury should be placed in the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus.
Four times as much purified lead as that, separately melted,
should be placed in that apparatus; he should collect the mass that is produced.
An equal amount of purified <s>mākṣika</s> should be mixed with it and thoroughly ground.
For a day, with liquids produced from <s>dhattūra</s>, he should cook it in an earthen vessel.
Until it becomes the color of saffron, he should take it out from the hearth.
One <s>pala</s> of this very substance, combined with the perfected powder,
when sealed and blown, becomes a mass; he should grind it for a day with honey and sour liquids.
Having sealed it, he should cook it with forest cow-dung cakes and honey <s>puṭas</s>.
With this, mixed with honey, he should coat sheets of silver.
Having sealed them, they should be blown; after being coated again three times, they become gold.
They become richly endowed with divine appearance; this is true, spoken by <s>Śaṃkara</s>.

children.text: mākṣikasya tvabhāve tu vaikrāntaṃ vātra yojayet ||
children.translated_text: If <s>mākṣika</s> is unavailable, then <s>vaikrānta</s> may be used here.

children.text: drutasūtaṃ hiṅgulaṃ ca kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ gandhakaṃ śilā
children.translated_text: Liquefied mercury, cinnabar, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, sulfur, and orpiment
should be, in order, one, two, three, four, and five <s>palas</s>.
All that should be ground with cow bile for four <s>yāmas</s>.
Purified sheets of lead should be coated with an equal measure of it.
After sealing them, he should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; having taken them out, he should then grind them
with an equal amount of the previous paste, seal them, and cook them in a <s>puṭa</s> in the same way.

children.text: evaṃ śatapuṭaiḥ pakvo mriyate pannago dhruvam
children.translated_text: Thus, cooked with one hundred <s>puṭas</s>, the lead is certainly killed.
With one hundredth part of this, through transmutation of silver, gold is produced.
Or with that killed <s>nāga</s> (lead), ground with acid, one should smear it.

children.text: samāṃśaṃ svarṇapatraṃ tu ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: A gold sheet of equal measure should be sealed and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
The <s>nāga</s> should be added again and again; in this way three <s>puṭa</s> cookings should be given.

children.text: anena mṛtahemnā tu drutaṃ tāraṃ tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: With this killed gold one should pierce molten <s>tāra</s> (silver) quickly.
When perfected by a thousandth part of it, that becomes divine gold.
With the liquids of <s>tumbaru</s> creeper, grain-mica should be steeped through seven heatings in the sun.
Afterward one should make it into a <s>khoṭa</s> mass in one <s>karṣa</s> of molten mercury.
One should throw in a <s>māṣa</s> measure of this and triturate it in a heated mortar.
Having put it in a crucible shaped like a cow's teat, one should cook it with a gentle fire.

children.text: vālukāyantramadhye tu jīrṇe vāpaṃ punaḥ kṣipet
children.translated_text: In the middle of a sand-apparatus, when it has been digested, one should again add a quenching portion.
Thus one should digest an equal amount; the mercury becomes bound as a <s>khoṭa</s>.
Of this bound substance, one <s>māṣa</s>; of purified gold, half a <s>māṣa</s>;
and of purified mercury, half a <s>māṣa</s>: all should be triturated together.
For three days one should smear with this paste, using the acids of citron.
One <s>karṣa</s> of lead sheets should likewise be treated with the liquids of <s>vṛścikālī</s>.
After smearing them, one should cook them for three days in a distillation apparatus.
After grinding it for the period of a day.
With this one should smear one <s>karṣa</s> of silver sheets.
As before, one should cook them for three days in the distillation apparatus.
With this very substance one should pierce molten copper with a thousandth part.
Divine gold is produced, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.
Purified mercury should be ground for three days with the milk of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>.
In a heated mortar, indeed, one should grind that.
In a cow-dung fire by day and night for three days, or in a husk fire,
after taking it out, it should again be ground; then, sealed in the same way, it should be cooked.

children.text: tadvanmardyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ mriyate pāṇḍuro rasaḥ
children.translated_text: It should be ground in the same way and cooked again; the pale mercury is killed.
Ginger, <s>tuvarī</s>, rock salt, <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil, and honey,
together with <s>amlavetasa</s>: with these one should grind that mercury for a day.
One should bind it into a ball in cloth and cook it for three days in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
In the midst of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil that mercury becomes bound.

children.text: tadrasaṃ hāṭakaṃ nāgaṃ samaṃ ruddhvā dhamed dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: That mercury, gold, and <s>nāga</s> should be sealed in equal parts and smelted strongly.
That <s>khoṭa</s> mass should be made into fine powder, with molten mercury equal to the powder.
Ground with acids, it becomes a ball; it should be steamed for a day with sour gruel.
There should be three parts of sulfur, <s>suvarcala</s> equal to the sulfur,

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakaṃ tu bhāgaikaṃ sarvaṃ stanyena peṣayet ||
children.translated_text: and one part of black mica; all should be ground with breast milk.
The ball smeared with this should be placed in a blind crucible and smelted.
As long as mercury remains, it should be smelted again and again.
After adding the former powder again, it should be digested in the same way, gradually.
In this way, until the gold has been digested to three times its amount.
Having melted it together with gold and passed it through the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations,
one should pierce silver and copper with it; from a hundredth part it becomes gold.
Gold equal to the <s>piṣṭī-khoṭa</s> should be taken, and <s>pannaga</s> equal to the gold.
Magnetic iron and mica essence should each be half the amount of the <s>pannaga</s>.
Having combined them into one, one should smelt them until only gold remains.
After adding a <s>viḍa</s> pellet, one should carry out the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations.
With a hundredth part of this, copper becomes gold.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca mākṣikam
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, magnetic iron, sharp iron, and <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca samaṃ ruddhvā dhamed dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: and the essence of black mica should be sealed in equal parts and smelted strongly.
That <s>khoṭa</s> mass should be made into fine powder; then molten mercury equal to one quarter
should be added and ground with acids until it becomes a ball.
Of the ball, four parts, and one part killed diamond,
should be ground in a heated mortar for one day with the liquids of <s>kanyā</s>.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; at the end of the day one should take it out.

children.text: tanmadhye drutasūtaṃ ca punaḥ kanyāsu mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Into it one should add molten mercury and again grind it in <s>kanyā</s> juice.

children.text: pūrvavad bhūdhare pacyādevaṃ deyaṃ tu saptadhā
children.translated_text: It should be cooked in the <s>bhūdhara</s> as before; in this way it should be given seven times,

children.text: drutasūtaṃ krameṇaiva mardanaṃ ca puṭaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: with molten mercury in sequence, and with grinding and <s>puṭa</s> heating likewise.
That ash, equal in amount to sulfur, should be placed in a blind crucible and smelted.

children.text: jāyate khoṭabaddhaṃ tu rañjanaṃ cāsya kathyate ||
children.translated_text: It becomes bound as a <s>khoṭa</s>; its coloring process is now described.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrasattvaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca dvaṃdvaṃ melāpayed drutam
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica and tin should be combined as a molten pair.
Smelted in equal parts in a blind crucible, it becomes that <s>khoṭa</s> mass.
One <s>pala</s> of that <s>khoṭa</s> should be combined with the perfected powder.
One should grind it with sulfuric acid, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
It should be ground again and cooked again; in this way fourteen times.

children.text: anena pūrvakhoṭe tu drāvitaṃ rañjayet kramāt ||
children.translated_text: With this, the earlier <s>khoṭa</s> when melted should be colored gradually.
One should color it one hundred times; it becomes like saffron.
Having melted it together with gold, one should carry out the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations.
With a thousandth part of that very substance one should pierce <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.

children.text: candrārkaṃ tāpyaśulbaṃ tu divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: Silver, copper, heated metal, and copper become divine gold.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ śulbaṃ samaṃ cūrṇya vajramūṣāndhitaṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: Sharp iron and copper should be powdered equally and smelted in a diamond crucible with its mouth closed.
One <s>pala</s> of that <s>khoṭa</s> should be combined with the perfected powder.
One should grind it with sulfuric acid, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
It should be ground again and cooked again; in this way fourteen times.

children.text: taddeyaṃ drāvite svarṇe śatavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: That should be added to molten gold, repeatedly, one hundred times.
Then it becomes a cooked seed; it should be mixed with molten mercury equally for a day.
One should grind four parts of it with an acid mixture.
Thus one part of diamond should be triturated for a day in a heated mortar,
with the fluids of <s>kanyakā</s>; after sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace.

children.text: drutasūtaṃ punastulyaṃ dattvā mardyaṃ puṭe tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after adding an equal amount of liquefied mercury, it is to be ground and placed in a <s>puṭa</s>.
In just this way liquefied mercury should be applied seven times, up to the end of the <s>puṭa</s> treatments.

children.text: tatastaṃ mardayed amlai ruddhvā mūṣāṃ puṭettathā ||
children.translated_text: Then one should triturate it with sour liquids, seal the crucible, and subject it likewise to a <s>puṭa</s>.
Again it should be ground and again cooked, three hundred and sixty times.
A <s>puṭa</s> should be given carefully; it becomes shining like cinnabar.
For molten lead and silver, in the proportion of one thousandth part,
penetration should be applied; it becomes gold, excellent and fit for divine ornaments.
Sulfur, made into a fine powder, should be impregnated with sour chickpea gruel.
This is to be done carefully one hundred times, and seven times with <s>strīpuṣpa</s>.
Into melted mercury, combined with a little camphor,
one should add the sulfur in heat and evaporate it in a copper mortar.
Camphor and sulfur, a little at a time, again and again,
should be added for three times seven days; a sulfur paste is produced.
The seed of <s>kaṭukośātakī</s>, combined with the tuber of <s>cāṇḍālī</s>,

children.text: stanyena peṣitaṃ tulyaṃ piṣṭīṃ tena pralepayet ||
children.translated_text: ground in equal amount with breast milk: with that one should smear the paste.
On the outside clay should be smeared all around to the measure of a finger-width.
When it has dried, one should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace, turning it above and below.

children.text: jāyate stambhitaṃ golaṃ samuddhṛtyātha taṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: A fixed globule is produced; having taken that out, then again

children.text: tulyāṃśe saṃpuṭe hemni liptvā mūṣāndhitaṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: after smearing it onto gold in an equal enclosing fold, sealed in a crucible, one should smelt it.
With one eighth part of this, one should cause penetration in silver.
That silver becomes divine, with a brilliance equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
Or else, take the fixed globule without enclosing it in gold:
four parts of that and one part of calcined diamond
should be ground with <s>kanyakā</s> juices for one day; then again,
after it has been sealed, one should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace until four watches have passed.
Having removed it, one should again add to it the same previous portion of the former mercury.
After adding it, it should be ground and put into a <s>puṭa</s> as before; thus one should do it twenty-one times.
Into that, one <s>pala</s> of ash, and mercury and sulfur,
placed in a blind crucible and smelted, form that ingot together with an equal amount of lead.

children.text: pannagasya samaṃ svarṇaṃ trayāṇāṃ triguṇaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Gold equal to the lead should be added, and three times the amount of the three should be thrown in.
When melted, all that should be ground with the group of sour liquids.
At the end of the day, after sealing it in a diamond crucible, it should be smelted carefully.

children.text: jāyate pannagaṃ svarṇaṃ trayotthaṃ jāyate kramāt ||
children.translated_text: The lead becomes gold; what arises from the three is produced in due order.
One should refine the gold three times, and then pierce silver and copper with it.
With one thousandth part of that very substance, the gold becomes divine.

children.text: hemārkatīkṣṇacūrṇaṃ ca samaṃ ruddhvā dhamed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Powders of gold, copper, and sharp iron should be sealed in equal parts and smelted strongly.
One part of that ingot and three parts of liquefied mercury
should be ground with sulfur and sour liquid; after sealing, one should cook it properly in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Again it should be ground and again cooked, thus fourteen times.
With one hundredth part of this, one should pierce pale gold.
It becomes divine gold through sprinkling with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil.

children.text: baddhe drute rasavare varahemni jīrṇe dṛṣṭo mayā daśaguṇaḥ sukhasādhyalābhaḥ
children.translated_text: When the excellent <s>rasa</s> is bound and melted, and excellent gold has been digested in it, I have seen a tenfold gain that is easy to accomplish.

children.text: vajre mṛte gaganasattvayute narāṇāṃ tatraiva bhūriguṇitaṃ phalamasti satyam ||
children.translated_text: When calcined diamond is joined with the essence of mica, for people there is indeed a greatly multiplied result in that same operation.

children.text: kārpāsārkakarañjadhūrtamunijair bhallātaguñjāgnijaiḥ snugvajrīpayasā ca sūraṇabhavairdrāvaiśca mūlaiḥ phalaiḥ
children.translated_text: With juices, roots, and fruits produced from <s>kārpāsa</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>dhūrta</s>, <s>muni</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, <s>agni</s>, and with the milks of <s>snuk</s> and <s>vajrī</s>, and those from <s>sūraṇa</s>,

children.text: takrāktairbahutaptakharparagataṃ vaṅgaṃ niṣiñcyānmuhur yāvatpañcadinaṃ tad eva vimalaṃ vāde sadā yojayet ||
children.translated_text: tin placed on a much-heated potsherd, smeared with buttermilk, should be quenched repeatedly for up to five days; that same purified tin should always be used in alchemical transmutation.
Or else tin powder, together with black grams and fruits from <s>bhallāta</s>,
should be ground equally in a mortar for a day, combined with <s>bhallāta</s> oil.

children.text: tatpiṇḍaṃ māhiṣe śṛṅge kṣiptvā ruddhvā mahāpuṭe
children.translated_text: That lump should be placed in a buffalo horn, sealed, and cooked in a great <s>puṭa</s>.
After removing it from that, one should again grind it in the same way.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā kuryāt khoṭaṃ pākaṃ ca mardanam
children.translated_text: Thus one should perform the making of the ingot, the cooking, and the trituration seven times.
That tin, freed from impurity, should be used in the operation of fixation.
The essence of sharp stone should be thrown, melted, into molten tin.
With a sixty-fourth part it certainly attains fixation.
White mica, white glass, borax, and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpikā</s>,

children.text: viṣaṃ ca tulyatulyāṃśaṃ cūrṇaṃ bhāvyaṃ trisaptadhā ||
children.translated_text: and poison, each in equal part, should be powdered and impregnated twenty-one times
with juices of <s>kākamācī</s> and with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, in fierce sunlight.

children.text: drute vaṅge pradātavyaṃ prativāpaṃ ca secayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be added to molten tin, and at each casting it should be sprinkled.
Again and again, seven times, with oil produced from <s>putrajīva</s>,
that tin becomes divine silver, lasting as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
White mica, white glass, poison, rock salt, and borax
should be ground for a day with <s>snuhī</s> latex; a sheet of white tin
should be smeared with a paste amounting to one quarter part, placed in a blind crucible, and smelted.
Taking it out, one should melt it on the ground and sprinkle it with the previous oil.
The smearing and sprinkling of the sheet and the rest should be done seven times.
That tin becomes silver, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: samaṃ tālaṃ śilāṃ piṣṭvā devadālyā dravairdinam
children.translated_text: Equal amounts of orpiment and realgar should be ground with juices of <s>devadālī</s> for a day.
With the juices of <s>īśvaraliṅgī</s> too, one should triturate it for one day.

children.text: nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ samaṃ drāvyaṃ taccūrṇaṃ palapañcakam
children.translated_text: Lead and tin should be melted in equal measure; that powder should be five <s>palas</s>.
With an amount equal to the previous paste, he should mix it, seal it, and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ pācyaṃ pūrvakalkena saṃyutam
children.translated_text: In this way it should be cooked again and again, combined with the previous paste.
When perfected by sixty <s>puṭas</s>, it becomes a supreme agent for stabilizing tin.
It should be applied in a one-hundredth part; by transmutation it fully makes silver.
Mercury and orpiment, one part each, and human skull, two parts,
should be combined with poison equal to all of them, and with the whole plant of red <s>citraka</s>.
Powder equal to the poison should be added, after being impregnated with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>.
For a full month, by day and night, its casting should be made in a sixteenth part.

children.text: datte vāratrayaṃ vaṅge tāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: When it is given three times to tin, the result is fine silver.
The herb named <s>gorambhā</s> should be ground with human urine.
Having made two lumps with it, he should place on top of one of them
powder of the three alkalis, and over that, powdered tin.

children.text: kṣāratrayaṃ tato dattvā piṇḍaṃ tasyopari kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after adding the three alkalis, he should place the other lump on top of it.
After sealing the opening, he should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> and take it out when it has cooled of itself.
He should do this three times; it becomes fine silver.

children.text: vasante jāyate sā tu gorambhā pītapuṣpikā
children.translated_text: That <s>gorambhā</s> is born in spring and has yellow flowers.
In the middle half of its stalk it is like white cotton.
Or, if that is absent, he should use <s>vasantapuṣpikā</s>.

children.text: bālā nāma samākhyātā kaṭyā dhūlīsamā tathā ||
children.translated_text: It is known by the name <s>bālā</s>, and at its waist it is likewise dust-colored.
White <s>palāśa</s> flowers, dried in the shade, should be powdered.
They should be impregnated twenty-one times with ewe's milk.
That powder should be given in a sixteenth part to melted tin.
It becomes silver rich in beauty, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
That flower and orpiment should be ground with ewe's milk.
Its casting should be given in a sixteenth part to melted tin.
It becomes silver rich in beauty, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
After those flowers have been impregnated with buttermilk three times seven times,
he should coat sheets of tin with that paste.
Placed in a sealed crucible, it should be blown; he should do this three times seven times.
That silver becomes divine, bestowing the fruits of <s>dharma</s> and desire.
Mercury, <s>mūṣakapāṣāṇa</s>, alum, and blue collyrium
should all be ground for a day with juices of <s>agasti</s> leaves.
Then, having placed it in a vessel, he should cook it with the flame of a lamp.
As the <s>agasti</s> leaf juice is absorbed, he should add more again and again.
At the end of the day, after taking it out, he should apply it to melted tin.
With a thirtieth part of that, the silver becomes fit for the adornment of gods.
With silver he should alloy diamond, just as it is alloyed with gold.

children.text: asya dvaṃdvasya bhāgau dvau tribhāgaṃ śuddhapāradam
children.translated_text: Of this alloy there should be two parts, and purified mercury three parts.
He should grind it with acid until it becomes a ball.
The whole plant of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> should be ground with a woman's breast milk.
With this he should wrap the ball, and outside it with a binding enclosure.
Steaming and the other operations, up to blowing, should be done as in the case of gold paste.
He should coat that <s>khoṭa</s> mass with the milks of <s>uttarāvāruṇī</s>.

children.text: mūṣāmadhye nidhāyātha tāraṃ dattvā samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Then, having placed it in a crucible and added silver in equal measure each time,
and after adding a <s>viḍa</s> pill, he should blow it until only mercury remains.
In this way it should be heated again and again twenty-one times.

children.text: dattvā samaṃ samaṃ jāryaṃ tridhā tāreṇa sārayet ||
children.translated_text: Adding equal measures, he should digest it, and conduct the <s>sāraṇa</s> three times with silver.
This very substance should be cast into melted tin in a thousandth part.

children.text: tad vaṅgaṃ jāyate tāraṃ vaṅgastambhaṃ śivoditam ||
children.translated_text: That tin becomes silver, a stabilizer of tin, as declared by <s>Śiva</s>.
One part of red mercury and one part of powdered conch,
together with the essence of white mica, should properly make up two parts.
And one part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>; all this, for three days,
should be thoroughly ground with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>, thus for fourteen turns.

children.text: anena śatamāṃśena drutaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca vedhayet
children.translated_text: With a hundredth part of this he should transmute melted tin.
It is stabilized; there is no doubt here, and it becomes fine silver.
Just as a fine paste-mass is produced from gold and mercury,
so, in the same way, he should make a paste-mass from silver and mercury.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ tāravaṅgaṃ ca sattvaṃ śvetābhrajaṃ samam
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s> mass, silvered tin, and the essence produced from white mica should be taken in equal measure.
It should be digested with the addition of a <s>viḍa</s> pill until only the <s>khoṭa</s> remains.

children.text: jāraṇena tridhā sāryaṃ drute śulbe niyojayet
children.translated_text: Through digestion it should be conducted three times, and then applied to melted copper.
With a hundredth part of that, it becomes silver; this was spoken by <s>Śambhu</s>.
Melted mercury and powdered sharp iron, in equal parts, should be placed in a heated mortar.
It should be ground with juices of <s>ṭeṇṭūchallī</s> until it becomes a ball.
For four parts of the ball, there should be one part of calcined diamond.
It should be ground for a day in a heated mortar with fresh juices of <s>ṭeṇṭūchallī</s>.
After being sealed, it should be cooked in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; at the end of the day he should take it out.

children.text: pūrvatulyaṃ drutaṃ sūtaṃ dattvā mardyaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Having added melted mercury equal to the previous amount, he should grind it as before.
He should cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> as before; in this way, seven times in sequence,

children.text: drutasūtaṃ pradātavyaṃ mardanaṃ ca puṭaṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: melted mercury should be added, with grinding and <s>puṭa</s> heating in due order.

children.text: anena ṣoḍaśāṃśena drutaṃ vaṅgaṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: With a sixteenth part of this he should transmute melted tin.
It becomes divine, rich in beauty, silver resembling jasmine and the moon.
There is another method for the tin to which a sixteenth part has been added.

children.text: tattulyaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ ruddhvā dhmāte khoṭaṃ prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it with sulfur equal to that, when it is blown, a <s>khoṭa</s> mass is produced.
That <s>khoṭa</s> mass and powdered sharp iron should be prepared in equal parts.

children.text: tābhyāṃ tulyaṃ drutaṃ sūtaṃ tatsarvaṃ taptakhalvake ||
children.translated_text: Melted mercury equal to those two should be taken; all of that is to be placed in a heated mortar.
He should grind it with the liquids of <s>ṭeṇṭuja</s> until it becomes a ball.
Then, after sealing it, he should cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> for a day and night and take it out.

children.text: pūrvāṃśaṃ drutasūtaṃ ca dattvā tadvacca mardayet
children.translated_text: Having added the previous portion and liquefied mercury, he should grind it in the same way.
After sealing it, he should subject it to a <s>puṭa</s> in the same way; thus he should do it twenty-one times.
It is to be blown in a sealed crucible; that mercury becomes a solid mass.
He should grind it with an equal amount of sharp-iron powder and, after sealing it, blow it.

children.text: anena kramayogena tīkṣṇaṃ deyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: By this ordered procedure, sharp iron should be added again and again.

children.text: yāvat saptaguṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ dattvā dattvā dhameddhi tat ||
children.translated_text: Until seven times as much sharp iron has been added, he should add it repeatedly and blow it.
Afterward he should refine that mass with alkali alone, three times in sequence.
With one hundred-thousandth part of that very substance, he should cause the transmutation of tin.
It becomes fine silver, with the appearance of conch, jasmine, and the moon.
Having ground <s>madhusaṃjīvanī</s> with the urine of a donkey,

children.text: saptāhaṃ tena mūtreṇa bhāvayitvā tataḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having impregnated it for seven days with that urine, then again
he should grind mercury with that same substance in a heated mortar for three days.
Having added an equal amount of sulfur, he should blow it in a sealed crucible.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ jāyate divyaṃ rañjanaṃ tasya kathyate
children.translated_text: That mass becomes excellent; its coloring process is described.
Tin and the essence of white mica, combined through paired fusion,
should be powdered in a crucible, that mass being one <s>pala</s> in measure.
He should grind it with sulfurous acid, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
It should be ground again and cooked again; in this way, fourteen times.
With this he should color the previous mass seven times.
As with tin and mica, so again with lead and mica
he should color it seven times and make it into a fine powder.
Combined with liquefied mercury, it should be melted according to the previous procedure.
He should carefully digest the melted silver by <s>dolāsveda</s>.

children.text: triṣaḍguṇaṃ yadā tāraṃ jīrṇaṃ bhavati pārade
children.translated_text: When eighteenfold silver has become digested in the mercury,
he should perform three <s>sāraṇā</s> refinements and transmute with a thousandth part.
Molten copper becomes silver, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
The essence of white mica, magnetic essence, and iron,

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ ca vaikrāṃtaṃ kadambaṃ nāgameva ca ||
children.translated_text: tin, silver, <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>kadamba</s>, and also lead,
in equal parts, when blown in a sealed crucible, should be powdered as a mass.
It should be thoroughly ground with liquefied mercury and sour liquid until it becomes a ball.
For four parts of the ball there should be one part of calcined diamond.
He should grind it in a heated mortar for one day with the liquids of <s>kanyakā</s>.
Then, after sealing it, he should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s>; thus he should do it twenty-one times.
Having added an equal amount of sulfur, he should blow it in a sealed crucible.
After combining it with silver and refining it through three <s>sāraṇās</s>,
he should apply one thousandth part of it upon molten copper.

children.text: tattāraṃ jāyate divyaṃ puṭe datte na hīyate ||
children.translated_text: That becomes excellent silver; when put into a <s>puṭa</s>, it is not diminished.

children.text: vajreṇa sāritaṃ yattu sūtabhasma purā kṛtam
children.translated_text: The mercury ash that was previously made and refined with diamond,
with that very substance ground with acid, he should coat silver leaf fourfold.
After coating it, sealing it, and cooking it in a <s>puṭa</s>, he should take it out and then grind it.

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ bhasmasūtaṃ ca dattvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having added a quarter part of ash-mercury, he should seal it and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ catuḥpuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ tattāraṃ mriyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: Thus, cooked with four <s>puṭas</s>, that silver is certainly killed.

children.text: tenaiva ṣoḍaśāṃśena drutaṃ tāmraṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: With one sixteenth part of that, he should transmute molten copper.

children.text: athavā drāvitaṃ vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: Or else, molten tin becomes fine silver.

children.text: tāravanmārayed vaṅgaṃ tena tāmraṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: He should kill tin in the same way as silver; with that he should transmute copper.

children.text: tattāraṃ jāyate divyaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśe na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That becomes excellent silver with a sixteenth part, without doubt.
He should grind <s>rājī</s>, equal to purified mercury, with the liquids of <s>kanyakā</s>.
For three days in a heated mortar; that mercury should then be placed inside an earthen saucer.
It should be cooked on a hearth with fierce fire and sprinkled with the liquids of <s>kanyakā</s>.
At the end of three days he should take it out, and add four times as much rock salt.
Having added it, he should grind for one <s>yāma</s> and cook it in a distillation apparatus.
After four <s>yāmas</s> he should take it out and wash it with sour gruel.
He should collect what is situated below; the mercury becomes pure and auspicious.
This mercury, killed tin, white mica essence, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
poison too, each in equal parts, and four times as much essence of <s>tāla</s>,
should be ground with the latex of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> in a mortar for three days.

children.text: tadvaṭīḥ kācakūpyāntaḥ kṣiptvā kūpīṃ mṛdā lipet
children.translated_text: He should make pills of it, place them inside a glass bottle, and coat the bottle with clay.
In a perforated sand-bath apparatus, he should cook the pot with gentle fire.

children.text: śuṣke drāve mukhaṃ ruddhvā śanairyāmāṣṭakaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: When it is dry and melted, he should seal the mouth and cook it gently for eight <s>yāmas</s>.

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ samuddhṛtya drutaṃ śulbaṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, he should take it out and transmute molten copper.
With a sixty-fourth part, it becomes fine silver.

children.text: palaṃ sūtaṃ palaṃ tālaṃ tālasthāne'thavā śilā
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of mercury and one <s>pala</s> of <s>tāla</s>; or else realgar may be used in place of <s>tāla</s>.
It should be ground with the liquids of black <s>unmatta</s>; at the end of three days he should take it out.
Sealed in a diamond crucible, it should be cooked for one day in a <s>cakrayantra</s>.
It should be ground again and cooked again; when this has been done seven times,
that killed substance should be wrapped successively with equal amounts of tin, silver, and <s>arka</s>.

children.text: ruddhvā tīvrāgninā dhāmyaṃ tāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: Sealed and blown with intense fire, it becomes fine silver.
Three parts of purified mercury and one part of copper leaf
should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> in woman's breast milk; a silver paste is produced.
He should grind the seeds of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s> with woman's breast milk.
With that very substance he should coat the paste and seal it in a diamond crucible.
He should cook it for one day in a <s>bhūdhara</s>; after coating it again, he should cook it.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā pācyaṃ piṣṭīstambho bhaved dṛḍhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way it should be cooked seven times; the fixation of the <s>piṣṭī</s> becomes firm.
With one thirty-second part of that very substance, he should cause transmutation in copper.

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ ca kṣipettāraṃ raupyaṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: And he should add one tenth part of silver; it becomes fine silver.
<s>Śṛṅgāṭī</s> and powdered conch should be ground with cow urine and sour gruels,

children.text: piṣṭvā tatkalkamadhye tu taptaṃ taptaṃ niṣiñcayet ||
children.translated_text: and into the middle of that paste he should repeatedly plunge the heated metal.
When the copper sheet has become fully digested, he should take it out,
place it in a crucible together with honey, ghee, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and blow it.

children.text: tārārdhena samāvartya śuddhaṃ tāraṃ bhavettu tat ||
children.translated_text: After smelting it with half as much silver, it then becomes purified silver.
The alkalis of <s>arka</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and plantain, stirred with an acid liquid,

children.text: tena liptaṃ tāmrapatraṃ dhāmyaṃ mūṣāgataṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be smeared on a copper sheet; it should again be put in a crucible and blown.

children.text: patraṃ kṛtvā pralipyātha tadvad dhāmyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After making it into a sheet, he should smear it and blow it again and again in the same way.
Doing this seven times, it becomes suitable as foil for the alchemical operation.
Or else he should quench thoroughly heated copper sheets
one hundred times in salt and sour gruel; it becomes as described before.
Alkali made from the root of <s>palāśa</s> and alum should be ground with an acid liquid.
Having smeared copper sheets with it, he should melt them and again make them into sheets.
Doing this seven times, it becomes fit for making foil.
Well-purified <s>tālaka</s>, mercury, and sea salt should be taken in equal measure.
He should grind them for two <s>yāmas</s> in a mortar and cook them in a new vessel.
He should stir over a gentle fire until the substance becomes drawn together.
Then he should separately grind sea salt in an amount equal to the <s>tālaka</s>.
When the crackling sound has ceased, he should collect it.
When it has been powdered, he should then place half the salt in an earthen apparatus.
On top of that he should put the previous three ingredients, and in the middle the remaining half of the salt.

children.text: kṣiptvā mṛllavaṇaiḥ saṃdhiṃ liptvā śuṣkaṃ vicūrṇayet ||
children.translated_text: After placing it there, he should seal the joint with clay and salt, dry it, and pulverize it.
For up to twelve <s>yāmas</s>, on the top of the vessel, with a strong fire,
he should collect the essence adhering above, resembling killed mercury.
Tying it in cloth on the end of a rod, he should apply it for <s>kunta-vedha</s>.
Into molten copper, in a tenth part, he should pour it and cast it into curds and cow-dung.
After smelting it with half as much silver, it becomes like conch, jasmine, and the moon.
