In this way he should grind lead with one eighth part of magnetic iron.
In a crucible smeared with the paired coating, he should blow all the powder strongly.
When that mass is melted with an equal amount of silver, it takes on the state of silver.
Copper, iron, magnetic iron, and lead, powdered, should be blown as before.
After smelting it with half as much silver, it becomes fine silver.

children.text: tāraṃ baṃgaṃ tathā kāṃsyaṃ samaṃ drāvyaṃ saṭaṅkaṇam
children.translated_text: Silver, tin, and bronze should likewise be melted in equal parts with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
One part of this mass and three parts of purified copper

children.text: samāvartya kṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ same tāre vimiśrayet
children.translated_text: should be smelted together into a mass and mixed with an equal amount of silver.
That silver becomes pure, resembling snow, jasmine, and the moon.
He should take five parts of powder of <s>muṇḍaloha</s>.
Inside it he should place one part of the essence of <s>tāla</s>.

children.text: ṭaṃkaṇaṃ śvetakācaṃ ca ūrdhvaṃ dattvā nirodhayet
children.translated_text: Having placed <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and white glass above it, he should seal it.

children.text: dhmātaṃ tīvraṃ tu saṃcūrṇya punaḥ sattvaṃ tu dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: When it has been strongly blown, he should pulverize it and again add the essence.

children.text: kācaṃ ṭaṃkaṇakaṃ dattvā mūṣāyāṃ cāndhitaṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: After adding glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, he should blow it sealed in a crucible.

children.text: ityevaṃ pañcadhā kuryāt sattvaṃ dattvā punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should do this five times, adding the essence again and again.
An equal amount of purified silver, and calcined tin ash raised from the killed metal,

children.text: tritayaṃ tu samāvartya tāmrāre drāvite same ||
children.translated_text: these three should be smelted together into an equal amount of molten copper.

children.text: vedho deyo daśāṃśena bījaṃ pādaṃ ca yojayet
children.translated_text: The transmuting agent should be applied in a tenth part, and a quarter part of seed should be added.
That silver becomes splendid, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ mṛtaṃ baṃgaṃ śvetābhraṃ ṭaṃkaṇaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, killed tin, white mica, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should be equal,
and <s>mūṣakapāṣāṇa</s> should be four times the amount of the five.
He should combine purified <s>tālaka</s>, firmly ground with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>.
All of it should be ground for three days and placed in a glass bottle.
When the bottle has been properly coated with clay and cloth and thoroughly dried, he should then cook it.
He should cook it in a perforated sand-bath apparatus, with the bottle set upon it.

children.text: śuṣke drave mukhaṃ ruddhvā loṇamṛttikayā dṛḍham
children.translated_text: When the liquid has dried, he should seal the mouth firmly with salt and clay.
Then he should cook it with a fierce fire for sixteen <s>yāmas</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, he should take it out and break the glass bottle.
Having collected the essence of <s>tāla</s> adhering at the top, he should use that for transmutation.
With one sixteenth part he should treat copper and cast it into curds and cow-dung.

children.text: tataḥ śuddhena tāreṇa samāvartya samena tu
children.translated_text: Then he should smelt it with an equal amount of purified silver.
That silver becomes pure, resembling snow, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: tālakaṃ sābuṇītulyaṃ piṣṭvā bhraṣṭaṃ ca kharpare ||
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>tālaka</s> equal to <s>sābuṇī</s>, he should roast it on a potsherd.
He should keep stirring it over a light fire until it becomes black.
After putting it into a clay-coated glass bottle, he should again put into it
roasted salt, one tenth the amount of the <s>tālaka</s>.
Cooking it as before in a sand-bath apparatus, he should collect the essence.
After adding a quarter part of the essence of <s>sābuṇī</s>, he should grind it and cook it again.
As before, he should cook the bottle in a sand-bath apparatus for eight <s>yāmas</s>.

children.text: tatsattvaṃ tilatailaṃ ca samāṃśe piśite pacet
children.translated_text: That essence and sesame oil, in equal portions, should be mixed and cooked.
He should stir it in an iron vessel until the oil is digested.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā pācyaṃ samaṃ taile punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: In this way it should be cooked seven times, again and again with an equal amount of oil.

children.text: tadvacca saptadhā pācyaṃ siddhaṃ kathakena samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: In the same way it should be cooked seven times with an equal amount of <s>kathaka</s>; it is perfected.
With one sixty-fourth part, he should transmute molten copper.
One should pierce it by the <s>kuntavedha</s> method and cast it into curd mixed with cow dung.

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ dāpayed bījaṃ tāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: One should add seed equal to a quarter part; the <s>tāra</s> (silver) becomes excellent.
Borax should be added in a tenth part to purified <s>tāla</s> (orpiment).
It should be ground in a mortar for three days with ewe's milk and likewise with ghee.
For a day it should be ground with castor oil and placed in a bottle.
It should be cooked in the apparatus as before; when the liquid has dried, it should be put in.
At the end of sixteen <s>yāmas</s>, the essence should be taken; it is great and very soft.
With one sixteenth part of just that, one should pierce copper.

children.text: tārārdhaṃ ca drutaṃ drāvyaṃ śuddhaṃ bhavati pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: And half as much <s>tāra</s>, melted and liquefied, becomes purified as before.
After melting six <s>niṣkas</s> of copper, one <s>niṣka</s> of <s>ākhupāṣāṇa</s> should be used.
It should be added by the <s>kuntavedha</s> method; with half the seed it becomes <s>dala</s> (sheet metal).
<s>Tālaka</s> (orpiment), borax, mineral alkali, and alkali from <s>apāmārga</s>
should be ground equally with <s>vajrī</s> latex in a mortar for four <s>yāmas</s>.
With half of this, one should smear copper sheets.
When it has been placed in a blind crucible and smelted, and this has been done three times,
then, melted together with half as much <s>tāra</s>, it becomes purified <s>tāra</s>.
One should obtain the oil of one among <s>guñjā</s>, cotton, and <s>śigru</s>.
Molten copper should be cast into that oil three times seven times.

children.text: ṣaḍaṃśaṃ dāpayed bījaṃ śuddhatāraṃ bhavettu tat
children.translated_text: One should add seed in a sixth part; it becomes purified <s>tāra</s>.
Then one should melt it in a crucible smeared with <s>śigru</s> root.
One should stir it with water made from the ashes of <s>arka</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and plantain.
The water filtered through cloth should be taken when clear, and then dried in the sun.
The salt dried from it should then be carefully collected.

children.text: raupye vā yadi vā svarṇe drāvite śatamāṃśataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Into melted silver, or else into melted gold, in a hundredth part,
that same substance should be added as the casting additive, and it should be cast into sesame oil.

children.text: ityevaṃ tu tridhā kuryād atyantaṃ mṛdutāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should do it three times; it becomes extremely soft.
One should collect the hooves and horns of horses, cows, and buffaloes.
By merely adding that powder as the casting additive, it becomes extremely soft.

children.text: gajadantasya cūrṇaṃ vā śuṣkaṃ vātha nṛṇāṃ malam
children.translated_text: Or the powder of elephant tusk, or dried human excrement,
should be added as the casting additive to hard metal; it becomes very soft and great.
Many kinds of ornaments are to be made from <s>dala</s>.
White and red roots of <s>varṣābhū</s> should be ground with sour gruel.

children.text: piṣṭvātha lavaṇaṃ kiṃcit kṣiptvā tatraiva peṣayet
children.translated_text: Then, after grinding a little salt, one should throw it in there and grind it again.
That small amount of produced <s>dala</s> should be taken out after half a <s>ghaṭikā</s>.
Rubbing it with salt and sour liquid, one should blow it in the fire and cook it again.

children.text: ityevaṃ tu tridhā kuryāt dalaṃ bhavati nirmalam ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should do it three times; the <s>dala</s> becomes stainless.
Having taken powdered <s>phaṭkarī</s> (alum), one should place it in a potsherd below and above,
putting it with the <s>dala</s>, sealing it, and cooking it properly in an elephant-<s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: ādāya rajjukāṃ baddhvā dolāyaṃtre dinaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: After taking it out, tying it with a cord, one should cook it for a day in a swing apparatus.
In a vessel of tamarind sour gruel, it becomes white like a conch.

children.text: abhinavasukhasādhyaiḥ sādhane yuktigarbhairgaditamiha susiddhaṃ stambhanaṃ śuddhabaṃge
children.translated_text: Here has been taught the well-accomplished fixation of purified tin, by procedures easy to accomplish, convenient, and full of method,

children.text: sugamamapi ca tāraṃ sūtaśulbārayogaiḥ dalam atimalahīnaṃ vārtikānāṃ hitārtham ||
children.translated_text: and also easy <s>tāra</s> through combinations of mercury, copper, and <s>āra</s>, and <s>dala</s> exceedingly free from impurity, for the benefit of practitioners.

children.text: vajreṇa hemamilitena tu rañjitena sūtena hemamilitena surañjitena
children.translated_text: With diamond joined with gold and colored, and with mercury joined with gold and well colored,

children.text: yogaiḥ susundarataraiḥ kanakādrikūṭaṃ kṛtvātha śakrapadahetumakhāṃśca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: by very beautiful combinations, after making a peak like a golden mountain, one should then perform rites leading to the station of <s>Śakra</s>.
The mouth of lodestone and <s>guñjā</s>, with sulfur twice as much as those two,
ground with woman's breast milk, should be smeared on the crucible as a joining agent for the pair.
Sulfur and hare's teeth, and likewise the mouth of <s>bhrāmaka</s>,
sour <s>vetasa</s> and <s>śilādhātu</s>: all should be ground in equal measure.
With that very crucible-smearing, the diamond pair combines fully.
Powdered dirt produced from a buffalo cow's ears and eyes, and borax,
woman's breast milk, crab bones, and <s>śilājatu</s>, each in equal measure,
having been ground, serve as a crucible-smearing by which there is joining among diamond pairs.
Bee bones and human hair, borax, and the mouth produced from <s>kānta</s>,
and the dung of a young calf should be ground with woman's breast milk.
In a crucible smeared with that paste, the diamond pair combines fully.
<s>Bhūnāga</s>, lodestone, pyrite, borax, and honey,
<s>snuk</s> latex, crab bones, glass, and <s>arka</s> latex, in equal measure,

children.text: strīstanyaiḥ peṣitaṃ sarvaṃ mūṣālepaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: should all be ground with woman's breast milk, and one should make a crucible-smearing.
Diamond-mercury placed in its midst combines fully when smelted by force.
Four parts of calcined diamond, twelve parts of gold,

children.text: nāgasya ca trayo bhāgāḥ ṣaṭ śuddhasya ca pāradāt ||
children.translated_text: three parts of lead, and six parts of purified mercury
should be combined and ground for a day with some sour liquid.
The paste should be taken up from the heated mortar and sealed.
In a crucible smeared for joining, when smelted by force, it combines fully.
One should impregnate calcined diamond with the alkalis of <s>utpalasāriṇī</s>.
After it has been purified and ground for one day, each should be made into a pill.
Three parts of mercury and four parts of gold
should be made into a paste with sour liquid, and that pill should be placed in its center.
Having wrapped that with birch bark, one should put it into a heap of grain.
After taking it out after only a fortnight, one should blow it in the former crucible.

children.text: milatyeva na saṃdeho dhāmyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It surely combines, there is no doubt, when smelted again and again.
One part of calcined diamond should be wrapped in gold leaf.
Properly, in a sixteenth part, he should place it in a crucible as before.
White glass equal in quantity to the gold, or else a human skull,
he should powder and put into it; after sealing it, he should blow it with a fierce fire.
After taking it out, glass or a human skull should again be added.
Having coated the crucible, he should blow it; thus this is to be done in seven crucibles.
Then that diamond combines with gold; in this way he should mix it again,
until the calcined diamond combines with the gold up to a quarter portion.
There should be two parts of the <s>dvaṃdvakhoṭa</s> and three parts of molten mercury.
He should grind them with an acidic medium; at the end of the day, that pellet
should be ground with the five parts of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> and with woman's milk.
With this he should pierce the pellet, and also with the outer binding.
He should carry out the operations from steaming up to combination, as in the case of gold paste.
He should grind that <s>khoṭa</s> for a short time with alkalis produced from <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>.
With that he should coat the inside of a crucible and put in an equal amount of gold.
He should blow it until it is digested, and then have gold added again.
He should digest it by this same blowing, giving <s>viḍavaṭī</s> pellets in sequence.
In this way he should digest gold until it reaches twenty times the amount.
After smelting it together with gold by the method of three <s>sāraṇā</s>s,
with that, in a thousandth part, he should transmute copper into gold.
It becomes endowed with a divine form, with a brilliance equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
The <s>dvaṃdvakhoṭa</s>, placed in a diamond-crucible, is blown with forced fire,
or washed essence from pyrite, or essence produced from pyrite,

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣipettasmindhmāte jīrṇe punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: should be added to it little by little when it is being blown and when it is repeatedly digested.
When it has become saffron-colored, then the diamond should be taken out.

children.text: lakṣāṃśena tu tenaiva sitahemaṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: With this same substance, in a one-lakhth part, he should transmute white gold.
Divine gold is produced, excellent as an ornament for the gods.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, pyrite, blue vitriol, <s>rasaka</s>, collyrium, and red ocher,
as well as <s>vimalā</s> and <s>vaiḍūrya</s>: of these, one should be taken in a half-<s>pala</s> amount.
Of lead, tin, and <s>arka</s>, one should likewise be taken, as available, in a half-<s>pala</s> amount.
Then the <s>dvaṃdva</s>-powder should be sealed and blown, placed in a diamond-crucible.

children.text: pūrvavad gaṃdhakāmlena mardyaṃ ruddhvā puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: As before, it should be ground with sulfurous acid, sealed, and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
By fourteen such <s>puṭa</s>s it becomes like the young sun.

children.text: anena vajrakhoṭaṃ tu yathāpūrvaṃ tu rañjayet
children.translated_text: With this he should color the diamond-<s>khoṭa</s> as before.
Likewise white gold is to be killed; from a one-lakhth part it becomes gold.

children.text: athavā dvaṃdvakhoṭaṃ tu sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: Or else he should make the <s>dvaṃdvakhoṭa</s> into a fine powder.
This purified <s>khoṭa</s>-powder should be blown, placed in a blind crucible.
He should grind it for a day with equal <s>āroṭa</s> juice and citrons.

children.text: vastre baddhvā dinaṃ svedyaṃ dolāyaṃtre sakāṃjike ||
children.translated_text: Tied in cloth, it should be steamed for a day in a swing-apparatus with sour gruel.
Afterwards, still with the cloth, he should cook it in sulfur-oil for the span of a day.
Then, taking it out from the cloth, he should cook it with the binding in the balance apparatus.
He should carry out the operations from steaming up to blowing as in the case of gold paste.
After taking out that <s>khoṭa</s>, he should color it; that procedure is now stated.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ śulbaṃ samaṃ cūrṇya aṃdhamūṣāgataṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: He should powder equal amounts of hard iron and copper and blow them in a blind crucible.
One <s>pala</s> of that <s>khoṭa</s>, combined with the perfected powder,

children.text: cūrṇaṃ ruddhvā dhamed gāḍhaṃ tatkhoṭaṃ mardayetpunaḥ
children.translated_text: should be sealed as powder and blown strongly; then he should grind that <s>khoṭa</s> again.
As before, with sulfurous acid, he should give it fourteen <s>puṭa</s>s.

children.text: anena pūrvakhoṭaṃ tu mūṣāmadhye ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: With this, the previous <s>khoṭa</s> should be placed in the middle of a crucible as before,
as many times as needed until it becomes saffron-colored, gradually and gently.
After smelting it together with gold and processing it by three <s>sāraṇā</s>s,

children.text: anena lakṣabhāgena drutaṃ śulvaṃ tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: with this, in a one-lakhth part, he should transmute molten copper.
Divine gold is produced; this is true, spoken by <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
One <s>karṣa</s> of molten mercury, eight <s>guñjā</s>s of gold,
and four <s>guñjā</s>s of calcined diamond should be ground for a day with the juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s>.
He should grind it in a heated mortar and cook it enclosed in a diamond-crucible.
After one <s>bhūdhara</s>-type <s>puṭa</s>, he should take it out and then grind it.
Thus, with the juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s>, in a heated mortar, for the span of a day,
he should cook it as before in a <s>bhūdhara</s>; thus he should cook it with one hundred <s>puṭa</s>s.
It becomes a red-colored ash, to be used in all formulae.
With the juices of <s>vartulapatrā</s>, or with the juices of <s>somavallī</s>,
<s>dhānyābhra</s> should be impregnated seven times; then he should begin the digestion.
In a cow-udder-shaped crucible he should place purified mercury.
The previously prepared mica, in a sixteenth part, should be put in the crucible with chickpea juices.
In the middle of a sand vessel, on the hearth, he should cook it with a gentle fire.
When the chickpea liquid has been digested in the mica, he should add it again and again.
In this way he should gradually digest mica into mercury in an equal amount.
Then the <s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be ground for a <s>yāma</s> with the juices of <s>somavallī</s>.

children.text: ruddhvā vanotpalair dadyāt kramād evaṃ puṭatrayam
children.translated_text: After sealing it, he should give three <s>puṭa</s>s in sequence with forest fuel-cakes.
For a day in the sun he should impregnate it seven times with the juices of <s>somavallī</s>.
With roots of white <s>śarapuṅkhā</s> ground with cow's milk,
made into a paste, he should coat an earthen vessel and place the mica there.
In its middle he should place mercury, and on top of it again mica.
Having first treated that vessel with <s>somavallī</s> juices, he should keep it in strong sunlight.
It acts for a long time, and <s>vyomapiṣṭikā</s>, mica-paste, is produced.

children.text: pūrvoktā gandhapiṣṭī yā stambhitā jāraṇaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: This is the previously mentioned sulfur-paste, stabilized without digestion.
Thus there are mica paste, and mica essence as the third item,
and, as the fourth, the red ash that was previously made with diamond.
These four, each in a <s>prakarṣa</s> portion, should be digested into one <s>pala</s> of mercury.
All this should be ground for a day in a heated mortar with the liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s>.
After taking it out, he should cook it in a tortoise apparatus,
and it should indeed be digested by heating with <s>puṭa</s> until only the mercury remains.
To this mercury he should add an equal portion of the pair of diamonds,
and it should be cooked by swinging-steaming until it becomes a pellet.
He should digest it in the tortoise apparatus until only the mercury remains.
In just this way, with care, the diamond-pair should be digested to six times the amount.
With that very diamond-pair he should perform the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations.

children.text: anena koṭibhāgena drutaṃ śulbaṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: With one ten-millionth part of this, he should transmute molten copper,
and divine gold is produced, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.
One part of killed diamond and sixteen parts of purified mercury
should be ground with the group of sour liquids in a heated mortar for a whole day.
Leaves of cooked seed, equal in amount, should be smeared with this,
and the smeared leaves should be wrapped with thoroughly cooked <s>bhānu</s> leaves.
Having sealed them in a covered earthen dish, he should bury it in the middle of a stove.
There he should kindle the fire for three days, little by little and gradually.
Then he should seal it in a crucible smeared with <s>nigaḍa</s>-clay,
cook it with a cow-dung fire, and take it out after a day and night.
He should grind it a little with honey; then, with that in a hundredth part,
after smearing leaves of silver and copper, he should blow them in a blind crucible.
It becomes gold rich in beauty; this is the truth spoken by <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
One part of killed diamond and one part of gold,
with three parts of molten mercury, should all be ground with breast milk.
He should bind that pellet in cloth and cook it for three days in sulfur oil.
Then he should cause it to be melted together with an equal amount of gold.
Having added a <s>viḍa</s> pellet twenty-one times,
when it has been digested to twenty-one times its amount, he should perform the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations.
With a thousandth part of that very substance, he should cause transmutation in copper.
Divine gold is produced, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ haṃsapādyā dravaiḥ samam
children.translated_text: Purified mercury and killed diamond, together with the liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s>,
should be ground in a heated mortar and taken out after three days.

children.text: bījair divyauṣadhānāṃ ca piṣṭvā mūṣāṃ pralepayet
children.translated_text: After grinding the seeds of divine herbs, he should smear a crucible with them.

children.text: tatra pūrvarasaṃ kṣiptvā ruddhvā tat kariṣāgninā ||
children.translated_text: Having put the earlier mercury preparation there and sealed it, he should cook it with a cow-dung fire.
After taking it out, he should again put an equal amount of purified mercury into it.
It should be ground with the liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s> for three days as before.
Having sealed that pellet in the previous crucible, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
This mercury becomes ash, and he should apply it in all operations.

children.text: asya tulyaṃ śuddhasūtaṃ sūtapādaṃ ca ṭaṃkaṇam
children.translated_text: An equal amount of purified mercury, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> equal to one quarter of the mercury,
should all be ground for a day with sour liquids, made into a pellet, and taken out.
The seeds of red cotton and white cotton, mustard, tamarind,
and barren <s>karkoṭakī</s> should be ground, and the pellet should be smeared with them.

children.text: ūrdhvādho lavaṇaṃ dattvā ruddhvā mūṣāṃ viśoṣayet
children.translated_text: Having placed salt above and below, he should seal the crucible and dry it.
After cooking it in a cow-dung fire for a day and night, he should take it out.
Putting that pellet into the previous paste, he should then seal it as before,
and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> for a day and night; he should do this seven times.
Then, after smearing it with that same paste, sealing it, and drying it,
he should cook it in a proper <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then he should blow it while it is in the crucible.
With a hundredth part of that very substance, he should quickly transmute silver and copper.
Divine gold is produced, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.
Alternatively, that mercury ash should be prepared joined with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
When it is blown in a blind crucible, it becomes an excellent <s>khoṭa</s> mass.
He should melt together purified gold equal to the <s>khoṭa</s>.
With that he should transmute silver and copper; as before, it becomes gold.
Diamond ash should be ground for one day with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>.

children.text: ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacyāt evaṃ śatapuṭaiḥ pacet ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; in this way he should cook it with one hundred <s>puṭa</s>s.

children.text: tattulyaṃ pāradaṃ śuddhaṃ kṣiptvā mardyaṃ dinatrayam
children.translated_text: Having added purified mercury equal to it, it should be ground for three days.
With the liquids of <s>devadālī</s> in this way, that pellet, enclosed in a blind crucible, should be heated by <s>puṭa</s>.
After taking it out from the cow-dung fire after a day and night, he should grind it,

children.text: devadālyā dravais tryahaṃ tadvadruddhvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: with the liquids of <s>devadālī</s> for three days, and then cook it in a sealed <s>puṭa</s> as before.

children.text: evaṃ daśapuṭaiḥ pācyaṃ vajratulyaṃ ca hāṭakam
children.translated_text: After it has been cooked with ten <s>puṭa</s>s in this way, gold equal to the diamond
should be added, and it should be ground for three days with the liquids of <s>kāñcanaka</s>.
By <s>puṭa</s>-cooking as before, he should cook it with ten <s>puṭa</s>s in this way.
Then he should add sharp iron powder equal to the gold.
He should grind all that with the liquids of <s>triphala</s> for three days,
and heat it by <s>puṭa</s> according to the previous procedure; thus he should cook it with ten <s>puṭa</s>s.

children.text: tīkṣṇatulyaṃ mṛtaṃ nāgaṃ dattvā sarvaṃ vimardayet
children.translated_text: After adding killed lead equal to the sharp iron, he should grind everything,
in a mortar for three days with liquids produced from <s>vāsā</s>, red <s>aśvamāra</s>, and related plants.

children.text: ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacyāt punarmardyaṃ ca pācayet
children.translated_text: After sealing it, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then it should again be ground and cooked.
After it has been cooked with ten <s>puṭa</s>s in this way, he should take it out and then grind it.
All that should be ground with the group of sour liquids for four <s>yāma</s>s.

children.text: ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacyāt punarmardyaṃ ca pācayet ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then it should again be ground and cooked.
When it has been cooked with ten <s>puṭa</s>s in this way, it becomes like vermilion.
With a hundredth part of this, one should quickly pierce silver and copper.
Or, after smearing silver and copper with it mixed with honey,

children.text: jāyate kanakaṃ divyaṃ puṭe datte na hīyate ||
children.translated_text: divine gold is produced; when it has been put into a <s>puṭa</s> (heating pit), it does not diminish.
Or one should smear leaves of silver with it mixed with honey;
with a sixty-fourth part it becomes divine gold.
Sixty-four parts of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and one part of calcined diamond
should be ground for three days with the group of sour liquids in a heated mortar.
With this very preparation one should smear three parts of gold leaf.
Then, after sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace; after removing it, one should grind it.
It is to be combined with purified king <s>sūta</s> in threefold quantity,
ground for three days with sour liquids, sealed, and then heated in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace.
It should be ground again and cooked again twenty-one times.
With a hundredth part of this, one should smear silver and copper together with honey,

children.text: liptvā ruddhvā dhamed gāḍhaṃ divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: then, after sealing it, blow strongly; it becomes divine gold.
One should smear with the previously mentioned calcined mercury ground with sour liquid.
Gold leaf four times its quantity should be sealed and cooked in an elephant-<s>puṭa</s>.
Again one should add calcined mercury to it in a quarter portion.
It should be ground with the group of sour liquids, and in the same way, after sealing, cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ catuḥpuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ mriyate hāṭakaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Cooked thus through four <s>puṭas</s>, the fine gold is reduced to ash.

children.text: tenaiva ṣoḍaśāṃśena drutaṃ tāraṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: With that same substance, in a sixteenth part, one should pierce molten silver;
or, by smearing the leaves, it becomes divine gold.
One part of calcined diamond and sixteen parts of purified mercury
should be ground for three days with the juices of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>.
Sealed inside a diamond crucible, it should be cooked for one day in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace.
After removing it, one should grind it for a day with those liquids and seal it again.

children.text: dinaikaṃ bhūdhare pacyāt tadvanmardyaṃ ca pācayet
children.translated_text: It should be cooked for one day in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace; in the same manner it should be ground and cooked.
Doing this seven times, calcined mercury is produced.
That calcined mercury, in an equal amount and enclosed in a diamond crucible, should be blown in the fire.
That becomes a divine <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot); its coloring is now explained.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ śulbaṃ samaṃ cūrṇya aṃdhamūṣāgataṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: Having powdered equal parts of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (sharp iron) and copper, one should heat them in a closed crucible.

children.text: tat khoṭaṃ siddhacūrṇaṃ tu gaṃdhakāmlena mardayet ||
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, the perfected powder, should be ground with sulfuric sour liquid.
By the sequence of procedure given before, fourteen <s>puṭas</s> should be applied.

children.text: anena pūrvakhoṭaṃ tu drutaṃ vāpyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With this, the previous <s>khoṭa</s> should be repeatedly cast into molten metal.
That ash and sulfur, in equal amount, should be enclosed in a diamond crucible and blown in the fire.
After ten repetitions, that <s>khoṭa</s> becomes saffron-colored.

children.text: svarṇena ca tridhā sāryaṃ śatavedhī bhavecca tat
children.translated_text: It should be processed three times with gold, and it becomes capable of a hundredfold <s>vedha</s> (piercing transmutation).
It should be added to molten copper; it becomes divine gold.
One <s>pala</s> of the previously mentioned calcined mercury, together with an equal amount of lead,
should be ground for one day in an iron vessel with an iron pestle.
With a gentle fire, one should grind and cook it slowly in that vessel,
until it is mixed; after removing it, one should seal it and cook it in an elephant-<s>puṭa</s>.
It should be ground with the juices of <s>vāsā</s> and cooked; this is to be done fourteen times.
Again it should be ground with cow bile, and fourteen <s>puṭas</s> should be given.

children.text: tattulyaṃ svarṇacūrṇaṃ ca dattvā pittena mardayet
children.translated_text: After adding an equal amount of gold powder, one should grind it with bile.
At the end of the day, after removing it, it is to be combined with a <s>krāmaṇa</s> agent.
With a thousandth part of that, one should pierce defective silver.
Divine gold is produced, an excellent ornament for the gods.
When tin is used in place of lead, by the sequence of procedure given before,
combined with silver powder, one should cause <s>vedha</s> in copper.
With a thousandth part, that becomes silver resembling jasmine and the moon.
With molten mercury and diamond, or with diamonds and purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury),
or with calcined mercury and diamond, or with diamonds and purified <s>rasa</s>,

children.text: divyayogavaraiḥ khoṭaṃ pūrvaṃ nānāvidhaṃ tu yat
children.translated_text: whatever <s>khoṭa</s> of various kinds was previously taught by excellent divine procedures,
that single <s>khoṭa</s> should be melted like a paste-<s>khoṭa</s>.
Molten mercury is divine, destroying death and poverty.
Now one should make the cooked seed digest in this molten mercury.
Gradually, until it is sixfold, with the <s>viḍa</s> called <s>kacchapa</s>,
by the method to be described, just as one would digest the essence of mica.

children.text: jāritaṃ tattridhā sāryaṃ pakvabījena vai kramāt
children.translated_text: When it has been digested, it should be processed three times in sequence with cooked seed.
With a ten-millionth part of this, one should pierce molten copper.
Divine gold is produced, an ornament among ornaments for the gods.
Now there is another procedure for this lord of mercury capable of crore-fold <s>vedha</s>.

children.text: viṣṇukrāntā ca cakrāṅkā kaṇṭārī caiva ciñcikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>cakrāṅkā</s>, <s>kaṇṭārī</s>, and <s>ciñcikā</s>:
taking the liquid of these, one should make a crucible-smearing.

children.text: tasyāṃ pūrvarasaṃ kṣiptvā dhamed drāvaṃ kṣipan kṣipan ||
children.translated_text: After placing the previous mercury in that crucible, one should blow it, adding the liquid again and again.

children.text: vajraṃ tatraiva dātavyaṃ dravatyeva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Diamond should be added there; it certainly melts, without doubt.
Then, after removing it from that, one should cook it for three days in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
After removing it, one should blow it openly in a crucible smeared with <s>viḍa</s>.
It surely consumes it; there is no doubt, by the fire blown intensely.

children.text: vajraṃ vā padmarāgaṃ vā jāryaṃ daśaguṇe rase
children.translated_text: Diamond or ruby should be digested in tenfold mercury.
One should prepare it with diamond-seed; the mercury becomes <s>śabdavedhī</s> (piercing by sound).
Or, when that has been killed, one should again carry out digestion and <s>sāraṇa</s>.
<s>Uccaṭā</s>, <s>mīnanayanā</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and red <s>citraka</s>:

children.text: etāsāṃ nikṣiped drāvaṃ drute mūṣāgate rase
children.translated_text: one should pour the liquid of these into the molten mercury placed in the crucible.
One should add sapphire there; it certainly melts, without doubt.
As before, by steaming and by the use of <s>viḍa</s>, one should digest it.

children.text: ityevaṃ triguṇaṃ jāryam indranīlaṃ krameṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>indranīla</s> should be digested threefold, step by step.

children.text: tadrasaṃ vaktramadhye tu yaḥ karoti narottamaḥ
children.translated_text: The best of men who places that <s>rasa</s> in the middle of his mouth
is worthy of worship by the gods of gods and rejoices in the state of a sky-goer.
By his urine and feces all metals
become gold, endowed with divine beauty. This is true, spoken by <s>Śaṃkara</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ viṣṭikhoṭaṃ parirasam aparaṃ saṃkaraiḥ khoṭabaddhaṃ jātaṃ taddrāvitaṃ vai mṛtamatha vimalaṃ svarṇarāśiṃ karoti
children.translated_text: Thus this <s>viṣṭikhoṭa</s>, another <s>parirasa</s>, bound into a <s>khoṭa</s> by mixtures, when produced, melted, and then purified and calcined, makes a heap of gold.

children.text: kiṃvā sā pakvabījaṃ grasati yadi druto jāyate koṭivedhī vajrābhraṃ ratnajātaṃ carati yadi rasaḥ khecaratvaṃ pradatte ||
children.translated_text: Or, if it consumes <s>pakvabīja</s>, it swiftly becomes a substance capable of piercing ten million; if the <s>rasa</s> operates on diamond, mica, and kinds of gems, it grants the state of a sky-goer.

children.text: lohair mahārasavarair viḍapakvabījaṃ kṛtvātha pāradavare vidhivacca jāryam
children.translated_text: After making <s>viḍa-pakvabīja</s> with metals and excellent <s>mahārasas</s>, it should then be digested according to rule in excellent mercury.
It is to be applied in every operation of <s>sāraṇa</s>; now the section on the various seeds and <s>viḍas</s> will be taught.
An equal amount of purified copper, melted, should again be coated.
With a sour paste of <s>tāpya</s>, one should blow it in the fire until gold remains.

children.text: evaṃ daśaguṇaṃ vāhyaṃ tāpyaṃ vā tutthasattvakam
children.translated_text: In this way <s>tāpya</s>, or else the essence of <s>tuttha</s>, should be fed into it tenfold.
This is known as <s>pakvabīja</s>; the gold residue should be collected.

children.text: nāgābhraṃ dvaṃdvitaṃ tulyaṃ svarṇe vāhyaṃ dviṣaḍguṇam
children.translated_text: Lead and mica, paired in equal amount, should be fed into gold twelvefold.
As before, the gold residue is to be taken; it becomes <s>pakvabījaka</s>.

children.text: svarṇaṃ pītābhrasattvaṃ ca tulyāṃśaṃ dvaṃdvitaṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: Gold and the essence of yellow mica, in equal parts and paired, should be smelted.
With an addition of <s>tāpya</s> and <s>tālaka</s>, the gold residue should be collected.
In this way the essence should be fed in tenfold; it becomes <s>pakvabījaka</s>.
The essences of <s>rasaka</s> and mica, copper, and lead, each in successive order,
should be powdered and smelted, sealed inside a crucible smeared with a pairing paste.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ mākṣikaṃ tuttham amlaiḥ piṣṭvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, with <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>tuttha</s> ground in sour liquids, should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
After taking it out, it should again be ground with sour liquids, sealed, and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ pañcapuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ drute svarṇe tu vāhayet
children.translated_text: Cooked thus with five <s>puṭas</s>, it should be fed into melted gold.
One should smelt until it is tenfold; then it becomes <s>pakvabījaka</s>.
When iron has been thoroughly heated and is being hammered, flakes of it
fall off; having collected those, this is known as iron <s>parpaṭa</s>.
Iron <s>parpaṭa</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>vimala</s> mica,
calcined copper, <s>śilāsūta</s>, <s>darada</s>, and the milks of <s>arka</s> and <s>snuhī</s>:

children.text: etaiḥ samaṃ nāgacūrṇaṃ mardyaṃ ruddhvā puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: with these, an equal amount of powdered lead should be ground, sealed, and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
It should be ground again and cooked again, for fourteen repetitions.

children.text: evaṃ śataguṇaṃ vāhyaṃ śuddhahemni dhaman dhaman
children.translated_text: Thus it should be fed a hundredfold into purified gold, smelting again and again.
That gold becomes <s>nāgabīja</s> and should be like <s>gorocanā</s>.
Into lead melted in a potsherd one should put pieces of <s>brahmabīja</s>.
Then one should kindle a fierce fire and stir it with a <s>brahmadaṇḍa</s>.
After four <s>yāmas</s>, the ash that has formed should be taken out of the vessel.

children.text: ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacyāt pādāṃśaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be sealed and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then one-fourth part of sulfur
should be added, ground with sour liquid, and cooked. Thus one should do this fourteen times.
The ash becomes red in color. One part of that should be placed in a potsherd.
Three parts of powdered <s>śilā</s> should be placed separately in a vessel.
One should take powder of the five parts of <s>vāsaka</s> and powder of <s>arjuna</s> bark.
One should collect the flowers of <s>śāka</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, <s>koraṇṭa</s>, and <s>śigrū</s>,
and <s>nāginī</s>, <s>nāgakanyā</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, and <s>ahimāraka</s>.
One part of each of all these should be placed amid the <s>śilā</s>.
With four times as much goat urine, one should make a decoction of everything.
Together with the lead substances mentioned before, it should be poured onto what is in the potsherd.
One should stir it and cook it on a hearth for as long as seven days.

children.text: yatnena mṛtanāgena vāpo deyo drutasya ca
children.translated_text: With care, an addition made from calcined lead should be given to the melted substance
and to the <s>pakvabīja</s> three times; it becomes beautifully colored and auspicious.
For leaves and seeds, especially in the fixing of a paste,
the aforementioned calcined lead should be applied in <s>uccāṭa</s> and <s>krāmaṇa</s>.

children.text: mañjiṣṭhā brahmapuṣpaṃ ca puṣpaṃ ca karavīrakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>brahmapuṣpa</s>, and the flower of <s>karavīra</s>
and the red flowers of all kinds of trees should be collected.
<s>Khādira</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, the two <s>niśās</s>, and red sandalwood

children.text: sarvaṃ lākṣārasaiḥ piṣṭvā kṣiptvā tailaṃ caturguṇam
children.translated_text: should all be ground with lac juice, and four times as much oil should be added.
One should cook it until only oil remains; in that oil one should quench
the <s>pakvabīja</s> twenty-one times. It becomes well colored and auspicious.
It should be used with <s>garbhadrāvas</s>, and likewise everywhere in <s>sāraṇa</s>.
One should digest mercury with an equal amount, and carry out <s>sāraṇa</s> with twice as much.
With three times as much of this very substance, <s>pratisāraṇa</s> should be performed.
What has undergone <s>sāraṇa</s> should be employed with <s>krāmaṇa</s> at the time of <s>vedha</s>.

children.text: vimalā tīkṣṇacūrṇaṃ ca sattvaṃ śvetābhrakasya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vimalā</s>, powder of <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and the essence of white mica,
<s>rasaka</s> and <s>tāramākṣika</s>, should be powdered in equal parts.
Tin, four times the amount of the powder, should be smelted as a joining agent for the pair.
It should be ground with a sour preparation, sealed, and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ pañcapuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ tatastāre tu vāhayet
children.translated_text: Cooked thus with five <s>puṭas</s>, it should then be fed into silver.
Smelting until it is tenfold, that silver becomes <s>tārabījaka</s>.

children.text: tāpyena mārayed baṃgaṃ yathā tālena māritam
children.translated_text: One should calcine tin with <s>tāpya</s>, just as it is calcined with <s>tāla</s>.
It should be fed thirty-twofold into silver, with <s>tāla</s> as the casting addition.

children.text: tāmrabījaṃ tu tacchreṣṭhaṃ sāraṇe rañjane hitam ||
children.translated_text: That is the best copper seed, useful in <s>sāraṇa</s> and coloring.

children.text: kuṭilaṃ vimalā tīkṣṇaṃ samaṃ cūrṇaṃ prakalpayet
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṭila</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> should be prepared as an equal powder.
The <s>khoṭa</s>, ground with sour liquid, should be blown in a crucible smeared with the alloy-mixture.

children.text: puṭitaṃ pañcavāraṃ tu tāre vāhyaṃ śanairdhamet
children.translated_text: After it has been cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> five times, it should be added to silver and blown gently.
Until it has become ten times as much, that excellent <s>tārabīja</s> (silver seed) is produced.
Tin, the essence of white mica, and the essence of silver pyrite,
the three, powdered in equal amount, should be blown in a crucible for alloying.
It should be added to silver in tenfold amount by the addition of silver pyrite.
That silver becomes a seed capable of accomplishing every operation.
With whatever white flowers are obtained, produced from various trees,
one should combine mercury in fourfold amount by adding <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil.
He should cook it until only oil remains; in that oil he should quench
the melted <s>tārabīja</s> twenty-one times.
That, when colored, becomes a coloring agent for the king of mercury.
Taking one oil produced from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>akṣa</s>, or bitter gourd,
in equal amount with frog fat,
or fat from tortoise, boar, ram, snake, leech, or fish,
one of these fats should be taken and combined with the previous oil.
A red group and a yellow group should be prepared with fourfold milk.
He should extract the liquid of each of the red and yellow flowers separately.
This is the division of the pair; the four earlier decoctions should be made.
There is also liquid from <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, and <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>.
One part of each should be combined with the former oil and fat.
Two parts should be added there, namely <s>bhūlatā</s> and <s>malatāpyaka</s>.
Of the alloy-mixers, one sixteenth part of the oil
should be added separately into it, and everything should be cooked together.
When only oil remains, it should be collected, strained through cloth, and carefully preserved.
It is renowned as <s>sāraṇātaila</s>, the oil for the operation of the king of mercury.

children.text: nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ mṛtaṃ tulyamamlena ca vaṭīkṛtam
children.translated_text: Killed lead and tin, in equal amount, should be made into pills with sour liquid.
They should be applied for the sake of <s>krāmaṇa</s> at the time of mercury's penetration.

children.text: saurāṣṭrīṃ bhāvayed gharme gavāṃ pittaiḥ tridhātataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> should be impregnated in the heat with cow bile in three stages.
Its essence should be taken as with <s>soma</s>; he should add the advancing agent to the mercury.
Realgar, poison, pyrite, dirt from a buffalo's ear,
crow dung, and donkey blood, together with <s>snuhī</s> milk, form a <s>krāmaṇa</s> agent.
Human blood, milk of <s>arka</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>bhūlatā</s>, and orpiment,

children.text: samāṃśaṃ krāmakaṃ yojyaṃ vedhakāle rasasya tu ||
children.translated_text: in equal parts, should be added as a <s>krāmaka</s> at the time of mercury's penetration.
<s>Indragopa</s>, poison, lodestone, human blood, and <s>snuhī</s> milk,
calamine, cinnabar, and oil should all be ground together.
The <s>krāmaka</s> should be applied by casting in and smearing at the time of penetration.
Mercury, grain-mica, essence, crow dung, and orpiment,
the eye of <s>sahadevā</s> plants, and earthworm, each in equal amount,

children.text: piṇḍitaṃ krāmaṇe siddhaṃ kṣepe lepe niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: when made into a lump, are ready for <s>krāmaṇa</s>; he should apply them in casting and smearing.
Banana bulb and <s>sauvīra</s>, soaked in the juice of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>,
are a <s>krāmaṇa</s> for all metals and a mixer in all alloys.
Without <s>krāmaṇa</s>, mercury does not advance in body or metals.
Therefore it should be added in all the formulas and operations in the places stated.
Burned conch, impregnated with the milk of <s>ravi</s> under the sun one hundred times,

children.text: tataḥ pañcapuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ ruddhvā ruddhvātha saṃpuṭe ||
children.translated_text: is then cooked with five <s>puṭa</s>s, sealed again and again in a closed capsule.
Having added an equal amount of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, he should impregnate it with the sour group.

children.text: rājāvartaṃ pravālaṃ ca daradaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ śilā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s>, coral, cinnabar, sulfur, and orpiment,

children.text: pañcānāṃ tu samaṃ cūrṇaṃ śaṅkhatulyaṃ niyojayet
children.translated_text: the powder of these five in equal amount, should be added in an amount equal to the conch.
All that should be ground with the sour group for three days.

children.text: ayaṃ mahāviḍaḥ khyātaḥ khoṭānāṃ jāraṇe hitaḥ
children.translated_text: This is famous as the great <s>viḍa</s>, useful for digesting <s>khoṭa</s> masses.
In digestion, a crucible coating should always be applied everywhere.
At that very moment mercury digests diamonds and the like; there is no doubt.
The three alkalis, the five salts, <s>navasāra</s>, and the three pungents,
<s>indragopa</s>, dense mica, <s>śigru</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s>, and wild <s>sūraṇa</s>,
should be impregnated with the sour group for three days in fierce sunshine.
Mercury ground with this will consume the eight metals.
The three pungents, sulfur, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>svarṇapuṣpī</s>, and <s>suvarcala</s>,
<s>sarjī</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>sauvīra</s>, and rock salt, with liquids from <s>śigru</s>,

children.text: daśāhaṃ bhāvayed gharme viḍo'yaṃ jāraṇe hitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be impregnated in the heat for ten days; this <s>viḍa</s> is useful for digestion.
Burned conch, impregnated with the milk of <s>ravi</s> under the sun one hundred times,
and then cooked with five <s>puṭa</s>s, is an excellent <s>viḍa</s> for digestion.
The three alkalis and the five salts, joined with sour <s>vetasa</s>,
with this he should grind mercury; it readily consumes mica essence.
Sulfur should be impregnated in cow urine one hundred times in the heat.
Likewise, burned conch should be impregnated with liquids from <s>śigru</s> root.
With that sulfur and conch, equal parts of poison and rock salt
are used; mercury thoroughly ground with these consumes every metal.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should be impregnated one hundred times with liquids from the <s>palāśa</s> tree.

children.text: viḍo vahnimukho nāma hitaḥ sarvasya jāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: The <s>viḍa</s> named Fire-Mouthed is useful for the digestion of everything.

children.text: gaṃdhakaṃ navasāraṃ vā mukhaṃ kāṃtasya cātape
children.translated_text: Sulfur or <s>navasāra</s>, and the mouth of lodestone, in the sun,

children.text: śatadhā mūtravargeṇa bhāvitaṃ syād viḍaṃ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: when impregnated one hundred times with the urine group, becomes a separate <s>viḍa</s>.
The three alkalis, sulfur, orpiment, <s>bhūkhaga</s>, and <s>navasāra</s>,

children.text: saiṃdhavaṃ ca samaṃ sarvaṃ mūtravargairdinaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: and rock salt, all in equal amount, should be cooked for a day with the urine group.

children.text: jvālāmukho viḍo nāma hitaḥ sarvatra jāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: The <s>viḍa</s> named Flame-Mouthed is useful everywhere in digestion.
Sulfur should be impregnated one hundred times with liquids from the roots of wild <s>śigru</s>.
Or <s>navasāra</s>, treated with citron juices, should separately become a <s>viḍa</s> preparation.
<s>Vāsaka</s>, castor, plantain, <s>devadālī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>vāsā</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>nicula</s>, sesame, and <s>kāñcanamokṣaka</s>:
taking these together with their roots, not too dry, he should break them into pieces.

children.text: pañcāṅgaṃ mūlakaṃ dagdhvā tilakāṇḍaṃ ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: Having burned the five-part radish plant and an equal amount of sesame stalk,
with these alkalis he should impregnate the earlier paste using the class of urines.
He should cook the cloth-filtered liquid over a gentle fire in an iron vessel.

children.text: bāṣpāṇāṃ budbudānāṃ ca bahūnām udgamo yadā
children.translated_text: When many vapors and bubbles begin to rise,
then <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, the three alkalis, the three pungents,
sulfur, the five salts, <s>navasāra</s>, and <s>hiṅgula</s>,
he should add the powders of these into that vessel and then stir them.
After removing it at the stage of a molasses-like syrup, he should put it into an iron covered vessel.
Then it should remain for a week in the belly of the earth, and again likewise in a heap of grain.
After it has stood for a week, this <s>viḍa</s>, called <s>Vaḍavānala</s>, is perfected.
He should impregnate <s>nicula</s> alkali with the juices of <s>devadālī</s> leaves,
twenty-one times; this <s>viḍa</s> is for the digestion of <s>sattva</s>.
<s>Devadālī</s> root or seed, <s>guñjā</s>, rock salt, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
in equal parts, together with <s>nicula</s> alkali, should be treated seven times with the sour group.
He should impregnate it with the juices of <s>kośātakī</s> leaves for seven days.
The <s>viḍa</s> named <s>Tīvrānala</s> is prescribed for the digestion of gold.
The alkali of radish, fresh ginger, and <s>vahni</s>, stirred with cow urine,

children.text: vastrapūtaṃ dravaṃ grāhyaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ tena bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: should be taken as a cloth-filtered liquid; with it he should impregnate sulfur.
A hundred times in fierce heat: this <s>viḍa</s> is for the digestion of gold.
The three alkalis, the five salts, conch shell, <s>tāla</s>, and <s>manaḥśilā</s>,
cooked for one day with the sour group, are for the digestion of gold.
Sulfur and <s>navasāra</s> should be ground with the sour juice of citron.
A hundred times in fierce heat: this <s>viḍa</s> is for the digestion of gold.
Sulfur should be impregnated with the liquids of <s>kanyā</s>, <s>hayāri</s>, and <s>dhattūra</s>.

children.text: śatadhā taṃ khare gharme viḍo'yaṃ sarvajāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: A hundredfold in fierce heat: this <s>viḍa</s> is for every kind of digestion.
By this, it quickly consumes in a covered vessel made from oyster shell.
Rock salt and sulfur in equal amount, soaked with the liquids of <s>tāmravallī</s>,
by this <s>viḍa</s> formula, mercury consumes <s>gagana</s> (mica).
<s>Śilā</s>, sulfur, and salt-born material, each one <s>pala</s>,
and three <s>pala</s>s of <s>bhūnāga</s>: he should grind everything together.
He should dry it, and again add three <s>pala</s>s of <s>bhūnāga</s>.
In the same way it should be ground, dried again, and cooked over a slow fire.

children.text: evam aṣṭaguṇaṃ dattvā mardyaṃ pācyaṃ vicūrṇayet
children.translated_text: After adding eight times in this manner, it should be ground, cooked, and powdered.
This perfected <s>viḍa</s> should be applied in digestion, in operations concerning gold.

children.text: samyak saṃskṛtagaṃdhakādyuparasaṃ sattvaṃ tato vyomajaṃ paścānmākṣikasattvahāṭakavaraṃ garbhadrutau drāvitam
children.translated_text: Then the <s>sattva</s> of properly processed sulfur and the other secondary minerals, then the mica-born <s>sattva</s>, and afterward <s>mākṣika-sattva</s> and excellent gold, melted in internal liquefaction,

children.text: rāgai rañjitabījajālam akhilaṃ bāhyāṃ drutiṃ dvaṃdvitāṃ sūte sarvamidaṃ krameṇa vidhinā siddhairbiḍairjārayet ||
children.translated_text: the whole array of seed-metals colored with tinctures, and the external liquefaction made into paired forms: mercury should digest all this in sequence, according to rule, with perfected <s>viḍa</s>s.

children.text: siddhaiḥ sūtavarasya karma vividhaṃ khyātaṃ vicitraiḥ kramaiḥ sādhyāsādhyavivekato hy anubhavan dṛṣṭvā samastaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: The varied operations of excellent mercury with perfected preparations are famous through diverse procedures; having experienced and seen everything according to the distinction between what is possible and impossible,

children.text: yuktyāṣṭādaśadhā viśeṣavidhinā svedādivedhāntakaṃ dakṣāṇāṃ sukhasādhyameva sukhadaṃ saṃtanyate sāmpratam ||
children.translated_text: I now set forth, for the skilled, an easy-to-accomplish and beneficial procedure in eighteen forms, by a special rule, from steaming through penetration.
Steaming, grinding, stupefaction, raising up, and the three kinds of distillation,
confinement, regulation, kindling, and <s>anuvāsana</s>,
digestion and <s>cāraṇa</s>, and also internal and external liquefaction,

children.text: rañjanaṃ sāraṇaṃ cānusāraṇā pratisāraṇā krāmaṇaṃ dehaloheṣu ||
children.translated_text: coloring, <s>sāraṇa</s>, <s>anusāraṇa</s>, <s>pratisāraṇa</s>, and <s>krāmaṇa</s> in bodies and metals.
With various grains obtained as available, without husks and mixed with water,
one should keep an earthen vessel filled until it becomes sour.
Into it, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
and also <s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,

children.text: triphalā girikarṇī ca haṃsapādī ca citrakam
children.translated_text: <s>triphala</s>, <s>girikarṇī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
cut up together with their roots, should be placed as available.
Within the earlier sour vessel, this becomes the grain-sour preparation.
He should apply it everywhere in the operations beginning with steaming for the king of mercury.
Or, in its absence, he should use very sour <s>āranāla</s>.
The three pungents, salt, mustard, <s>citraka</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and fresh ginger,
<s>mahābalā</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: meṣaśṛṅgī citrakaṃ ca navasāraṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>navasāra</s>, each in equal amount:

children.text: etat samastaṃ vyastaṃ vā pūrvāmlenaiva mardayet ||
children.translated_text: all these, either together or separately, he should grind with the previous sour liquid.
With that paste he should smear a cloth to the thickness of a finger.
In its middle he should place mercury, tie it up, and cook it for three days.
When steamed in a <s>dolāyantra</s> containing sour liquid, the mercury becomes steamed.
After washing it with warm <s>kāñjika</s>, he should take it and grind it thoroughly.
He should use very sour <s>āranāla</s>; in its absence, that should be employed.
House soot, brick powder, burnt wool, salt, and jaggery,

children.text: rājikā triphalā kanyā citrakaṃ bṛhatī kaṇā ||
children.translated_text: mustard, <s>triphala</s>, <s>kanyā</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>,
and then barren <s>karkoṭakī</s>, either separately or all together,
he should decoct with <s>āranāla</s>; with that, mercury is to be ground for three days.
After washing it with <s>kāñjika</s> and taking it up, he should make it undergo <s>mūrchana</s>.
<s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, black <s>dhūrta</s>, <s>balā</s>, and white <s>aparājitā</s>,
<s>kanyā</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>triphala</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s>, and <s>vacā</s>
<s>gojihvā</s>, <s>cāṅgulī</s>, <s>nīlī</s>, <s>muruṇḍī</s>, and <s>kṣīrakandaka</s>;

children.text: rājikā kākamācī ca ravikṣīraṃ ca kāñcanam
children.translated_text: and <s>rājikā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>ravikṣīra</s>, and <s>kāñcana</s>;
With the liquids of these, separately or all together, he should grind it.
He should grind <s>rasarāja</s> (king mercury) for one <s>yāma</s> and enclose it in a crucible.

children.text: puṭaikena pacettaṃ tu bhūdhare vātha mardayet ||
children.translated_text: He should cook it with one <s>puṭa</s> heating, or else grind it on a stone.
With all the liquids, as before, he should seal it again and again and cook it thoroughly.
Doing this seven times, the mercury becomes <s>mūrchita</s> (stupefied, immobilized).
By rolling it in water or in warm <s>āranāla</s>, it becomes revived.
Or, by cooking it in a distillation apparatus, it becomes revived.
The <s>sūta</s> (mercury), revived in this way, should then be distilled in three ways, in sequence.
<s>kākamācī</s>, <s>jayā</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>cāṅgerī</s>, red <s>citraka</s>,
<s>aṅkolī</s>, <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, <s>tilaparṇī</s>, and <s>kumārikā</s>;
<s>maṇḍūkī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>;
<s>bhūpāṭalī</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>girikarṇikā</s>;
<s>śaṇapuṣpī</s>, fresh ginger, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, and <s>kṣīrakandaka</s>;

children.text: nīlī caiṣāṃ samastānāṃ vyastānāṃ ca dravairdinam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>nīlī</s>: with the liquids of all these, collectively or separately, for a day,
he should grind <s>sūta</s> (mercury) mixed with a quarter part of copper, together with sour liquids.
When it has become a paste, he should again distill it in an upward-distillation apparatus.
Having taken it, he should grind it in the same way, combined with copper powder.
He should distill it and grind it, again and again adding copper.
Thus, seven times, he should perform grinding and distillation in order.
Taking what has adhered above, he should distill it by downward distillation.
<s>triphala</s>, <s>rājikā</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>tryūṣa</s>, salt, and <s>citraka</s>,
all of that, equal in amount to the mercury, he should grind for a day with <s>kāñjika</s> sour gruel.

children.text: tena limped ūrdhvabhāṇḍaṃ pṛṣṭhe deyaṃ puṭaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: With that he should smear the upper vessel; a small <s>puṭa</s> heating should be applied on its back.
He should collect what has been distilled in the downward-distillation apparatus.
<s>triphala</s>, <s>rājikā</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>tryūṣa</s>, salt, and <s>citraka</s>,
<s>dhānyābhraka</s> and all the mercury should be ground with <s>āranāla</s> sour gruel.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu tat pātyaṃ tiryagyantre dṛḍhāgninā ||
children.translated_text: When the paste has disappeared, it should be distilled in a transverse apparatus with a strong fire.
The mercury placed inside a pot, with salt ground in water,

children.text: ācchādyātha jalaṃ kiṃcit kṣiptvā śrāveṇa rodhayet
children.translated_text: should then be covered; after a little water has been poured in, he should seal it with a saucer-lid.
A light <s>puṭa</s> should be applied above; when obtained, the mercury will be below.
The three alkalis, the five salts, <s>bhūkhaga</s>, <s>śigru</s> root,

children.text: svarṇapuṣpī ca kāsīsaṃ maricaṃ rājikā madhu ||
children.translated_text: <s>svarṇapuṣpī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, black pepper, <s>rājikā</s>, and honey;
<s>kṣīrakanda</s>, <s>jayā</s>, <s>kanyā</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, and <s>girikarṇikā</s>;
<s>kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>śoṇapuṣpī</s>, <s>pātālagaruḍī</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>;
<s>vandhyākarkoṭakī</s> and <s>vahni</s>, either separately or all together,
he should grind with the sour group, and with their liquids he should grind the mercury.
At the end of the day he should bind it in cloth and cook it for three days in a swing apparatus.
When the vessel is filled with the previous liquids, the mercury becomes eager for grāsa, the taking of a morsel.
The kindled <s>rasarāja</s> (king mercury), joined with lemon juice,

children.text: dinaikaṃ dhārayed gharme mṛtpātre vāsito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: should be kept in the heat for one day; kept in an earthen vessel, it becomes impregnated.
Purified by the auspicious operations beginning with steaming, it becomes free from the seven sheaths.

children.text: aṣṭamāṃśam avaśiṣyate tadā śuddhasūta iti kathyate budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When an eighth part remains, it is called purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) by the wise.
For mercury with a mouth and without a mouth, I shall explain, for the sake of <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion), the feeding of sulfur by various easy procedures.

children.text: tadanu ca ghanacūrṇairbhojanaṃ pācanaṃ syāt nikhilasūtavibhūtyai vārtikānāṃ sukhāya ||
children.translated_text: Thereafter there is feeding and cooking with powders of <s>ghana</s>, for the complete power of mercury and for the ease of practitioners.
Sulfur, made into fine powder, should be impregnated seven times with the liquids of <s>bṛhatī</s>,
or else seven times with the juice of <s>vṛntāka</s>.
He should place one <s>pala</s> of purified mercury inside a glass bottle.
He should add one <s>karṣa</s> of treated sulfur and camphor in the measure of one <s>māṣa</s>.

children.text: kṣiptvā tatra mukhaṃ ruddhvā mṛdā kūpīṃ ca lepayet
children.translated_text: After putting them there, he should seal the mouth and coat the bottle with clay.
He should cook it for a day with a lamp flame and then open the mouth again.

children.text: jīrṇe gaṃdhaṃ ca karpūraṃ dattvā tadvacca jārayet
children.translated_text: When the sulfur has been digested, he should add sulfur and camphor and digest it likewise.
When it has been digested a hundredfold in this way, sulfur should be digested in the mercury.
<s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, and <s>sajjīkṣāra</s> should be made into a pellet,
combined with <s>śigru</s> water; with this, indeed, it is to be impregnated.

children.text: saptāhaṃ cūrṇitaṃ gaṃdhaṃ taṃ gaṃdhaṃ jārayetpunaḥ
children.translated_text: For seven days the powdered sulfur should be treated; that sulfur he should again digest.
Into the middle of a hollow in a brick he should place thoroughly purified mercury.
He should cover its mouth with a clean cloth, on the upper side.
After adding one-tenth part of sulfur, he should seal it with a saucer-lid.

children.text: pṛṣṭhe laghupuṭaṃ deyaṃ jīrṇe gaṃdhaṃ punaḥ kṣipet
children.translated_text: A light <s>puṭa</s> should be applied on its back; when it is digested, he should add sulfur again.

children.text: evaṃ śataguṇaṃ jāryaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ pārade śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus sulfur should slowly be digested in mercury to a hundredfold amount.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ taptakhalve tu kṣipedvastreṇa gālitam
children.translated_text: He should put that mercury, filtered through cloth, into a heated mortar.
After adding a quarter part of cooked <s>bīja</s> (seed-material), he should grind it for a day with sour liquids.
He should put it into a <s>cāraṇā</s> apparatus, joined with lemon juice.

children.text: taṃ yaṃtraṃ dhārayed gharme jārito jāyate rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should keep that apparatus in the heat; the mercury becomes digested.

children.text: saviḍaṃ kalayedyaṃtre dinaikaṃ tu puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: He should mix it with <s>viḍa</s> in the apparatus and cook it for one day in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: jāritaṃ syātpunarbījaṃ dattvā jāryaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: It will be digested; then, after adding <s>bīja</s> again, it should be digested as before.
And he should digest it again in that same way; thus it should be digested in equal measure, in sequence.
When digested, he should place it in a <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus with oil mixed with fat.
It should be melted in a tube-crucible, together with cooked <s>bīja</s> and mercury.
He should keep it in that apparatus in this way; when it has undergone <s>sāraṇā</s>, he should digest the mercury.
That <s>sārita</s> preparation should again be ground as before, mixed with <s>biḍa</s>.

children.text: jārayetkacchape yaṃtre jīrṇe bīje tu sārayet
children.translated_text: One should digest it in a tortoise apparatus; when the seed has been digested, one should carry out <s>sāraṇā</s>.
As before, in the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus, indeed with twice as much seed.
Again one should digest it in that same way, and likewise perform <s>pratisāraṇā</s>.
Then, with three times as much seed, one should digest it again as before.
That mercury, an equal amount of <s>tālaka</s>, oil produced from <s>dhattūra</s>,
and the liquid of a group of divine herbs should all be ground for the span of a day.
It should be cooked, sealed in a <s>vajramūṣā</s>, in a cow-dung fire for the span of a day.
Again it should be ground with liquids of divine herbs and cooked for the span of a day.

children.text: ityevaṃ ca punaḥ kuryātsūto baddhamukho bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Doing this again in just this way, the <s>sūta</s> becomes closed-mouthed and fixed.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ dhautamākṣīkaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ śulbaṃ rasaḥ śaśī
children.translated_text: That mercury, washed <s>mākṣīka</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, copper, <s>rasa</s>, and <s>śaśī</s>
should be ground in equal parts for a day with liquids arising from <s>devadālī</s>.
Ground for three days with honey and ghee, it should be made into a ball.
After placing it in a <s>vajramūṣā</s>, sealing it, and drying it, one should blow it with fierce fire.
By the use of <s>khadira</s> charcoal, the mercury becomes bound as a <s>khoṭa</s> lump.
That <s>khoṭa</s> should be purified with borax and glass by repeated blowing.
The bound mercury becomes a mass of brilliance, like the young sun.
Having wrapped that mercury with wax, one should worship it.

children.text: śatāṃśaṃ tu drute tāre krāmaṇenaiva saṃyutam ||
children.translated_text: One hundredth part, joined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, should be applied to melted silver.
That silver becomes gold, with a brilliance equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
It is said to be a penetrative agent for ninety-eight parts in this way.

children.text: atha vakṣye rasendrasya vāsitasya mukhaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: Now I shall explain in order the mouth of perfumed <s>rasendra</s>,
by which, when quickly sprinkled, it moves through mica and the other substances, including <s>vaikrānta</s>.
With <s>amlavetasa</s>, <s>jambīra</s>, <s>bījapūraka</s>, and <s>bhūkhaga</s>,
one should grind the <s>sūta</s> for three days, and also with <s>bhūnāga</s> for three days.

children.text: taptakhalve dinaṃ mardyaṃ sūtasyetthaṃ mukhaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: It should be ground for a day in a heated mortar; thus the mouth of <s>sūta</s> comes about.
One should make two bricks provided with a central hollow.
Grain-mica, purified sulfur, ten <s>niṣkas</s> of each,
should be ground for a <s>yāma</s> with liquids from <s>jambīra</s>, and the hollow should be smeared with that very mixture.
The two hollows should be smeared equally, and the lower hollow should be well cleaned.
One should place twenty <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>sūta</s> in it, and the other brick should be placed above.
After sealing the joint with clay and salt, one should kindle a blazing fire below.
It should be uninterrupted, day and night, for the span of seven days.
When self-cooled, one should take out the mercury, free from dross.

children.text: ityevaṃ tu tridhā kuryādrasasya tu mukhaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: One should do this three times in just this way; then the mouth of the mercury comes about.
<s>Sūta</s> enclosed in a bamboo tube, in a vessel filled with cow urine,
should be cooked on a hearth for three weeks; thus the mouth of <s>sūta</s> comes about.

children.text: samukhe nirmukhe sūte vakṣyate jāraṇaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: For <s>sūta</s> with a mouth and without a mouth, the procedure for digestion will be explained.

children.text: khalvapītaṃ raso liṅgaṃ mardanaṃ mārjanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Mercury drunk by the mortar is called the <s>liṅga</s>; grinding is remembered as cleansing.
Bathing is with the juices of many herbs; worship is with essences and seeds.
One should prepare the offering with gold and the other classes of jewels.
The food offering is divine coloring; <s>sāraṇā</s> is the dismissal.
Penetration in bodies and metals is the fruit of the proper rite of worship.

children.text: yāvaddināni vahnau tu dhāraṇe jāryate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: For as many days as mercury is digested while being held in the fire,
for that many thousands of ages one is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
Whatever expense there may be for the accomplishment of the king of mercury,

children.text: tatsarvaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ datte śrī bhairavī dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: all that, multiplied ten millionfold, <s>Śrī Bhairavī</s> certainly gives back.

children.text: sādhakānāṃ sudhīrāṇām iha loke paratra ca
children.translated_text: For wise practitioners, both in this world and in the next,
therefore it should be accomplished by kings and leading merchants, since it grants enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: arkakṣīreṇa dhānyābhraṃ dinaṃ mardyaṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Grain-mica should be ground for a day with the milk of <s>arka</s> and then sealed.
It should be cooked in the <s>kapota</s> type of <s>puṭa</s>, and ground for a <s>yāma</s> with milks.
After sealing it below, one should cook it as before; this should be done four times.
It should also be done three times with the liquids of radish, and three times with the liquids of the plantain corm.
<s>Apāmārga</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>muni</s>,
<s>punarnavā</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and likewise <s>citraka</s>:
with the liquids of these in sequence there should be grinding and cooking in a <s>puṭa</s>.
After giving each one once, one should again impregnate it with that liquid.
<s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>tālamūlī</s>, <s>kadalī</s>, <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>,
<s>arka</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>yavaciñcā</s>, in sequence:

children.text: pratidravair dinaikaṃ tu bhāvitaṃ cāraṇe hitam ||
children.translated_text: when impregnated for one day with each liquid, it is useful for <s>cāraṇa</s>.

children.text: arkakṣīraistu dhānyābhraṃ yāmaṃ mardyaṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Grain-mica should be ground for a <s>yāma</s> with the milks of <s>arka</s> and then sealed.
It should be cooked in the <s>kapota</s> type of <s>puṭa</s>; this should be done fourteen times.
<s>Kadalī</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>aṅkolla</s>, <s>arka</s>, and <s>pīluka</s>,
<s>nāgavallī</s>, <s>kuberākṣī</s>, <s>bhūmyapāmārga</s>, and <s>tumburu</s>:
one liquid from these should be taken, together with sour gruel and mica.
All this should be put in a vessel, and in its midst it should be cooked for three days.
Then the earlier mica should be taken out from the <s>dolikāyantra</s> and dried.

children.text: kāsīsaṃ tuvarī sindhuṣṭaṃkaṇaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāsīsa</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, salt, and borax should be in equal amounts.
Putting in one-tenth of all this, one should grind it in that.
For one day in a heated mortar, having placed it there, one should grind it in that.

children.text: dinaikaṃ taptakhalve tu tadabhraṃ cāraṇe hitam ||
children.translated_text: For one day in a heated mortar, that mica is useful for <s>cāraṇa</s>.
One should cast melted lead a hundred times into the liquid of <s>muṇḍī</s>.

children.text: tena drāveṇa dhānyābhraṃ marditaṃ saptadhā puṭet
children.translated_text: With that liquid, grain-mica should be ground and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> seven times.

children.text: mardyaṃ mardyaṃ nirudhyātha kapotākhye puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: After grinding it again and again and then sealing it, one should cook it in the <s>kapota</s> type of <s>puṭa</s>.
Having added an equal amount of sulfur, one should use the previously mentioned liquids of <s>muṇḍikā</s>.
It should be impregnated for a day with milky liquids obtained from <s>bījapūra</s>.

children.text: etadabhraṃ tu sūtasya cāraṇe paramaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: This mica is supremely useful for the <s>cāraṇā</s> (feeding) of <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
<s>vyāghrapādī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, plantain, and <s>agnikumārikā</s>,
<s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>vajrī</s>, <s>khaṇḍajāri</s>, and <s>indravāruṇī</s>,
<s>vandhyākarkoṭakī</s>, <s>mūṣā</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpikā</s>,
<s>maṇḍūkī</s> and <s>agnimathana</s> are well-known <s>siddhamūlikā</s> plants.

children.text: etāḥ samastā vyastā vā coktasthāne niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: These should be employed, all together or separately, in the place that has been stated.
Now, in the case of <s>sūta</s> with a mouth, one should add a sixteenth part of the aforesaid mica
and grind it in a heated mortar for a day with the juices of the <s>siddhamūlī</s> plants.
Then, in the <s>cāraṇā</s> apparatus, joined with lemon juice,

children.text: gharme dhāryaṃ dinaikaṃ tu caratyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it should be kept in heat for one day; it certainly feeds, without doubt.
What has been fed should be tied in cloth and kept in a swing apparatus for a day.
Combined with the juices of the <s>siddhamūlī</s> plants, by distillation it is indeed sufficiently digested.
If it remains undigested, one should cook it for a day in the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s>.

children.text: aṣṭamāṃśaṃ viḍaṃ dattvā caratyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After adding an eighth part of <s>viḍa</s>, it certainly feeds, without doubt.

children.text: anena kramayogena cāryaṃ jāryaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: By this sequential procedure it should be fed and digested again and again.
When it has been properly digested a hundredfold, it pierces with a thousandth part.
When it has been digested a thousandfold, the mercury becomes capable of piercing a lakhfold amount.
Likewise, when it has been digested a lakhfold amount, the mercury becomes capable of piercing a crore-fold amount.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhraṃ vā suvarṇaṃ vā yathāśaktyā tu jārayet
children.translated_text: Black mica or gold should be digested according to one's capacity.
By the same sequence as before, the result is the same for both.
By this very same procedure, either <s>tāra</s> (silver) or white mica
should be digested according to one's capacity; it is commended for silver work.
As before, with cooked <s>bīja</s> (seed-material), the operations beginning with <s>sāraṇā</s> should be performed in order.
For <s>rasarāja</s> (king mercury), piercing and <s>krāmaṇa</s> should likewise be carried out.
For silver work one should digest all the <s>candrārka</s>, or copper.
When it has been digested a hundredfold in this way, one should pierce with a thousandth part.
When it has been digested a thousandfold, the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations should be performed as before.
Then it should be digested again in the same way, and again fed three times.

children.text: ityevaṃ ca punaḥ sāryaṃ punaḥ sāryaṃ ca jārayet
children.translated_text: Thus it should again undergo <s>sāraṇā</s>, again undergo <s>sāraṇā</s>, and be digested.
With the mercury, one should perform the procedure as before, from the binding of the mouth through piercing.
By a mere lakhth part of that, gold becomes excellent and divine.

children.text: yadā lakṣaguṇe jīrṇe tridhā sāryaṃ ca jārayet ||
children.translated_text: When it has been digested a lakhfold amount, it should be treated three times with <s>sāraṇā</s> and digested.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā kāryaṃ bandhayecca tato mukham
children.translated_text: Thus this should be done seven times, and then the mouth should be bound.
And, as before, when it has been brought through <s>krāmaṇa</s>, that prepared mercury is produced.
It is crore-piercing in <s>candrārka</s>; this is the truth spoken by <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
Now I shall explain the <s>cāraṇā</s> and <s>jāraṇa</s> for <s>sūta</s> without a mouth.
Into purified <s>sūta</s> one should put a sixteenth part of killed <s>vaikrānta</s>.
It should be ground in a heated mortar for three days with the juices of the <s>siddhamūlī</s> plants.
By this very processing, even without a mouth, it surely feeds.
Or else, in a heated mortar, one should grind mercury combined with <s>bhūlatā</s>
for three days; afterward it should be distilled in a distillation apparatus.
By this processing too, the mouthless mercury feeds at once.
For its <s>jāraṇa</s>, the suitable preparation of <s>vyoma</s> (mica) is now stated.
One should cook <s>dhānyābhra</s> with the acid group for three days in a swing apparatus.
Then it should be ground with the latex of <s>snuhī</s> for one <s>yāma</s>, covered, and fired.
After one heating called <s>kapotapuṭa</s>, one should take it out and then grind it.
<s>mūlaka</s>, plantain bulb, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, and <s>kākamācikā</s>,
<s>muni</s>, fresh ginger, <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, and <s>apāmārga</s>,
and castor: with the juices of these, separately, a light <s>puṭa</s> heating should be given.
Then one should cook it for a day in a swing apparatus with the latex of <s>vajrī</s>.

children.text: vacā nimbaṃ dhūmasāraṃ kāsīsaṃ ca sucūrṇitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>vacā</s>, neem, <s>dhūmasāra</s>, and <s>kāsīsa</s> should be finely powdered.
Then each should be mixed in at one sixteenth the amount of the mica.
It should be ground in a copper mortar for a day with chickpea sour-gruel.
One should smear an iron vessel with <s>navasāra</s> and place in it

children.text: pāradaṃ sādhitaṃ sābhraṃ caṇakāmlaṃ ca kāṃjikam ||
children.translated_text: the prepared mercury together with mica, chickpea sour liquid, and <s>kāñjika</s> sour gruel.
It should be cooked on a stove with a gentle fire; the mercury feeds at that very moment.
One should digest it by the previous procedure; then it should be fed and digested.
The measure and method are as before; this is the <s>jāraṇa</s> of mouthless mercury.
Black mica and gold should be digested in gold work.

children.text: tāraṃ vā śvetamabhraṃ vā jāryaṃ syāttārakarmaṇi
children.translated_text: Silver or white mica should be digested in silver work.
As before, it should be digested through the operations beginning with <s>sāraṇā</s> and ending with <s>krāmaṇa</s>.

children.text: kartavyaṃ sūtarāje tu tadvad bhavati kāṃcanam
children.translated_text: This should be done with <s>sūtarāja</s>; gold comes about in the same way.
