With a white substance one should digest what is white; as the seed is, so is the sprout.

children.text: proktaṃ yathā sugamasādhitapītagaṃdhaṃ kṛṣṇābhrahemarajataṃ sitamabhrakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: As has been taught, the easily prepared yellow sulfur, black mica, gold, silver, and white mica
are to be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> in that excellent mercury; the best chief practitioner may make many thousands of loads of great gold.
It surely grants success in the visible result of the procedure and is beneficial for the excellent <s>jāraṇa</s> of mercury.
The extraction of essence by many procedures, the joining of pairs, the consecration, and the noble operation are taught.
One should make <s>dhānyābhraka</s> soaked for seven days in a decoction of <s>mustā</s>.
It may be drenched with the liquids from the bulb of any one of <s>śigru</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s>, or <s>rambhā</s>,
or soaked thoroughly with liquids from <s>peṭārī</s> root and <s>jambīra</s>.
Into mica thus soaked, one should add <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> in a quarter part.
It should be ground for one day in a mortar, combined with some acid liquid.
<s>guñjā</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, lac, wool, <s>sarjī</s>, <s>sarjarasa</s>, and jaggery
<s>kṣudramīna</s>, <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali), glass, oil-cake, and <s>sūraṇa</s>,
<s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>triphala</s>, <s>vahni</s>, <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>dhattūra</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>balā</s>, and bitter sulfur,
cow's milk, the five salts, poison of snake and scorpion, honey,
<s>ṣaḍbindu</s>, small shellfish, and also the bones of a hare,
pigeon dung, <s>tryūṣa</s>, <s>indragopa</s>, and <s>śigru</s>,
wheat and mustard in equal quantity: these should be ground with goat's milk.
These, either separately or all together, should be made into a lump within one <s>yāma</s>.
One part of this lump and two parts of purified <s>abhraka</s> (mica),
together with one part of <s>pañcamāhiṣa</s>, should all be mixed together.
Pellets of one <s>karṣa</s> each should be made and dried somewhat in the shade.
In a furnace apparatus heated with <s>khadira</s> charcoal, repeatedly throwing them in,
he should blow the pellets, five at a time, with a curved tube.
When it is finished, he should take the slag and break it open after it has cooled by itself.
He should take the round <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) and pulverize the remaining slag.
Half of the powder, the previous lump, and the fivefold <s>māhiṣa</s> preparation as before
should be combined and blown in the same way; he should collect each resulting <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ ca punaḥ kuryāttridhā sattvaṃ vimuñcati
children.translated_text: He should do this again in just this way three times; it releases the <s>sattva</s>.
By this ordered procedure, <s>kāntasattva</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>,
as well as other hard <s>uparasa</s> minerals and purified <s>bhūnāga</s> clay,
give forth aggregates of <s>sattva</s>; he should collect them each separately.
Having taken <s>abhrasattva</s> (mica essence), he should add equal parts of glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax).

children.text: dattvā dattvā trivāraṃ tu vajramūṣāgataṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: Adding them again and again, he should blow it three times in a diamond-crucible.
The sour group, <s>snuhī</s> leaves, and tamarind seed together with its bark
should be made into a paste; in that he should quench that <s>sattva</s> seven times.
The <s>sattva</s> becomes soft and white; he should quench it seven times.
There should be ten parts of <s>dhānyābhra</s> and three parts of purified <s>nāga</s> (lead).
Thoroughly purified <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should each be one part.

children.text: ūrṇā sarjī yavakṣāraṃ bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ vimiśrayet
children.translated_text: Wool, <s>sarjī</s>, and <s>yavakṣāra</s> should be mixed in one part each.
It should be ground for up to a day with the urine group and the sour group, as obtained.
Together with <s>ajāpañcāṅga</s>, the extraction of <s>sattva</s> should be performed as before.
Having done this and taken the soft, visibly pure essence, he should use it below.
In a swing apparatus, in a <s>sāra</s> tube, he should steam <s>mākṣika</s> for a day.
When powdered, he should cook it for a day in an iron vessel with honey and ghee.
Having taken it, he should treat it in the sun for a day with the milks of <s>vajrī</s> plants.
Mixed with house soot, ghee, and honey, it should be ground for a day.
When blown inside a closed crucible, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like <s>guñjā</s> berries.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, treated through a hundred sun-heatings with the water of plantain rhizome,
should be cooked for a <s>yāma</s> with ghee and <s>vātāri</s> oils.
By blowing as before, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like <s>indragopa</s> insects.
He should grind <s>mākṣika</s> for a day with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> and with breast milk.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should also be mixed in quarter-portions.
When blown inside a sealed crucible, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like a jewel.
With the liquids of plantain rhizome, <s>tulasī</s>, and citron, in sequence,
he should treat fine <s>mākṣika</s> seven times with each liquid.
When sealed and blown, excellent <s>sattva</s> falls out, resembling a parrot.
He should treat it for twice seven days with the urine group and the sour group.
He should grind <s>mākṣika</s> with intense heat and with sour liquids for several days.
Combined with the <s>mitrapañcaka</s>, it should be made into pellets and blown strongly.
As with <s>vyoman</s> (mica), by means of the curved tube, the <s>sattva</s> becomes copper-like.
With breast milk and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, together with plantain water,
and combined with the <s>mitrapañcaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s> should be treated for seven days.
It should be ground for a <s>yāma</s>, then for a day with <s>vātāri</s> oils.
It should be cooked for a <s>yāma</s> on a gentle fire, until it becomes a ball.
By blowing as with <s>vyoman</s> (mica), the <s>sattva</s> becomes the color of <s>kiṃśuka</s> flowers.
For purified <s>vimala</s> minerals too, the procedure should be exactly as for <s>tāpya</s>.
Well-purified <s>mākṣika</s> powder should be ground with some sour liquid.
It should be washed with <s>āranāla</s> sour gruel; what settles below is like gold powder.
After lifting that out, this is the washed <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: yojayedvāpane caiva bījānāṃ yatra yatra vai ||
children.translated_text: It should be used in the impregnation of <s>bīja</s> materials wherever required.
<s>Mākṣika</s> smeared with <s>pañcamitra</s> should, at the end of a week, be made into pellets.
By blowing just as before, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like lac.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) should be treated for three days with waters from <s>agastya</s> and <s>śigru</s>.
Through combination with the <s>tālaka</s> medicine, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like gold.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> should be treated for a day with cow urine and the sour juice of citron.
He should treat it with the juices of red and yellow flowers and with biles.
At the end of the day he should grind it for a <s>yāma</s>, combined with <s>mitrapañcaka</s>.
Putting the pellet inside a glass bottle, that glass bottle
should be coated all around to the measure of a finger's breadth with cloth and clay.
When it is dry, he should cook it in a sand apparatus, slowly, with a gentle fire.
When the liquid has dried, he should then seal the mouth properly with clay and salt.
He should cook it with a fierce fire until twelve <s>yāmas</s> have passed.
After it has cooled by itself, he should take it out, break the bottle, and collect it.
The <s>śilāsattva</s> adhering above is like the rays of the young sun.
Sixteen parts of <s>tāla</s>; poison, mercury, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>...
One should mix equal portions of powder of white mica and tin.
All of it should be ground with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> for three days.
From <s>tālaka</s> one should obtain the <s>sattva</s> (essence), hard like stone and resembling crystal.
<s>Tāla</s> should be impregnated fourteen times with products from the milk of <s>snuhī</s> and from bitter gourd.
Sesame, mustard, <s>śigru</s>, salt, and the five allies
should be ground for one day with the previous <s>tāla</s>, in equal amount.
When it is placed in a perforated crucible and blown in the furnace, one should obtain the <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: lākṣā rājī guḍaṃ śigruṣṭaṃkaṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ tilāḥ
children.translated_text: Lac, black mustard, jaggery, <s>śigru</s>, borax, salt, and sesame
should be ground, in equal amount, with purified <s>tāla</s> and the milks of <s>arka</s>.
Or it should be ground for a day with the milks of <s>vajriṇī</s>, and likewise with the juices of white gourd.
With that paste one should smear the inside of a perforated crucible and seal it.
The <s>sattva</s> is to be obtained either by a <s>puṭa</s> heating or by blowing, in the <s>pātāla-yantra</s>.
For <s>tālaka</s>, mercury and borax should be added in one-eighth part.
It should be ground for three days with the juices of white gourd and the milks of <s>snuhī</s>.
That ball should be put into a perforated crucible, and the <s>sattva</s> should be obtained as before.
Lac, <s>abhayā</s>, earthworm, household soot, and <s>jaṭākaṇā</s>,
turmeric, borax, honey, and ghee: with these, <s>tuttha</s> should be in equal amount.
Everything should be ground with goat's milk and blown in a closed crucible.
A <s>sattva</s> resembling <s>kiṃśuka</s> flowers is produced; there is no doubt about this.
Turmeric, elephant-foot yam, <s>aṅkolla</s>, <s>taṇḍulī</s>, sulfur, and jaggery,
with honey, ghee, and borax in equal amount: <s>tuttha</s> should be equal to these.
One should grind everything with breast milk and smear a perforated crucible.
After sealing it, when it is blown by means of the <s>pātāla-yantra</s>, it releases <s>sattva</s>.
For <s>tuttha</s>, one should powder a quarter part of borax with honey and ghee.
Mixed with <s>tuttha</s>, it should be blown in a furnace apparatus with a strong fire.
When blown, it releases <s>sattva</s> having a brilliance like a parrot's beak.
<s>Sauvīra</s> and powdered <s>tīkṣṇa</s> should be sealed in equal amounts in a crucible.
When forcibly blown, <s>sattva</s> comes forth; that is called excellent <s>nāga</s>.

children.text: kṣārāmlaṃ snehapittaiśca kramād bhāvyaṃ dinaṃ dinam
children.translated_text: It should be impregnated day by day, in order, with alkaline, sour, oily, and bile substances.
It should be impregnated for two days with the juices of red and yellow flowers.
Afterwards one should powder <s>rasaka</s>; wool, lac, turmeric, and <s>abhayā</s>,

children.text: ṭaṃkaṇaṃ śigrudhūmaṃ ca bhūnāgaṃ saptamaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: borax, smoke of <s>śigru</s>, and earthworm are the seventh ingredient.
That powder should be ground with these in equal amount, using goat's milk.
For one <s>yāma</s>, an eggplant-shaped crucible should be smeared with this paste.
When dried and blown with charcoal up to half its mouth, one should collect the <s>sattva</s>.
For <s>rasaka</s>, one part, together with <s>triphala</s> and the five allies,
and turmeric and household soot should each be one part among the ten.
It should be ground for one day with goat's milk, or else with any sour liquid.
As before, one should obtain from <s>rasaka</s> a <s>sattva</s> with a curved luster.
Powder of <s>vandhyā</s> and <s>vaikrānta</s> should be ground equally in the shade.
With goat's urine for one day, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like silver.
Alkali of <s>mokṣa</s>, <s>moraṭa</s>, and <s>palāśa</s>, filtered through cow urine,
should be collected and dried in the sun, together with <s>vajrakanda</s> and borax.
Lac and <s>śikhiśikhā</s> should be equal, and <s>vaikrānta</s> should be equal to all of them.
All this should be ground with the liquids of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> for the span of a day.
Having made it into a lump and placed it inside a closed crucible, it should be blown with a forced fire.
There itself the <s>vaikrānta</s> releases <s>sattva</s>, which binds mercury.

children.text: vaikrāṃtānāṃ palaikaṃ tu karṣaikaṃ ṭaṃkaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of <s>vaikrānta</s> and one <s>karṣa</s> of borax
should be impregnated for a day with the milks of <s>arka</s>, and then for a day with the liquid of <s>śigru</s>.
One should add one <s>karṣa</s> each of <s>guñjā</s>, oilcake, and <s>vahni</s>.

children.text: etena gulikāṃ kṛtvā koṣṭhīyantre dhamed dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: Having made a pill with this, one should blow it strongly in a furnace apparatus.
The <s>sattva</s> born from <s>vaikrānta</s> becomes like conch, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: vaikrāṃtaṃ vajrakaṃdaṃ ca samaṃ snukpayasā samam
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> and <s>vajrakanda</s>, in equal amounts, should be combined with an equal amount of <s>snuhī</s> milk.
Buffalo butter, together with honey, should also be ground for one day.
By blowing as before, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like an <s>indragopa</s> insect.
<s>Gairika</s> should be impregnated with the red group and the yellow group.
For seven days one should grind it for a <s>yāma</s>, joined with the five allies.
That pill releases pure <s>sattva</s> in the furnace apparatus.
White and black <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>: one should impregnate it with cow bile.
One should do this carefully a hundred times, with the five allies added.
By blowing it releases a penetrating <s>sattva</s> in the furnace apparatus.
Powdered <s>sasyaka</s> should be impregnated for one day with hare's blood.
Or with women's urine, or with cow urine; one should add one quarter part of turmeric.

children.text: mardyaṃ karaṃjatailena yāmaikaṃ golakaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: It should be ground with <s>karañja</s> oil for one <s>yāma</s>, and that ball
should be placed in a closed crucible and blown for half a <s>ghaṭikā</s> with a strong fire.
It releases an excellent <s>sattva</s>, resembling an <s>indragopa</s> insect.

children.text: caturvidhaṃ tu kāsīsaṃ raktaṃ pītaṃ sitāsitam
children.translated_text: <s>Kāsīsa</s> is fourfold: red, yellow, white, and black.
One should grind it with the bile group and with the juices of bitter <s>kośātakī</s>.
And also with the juices of <s>kāsamarda</s>, together with the five allies.
When those pills are blown in the furnace apparatus, it releases <s>sattva</s>.
One should cook <s>rājāvarta</s> in an iron vessel with buffalo ghee.
It should be cooked for a day with milk, together with the five allies.
One should make it into a lump with turmeric and the five products of the cow.
Through contact with <s>khadira</s> charcoals, it releases <s>sattva</s> in the furnace.
It has the form of the peak of an anthill; when broken it has the splendor of a blue lotus.
When rubbed it has the color of red ochre: this should be <s>srotoñjana</s>.
The <s>sattva</s> (essence) should be taken like <s>rājāvartaka</s>, even from <s>srotoñjana</s>.
The powder of mica-essence, and any powder of metal whatsoever,
both in equal amount, should be put into a crucible smeared for the joining of pairs.
It should be blown with the class of enemies; when they are cast in, it joins at once.

children.text: viṣaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaguṃjāśca khuraṃ śṛṅgaṃ ca bheṣajam
children.translated_text: Poison, borax, <s>guñjā</s>, hoof, horn, and a medicinal substance
should be ground with frog fat, and one should make a crucible coating.

children.text: tasyāṃ milati sattvāni cūrṇāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: In that, essences and various powders join.

children.text: trikṣāraṃ dhātakīpuṣpaṃ gugguluṃ ca samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: The three alkalis, <s>dhātakī</s> flower, and <s>guggulu</s>, each in equal amount,
ground with women's breast milk, make a coating useful for joining pairs.
<s>Varṣābhū</s>, plantain corm, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
together with <s>guñjā</s>, human skull, and borax, should be ground in equal amount.
With a coating made from this, as before, gold and mica join instantly.

children.text: tāraṃ ca vyomasattvaṃ ca anenaiva tu melayet
children.translated_text: Silver too and mica-essence should be joined by this same means.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, yak-tail hair, and the fruit of <s>kuśa</s> and cotton,
<s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>indragopa</s>, and <s>pāṣāṇabhedikā</s>, in equal amount,
should be ground with women's breast milk, and one should make a crucible coating.
All metals, essences, and also the great minerals
join; there is no doubt here, through the fire of intense blowing.
Poison, musk-rat flesh, and borax, ground together in equal amount,
should be made into a crucible coating by this very means, and one should place the material there.
Whatever joining of pairs there may be, it joins completely by blowing.
The ash of <s>apāmārga</s>, ground together with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil,
should be used to smear the crucible; having placed the pair in it, one should blow forcefully.
It certainly joins; there is no doubt, through the casting of the particular killing agents.
Gold-mica with lead and pyrite, copper-mica with sulfur,
and iron-mica with rock salt and cinnabar become firm through blowing.

children.text: nāgābhraṃ śilayā yuktaṃ vaṅgābhraṃ tālakena ca
children.translated_text: Lead-mica is combined with orpiment, tin-mica with <s>tālaka</s>,
and silver-mica with tin and <s>tāla</s>; every essence is like <s>tāla</s>.
It surely joins, there is no doubt, instantly when placed in the former crucible.

children.text: śvetābhrakasya sattvaṃ tu vaṅgacūrṇaṃ samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: The essence of white mica and tin powder should be in equal amounts.
One should grind them with plantain-corm water together with borax.
When blown in a sealed crucible, tin-mica joins instantly.
<s>Guñjā</s>, human skull, borax, and forest <s>śigru</s>

children.text: strīstanyena samaṃ piṣṭvā mūṣālepaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground together with women's breast milk, and one should make a crucible coating.

children.text: baṃgaṃ śvetābhrasattvaṃ ca cūrṇitaṃ tatra nikṣipet
children.translated_text: Tin and the essence of white mica, powdered, should be placed there.
After sealing and blowing, it certainly joins; one should digest it for work with silver.
First one should powder mica-essence, and add borax equal to a quarter of it.
Mercury and an equal part of borax should be ground for a day with the juices of <s>kākamācī</s>.
That pellet should be ground with mica portions and tin leaves.
When blown in the former crucible, tin-mica joins instantly.
One should cast one pala of well-melted lead into sour gruel,

children.text: palānāṃ śatamātre tu śatavāraṃ drutaṃ drutam ||
children.translated_text: in the measure of one hundred palas, a hundred times, quickly again and again.
With this very sour gruel one should impregnate it a hundred times.
Whatever substance for <s>cāraṇa</s> there may be, one should then digest it in mercury.

children.text: abhiṣeko hyayaṃ khyātaḥ kathyate tu matāntaram ||
children.translated_text: This is known as <s>abhiṣeka</s>; now another opinion is stated.
The three alkalis, the five salts, alum, green vitriol, and sulfur,
together with buffalo sour gruel, should stand in a copper vessel for three days.

children.text: sthitaṃ gharme punastasmin drutaṃ nāgaṃ vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: After it has stood in the heat, one should cast melted lead into it.
For silver work, or tin, one should sprinkle it a hundred times.
The wise know that liquid, standing in a copper vessel, as <s>abhiṣeka</s>.
With this, one should impregnate the substance for <s>cāraṇa</s> a hundred times.

children.text: dvaṃdvitaṃ vyomasattvaṃ ca bījāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Paired mica-essence, and various seeds,
and paired diamond-seed, when impregnated, should always be made to flow.

children.text: svarṇādi lohamakhilaṃ kṛtaśuddhacūrṇaṃ yojyaṃ pṛthaggaganasattvavare samāṃśam
children.translated_text: All metal, beginning with gold, purified and powdered, should be combined separately, in equal portion, with the excellent essence of mica.

children.text: taddvaṃdvitaṃ carati sūtavaro'bhiṣiktaṃ vipro yathā madhurapāyasamājyayuktam ||
children.translated_text: That paired material, when sprinkled, is consumed by the excellent <s>sūta</s> just as a Brahmin consumes sweet milk-rice mixed with ghee.
With <s>sūta</s> prepared from essence and digested, and well made to flow according to the number of qualities of the seed called cooked,

children.text: vijñāya yastu matimān sa tu vārtikendraścaṃdrārkavedhavidhinā kanakaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: the wise man who understands this becomes foremost among alchemists and makes gold by the method of piercing the moon and sun.

children.text: svarṇe nāgaṃ samāvartya māṣamātraṃ tu gharṣayet
children.translated_text: Having cast lead into gold, one should rub a measure of one <s>māṣa</s>
in a heated mortar; then one should place in it one pala of mercury.
Having added the juice of <s>siddhamūlī</s>, one should grind for a day with sour gruel,

children.text: gharme vā taptakhalve vā tato grāsaṃ tu dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: in the heat or in a heated mortar; then one should give it a morsel.
First the paired, impregnated essence, in a sixty-fourth part,

children.text: dattvā mardyaṃ dinaikaṃ tu cāraṇāyaṃtrake kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: should be added and ground for one day, then placed in the <s>cāraṇa</s> apparatus.
Kept for a day in the heat with citrons, it certainly consumes it.
For digestion: the three alkalis, the five salts, the sour class, and the milk of <s>snuhī</s>
should all be stirred with cow urine; with that one should smear a thick cloth.

children.text: tanmadhye jāritaṃ sūtaṃ baddhvā bhūrjena veṣṭayet
children.translated_text: In the middle of that, one should bind digested <s>sūta</s>, wrapping it with birch bark.
Combined with <s>siddhamūlī</s> and sour substances, it should be cooked for three days in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
Having taken it out, one should wash it with hot sour gruel in an iron vessel.
Then, after straining it through cloth, one should grind it in a heated vessel.
Again, the <s>pārada</s> (mercury) should be thoroughly washed by hand for as long as is needed.
It should be washed through a fourfold cloth; then it becomes stainless.
If it has not digested, it should again be ground for a day after adding an acid.
It should likewise be steamed in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus; it will become digested, without doubt.
Brick, wool burnt with jaggery, household soot, and <s>sarjikā</s>,

children.text: saiṃdhavena yutaṃ sarvaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ rasasya tu ||
children.translated_text: all combined with rock salt, should be one sixteenth of the <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
After adding that, it should be ground for a day in heat with the acid group.
With the acid group beginning with brick, it should be cooked for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe tvidaṃ kuryād grāsagrāhī bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whenever it is digested, one should do this; the mercury becomes able to take morsels.

children.text: dvātriṃśāṃśaṃ tato grāsaṃ dattvā cāryaṃ ca jārayet
children.translated_text: Then, after giving a morsel measuring one thirty-second part, one should feed and digest it.
After carrying out the same procedure as before up to steaming, the third morsel should be given.
A sixteenth part should be given; when that is digested, an eighth part should be given.
It should be digested by the previous method; thus the four morsels are completed.
Then it should be digested by means of the <s>kacchapayantra</s>; that is now described.
For each morsel one should put in <s>biḍa</s> above and below, in the amount of one eighth.

children.text: caturthāṃśaṃ tato grāsaṃ grāsaṃ deyaṃ samaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then a morsel of one fourth part is to be given, and again an equal morsel is to be given.

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe samaṃ deyamevaṃ jāryaṃ ca ṣaḍguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Whenever one is digested, an equal amount should be given; in this way it should be digested to six times the amount.

children.text: rāgāṇāṃ grahaṇārthaṃ ca grāse grāse tu pūrvavat
children.translated_text: For the sake of taking on colors, at each morsel the procedure is as before.
Thus it applies especially to paired combinations and to the essences.
It is beneficial for the digestion of the seeds of all metals, beginning with gold.
There the proper measure and method should be applied as before; it will be explained.
In the absence of mica essence, the essence of magnetic stone,
or the essence of sharp stone, paired as with mica essence,
should be digested by the previous method; the result will be the same for all of them.
In this way, whatever paired substance one digests sixfold in mercury,
once it has been digested with the perfected seed, it should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s>; that is now stated.
Essence of <s>tāpya</s>, resonant copper, and purified gold should be taken in equal amounts.
They should be melted in a crucible smeared for paired treatment and then sealed up.
After taking it out, it should again be smelted; it should be blown in an open crucible.
The washed essence from <s>mākṣika</s> should be added little by little.
It should then be cooked until only gold remains.
As before, it should be blown until only gold is left.
With <s>tāpya</s> essence and copper, the paired operation should be done again and again.
After blowing six times, the gold residue should be taken.
This is known as the perfected seed; it should be like a pomegranate flower.
With this perfected seed, the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations should be performed as before.
Then it should be digested in the same way; when it is digested, the mouth should likewise be bound.

children.text: bandhanaṃ śodhanaṃ caiva krāmaṇaṃ caiva pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Binding, purification, and <s>krāmaṇa</s> are to be done just as before.
When it is applied to melted <s>candrārka</s>, gold is produced with a thousandth part.
Now, regarding the digestion of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury), the substance previously impregnated should be used.
Then, for the purified essence, what was taught before should be digested.
Sulfur, however, in the <s>tulāyantra</s>, afterward consumes everything thoroughly.
There should be an upward-facing vessel with a mouth-tube, twelve finger-breadths long.
One should make it strong and made of iron, and another one similar to it.
In one vessel one should place the <s>sūta</s>; in the other, an equal amount of sulfur.

children.text: ekasyā mukhamadhye tu hyaparasyā mukhaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: The mouth of the other vessel should be inserted into the middle of the mouth of the first.

children.text: liptvā mṛllavaṇaiḥ saṃdhiṃ gaṃdhakādhaḥ puṭaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: After sealing the joint with clay and salt, a light <s>puṭa</s> heating should be placed beneath the sulfur.
Water should be placed below the mercury; it drinks in the sulfur smoke thoroughly.

children.text: jīrṇe gaṃdhe samudghāṭya tulyaṃ gaṃdhaṃ ca dāpayet
children.translated_text: When the sulfur is digested, one should open it and add an equal amount of sulfur.

children.text: ityevaṃ ṣoḍaśaguṇaṃ gaṃdhaṃ jāryaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way sulfur should be digested again and again to sixteen times the amount.
This digested king of <s>sūta</s> becomes opened by impregnation.

children.text: vyomasattvaṃ tāpyasattvaṃ śulbaṃ śuddhaṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Mica essence, <s>tāpya</s> essence, and purified copper should be taken in equal amounts.
They should then be melted in a crucible smeared for paired treatment and powdered.
It should be impregnated by sprinkling, as before, one hundred times.
As before, this should be fed into the mercury whose mouth has been opened by impregnation.
It should be digested in the same way, with care, until it becomes sixfold.

children.text: tatsūte sāritaṃ jāryaṃ siddhabījaṃ tu pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: In that mercury the perfected seed, processed by <s>sāraṇā</s>, should be digested as before.

children.text: mukhaṃ ca baṃdhanaṃ kṛtvā vedhāyāntaṃ pradāpayet
children.translated_text: After making the mouth and the binding, it should be administered up to the stage of piercing.
Combined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, <s>candrārka</s> becomes gold.
With a thousandth part, this is true; this mercury is <s>kāmarūpaka</s>, able to assume the desired form.
As before, the sulfur previously processed for purified <s>sūta</s>
should be properly digested sixfold by means of the <s>tulāyantra</s>, as before.
The juice of bitter <s>kośātakī</s>, combined with the juice of <s>lāṅgalī</s>,
should be added to the previous mercury in a mortar and ground for a day.
After feeding a quarter part of cooked seed, one should then digest it.
With the <s>biḍa</s> mixture as before, it should be digested in the same sequence.
Then, after subjecting the cooked seed three times to <s>sāraṇā</s>, it should be digested.
When piercing is applied to silver with a hundredth part, it becomes gold.
The silver should be ninety-eight parts, with one part of gold.
One part should be the piercing mercury; this is reckoned as hundredfold piercing.
The essence of <s>rasaka</s>, powdered or else impregnated,

children.text: pūrvavat kramayogena rase cāryaṃ ca jārayet ||
children.translated_text: should be fed into mercury and digested by the sequence as before.
Afterward, when it has reached eightfold, an equal amount of black mica essence
should be fed and digested in order, and cooked seed fourfold.
It should again be digested in mercury, furnished with <s>viḍa</s>, in the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s>.
Having brought that <s>rasa</s> (mercury) up to the point of taking color, one should wash that <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Unmattamuni</s> leaves, turmeric, and <s>kākamācikā</s>,
one should grind in equal parts with grain-sour gruel; with their liquids one should grind the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: saptāhaṃ taptakhalve tu kacchape tu dinaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: For seven days in a heated mortar, and in a tortoise apparatus, one should cook it for a day;
then with divine herbs alone one should grind it for three days.
Having sealed it in a diamond-crucible, for three days with a husk fire,

children.text: sveditaṃ ca punarmardyaṃ tadvadruddhvā dhamed dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: after heating it by steam, one should grind it again; sealed in that way, one should blow it strongly.
It becomes fixed, resembling a hen's egg; one should powder it again.
It should be ground for one day with the juice of <s>brahmapuṣpa</s>, and sealed again.
It should be cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; in this way four firings should be given.
With the juices of <s>vṛścikālī</s>, likewise, four firings.
With the juice of saffron, likewise, four firings;
having given one firing with citron juice, one should collect it.

children.text: sahasrāṃśena tenaiva taṃ śulbaṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: With that very substance, in a thousandth part, one should pierce that copper.

children.text: śuddhaṃ vā drāvitaṃ nāgaṃ vedhaṃ syātkrāmaṇena vai
children.translated_text: Or purified molten lead: the piercing occurs through <s>krāmaṇa</s> (activation).
All that becomes gold, excellent for divine ornaments.

children.text: svarṇārkaṃ tīkṣṇanāgaṃ ca samyak sasyābhrakasya ca
children.translated_text: Gold, <s>arka</s>, iron, lead, and properly the essence of green mica,

children.text: vaikrāṃtasya ca sattvaṃ ca cūrṇaṃ kuryātsamaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: and the essence of <s>vaikrānta</s> should each be powdered in equal amounts.
In a crucible smeared with a pairing mixture, after it has been sealed, one should blow it.

children.text: samuddhṛtya tu tatkhoṭaṃ mūṣāyāṃ prakaṭaṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: Having taken out that ingot, one should blow it uncovered in a crucible.

children.text: vāpo mākṣikacūrṇena datte deyaḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: A casting should be given with powdered pyrite, slowly, slowly;
until only gold remains, one should put it again into the <s>arka</s>.
As before, by the methodical sequence, one should blow it until only gold remains.
Doing it again just so, a gold <s>bīja</s> (seed) is produced.

children.text: abhrasattvāyasaṃ tāmraṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Mica-essence, iron, and copper should be powdered in equal amounts,

children.text: śuddhatāpyasya cūrṇaṃ ca tāmrasya dviguṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and the powder of purified pyrite should be twice the copper.
Sealed in a crucible smeared with a pairing mixture, one should blow with intense fire.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ ca ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: That ingot, made into fine powder, should be sealed and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ pañcapuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ drute svarṇe ca vāhayet
children.translated_text: Cooked in this way with five firings, it should be carried into molten gold.
One should blow it in an open crucible until it is tenfold, gradually.
Pyrite powder should be added; one should cast it little by little.
Having removed the gold remainder, this is a gold <s>bīja</s>.
One should digest an equal amount of gold <s>bīja</s> in <s>sūta</s> (mercury), as with mica-essence.
Then with a hundredth part of that, smeared with honey, one should coat
equal leaves of moon and sun, that is, silver and copper, and wrap them with <s>arka</s> leaves.
In a <s>dolāyantra</s>, in a <s>sāranāla</s>, one should cook them gently for ten days.
Having taken them out, one should melt them down; it becomes divine gold.
A part of killed iron and <s>arka</s>, and pyrite powder in equal amount,
this should be carried into molten gold, gradually, until tenfold.
Taking the gold remainder, this is a gold <s>bīja</s>.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ kāṃtaṃ mṛtaṃ caiva śulvaṃ tāraṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Iron, magnetite, killed material, copper, and silver, each in equal amount,
sealed in a crucible smeared with a pairing mixture, one should blow with intense fire.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ drāvite svarṇe vāhyaṃ daśaguṇaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: That ingot should be carried into molten gold, gradually in tenfold quantity.
As before, with pyrite powder, this is the supreme gold <s>bīja</s>.
As desired, one should digest one gold <s>bīja</s>, a quarter part, in <s>rasa</s>.
As before, by the methodical sequence, one should make it flow with essence-seed.
When it has been made to flow, one should digest it in the same way; with the follow-up flux one should digest it.

children.text: pratisārya tato jāryaṃ mukhaṃ baddhvā ca bandhayet ||
children.translated_text: After counter-fluxing, it is then to be digested; having closed the mouth, one should bind it.
With a fifth part, through ten operations, one should cause piercing in silver.
Combined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, it becomes divine gold.

children.text: nāgaṃ rasakasattvaṃ ca tāmraṃ bhāgaṃ kramottaram
children.translated_text: Lead, the essence of calamine, and copper, in successively increasing parts,
having been blown, should be carried into gold; one should cast sixfold quantity gradually.

children.text: svarṇaśeṣaṃ tu tajjāryaṃ samāṃśaṃ pārade kramāt
children.translated_text: The gold remainder is then to be digested, in equal part, in mercury, in order.
As before, one should carry out the operations from killing through binding.
With a sixtieth part of this, as before, gold will be produced.
One should kill copper with pyrite, as it is killed with sulfur.
That copper should be carried into lead in the middle of a crucible, blowing again and again.
Until it is a hundredfold, adding pyrite powder gradually again and again,
one should carry that copper into gold, thirty-twofold, in sequence.
The gold remainder, that <s>bīja</s>, should be digested in equal part in <s>rasa</s>.
With this very <s>bīja</s> one should make it flow and digest it again.
As before, by the methodical sequence, one should carry it through to binding.
Combined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, one should pierce with a thousandth part.
Moon and sun become gold, excellent for divine ornaments.
The essences of calamine and mica, and copper powder, in successively increasing quantity,
sealed in a crucible smeared with a pairing mixture, after blowing, one should take it out.
Having added pyrite powder equal to that ingot portion, one should grind with acid.
Sealed, one should cook it in a light firing; in this way one should cook it with five firings.
That powder should be carried into gold while it is being blown, gradually.
Until it is multiplied a thousandfold, that <s>bīja</s> should be digested in <s>rasa</s>.
With this very substance one should carefully make it flow until it is a hundredfold.

children.text: jāraṇaṃ sāraṇaṃ caiva baṃdhanāntaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Digestion and flowing, and up to binding, are as before.
Having done this, silver becomes gold with a hundred-thousandth part.
Mica-essence, copper, and lead should be powdered in increasing sequence.
Sealed in a crucible smeared with a pairing mixture, one should blow with intense fire.
One should grind powdered <s>tāpya</s> in an equal amount with every acid substance.

children.text: ruddhvā pañcapuṭaiḥ pacyāt taccūrṇaṃ vāhayed drutam ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, one should cook it with five <s>puṭas</s>; that powder should quickly be introduced into the molten metal.
In gold, up to a hundredfold, that gold should be digested.
By the proper method, up to a hundredfold, one should make it flow by that same threefold placing.

children.text: sārite jāraṇaṃ kuryād baṃdhanāntaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: When it has been made to flow, one should perform digestion, and the binding at the end, as before.
By a ten-thousandth part of that very substance, silver becomes gold.
Or else the former powder, increased a thousandfold, should be used in molten
gold, introduced gradually; that seed should be digested in mercury.
Until it is increased a thousandfold, one should make it flow three times with that same substance.

children.text: sāritaṃ jārayetpaścāt punaḥ sāryaṃ ca jārayet ||
children.translated_text: After it has been made to flow, one should digest it; then again it should be made to flow and digested.
Through the procedure of the seven chains, the wise man should digest what has been made to flow.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā koṭivedhī bhavedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: Having bound the mouth and bound the mercury, the mercury becomes capable of piercing ten million parts.
Joined with <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrative action), the moon and sun metals become gold.
One should powder <s>vimalā</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, increasing the portions successively.
In a crucible smeared with a paired compound, one should form that lump and powder it well.
It should be ground with acids and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>; in this way one should heat it five times.
It should be introduced tenfold into silver, repeatedly throwing in powdered <s>tāla</s>.

children.text: etad bījaṃ samaṃ sūte jārayet pūrvavat kramāt
children.translated_text: This seed, in equal amount, should be digested in mercury in the former sequence.
Then, with the silver-seed, one should make it flow through the threefold <s>sāraṇā</s> procedure.

children.text: tenaiva tu śatāṃśena drutaṃ tāmraṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: With just a hundredth part of that, one should pierce molten copper.
It becomes fine silver, shining like a conch, jasmine, and the moon.
Calcined tin and the essence of <s>tāla</s> should be prepared as an equal powder.
One should introduce it sixteenfold into silver, blowing it again and again.
That seed should be digested in mercury, gradually, until it is tenfold.
Then, with that silver-seed, one should make it flow through the threefold <s>sāraṇā</s> procedure.
With a thousandth part of this, one should cause the piercing of copper.
That copper becomes silver, resembling a conch, jasmine, and the moon.
The essence of white mica and of <s>tāla</s>, and the essence of <s>rasaka</s>,
with silver <s>mākṣīka</s> as the fourth, should be prepared as an equal powder.
Tin powder equal to the powder should all be blown together in one place.
In a crucible smeared for paired union, the lump that is produced should be powdered.
Ground with acids, it should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>; in this way one should heat it five times.
That powder should be introduced into silver, and one should blow until it is tenfold.

children.text: tattāraṃ rasarājasya samaṃ jāryaṃ krameṇa vai
children.translated_text: That silver should then be digested, in equal amount, with the king of mercury, in due order.
As before, it should be made to flow three times; the mercury becomes capable of piercing a hundred parts.

children.text: evaṃ sattvābhrasattvaṃ ca cūrṇaṃ dvaṃdvaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: In the same way, essence and mica-essence, together with a paired powder, are prepared as before.

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ tālakaṃ dattvā amlaiḥ piṣṭvā nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: Having added one quarter part of <s>tālaka</s>, and having ground it with acids and sealed it,
one should cook it with five <s>puṭas</s>; in this way it should be introduced twelvefold into silver.
This seed, in equal amount, should be digested, each component in ten parts.
Tin and the essence of white mica should each be ten parts.
<s>Vimalā</s> called silver, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, should each be five parts.
In a crucible smeared with a paired compound, one should blow it forcefully.

children.text: amlapiṣṭaṃ puṭe pācyaṃ pañcavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ground with acids, it should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> five times, again and again.
That should be introduced into the portion of silver, repeatedly throwing in silver powder.
That seed should be digested gradually into the king of mercury until it is a hundredfold.
With the silver-seed, one should perform the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations according to rule.
With a ten-thousandth part of this very substance, one should pierce molten copper.
It becomes divine silver, resembling a conch, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: itthaṃ rase kanakabījamanantayogaiḥ kṛtvā bhiṣak tamakhilaṃ vidhivacca jāryam
children.translated_text: Thus, having made in mercury a gold-seed by countless procedures, the physician should digest all of it according to rule.

children.text: tenaiva hemanicayaṃ rajataṃ ca kṛtvā dāridryadāhamakhileṣu janeṣu kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: With that very substance, after making masses of gold and silver, he should burn away poverty among all people.
Now the preparation of seeds fit for the womb-procedure, useful in coloring by many methods,
for digested human mercury: all of that is now stated.

children.text: gaṃdhakaṃ mākṣikaṃ nāgaṃ sarvaṃ tulyaṃ vicūrṇayet
children.translated_text: Sulfur, <s>mākṣika</s>, and lead should all be powdered in equal measure.

children.text: triguṇaṃ vāhayetsvarṇaṃ drāvitaṃ tu dhaman dhaman ||
children.translated_text: One should introduce them threefold into melted gold, blowing again and again.
This coarse <s>pūtibīja</s> (putrid seed) melts at once in the womb.

children.text: nāgaṃ svarṇaṃ samaṃ tāpyaṃ śilācūrṇaṃ kṣipan kṣipan
children.translated_text: Lead, gold, and equal <s>tāpya</s> should be treated by repeatedly adding powdered <s>śilā</s>.

children.text: jīrṇe nāge punardeyam evaṃ vāratrayaṃ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: When the lead has been digested, more should be added; in this way, slowly, three times.

children.text: etad bījaṃ dravatyeva rasagarbhe tu mardanāt ||
children.translated_text: This seed indeed melts in the womb of mercury through grinding.
The essence of <s>tāpya</s> and gold should be blown while repeatedly adding <s>tāpya</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ triguṇaṃ vāhyaṃ tāpyasattvaṃ ca hāṭake
children.translated_text: In this way the essence of <s>tāpya</s> should be introduced threefold into gold.
That seed melts at once in the womb of the king of mercury.
Then one should melt equal parts of the essence of <s>tāpya</s> and gold.
A sheet prepared for <s>kaṇṭavedha</s> should be treated with sulfur and salt.
Having added it together with acid, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> until only gold remains.
This seed melts in the womb of the lord of mercury through grinding.
<s>Tāpya</s>, with an equal amount of rock salt, should be ground with acids and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
It should be ground again and cooked again, up to twelve times.

children.text: asya tulyaṃ mṛtaṃ nāgaṃ sarvamamlena peṣayet
children.translated_text: An equal amount of calcined lead should be ground all together with acid.

children.text: anena svarṇapatrāṇi liptvā liptvā dhamed dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: With this, having smeared gold leaves again and again, one should blow them strongly.

children.text: drutaṃ ca vāpayettaṃ tu saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then one should cast that molten material seven times, again and again.
This seed melts in the womb of the lord of mercury through grinding.
<s>Śilā</s>, <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, <s>tāpya</s>, sulfur, lead, and borax
should all be ground with chickpea-acid for the length of a day.

children.text: rasasyaitat ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ dattvā bījaṃ ca dāpayet
children.translated_text: After giving one-sixteenth part of this <s>rasa</s> (mercurial preparation), he should also cause the seed to be added.

children.text: mucyate yatra yatraiva tattad dravati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Wherever it is released, that very thing melts at once.
One should collect the ash-alkali produced from <s>apāmārga</s> and <s>palāśa</s>.

children.text: ṭaṃkaṇaṃ ca yavakṣāraṃ kāsīsaṃ ca suvarcalam ||
children.translated_text: Also <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), barley-alkali, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and <s>suvarcala</s>,
sea salt, rock salt, <s>rājī</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>navasāraka</s>,
camphor and sour gruel in equal measure, triturated with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>.
With this very mixture one should make a coating for the crucible, and also with the <s>biḍa</s> mixture.
The coating should be one finger-breadth thick; this is the crucible apparatus.
Into it one should place <s>sūta</s> (mercury) from seed melted in the womb-apparatus.

children.text: ruddhvā svedyaṃ dinaikaṃ tu kārīṣāgnau grasatyalam ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, it should be steamed for one day in a cow-dung fire; it consumes fully.
Again one should melt the paired essences of <s>tāpya</s> and mica.
Dead copper and powdered <s>tāpya</s> should be fed into it little by little.

children.text: triguṇe vāhite tasmin rañjitaṃ vāhitaṃ tu tat ||
children.translated_text: When three times the amount has been fed into it, that substance is colored and assimilated.

children.text: gomūtrai raktavargaṃ tu piṣṭvā tenaiva bhāvayet
children.translated_text: One should grind the red group with cow urine and impregnate with that very mixture.

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ mākṣikaṃ gaṃdhaṃ śilācūrṇaṃ samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Cinnabar, <s>mākṣika</s>, sulfur, and powdered <s>śilā</s> should be in equal amounts.

children.text: bhāvitaṃ saptavārāṇi śoṣyaṃ peṣyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After being impregnated seven times, it should be dried and ground again and again.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ tāmraṃ samaṃ cūrṇya pūrvavad dvaṃdvamelitam ||
children.translated_text: Sharp iron and copper, in equal amounts, should be powdered and combined in paired treatment as before.
Into that, when melted, one should cast the previous powder and then quench it.
This should be done in oil made from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, combined with the red group.
Doing it in this way ten times, this becomes a coloring agent for <s>rasa</s>.
One should impregnate <s>darada</s> with the red group and cow urine three times.
When equal parts of <s>vimala</s> and copper have been melted, one should feed it in while blowing.

children.text: saptadhā daradaṃ taṃ tu syādidaṃ rasarañjakam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>darada</s> should be used seven times; this becomes a coloring agent for <s>rasa</s>.
Gold, lead, and mica essence, in equal parts, should be combined by paired treatment.
<s>Śilā</s>, red ocher, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, and the red group

children.text: samāṃśaṃ cūrṇayetsarvaṃ vāpo deyo hyanena vai
children.translated_text: should all be powdered in equal amounts; with this the casting is indeed to be given
again and again to the previously paired and melted <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: daśavāraṃ kṛte vāpe rañjako'yaṃ rasasya ca ||
children.translated_text: When the casting has been done ten times, this is a coloring agent for <s>rasa</s>.
Red <s>manaḥśilā</s> should be impregnated with the juices of barley and tamarind
twenty times with care; with that paste one should smear a lead sheet.
It should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> until it has become powder.
There should be three parts of <s>rasaka</s> and one part of <s>darada</s>,
and one part each of the three, <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, and poison.
One should grind them with the acid juice of citron and smear with that paste.
It should be placed in the womb of the crucible; then the earlier lead should be placed there.
When it is melted, one should take it out, smear the crucible, and blow it again.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā dhāmyaṃ nāgaṃ svarṇanibhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: In this way it should be blown seven times; the lead becomes like gold.

children.text: pītābhrakasya sattvaṃ tu pūrvanāgaṃ ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: The essence of yellow mica and the earlier lead should be in equal amount.
Combined in paired treatment by the previous method, it should also be sprinkled as before.

children.text: samukhe sūtarāje tu pūrvavat ṣaḍguṇaṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: In the open-mouthed king <s>sūta</s>, as before, it should be processed sixfold in sequence.
Then, for that <s>rasendra</s>, there is the seed that melts in the womb.
One should add a quarter part in a mortar together with citron juice.
One should grind it either with sour liquids from chickpea or with the womb-melting preparation.
It certainly melts within its interior; then one should digest it in the crucible apparatus.

children.text: ityevaṃ drāvitaṃ jāryaṃ yāvad bījasamaṃ rase
children.translated_text: Thus the melted substance should be digested until the seed is equal to the <s>rasa</s>.
At the end, with the three beginning with <s>sāraṇā</s>, it should be processed in order as before.
One should pierce, as desired, any one of silver, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, <s>mahi</s>, or copper.
With just a thousandth part of that, it becomes divine gold.
Diamond combined in paired treatment with gold and sprinkled as before
should be digested in open-mouthed <s>sūta</s>, in an equal amount, like mica essence.
With that gold-diamond, one should digest the already digested substance three times.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā krāmaṇena tu yojayet
children.translated_text: After binding the mouth and binding the <s>rasa</s>, one should combine it with <s>krāmaṇa</s>.

children.text: caṃdrārke tu sahasrāṃśaṃ divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: In <s>candrārka</s>, a thousandth part becomes divine gold.
One should take the urine of a bull, or of an elephant or buffalo.

children.text: tanmadhye sūtanāgaṃ tu drāvitaṃ saptadhā kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Into it one should put melted <s>sūta</s>-lead seven times.
Then one should make sheets of that, pierced at the neck.

children.text: gaṃdhakaṃ cūrṇitaṃ śuddhaṃ patrāṇāṃ tu caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Powdered purified sulfur should be four times the amount of the sheets.
Moistened with lac dye, it should be made like a cotton leaf or cloth.

children.text: tasya śuṣkasya pṛṣṭhe tu nararomāṇi dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: On the back of that when dry one should place human hairs.

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe cūrṇitaṃ gaṃdhaṃ tato nāgadalāni ca
children.translated_text: On its back, powdered sulfur should be placed, and then lead leaves.
Sulfur, human hairs, and that cotton should be placed on the back.
With this one should make a wick and wrap it outside with thread.
It should be kept in <s>karañja</s> oil for ten nights.

children.text: prajvālya cobhayāgre tu drutaṃ tailaṃ samāharet
children.translated_text: After lighting both ends, one should collect the melted oil.
It should be kept in a vessel together with sour gruel; after drawing it out from that, one should preserve it.
Carefully in a glass bottle: this is the sulfur-lead <s>druti</s>.
Purified <s>sūta</s> should be ground firmly together with turmeric powder
until the powder becomes black; it should be washed with hot sour gruel.
One should do this twenty-one times; then one should begin digestion.

children.text: amlairmanaḥśilāṃ piṣṭvā tena lepaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: After grinding <s>manaḥśilā</s> with acidic liquids, one should make a coating with it.
In this cow-udder-shaped crucible one should place the previous <s>rasa</s>.
The previously mentioned sulfur <s>druti</s> should be added gradually in one-sixty-fourth part.
After sealing the crucible and drying it, in a pit filled with cow dung,
one should place half the crucible there, with a fire of dung-cakes and husks.
A <s>puṭa</s> called pigeon-sized should be given, and when it has cooled by itself one should take it out.
If there is concern that it has not been digested, one should add juice of <s>siṃhavallī</s>.
The measure should be four drops; likewise one should cook it in a pit by <s>puṭa</s> heating.
In this way the melt of sulfur and lead should be digested again and again, in sequence.
When <s>sūta</s> (mercury) has been digested to three times the amount, it becomes like <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold in luster.
Of this mercury, one should take a quarter part of well-powdered cooked seed.
It should be ground with sour gruel of chickpeas; within a watch it liquefies fully in the womb.
The substance placed in the crucible apparatus should indeed be melted by sweating as before.

children.text: jīrṇe bījaṃ punardattvā drāvyaṃ garbhe'tha jārayet ||
children.translated_text: When it is digested, seed should again be added, and then the melted substance should be digested in the womb.

children.text: evaṃ bījaṃ samaṃ jāryaṃ pakvaṃ vā rañjane kramāt
children.translated_text: In this way an equal amount of seed should be digested, cooked, or else gradually used for coloring.

children.text: garbhaṃ drāvaṇabījaṃ vā yatheṣṭaikaṃ tu jārayet ||
children.translated_text: One should digest either the womb substance or the liquefying seed, whichever one is desired.

children.text: tatastu triguṇaṃ rītistāraṃ vāhyaṃ dhaman dhaman
children.translated_text: Then brass or silver should be externally treated to threefold measure, by blowing again and again.
That becomes the preparation for silver; after making it into leaf, one should smear it.
With honey, it should again be smeared with one thirty-second part of the former mercury.
It should be wrapped in leaves of <s>arka</s> and cooked in a <s>dolāyantra</s> with sour gruel.
At the end of ten days, after taking it out and melting it, it becomes gold.

children.text: samukhe nirmukhe vātha rasarāje tu jārayet
children.translated_text: Then one should digest it in the king of <s>rasa</s>, whether its mouth is opened or not opened.
Mica powder, fed as before, should be digested in sequence.
Until it becomes sixty-fourfold, it should then be subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s> and digested.
It should be fed and digested in that same way until it becomes sixtyfold.

children.text: tato mākṣikasatvaṃ ca pādāṃśaṃ tatra jārayet ||
children.translated_text: Then a quarter part of the essence of <s>mākṣika</s> should be digested there.
Whatever essence one extracts from the <s>mahārasas</s> and <s>uparasas</s>,

children.text: tanmadhyagaṃ tu pādāṃśaṃ sūte dattvā vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: a quarter part from among them should be added to the mercury and triturated.
It should be ground in a heated mortar for four watches, joined with the womb-melter.
All those substances certainly melt; then they should be digested in the crucible apparatus.
Thus all essences should be digested by the melting procedure as well.

children.text: rañjitaṃ pakvabījaṃ ca śuddhaṃ tāmraṃ ca hāṭakam ||
children.translated_text: The colored cooked seed, purified copper, and gold,
the womb-liquefying seed, and calcined <s>tīkṣṇa</s> should all be taken in equal amounts.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca marditaṃ khoṭaṃ kṛtvā dhāmyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After grinding everything and making a <s>khoṭa</s> mass, it should be blown again and again.

children.text: kṣipenmākṣikacūrṇaṃ ca tāmre tīkṣṇe kṣayaṃ gate
children.translated_text: When the copper and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> have diminished, one should add powdered <s>mākṣika</s>.

children.text: samuddhṛtya tu tad bījaṃ pādāṃśaṃ pūrvapārade ||
children.translated_text: Then, after taking out that seed, a quarter part should be put into the previous mercury.
As before, one should melt it in the womb and then digest it in the crucible apparatus.
By this sequence the seed should gradually be digested to thirty-two times the amount.
When the womb substance is digested, the melted mercury is colored; that is now explained.
Lead calcined with sulfur is the means for preparing cooked seed.
That lead, equal to gold, should be placed in a closed crucible and blown.
Its powder, after being sprinkled, should be given into the <s>rasa</s> as a quarter part.
It should be ground with the class of sour liquids or with the womb-liquefier.
It should be worked in a heated mortar for four watches and then digested in the crucible apparatus.
By this ordered procedure one should digest it to the <s>kalā</s> proportion.

children.text: mṛtaṃ śulbaṃ mṛtaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ svarṇe vāhyaṃ tu ṣaḍguṇam
children.translated_text: Calcined copper and calcined <s>tīkṣṇa</s> should be externally applied to gold in sixfold amount.

children.text: etad bījaṃ tato jāryaṃ kramād yāvaccaturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Then this seed should be digested gradually until it reaches fourfold measure.

children.text: pūrvavad drāvitaṃ khalve mūṣāyantre ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: It should be melted in the mortar as before, and in the crucible apparatus as before.
Then the mercury, with its color fixed, becomes saffron-like in appearance.

children.text: ityevaṃ rañjanaṃ sūte kṛtvā sāryaṃ tridhā kramāt
children.translated_text: Thus, after coloring has been done in the mercury, it should be subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s> in three stages.
What has undergone <s>sāraṇa</s> should be digested in urine in the crucible apparatus, with repeated <s>puṭa</s> heatings.
Afterward one should subject the digested substance to <s>sāraṇa</s>, and digest what has been subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s>.
By this ordered procedure, according to the course of seven chains,

children.text: tatastasya mukhaṃ baddhvā pūrvavad bandhayecca tam
children.translated_text: one should then bind its mouth and bind it as before.
Joined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, it should pierce with a ten-millionth part.

children.text: drutaṃ tāmraṃ tu taddivyaṃ bhavetsvarṇaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That melted copper becomes divine gold; there is no doubt.
Mercury extracted from cinnabar should be ground with <s>bhūnāga</s> for three days.
Then it should be distilled in a heated mortar, and what adheres above should be collected.
A quarter part of paired mica essence should be digested into it.

children.text: tato mākṣikasatvaṃ ca pādāṃśaṃ tatra jārayet ||
children.translated_text: Then a quarter part of <s>mākṣika</s> essence should be digested there.
The paired procedure is as before, and the measured cooking is also as before.
The essence that was previously distilled from the <s>mahārasas</s> and <s>uparasas</s>,

children.text: tatsattvaṃ ca pṛthakpādaṃ sūte dattvā vimardayet
children.translated_text: each such essence should be added separately to the mercury as a quarter part and triturated.
It should be worked for one day in a heated mortar, combined with the womb-liquefier.

children.text: dravatyeva tato jāryaṃ mūṣāyantraṃ tu pūrvavat
children.translated_text: It certainly melts; then it should be digested in the crucible apparatus as before.

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe punardeyaṃ pratisattvaṃ krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: As each portion is digested, each essence should again be added in order.
Then, in the same way, a quarter part of the womb-liquefying seed
should be melted as before and digested by this sequence until sixfold.
From <s>sāraṇa</s> and the other operations up to <s>krāmaṇa</s>, it should be made to pierce silver.
With a thousandth part, that silver becomes gold with the luster of <s>jāmbūnada</s>.
One should extract the juice of tender leaves of the <s>śākavṛkṣa</s>.
Likewise, the juice of <s>brahmapuṣpa</s> flowers and the juice of <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s> should be taken.
With these liquids, purified sulfur should be impregnated for seven days.
Very purified mercury should be placed in the middle of a brick chamber.
Its mouth should be covered from above with a clean cloth.

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ pūrvagaṃdhaṃ tu dattvā śrāveṇa rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: After adding one tenth part of the previously prepared sulfur, one should close it with a saucer-lid.

children.text: pṛṣṭhe laghupuṭaṃ deyaṃ jīrṇe gaṃdhaṃ punaḥ kṣipet
children.translated_text: A light <s>puṭa</s> heating should be applied on top; when the sulfur is digested, it should be added again.
In the same way it should be digested by <s>puṭa</s> heating, and sulfur should again be added.

children.text: evaṃ jāryaṃ samaṃ gaṃdhaṃ tato yaṃtrātsamuddharet
children.translated_text: Thus an equal amount of sulfur should be digested, and then it should be taken out of the apparatus.

children.text: athavā gaṃdhatulyaṃ tu jāryaṃ tena rasasya tu ||
children.translated_text: Or else sulfur equal to it should be digested with that mercury.
It should be digested by the former method, or else inside a glass flask.
Of this very king of mercury, an equal portion should be mica essence,
combined by the paired operation and digested as before; the rule for the dose is also as before.

children.text: tato rasakasatvaṃ ca jāryam aṣṭaguṇaṃ rase
children.translated_text: Then the essence of <s>rasaka</s> should be digested into the mercury to eight times its amount,
and likewise iron, copper, and lead, successively to eight times their amount in the mercury.
Each one should be digested carefully after being sprinkled and treated as before.
Then the cooked <s>bīja</s> (seed) should be digested, in order, until it is thirty-two times the amount.
Now, for this king of mercury, there is the <s>bīja</s> that melts the inner core.
Having placed an equal amount in a heated mortar, together with the inner-melting agent,

children.text: mardayeddinamekaṃ tu garbhe dravati tad drutam
children.translated_text: one should grind it for one day; then it quickly melts in the interior.
Afterward it should be digested in the crucible apparatus, by sweating, just as before.

children.text: tajjīrṇe raṃjakaṃ bījaṃ tulyaṃ dattvātha pūrvavat
children.translated_text: When that has been digested, one should add an equal amount of coloring <s>bīja</s>, and then, as before,

children.text: drāvayet dravagarbhe tu tadvajjāryaṃ krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: melt it in the molten interior; in the same way it should be digested in sequence.
Until it has become fourfold, the molten substance should carefully be digested within the interior.
By this ordered procedure the mercury becomes like lac in color.
Then, with cooked <s>bīja</s>, that mercury should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> and digested in sequence.
One should perform a repeated <s>sāraṇā</s>, then digest it and again subject it to <s>sāraṇā</s>.
By the procedure of the seven chains, one should close its mouth and then bind it.
When it is furnished with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, one should cause <s>vedha</s> (piercing transmutation) in copper.

children.text: nāge vā koṭibhāgena divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: Or, in lead, with a ten-millionth part, it becomes excellent gold.
Grain-mica should be treated in sequence with the juices of tamarind and <s>brahmamāṇḍūkī</s>.
One should grind it for three days, and then impregnate it with tamarind juice.

children.text: gharme dinatrayaṃ yāvat śoṣyaṃ peṣyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: It should be dried in the sun for three days, and ground again and again.

children.text: mṛtkharpare śuddhasūtaṃ kṣiptvā soṣṇaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: After placing purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in an earthen pan, one should make it warm.
Sulfur in the measure of a <s>truṭi</s>, and the previously prepared mica in the measure of a <s>truṭi</s>,
should be added again and again and cooked over a gentle fire; it becomes a mica paste.
The sulfur should be impregnated with the juices of <s>ekavīrā</s> in the sun twenty-one times.

children.text: taṃ gaṃdhakaṃ snigdhabhāṇḍe drāvya mṛdvagninā kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: That sulfur should be melted in a greased vessel over a gentle fire and added.

children.text: tanmadhye pūrvapiṣṭiṃ tu dolāyaṃtre vidhau pacet
children.translated_text: Into its midst one should put the previous paste and cook it according to the procedure of the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
In this way one should digest sulfur to six times the amount by a gentle fire.
One part of that mercury and sixteen parts of the cooked <s>bīja</s>,
well colored, should be powdered and then combined by the paired operation.
As before, in a crucible smeared for the paired operation, and by blowing,
this is known as mercury-seed; after powdering it, one should sprinkle and impregnate it.
Now, for purified <s>sūta</s> that has been placed in a glass flask,

children.text: pūrvavad bhāvitaṃ gaṃdhaṃ jāryaṃ tasyaiva ṣaḍguṇam ||
children.translated_text: the sulfur impregnated as before should be digested into that very mercury to six times the amount.
Or one should digest it in the <s>tulāyantra</s>, according to the procedure of the <s>gaurīyantra</s>.
Of that very king of mercury, the mercury-seed should be a quarter part.
As before, one should melt it in the interior, and then digest it in the crucible apparatus.

children.text: anena kramayogena drāvyaṃ jāryaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: By this ordered procedure it should be melted and digested again and again,
until the mercury-seed amounts to sixteen times the mercury.
Two parts of purified silver and one part of purified gold

children.text: samāvartya tu tatpatraṃ kṛtvā pūrvarasena vai ||
children.translated_text: should be melted together; then, after making that into leaf, with the previous mercury
one should coat it, smeared with honey, using a thousandth part of that again.
It should be wrapped in leaves born from <s>arka</s> and cooked in the <s>dolāyantra</s> with sour gruel.

children.text: daśāhaṃ pācitaṃ drāvyaṃ divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: When cooked for ten days, the melted substance becomes excellent gold.
Very pure lead powder, sprinkled and treated as before,
should be digested, like mica essence, in the mouth-opened lordly mercury.
It should be digested in sequence until it is thirty-six times the amount.
The inner-melting <s>bīja</s> too should be melted in sequence as before.
One should digest three times its amount; then the <s>bīja</s> that colors it again

children.text: samaṃ jāryaṃ punaḥ jāryaṃ pakvabījena vai kramāt ||
children.translated_text: should be digested in an equal amount; again it should be digested with cooked <s>bīja</s> in sequence.
By the procedure of the seven chains, one should stop up its mouth and then bind it.
When it is furnished with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, the mercury becomes capable of ten-millionfold <s>vedha</s>.
Tin should be digested like lead, in sequence, until it is thirty-six times the amount.
As before, after it has been melted in the interior, the silver-seed should be digested.
When it has become threefold, one should then subject it to <s>sāraṇā</s> with that very substance.
By the procedure of the seven chains, one should close its mouth and then bind it.
When it is furnished with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, one should cause <s>vedha</s> in copper.
With a ten-millionth part, that silver becomes like jasmine and the moon.

children.text: samukhe nirmukhe vātha sūtarāje tu jārayet
children.translated_text: In the king of <s>sūta</s>, whether with its mouth opened or not opened, one should digest

children.text: dvaṃdvitaṃ vyomasatvaṃ tu yāvad aṣṭaguṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: mica essence combined by the paired operation, until it likewise becomes eightfold.

children.text: tato rasakasatvaṃ ca jāryam aṣṭaguṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Then the essence of <s>rasaka</s> should likewise be digested to eight times the amount.
And an equal portion of cooked <s>bīja</s> should be digested like mica essence.

children.text: svarṇena dvaṃdvitaṃ vajraṃ samāṃśena tu jārayet
children.translated_text: Diamond combined with gold by the paired operation should be digested in an equal portion.
As before, in the <s>kacchapa</s> apparatus, and likewise with the <s>biḍa</s> mixture.
The inner-melting <s>bīja</s>, a quarter portion, should be placed in a heated mortar.
One should grind it with the acidic juice of citron; it melts in the interior at once.
Or, when the inner-melting compound is added, it melts through grinding.
That mercury should be cooked by means of the crucible apparatus over a cow-dung fire.
When it has been digested, the <s>bīja</s> should again be melted; one should digest it and melt it again.
In this way the inner-melting <s>bīja</s> should be digested until it is fourfold.

children.text: tatastu raṃjakaṃ bījaṃ tadvajjāryaṃ samaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: Then the coloring <s>bīja</s> should likewise be digested in an equal amount, in order.
From <s>sāraṇā</s> and the other operations through <s>krāmaṇa</s>, one should carry out the process in sequence as before.

children.text: tāre tāmre bhujaṃge vā koṭibhāgena yojayet
children.translated_text: It should be applied in silver, copper, or lead with a ten-millionth part.
It makes divine gold, the finest ornament of the gods.
One should digest it in the lordly king of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), with its mouth opened, as one does mica essence.
The eight metals, from gold and the rest down to <s>muṇḍa</s>, should each, separately and in sequence,
be treated to eight times the amount, each one with the sprinkling as before.
All the essences beginning with mica should each, separately and in sequence, be made threefold.
They should be digested separately in the <s>kūrma-yantra</s> with the <s>biḍa</s> mixture, as before.
Then a quarter-quarter portion of the inner-melting <s>bīja</s> should be taken.

children.text: pūrvavaddrāvitaṃ jāryaṃ triguṇaṃ tu yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: Melted as before, it should be digested until it becomes threefold.
Then one should perform <s>sāraṇā</s> with cooked <s>bīja</s> and digest it three times.
Thus one should do this seven times; then, after closing its mouth, one should bind it.
It becomes capable of <s>vedha</s> at the sight of smoke; copper becomes gold.

children.text: evaṃ cāraṇajāraṇaṃ bahuvidhaṃ kṛtvā rase saṃkramaṃ garbhe drāvaṇabījakaṃ ca vidhinā garbhadrutaṃ kārayet
children.translated_text: Having performed many kinds of feeding and digestion and introduced them into the mercury, one should, by rule, make the inner-melting <s>bīja</s> melted in its interior.

children.text: jīrṇe raṃjanasāraṇāmukhamatho baddhvātha baddhvā rasaṃ kuryātkāṃcanamabhramerusadṛśaṃ dānāya bhogāya vai ||
children.translated_text: When it has been digested, one should close the mouth with coloring and <s>sāraṇā</s>, then bind the mercury; it makes gold like a mountain of mica, for giving and for enjoyment.

children.text: yāsāṃ chedena raktaṃ pravahati satataṃ prāyaśo raktabhūmau
children.translated_text: Those <s>bhūlatā</s> plants from whose cut blood continually flows, generally on red ground,
should be gathered; in them one should extract the essence that removes poison and grants wealth.

children.text: tadyuktyā pāradendre carati yadi samaṃ sāraṇākarmayogairbaddho'yaṃ koṭivedhī samaravirajate yojayed bhāskare vā ||
children.translated_text: If, by that method and by the operations of <s>sāraṇā</s>, it moves evenly in the lord of mercury, this bound mercury is a ten-millionfold piercer; one may apply the shining substance in silver, or else in copper.

children.text: bhūlatā kāṃtapāṣāṇaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: One should make powders of <s>bhūlatā</s> and <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> in equal amounts.
Its essence should be taken like mica, together with the medicines found there.
<s>Sauvīra</s>, <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and powdered stone
should be prepared together with an equal amount of <s>bhūnāga</s> powder.
One should extract the essence like mica, blowing it with the medicines found there.
The powder of <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> and <s>sauvīra</s> should be equal to the <s>bhūlatā</s>.
One should extract the essence like mica; it is a binder of the king of mercury.
The powder of <s>sauvīra</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> should be equal to <s>bhūnāga</s> clay.

children.text: dhāryaṃ bhāṇḍe kṣipettasmin sajīvā bhūlatā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be kept in a vessel; into it one should again put living <s>bhūlatā</s>.
One should sprinkle it daily with water until they consume it.
Having bound that essence into a lump like mica, one should collect the essence.
Powder of <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> should be combined with powder of <s>bhūlatā</s>.
It should be impregnated with goat urine for twenty-one days in fierce sunlight.
That lump should be kept in a furnace; the very beautiful essence is to be collected.
Cow urine, turmeric, mustard, and salt should be ground into a paste in equal amounts.

children.text: tena siñcyāttu bhūnāgaṃ khare gharme dravatyalam ||
children.translated_text: With that one should sprinkle <s>bhūnāga</s>; in fierce heat it melts thoroughly.

children.text: kaṃkuṣṭhaṃ taddravaṃ tulyaṃ kṛtvā satvaṃ samāharet
children.translated_text: Making <s>kaṃkuṣṭha</s> equal to that liquid, one should collect the essence.
By the ordered procedure used for mica, it becomes a binder of mercury.
Sulfur and <s>rasaka</s> should be powdered in an amount equal to the powder of <s>bhūlatā</s>.
When sealed in a diamond-crucible and blown, an excellent essence is produced.
After powdering this essence, it should be sprinkled as before.
<s>Sauvīra</s> collyrium, equal to <s>bhūnāga</s>, should be ground for a day.
Having mixed it with <s>pañcamāhiṣa</s>, one should then make it into pellets.
From that, oil should be taken by the <s>pātāla-yantra</s>, through a heating.
The <s>bhūlatā</s> plants should be washed with cow urine; with them one should obtain
oil by the <s>pātāla-yantra</s>. That oil is useful in digestion.
In a heated mortar, purified <s>sūta</s> should be combined with living <s>bhūnāga</s>.
One should grind it firmly for three days; all of that should then be taken up.
It should be placed in a crucible furnished with <s>bhūnāga</s> powder.
Having put <s>bhūlatā</s> powder above it, one should seal it and dry it.
After putting cow dung together in a pit, one should place the crucible there.

children.text: pādamātraṃ tu tāṃ garbhe karīṣaṃ tuṣavahninā ||
children.translated_text: With a quarter measure in its interior, the cow-dung should be fired with husk-flame.
One should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> for one day; after taking it out, one should apply it.
Having put <s>bhūlatā</s> powder above and below, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> in the same way.
One should do this for a month; the mercury becomes able to withstand fire.
For the embodied, bound mercury there arises a fierce <s>vaḍavāmukha</s>.
It devours all metals and various essences.
It devours all substances beginning with diamond, both raw and calcined.
This is known as secret mercury; now its digestion will be described.
To this very substance one should add <s>bhūnāga</s> essence in a sixteenth part.
It should be ground for a day in a heated mortar; then it should be combined with perfected <s>viḍa</s>.
It should be placed in a crucible smeared with <s>bhūnāga</s> oil.

children.text: ruddhvā svedyaṃ karīṣāgnau jīrṇasatvaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, one should steam it in a cow-dung fire; the essence is digested as before.

children.text: dattvā mardyaṃ taptakhalve viḍaṃ deyaṃ daśāṃśataḥ
children.translated_text: After adding it, one should grind it in a heated mortar; <s>viḍa</s> should be added as a tenth part.
In a crucible smeared as before, one should digest it by steaming.

children.text: evaṃ satvaṃ samaṃ jāryaṃ pūrvavatkacchapena vā
children.translated_text: In this way an equal amount of essence should be digested, as before, or by the <s>kacchapa</s> apparatus.

children.text: garbhadrāveṇa bījaṃ ca pūrvavat ṣaḍguṇaṃ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the inner-melting agent, the <s>bīja</s> should slowly be digested to six times the amount, as before.

children.text: jārayed drāvitaṃ garte mūṣāyantre tu pūrvavat
children.translated_text: It should be digested, melted, in a pit, in the crucible apparatus as before.

children.text: tatastu raṃjakaṃ bījaṃ jāryam asyaiva ṣaḍguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Then the coloring <s>bīja</s> should be digested for this very mercury to six times the amount.
Then, with cooked <s>bīja</s>, by the procedure of the seven chains,

children.text: sāraṇaṃ jāraṇaṃ kuryānmukhaṃ baddhvā tu bandhayet ||
children.translated_text: one should perform <s>sāraṇā</s> and digestion; after closing its mouth, one should bind it.
With a ten-millionth part of this, silver and copper become gold.
Secret mercury and gold should be ground in equal amounts with an acid.

children.text: yāvad golaṃ tu taṃ kṛtvā sāraṇāyāṃ tu madhyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Until it becomes a ball, one should make it so and place it in the middle during <s>sāraṇā</s>.
Two equal portions of <s>bhūnāga</s>-essence should be quickly placed in the crucible,

children.text: tasmin satve tu taṃ ḍhālyaṃ sarvaṃ khoṭaṃ bhavettu tat ||
children.translated_text: and into that essence all that alloy should be poured; then it becomes a solid lump.
In a crucible smeared with <s>bhūnāga</s> oil, it should be sealed and subjected to <s>puṭa</s>-heating.
Until only the <s>sūta</s> remains, one should cook it with light <s>puṭa</s>s.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kuryāt liptvā mūṣāgataṃ puṭam
children.translated_text: One should do this again and again, smearing the charge placed in the crucible and heating it by <s>puṭa</s>.
Or, in a crucible smeared with <s>biḍa</s>, it should be sealed and subjected to <s>puṭa</s>-heating.
Until only the <s>sūta</s> remains, one should cook it with light <s>puṭa</s>s.
And the inner-melting <s>bīja</s>, in an equal amount, should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> with that very substance.
Then, in the midst of the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus, one should digest it as before.
After that, essences beginning with mica, each in equal and corresponding portions,
having been killed separately, should again be caused to be digested.

children.text: tatastu raṃjakaṃ bījaṃ sāritaṃ tasya jārayet ||
