children.translated_text: Then the coloring <s>bīja</s>, after being subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s>, should be digested into it.
As before, four times the amount should be put into a smeared crucible and heated by <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: tatsāryaṃ pakvabījena yathā pūrvaṃ krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: That should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> with cooked <s>bīja</s>, in due sequence as before.
Through the procedure of the seven chains, after closing its mouth, one should bind it.
With that very substance, in a ten-millionth part, copper becomes gold.
Secret <s>sūta</s> should be ground with an equal amount of <s>bhūnāga</s>-essence.
It should be ground with the juices of divine herbs in a heated mortar for three days.
All of that should be enclosed in a diamond crucible, and the joint should be dried.
It should be sweated day and night in a cow-dung fire, or for three hundred periods in a husk fire,
with gentle cooking; after removing it, one should then grind it.
Again, with the juices of divine herbs, in a heated mortar, for a full day.

children.text: tato ruddhvā dhamed gāḍhaṃ khoṭaṃ bhavati tadrasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after sealing it, one should blow strongly; that mercury becomes a solid lump.
Again, having added an equal amount of secret <s>sūta</s> to it, for three days
one should grind and sweat it in the same way, and perform the binding as before.
Then one should carry out <s>sāraṇā</s> with that very substance, using an equal amount of sour gruel.
By means of a hundredth part, one should effect <s>vedha</s>; silver and copper become gold.
Red-colored <s>vaikrānta</s>, very pure and measuring one <s>pala</s>,
should be cooked inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus with horse urine.
After half a watch, it should be removed and again, with the juices of <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber,
one should impregnate it seven times in the sun; afterwards, with an equal amount of gold,
and with one <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s>, the three should be ground together
with <s>vyāghrī</s>-tuber juices and horse urine for four watches.
That ball should be cooked in the pot apparatus for one watch over a gentle fire.
After removing it, one should grind it for a watch with the previous liquids mixed with urine.

children.text: śataṃ palaṃ svarṇapatre anenaiva tu lepayet
children.translated_text: With this very substance one should coat one hundred <s>pala</s>s of gold leaf.
After sealing it, one should cook it with light <s>puṭa</s>s twenty times, again and again.
It should also be ground with <s>vyāghrī</s>-tuber juices and horse urine.
This gold, anointed and made like an essence, in mercury whose mouth has been opened,
one should feed and digest in this way, gradually, until it is a hundred times the amount.
That mercury, with horse urine and with the juice of <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber,
and with the <s>bīja</s>s of divine herbs, should be thoroughly ground in a heated mortar.
At the end of three days, after removing it, it should be sealed in a diamond crucible and heated by <s>puṭa</s>.
Day and night in a cow-dung fire, and for three nights in a husk fire,
one should do this again and again: grinding and cooking by <s>puṭa</s>.
When this is done carefully seven times, that mercury is certainly killed.
With this, at the ten-thousandth part, after <s>krāmaṇa</s>, one should effect <s>vedha</s>.

children.text: caṃdrārkaṃ vā drutaṃ tāmraṃ nāgaṃ vā kāṃcanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Silver or copper, molten copper, or lead becomes gold.

children.text: cāritaṃ pūrvasūtaṃ yanmāraṇena vinā tu tat ||
children.translated_text: That earlier <s>sūta</s>, which has been fed, but without killing,

children.text: mārayet pakvabījāni tridhā taṃ jārayet kramāt
children.translated_text: one should kill; then one should digest cooked <s>bīja</s>s into it three times in sequence.

children.text: pūrvavadbaṃdhanatvaṃ ca kṛtvā taṃ krāmaṇena vai ||
children.translated_text: Having made it fit for binding as before, then, by means of <s>krāmaṇa</s>,
one should apply it to melted silver and copper in a hundred-thousandth part.
It becomes gold, rich in beautiful appearance; so it has been declared by <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: pītavarṇaṃ tu vaikrāṃtaṃ śuddhaṃ bhāvyaṃ dināvadhi
children.translated_text: Yellow-colored <s>vaikrānta</s>, purified, should be impregnated for a full day
with <s>vyāghrī</s> juice and horse urine, and cooked inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber.
In a <s>dolā</s> apparatus for a day and night; after removing it, one should powder it.

children.text: etaccūrṇaṃ palaikaṃ tu sūte daśaguṇe kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of this powder should be thrown into ten times as much <s>sūta</s>.
It should be ground with <s>vyāghrī</s>-tuber juices and horse urine for a full day.
Again, with this, one should coat one hundred <s>pala</s>s of gold leaf.
Having sealed it inside a diamond crucible, for three days with a husk fire
one should sweat it, or else day and night in a cow-dung fire; then one should remove it.
It should be ground with <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber and horse urine and cooked in <s>puṭa</s> in the same way.

children.text: evaṃ śatapuṭaiḥ pakvam abhiṣiktaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Cooked with a hundred <s>puṭa</s>s in this way, it should also be made anointed.
In the lordly king of mercury whose mouth has been opened, this should be fed and digested,
by the sequence of mica-essence and the like, gradually, until it is a hundred times the amount.

children.text: mūṣāyantre 'thavā jāryaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ krameṇa vai
children.translated_text: Or it should be digested in the crucible apparatus, in due sequence as before.
For the lord of mercury situated there, the inner-melting <s>bīja</s>
should be melted in the pit as before and digested in sequence to four times the amount.
The substance there should be digested with cooked <s>bīja</s> by means of the seven chains.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā koṭivedhī bhaved rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having closed the mouth and bound the mercury, the mercury becomes capable of ten-millionfold <s>vedha</s>.
Black-colored <s>vaikrānta</s> should be placed inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber.
It should be sweated for a day with horse urine; one part of that should be powdered.
One part of purified <s>sūta</s>, in a heated mortar for a full day,
should be ground with <s>vyāghrī</s>-tuber juices and with horse urine.
After adding <s>tāra</s> (silver) in a sixth part, one should again grind it in the same way.

children.text: sarvatulyaṃ punaḥ sūtaṃ dattvā tatraiva mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after adding <s>sūta</s> (mercury) equal to the whole, one should grind it there again.

children.text: jātaṃ golaṃ samuddhṛtya nigalena tu lepayet
children.translated_text: When a ball has formed, one should take it out and coat it with <s>nigala</s>.
Having sealed it inside a diamond-crucible, one should heat it for three days with a husk fire,
or steam it day and night, in a windless place, with a cow-dung fire.
Then, after taking it out, one should grind it with <s>bīja</s> and the juices of divine herbs.
For three days it is to be combined with horse urine in a heated mortar.
Coated as before and sealed, it should likewise be cooked by means of a <s>puṭa</s>.
By this ordered procedure one should cook it seven times with <s>puṭa</s> firings.
With this, one should perform <s>vedha</s> on melted copper at a hundredth part.

children.text: pūrvavat krāmaṇaṃ dattvā tāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: After adding <s>krāmaṇa</s> as before, it becomes fine <s>tāra</s> (silver).

children.text: śvetavarṇaṃ tu vaikrāṃtaṃ suśuddhaṃ pūrvavat kramāt
children.translated_text: White-colored <s>vaikrānta</s>, well purified step by step as before,
with the preparation of red <s>vaikrānta</s>, should be used to kill that very <s>tāra</s> (silver).
That silver should be digested in <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in the same way, slowly, up to a hundredfold amount.
It should likewise be killed by a <s>puṭa</s> firing; it becomes capable of ten-thousandfold <s>vedha</s>.

children.text: tadvat vai tārabījena sāritaṃ jārayet kramāt
children.translated_text: Likewise, with silver-<s>bīja</s>, one should carry out <s>sāraṇā</s> and digest it in sequence.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā lakṣavedhī bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After closing the mouth and binding the <s>rasa</s> (mercury), the mercury becomes capable of hundred-thousandfold <s>vedha</s>.

children.text: drute tāmre pradātavyaṃ tattāraṃ jāyate śubham ||
children.translated_text: It should be added to melted copper; that silver becomes excellent.
Copper-colored <s>vaikrānta</s>, combined with purified <s>hiṅgula</s>,
should be ground with the acidic group for three days in a heated mortar.
Gold leaves coated with this should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
After taking them out, they should again be ground, combined with the acidic group.
Cooking them in this way with seven <s>puṭa</s> firings, one obtains one <s>pala</s> of that ash.
One <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury), with the juices of divine herbs for three days,

children.text: marditaṃ kārayed golaṃ nirmalena ca lepayet
children.translated_text: having been ground, should be made into a ball and coated with <s>nirmala</s>.
Sealed, it should be steamed for three days with cow-dung and husk fire.
Then, with the liquids of divine herbs, it is to be ground and treated with <s>nigala</s>.

children.text: ruddhvā liptvā dhamed gāḍhaṃ baṃdhamāyāti niścitam ||
children.translated_text: After sealing and coating it, one should blow it strongly; it certainly comes to bondage.
With a hundredth part of this, <s>tāra</s> (silver) becomes gold.

children.text: raktavaikrāṃtasatvaṃ tu saha hemnā tu cūrṇayet
children.translated_text: The essence of red <s>vaikrānta</s> should be powdered together with gold.
In a crucible coated for the paired combination, it should be covered and blown.
That <s>khoṭa</s> lump, when sprinkled, should be digested in mercury whose mouth has been opened.
One should digest an equal amount of mercury according to the procedure for mica essence.
That mercury should be made to undergo <s>sāraṇā</s> with cooked <s>bīja</s>, as before, three times.

children.text: tadvacca jāraṇā kāryā mukhaṃ baddhvātha bandhayet ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the digestion is to be performed; after closing the mouth, one should then bind it.
By that very substance, in a thousandth part, <s>tāra</s> (silver) becomes gold.
The essence of red <s>vaikrānta</s> and purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury), in equal proportions,
should be ground with the liquids of divine herbs for three days in a heated mortar.
Then it should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> inside a crucible coated with <s>nigala</s> and covered.
It is to be heated in a cow-dung fire day and night, and for three days with a husk fire.
After taking it out, that ball should again be coated with <s>nigala</s>.

children.text: mūṣānte lavaṇaṃ dattvā ruddhvā saṃdhiṃ viśoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Putting salt at the end of the crucible, one should seal the joint and dry it.

children.text: punaśca lavaṇaṃ dattvā ruddhvā saṃdhiṃ viśoṣayet
children.translated_text: Again putting in salt, one should seal the joint and dry it.
One should coat that crucible all around, a finger's breadth thick, with conch powder.

children.text: koṣṭhīyantre haṭhād dhāmyaṃ baddho bhavati tadrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be blown forcibly in a furnace apparatus; that mercury becomes bound.

children.text: tāre tāmre bhujaṃge vā sahasrāṃśena vedhayet
children.translated_text: One should perform <s>vedha</s> in silver, copper, or lead with a thousandth part.
Divine gold is produced, excellent as an ornament of the gods.

children.text: raktā pītā sitā kṛṣṇā capalā tu caturvidhā
children.translated_text: Red, yellow, white, and black: <s>capalā</s> is fourfold.
They should be purified by the method for <s>vaikrānta</s>; they are binders of mercury.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>karavīra</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>girikarṇī</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
with an equal part of <s>sauvīrāñjana</s>, should be ground with woman's breast milk.
With this one should coat the inside of a diamond-crucible on all sides, a finger's breadth thick.
Red or yellow <s>capalā</s> should be powdered as one part.
There should be four parts of gold and two parts of purified mercury.
All this should be ground for three days with the liquids of divine herbs.
Then, having sealed it in the previous crucible, one should dry it in shade and blow it forcibly.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ jāyate khoṭaṃ śatāṃśena tu tena vai ||
children.translated_text: All of it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> lump; with a hundredth part of that,

children.text: suśuddhaṃ vedhayennāgaṃ bhaved guṃjānibhaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: one should perform <s>vedha</s> on very pure lead; it becomes like a <s>guñjā</s> berry.
With that lead one should perform <s>vedha</s> on copper, using just a hundredth part.
The copper becomes reddish; with that copper one should perform <s>vedha</s>
on purified silver with a hundredth part, and that silver becomes gold.

children.text: tadvacca jāraṇā kāryā mukhaṃ baddhvātha bandhayet
children.translated_text: Likewise the digestion is to be performed; after closing the mouth, one should then bind it.
By that very substance, in a thousandth part, <s>tāra</s> (silver) becomes gold.
One should perform <s>vedha</s> on very pure lead; and that becomes like a <s>guñjā</s> berry.
With that lead one should perform <s>vedha</s> on copper, using just a hundredth part.
There should be six parts of powdered <s>capalā</s>, and silver should be seven parts.

children.text: bhāgāṣṭakaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca navabhāgaṃ ca pāradam ||
children.translated_text: Gold is eight parts, and mercury is nine parts.
One should grind everything with the liquids of divine herbs for three days.
That ball should be coated thickly on all sides with <s>nigala</s>.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>karavīra</s>, <s>agni</s>, and vulture droppings should be equal in measure.
One should grind them with the sour juice of citron and coat the crucible with that.
Having sealed that ball as before, one should blow it; it then becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> lump.

children.text: tenaiva tu śatāṃśena nāge vedhaṃ pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: With that very substance, in a hundredth part, one should cause <s>vedha</s> to be applied to lead.

children.text: tena nāgena śulbaṃ ca śatāṃśenaiva vedhayet
children.translated_text: With that lead one should also perform <s>vedha</s> on copper, using just a hundredth part.
With the copper one should perform <s>vedha</s> on silver; as before, it becomes gold.
One should place one <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in a glass vessel,
and add to it three <s>palas</s> of sulfur digested as before.

children.text: jaṃbīrāṇāṃ dravaṃ dattvā gaṃdhatulyaṃ śanaiḥ pacet
children.translated_text: Having added the juice of citrons, equal in amount to the sulfur, one should cook it slowly
inside a sand-bath vessel until the sulfur is digested.
There indeed one should put one <s>pala</s> of previously prepared <s>dhānyābhra</s> (processed mica),

children.text: kṣiptvā jaṃbīranīraṃ ca biḍaṃ dattvātha pācayet ||
children.translated_text: and, after adding citron-water and then <s>biḍa</s> (alkaline flux), one should cook it.
As it becomes digested, one should keep adding acid and cook until it is fully so.
Into that one should put one <s>pala</s> of gold, powdered and moistened,
and then <s>biḍa</s> should be added to it, combined with citron juice.
One should cook it there itself over a gentle fire until it is digested.
Adding <s>biḍa</s> and acid as it becomes digested, one should remove it and grind it.
For three days, in a heated mortar, it should be combined with the juices of divine herbs.
One should grind root produced from <s>Īśvaraliṅgī</s> and also the root of <s>śigru</s>.
Having coated a diamond crucible with this very substance, one should put in the earlier <s>rasa</s> (mercurial compound).
After sealing it, it should be heated over a cow-dung fire; after a day and night one should take it out.
Ground as before and sealed, it should be blown with the bellows; the <s>rasa</s> becomes bound.
When this is applied to silver in a sixty-fourth part,
it effects <s>vedha</s> (transmuting penetration), producing divine gold approved by the siddhas.
One hundred <s>niṣkas</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> and ten <s>niṣkas</s> of sulfur
should be ground for a moment with the juices of <s>kanyā</s> and cooked in a distillation apparatus.
Taking what has adhered above, one should add ten <s>niṣkas</s> of sulfur,
grind it again in the same way, cook it in the apparatus, and remove it.
One should do this again and again twenty-one times.

children.text: gaurīyantre tu tatsūtaṃ kṣiptvā deyaṃ tu gaṃdhakam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after putting that mercury into the <s>gaurīyantra</s>, sulfur should be added,
impregnated by the previous formula and powdered to a twentieth part.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a light <s>puṭa</s>; when it is digested, sulfur should be supplied.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punarjāryaṃ yathāśakti krameṇa vai
children.translated_text: In this way it should be digested again and again, gradually according to capacity.
When sulfur has been digested to a hundredfold amount, the <s>rasa</s> becomes hundred-transmuting.
When a thousandfold has been digested, it transmutes by a thousandth part.
When a hundred-thousandfold has been digested, the <s>rasa</s> becomes hundred-thousand-transmuting, and then ten-million-transmuting.
When sulfur has been digested even to a ten-millionfold amount, it becomes higher and higher in this way.
One should perform <s>sāraṇā</s> with cooked <s>bīja</s> and digest it in sequence as before.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā tāre vedhaṃ pradāpayet
children.translated_text: Having closed the mouth and bound the <s>rasa</s>, one should cause <s>vedha</s> in silver.
Divine gold arises, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.

children.text: bhūsattvakaiḥ paramaguhyatamaiḥ sasūtair vaikrāntakaiḥ sacapalai rasagaṃdhakaiśca
children.translated_text: With earth-essences that are most secret, with mercury, with <s>vaikrānta</s>, with <s>capala</s>, and with <s>rasa</s> and sulfur,

children.text: dṛṣṭvānubhūya sakalaṃ sukhasādhyayogaiḥ samyak suvarṇakaraṇaṃ gaditaṃ sudhīnām ||
children.translated_text: having seen and experienced everything, the proper making of gold by easily accomplished formulas has been taught to the wise.

children.text: vajrābhrasatvavarahāṭakalohajālaṃ kuryād drutaṃ dravabhavaṃ kila baṃdhayogyam
children.translated_text: The mass of diamond, mica essence, excellent gold, and metals should quickly be made molten, fluid-born, and fit for binding.
That will now be taught through many kinds of easily prepared royal formulas, bringing supreme accomplishment to men.
One should coat purified leaves of black mica with <s>pīlu</s> oil.

children.text: gharme śoṣyāṇi saptāhaṃ liptvā liptvā punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should be dried in the sun for a week, coated again and again.
Likewise they should be dried for three days with the acid group; and then
one should collect the alkalis of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, <s>vajrī</s>, and <s>kaṭutumbī</s>,
together with the three alkalis; this eightfold group should be powdered in equal parts.
<s>Vajrakanda</s>, <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s>,
and <s>vanavṛntāka</s>: with the juices of these it should be impregnated for three days.
With this alkaline paste, one should coat the earlier leaves.

children.text: ātape kāṃsyapātre tu sthāpyaṃ lepyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: They should be placed in a bronze vessel in the sunlight and coated again and again.
One should do this for three days; a stainless <s>druti</s> (liquefied essence) comes about.
One should put the leaves with the acid group in the sun for three days.
Likewise, one should wash other mica leaves with <s>kṣīrakanda</s> preparations.
With alkalis, until a paste is formed; with that paste, the earlier leaf

children.text: liptvā liptvā kṣiped gharme kāṃsyapātre viśoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: should be coated again and again, placed in the sun, and dried in a bronze vessel.
After a week, without doubt, a mercury-like <s>druti</s> comes about.
Powder of the fruit of <s>kākāṇḍā</s>, combined with <s>mitrapañcaka</s>,
and an equal amount of <s>dhānyābhra</s> should be ground with acids for one day.
Placed in a blind crucible and blown, it becomes a stainless <s>druti</s>.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s>, together with cow's flesh, rock salt equal to a quarter part of the mica,
should be ground for three days with the milky juices of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>.

children.text: tadgolaṃ kadalīkaṃde kṣiptvā bāhye mṛdā lipet
children.translated_text: That ball should be put into a banana tuber and coated outside with clay.
One should cook it for three days in a cow-dung fire; it becomes a stainless <s>druti</s>.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s> should be ground for a day with the exudates of <s>agastya</s> leaves.

children.text: tadgolaṃ nikṣipet kaṃde sūraṇotthe nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: That ball should be placed in a tuber produced from <s>sūraṇa</s> and sealed.
One should bury that tuber in the ground of a cowshed and remove it after a month.
From inside the tuber, the <s>druti</s>, stainless and equal to mercury, should be taken.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s> should be ground for a day with the juices of <s>ajamārī</s>.
It should be placed in an earthen vessel; after three days in the sun it becomes fully prepared.
For a week, with <s>munitoya</s>, <s>dhānyābhra</s>, rock salt, and <s>śilā</s>
should be ground and impregnated in the sun; then <s>dārvī</s> and <s>suvarcala</s>,
black pepper, and a quarter-part of mica should be ground for a day with the juices of <s>mūrvā</s> leaves.
It should be ground with the juices produced from <s>vajravallī</s> and impregnated for a day.

children.text: śarāvasaṃpuṭe taṃ tu ruddhvā dhmāte drutirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed it in a pair of earthen saucers, when it is blown, <s>druti</s> comes about.
<s>dhānyābhraka</s> (rice-processed mica), equal to a <s>kākinī</s> seed, should be used.
It should be heated in the sun for seven days with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>; liquefaction will occur.
<s>dhānyābhraka</s>, together with <s>suvarcala</s>, should be ground with the juices of <s>vajravallī</s>,
in equal measure, for three days; then that should be placed in a sealed pair of dishes.

children.text: ruddhvā dhmāte dravatyeva rasarūpaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When it is sealed and blown upon, it certainly melts into the form of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: ityevaṃ rasarūpaṃ ca jāyate naiva saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in this very way, it becomes mercury-like; there is no doubt.
One should cook mica leaves with milk-saps produced from <s>uduṃbara</s>.
Or one may cook them in a pot; they become like fresh butter.

children.text: tatastaṃ vaṭakaṃ kṛtvā chidramūṣāṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Then, after making that into a pellet and sealing it in a perforated crucible,

children.text: yāmatrayaṃ dhamed gāḍham adhobhāṇḍe drutiḥ patet ||
children.translated_text: one should blow strongly for three watches; the <s>druti</s> (liquefied essence) will fall into the lower vessel.
<s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be ground for a day with milks from <s>kākoduṃbarī</s>.
The seeds of the forest mouse, with their skins removed, should be taken in equal measure with the mica.
After grinding that for half a watch, it should be liquefied by <s>pātālayantra</s> apparatuses.
A heating should be given for a day and night; a clear <s>druti</s> results.
<s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be firmly ground with an equal amount of fruits born from <s>kapitiṃdu</s> and <s>jāti</s>.
One should grind it for one day and place it in a glass flask.
Having stopped its mouth with human hair, one should coat the flask with clay.
It should be heated by the <s>pātālayantra</s>; at the end of a day one obtains <s>druti</s>.
Powder of the <s>guñjā</s> fruit, in equal part with <s>dhānyābhraka</s>,
when impregnated for seven days with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, will become effective through blowing.
<s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be ground for three days with the fluids of red lotus and of blue lotus,
then sealed and blown; when placed in a diamond-hard crucible, it should be blown.
<s>dhānyābhraka</s>, equal to powder of the <s>vegī</s> fruit, should be impregnated for three days
in the sun with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>; when blown in a sealed container, it melts.
Or one should impregnate powder from the <s>kapitiṃdu</s> fruit with goat's urine.

children.text: phalacūrṇaṃ tu tacchuṣkaṃ drute satve pravāpayet ||
children.translated_text: When that is dry, one should cast it into the molten essence.
By two or three applications, the <s>druti</s> becomes clear.
One should sprinkle the mica essence with oils produced from human hair.
Having smeared that ball with cow-dung, one should place it inside a diamond-hard crucible.
When blown forcefully, it certainly melts and remains like the king of <s>rasa</s>.
One should impregnate the powder of <s>kṣīrakanda</s> with human urine,

children.text: daśavāraṃ prayatnena śoṣyaṃ peṣyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ten times carefully, drying and grinding it again and again.

children.text: tenāvāpaṃ drute satve dattvā dattvā ca saṃdhamet
children.translated_text: With that, while giving castings again and again into the molten essence, one should blow it thoroughly,

children.text: yāvat tad dravatāṃ yāti tāvaddeyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: and as long as it reaches fluidity, so long it should be given again and again.

children.text: lohaṃ ca dravate tena haṭhād dhmāte na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that, iron too melts when blown forcefully; there is no doubt.

children.text: paṃcāṃgaṃ devadālyutthaṃ cūrṇaṃ bhāvyaṃ ca taddravaiḥ
children.translated_text: Powder of the five parts produced from <s>devadālī</s> should be impregnated with its juices.
It should be dried, ground, and impregnated again, a hundred times carefully.
One should heat that powder, in one-tenth part, into molten essence.

children.text: tatpunarjāyate baddho vāpo deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then it becomes bound again; a casting should be given again and again.
<s>kṣīrakandaka</s> should be impregnated a hundred times with the juices of <s>kṣīrakanda</s>.
By casting that, the essence melts, and so do all metals.
All the mica essence should be impregnated with preparations of sour grain gruel.
Combined with alkali of <s>nicula</s> and blown, it remains like <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
Powder of <s>indragopa</s>, with the fluids of <s>devadālī</s> fruit,
when impregnated for twenty-one days, should be cast into molten gold.
Little by little, in equal amounts, until it remains like <s>sūta</s>.
One should impregnate <s>devadālī</s> a hundred times with human urine.
By the mere casting of that powder, there will be <s>druti</s> of gold and silver.
The ash produced from <s>suradālī</s>, impregnated with human urine,
becomes a sharp-metal <s>druti</s> when that alkali is cast three times seven times.
One should cast <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, together with tortoise bone and <s>śilājatu</s>.
Truly, the essence becomes a <s>druti</s>; it should first be applied in melting and the like.
Sulfur and magnet-stone should be powdered in equal parts.

children.text: drute lohe pratīvāpo deyo lohāṣṭakaṃ dravet ||
children.translated_text: A counter-casting should be given into molten metal; the eight metals melt.
Sulfur should be impregnated for seven days with the fluids of <s>devadālī</s>.
By the mere casting of that, metal remains like <s>sūta</s>.
After removing the entrails of a very large frog, one should place
borax filling its belly, and keep that inside a vessel.
After eight days one should take oil from it in a <s>pātālayantra</s>.
One should cast that oil into melted gold and thereby obtain <s>druti</s>.
<s>indragopa</s>, horse saliva, and the fat of a hare and a frog,

children.text: asthīni ca samaṃ piṣṭvā drute hemni pravāpayet ||
children.translated_text: and their bones, ground in equal measure, should be cast into molten gold.
It becomes mercury-like and remains for a long time.
<s>indragopa</s>, crab bone, and the seed of <s>devadālī</s>,
powdered, should be impregnated for a day with fluids produced from <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: anena drāvite hemni vāpo deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: With this, castings should be given again and again into melted gold.
It remains mercury-like for a long time; this has been declared by <s>Śiva</s>.
Sharp-metal powder should be soaked for seven days with the juices of ripe <s>dhātrī</s> fruit,
and then impregnated in the sun with the juices of <s>kṣīrakanda</s> again.
For seven days one should impregnate it properly, likewise in a dripping sealed vessel.
When blown, it comes to a liquid state and remains for a long time like <s>sūta</s>.
Jackal, ram, tortoise, and snake bones, and <s>śilājatu</s>,
after all this has been powdered, into well-heated magnet powder

children.text: vāpayed dravatāṃ yāti yathā sūtaṃ suniścitam ||
children.translated_text: one should cast it; it reaches fluidity, certainly just like <s>sūta</s>.
Iron powder, any one desired, with the juices of the jackfruit fruit...
One should impregnate it for seven days in the heat, and indeed grind it with the group of sour substances.
It melts by blowing alone and becomes fit for application; there is no doubt.

children.text: gaṃdhakaṃ raktalavaṇaṃ tulyaṃ deyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Sulfur and red salt, in equal measure, should be added again and again.
For all molten, heated powders, this is the supreme liquefier.
Into the belly of a yellow frog one should place powdered <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s> (borax).

children.text: ruddhvā bhāṃḍe kṣiped bhūmau trisaptāhāt samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed it in a vessel, one should put it in the ground and take it up after three weeks.
Then, after powdering all of that, one should pour it into molten metal.
All metals remain in the form of <s>rasa</s>; not otherwise.
With oil produced from castor, <s>guṃjā</s>, honey, and <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s>,

children.text: marditaṃ tasya vāpena satvaṃ mākṣikajaṃ dravet ||
children.translated_text: when it is ground, by casting it the essence produced from <s>mākṣika</s> melts.
The three alkalis, <s>rāmaṭha</s>, sour chickpea, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
<s>jvālāmukhī</s>, <s>ikṣuraka</s>, and the fruits of <s>sthalakumbhī</s>,
should be ground smooth with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>; one should place that pellet there.
Diamond and the chief gems, tied in cloth, should be cooked forcefully.
By the <s>dolāyantra</s>, in sour grain-gruel, they become melted after eight watches.
Diamond, mica, blue stone, pearl, coral, and <s>mākṣika</s>,
<s>pauṇḍra</s>, beryl, ruby, lapis lazuli, and sapphire,
<s>vaikrānta</s> and crystal too melt, resembling <s>rasa</s>.
By these same medicines, the class of metals also melts through casting.
Having put a diamond inside <s>vajravallī</s> and sealed it up,
it should be steamed in a water-vessel; after seven days it goes to fluidity.
The fine powder should be placed for seven days in sour <s>vetasa</s> liquid.

children.text: saptāhād uddhṛtaṃ taṃ vai puṭe ruddhvā drutirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: When it has been taken out after seven days, sealed in a heating capsule, it becomes a <s>druti</s>.
White-colored <s>vaikrānta</s>, impregnated with sour <s>vetasa</s>,
melts thoroughly after seven days in intense heat; there is no doubt here.
One should take the expressed juice of <s>ketakī</s>, rock salt, and <s>svarṇapuṣpikā</s>,
combine them with <s>indragopa</s>, and place everything in a vessel.
If <s>vaikrānta</s> is steamed in it for seven days, it goes to fluidity.
So too the eight metals and the gems, by the power of this procedure.
This king of procedures brings about the supreme liquefaction of gems.
The <s>drutis</s> should be kept separately in the midst of safflower oil.

children.text: tiṣṭhanti cirakālaṃ tu prāpte kārye niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: They remain for a long time; when the intended work is at hand, one should employ them.

children.text: ityevaṃ drutisaṃcayaṃ samucitaiḥ sārātisārair mataiḥ kṛtvā vārtikapuṃgavo'tra satataṃ śrīpārade melayet
children.translated_text: Thus, having made a collection of <s>drutis</s> with suitable essences and super-essences that are approved, the eminent practitioner should here always combine them with venerable <s>pārada</s>.

children.text: tenaivādbhutabhakṣaṇaṃ sukanakaṃ kṛtvātha vidvadvare deyaṃ dīnajane ca duḥkhavimukhaṃ kuryātsamastaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: With that very substance, after making marvelous food and fine gold, he should give it to the best of the learned and to poor people, and should make the whole world free from suffering.

children.text: drutiriha paripācyā jārayet pāradendre munigaṇitam athāsau sāritaḥ koṭivedhī
children.translated_text: Here the <s>druti</s> should be thoroughly cooked and made to digest in the lord <s>pārada</s>; then, as reckoned by sages, when it has been driven, it has the power to pierce ten millionfold.

children.text: atha pavikṛtabījaṃ ratnagarbhaṃ drutaṃ vā carati yadi rasendraḥ syāttadā śabdavedhī ||
children.translated_text: And if <s>rasendra</s> takes in a seed made from thunderbolt-like material or a molten gem-filled seed, then it becomes capable of piercing by sound.
<s>Pāṭhā</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>tālamūlī</s>, indigo, cinnabar, and <s>citraka</s>,
lotus tuber, <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, and likewise <s>nāgabalā</s>, in equal measure:

children.text: eteṣāṃ grāhayet svacchaṃ rasaṃ vastreṇa gālitam
children.translated_text: one should take the clear juice of these, filtered through cloth,

children.text: drutiṃ samukhasūtaṃ ca auṣadhīnāṃ tathā dravam ||
children.translated_text: as well as the <s>druti</s>, mercury furnished with an opening, and the liquid of the herbs.
Having placed everything in a cowherd's vessel, one should dry it in fierce sunlight.
The liquid is to be added again and again until three watches have passed.

children.text: milanti drutayaḥ sarvāḥ pārade nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All the <s>drutis</s> unite with <s>pārada</s>; there is no doubt here.
The diamond-tuber, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>guṃjā</s> should be ground with liquids as before.

children.text: milanti drutayaḥ sarvā rasarāje na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All the <s>drutis</s> unite with the king of <s>rasa</s>; there is no doubt.
Black aloe-wood, sugar, asafoetida, musk, and <s>brahmabījaka</s>,

children.text: tulyaṃ cūrṇaṃ daśāṃśena sūte drutiyute kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: as equal powders, should be put into the <s>sūta</s> joined with <s>druti</s>, in a tenth part.

children.text: milanti drutayaḥ sarvā anenaiva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this very means all the <s>drutis</s> unite; there is no doubt.
Black aloe-wood, white asafoetida, sugar, garlic, and <s>nābhaya</s>,
by grinding just as before, cause the <s>drutis</s> to unite in <s>rasa</s>.
Horse saliva, fresh ginger, neem leaves, and garlic in equal measure,
combined with <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s>, are, as before, a means of joining the <s>druti</s>.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ saviṣaṃ guṃjā ṭaṃkaṇaṃ strīrajaḥ samam
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>, poison, <s>guṃjā</s>, <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s>, and menstrual blood, in equal measure,

children.text: strīstanyaṃ saṃyutaṃ piṣṭvā tena mūṣāṃ pralepayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground together with woman's milk; with that one should coat the crucible.

children.text: drutiyuktaṃ rasaṃ tatra kṣiptvā ruddhvā dināvadhi
children.translated_text: After placing <s>rasa</s> joined with <s>druti</s> there and sealing it for a day,
one should heat it set in a cow-dung fire, or for three days in a chaff fire.
All the <s>drutis</s> unite; after they have united, one should then digest them.

children.text: drutayo mīlitā yena mūṣāṃ tenaiva lepayet
children.translated_text: With the very substance by which the <s>drutis</s> have been united, one should coat the crucible.
And in that way, through the living procedure, this is known as the coated crucible.
One should combine equal <s>drutis</s> of gold and magnet-stone with opened <s>rasa</s>.
The whole should be one-sixteenth of the <s>rasa</s>; enclosed in a coated crucible, it should be heated.
Then, in chaff or in a cow-dung fire, until only the <s>sūta</s> remains,
one should combine it again in the same way, and then digest it according to all the rules.
Thus, by the proper sequence, one should digest an equal <s>druti</s> in the <s>sūta</s>.
Thereafter one should drive it with cooked seed, through three digestions.

children.text: mūṣāyantre tu tajjāryaṃ mukhaṃ baddhvātha bandhayet
children.translated_text: In the crucible apparatus, that should be digested; after binding the mouth, one should seal it.
It should be applied in silver-ore combined with copper, in a hundredth part.
When joined with the transmuting agent, it becomes divine gold.
The <s>drutis</s> of gold, mica, and copper should be digested in <s>rasa</s> in double quantity.
By the sequential procedure as before, then comes the coloring seed.
In the crucible apparatus it should be digested in equal measure, and one should drive it through three drivings.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā sahasrāṃśena vedhayet
children.translated_text: Having bound the mouth and having bound the <s>rasa</s> (mercury), one should make it penetrate with a thousandth part.
Silver with <s>āra</s>, combined with copper, becomes divine gold.
The <s>drutis</s> (liquefied essences) of magnetite, copper, and gold should be digested in mercury whose mouth is opened,
by the previous method, each successively in double quantity.
Then one should digest twice that amount of coloring seeds in it.
Then, by means of the seeds, it should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> three times; one should digest it and subject it to <s>sāraṇā</s> again.

children.text: jārito'tha mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvātha vedhayet
children.translated_text: When it has been digested, having bound the mouth and then having bound the <s>rasa</s>, one should make it penetrate.
By that very means, with a ten-thousandth part, gold is produced as before.
The <s>drutis</s> of magnetite, gold, and mica should be digested successively, up to fivefold quantity,
by the previous method, and then the coloring seed.
Fivefold quantity should be digested in it carefully in a crucible-apparatus.
One should perform <s>sāraṇā</s> with ripened seed three times, and again digest it.

children.text: punaḥ sāryaṃ punarjāryam evaṃ vāratraye kṛte
children.translated_text: Again it should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s>, and again digested; when this has been done three times,

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā lakṣavedhī bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having bound the mouth and having bound the <s>rasa</s>, the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of penetration at a hundred-thousandfold ratio.
The <s>drutis</s> of jewel and gold are digested in the <s>rasa</s> in sixfold quantity.
Then sixfold quantity of coloring seed should be digested in that same one.
It should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> three times and then digested again; thus for a set of four turns.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā nāgatailena vedhayet
children.translated_text: Having bound the mouth and having bound the <s>rasa</s>, one should make it penetrate with lead-oil.
By combination in a ten-lakh part, divine gold is produced.
The two <s>drutis</s>, mica and gold, each in an amount equal to the <s>sūta</s> (mercury),

children.text: melitaṃ pūrvayogena jārayet tat krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: should be mixed and digested successively by the previous method.
The <s>sūta</s> becomes a hundred-penetrator; when doubled, it penetrates a thousandfold.
When trebled it is a ten-thousand-penetrator, and when quadrupled a hundred-thousand-penetrator.
When fivefold quantity has been properly digested, it penetrates ten lakhs.
Thus, when digested according to the measure of the <s>rasa</s>, the <s>rasa</s> becomes a crore-penetrator.
After that, sevenfold quantity of coloring seed should be digested in it.
Then one should perform <s>sāraṇā</s> three times with ripened seed, successively as before.
Digestion and <s>sāraṇā</s> are to be done, and again <s>sāraṇā</s> and digestion.
By this method of procedure, according to the sequence of seven chains,

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā koṭivedhī bhavettu saḥ
children.translated_text: having bound the mouth and having bound the <s>rasa</s>, it becomes a crore-penetrator.
It should be applied to silver combined with copper up to the end of the <s>krāmaṇā</s> operation.
The <s>drutis</s> of white mica, silver, bell-metal, and <s>āra</s> should be digested equally in mercury whose mouth is opened,
as before; one should perform <s>sāraṇā</s> with silver-seed.

children.text: tridhā taṃ pūrvavajjāryaṃ mukhaṃ baddhvātha bandhayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be digested three times as before, and, having bound the mouth, one should then fix it.
The <s>drutis</s> of magnetite, silver, and <s>āra</s>, in double quantity, should be digested in mercury whose mouth is opened,
up to triple quantity; or else one should do it with ripened seed.
One should make it subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> and digested, as before, for three chains.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā ayutāṃśena vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having bound the mouth and having bound the <s>rasa</s>, one should make it penetrate with a ten-thousandth part.
In molten tin, that silver becomes resembling jasmine and the moon.
The <s>drutis</s> produced from silver, sharp metal, and bell-metal, in mercury whose mouth is opened,
one should make up to fourfold quantity; one should perform <s>sāraṇā</s> with silver-seed.
Up to four chains, having bound the mouth, one should then fix it.
By a hundred-thousandth part of this, the fixing of tin becomes firm.
The <s>drutis</s> of silver and magnetite should be digested in sevenfold quantity in the <s>rasa</s>.
It should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> with silver-seed, according to the sequence of seven chains.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā koṭivedhī bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having bound the mouth and having bound the <s>rasa</s>, the <s>rasa</s> becomes a crore-penetrator.
To the <s>rasendra</s> whose mouth is opened, one should make previously processed grain-mica enter,
and digest it in the same way, in equal portion, and then of that

children.text: ṣaḍguṇaṃ dvaṃdvite vyomni sarvaṃ jāryaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: sixfold quantity in paired mica should all be digested as before.

children.text: tato mākṣikasatvaṃ ca pādāṃśaṃ tasya garbhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should melt essence of pyrite, a quarter part of it, inside it,
and digest it in the same way; then the same amount of essence of <s>rasaka</s>,

children.text: pūrvavad drāvitaṃ jāryaṃ mūṣāyantre tu tat kramāt ||
children.translated_text: melted as before, should be digested successively in the crucible-apparatus.
The seed that melts within the interior, once melted, should again be digested
until it becomes fourfold; afterward, of mica and gold
one should combine equal <s>druti</s> with the <s>sūta</s> and then digest it.
By the previous sequence of method, again the <s>druti</s> of magnetite and gold
should be digested, each in equal amount; likewise the <s>druti</s> of gold and sharp metal.
One should digest the combined equal amount, and then the coloring seed.
By the previous sequence of method, fourfold quantity should be digested in it.
Then one should subject it to <s>sāraṇā</s> with ripened seed in three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations.
That very thing, digested, should again be treated in the crucible-apparatus as before.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptavārāṇi sāritaṃ tat tridhā tridhā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for seven turns, it should be subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> three times each.
Digestion is to be done as before; this is known as the seven-chain sequence.

children.text: sāraṇā yatra yatroktā vijñeyā vārtikaiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wherever <s>sāraṇā</s> is stated, practitioners should understand it again.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā koṭivedhī bhavedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: Having bound the mouth and having bound the <s>rasa</s>, the <s>rasa</s> becomes a crore-penetrator.
Joined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, the moon-metal and sun-metal become gold.
The penetration has been explained in order by means of the eighteen operations alone.
Mercury with mouth opened, without mouth opened, fixation, and fixation of mercury have likewise been stated.

children.text: gopitaṃ śaṃbhunā siddhaiḥ sūcitaṃ na prakāśitam
children.translated_text: This was hidden by <s>Śambhu</s> and only indicated by the siddhas, not openly revealed.
For the benefit of practitioners, I have made it manifest.
Diamond ash, purified gold, mica essence, and iron powder,
the four in equal parts, and lead powder equal to the four,
should be sealed and blown in a crucible smeared with a paired mixture.
When it has become one mass, one should take it out and blow it openly in a crucible.
Washed essence from pyrite should be added little by little.
When only gold and diamond remain, one should then remove it.
Into it one should put lead, mica essence, and iron powder, as before.
One should place it in a crucible smeared with the paired mixture, seal it, and blow it.
When it has become mixed, one should take it out and blow it openly in a crucible.
One should collect whatever remains, consisting of gold and diamond.
Thus, again and again, mica essence, iron, and <s>phaṇin</s> should be digested.
Again, by the previous ordered procedure, one should digest six times the quantity.
The washed essence from pyrites

children.text: kṣipan kṣipandhamettaṃ tu bāhyamevaṃ tu ṣaḍguṇam ||
children.translated_text: should be cast in repeatedly and blown; in this way the external material too is made sixfold.
This is known as <s>vajrabīja</s> (diamond seed), supremely useful for digestion.
Into <s>sūta</s> (mercury), whose mouth has been prepared by impregnation, one should put the paired mica essence.
Again, by the previous ordered procedure, one should digest six times the quantity.
Into that, the <s>vajrabīja</s> should be digested according to the sequence of mica essence.

children.text: grasate kacchape yaṃtre yathājīrṇaṃ tathā phalam ||
children.translated_text: It consumes it in the tortoise apparatus; according as it is digested, so is the result.
When twice as much has been digested, it pierces ten thousand; when threefold, it pierces one hundred thousand.
When fourfold has been digested, it pierces one million.
At fivefold it pierces ten million, and at sixfold one hundred million.
At sevenfold it pierces an <s>arbuda</s> part, and at the eighth grade it is conch-piercing.
At the ninth it becomes <s>kharva</s>-piercing; at the tenth it is lotus-piercing.
When thirteenfold has been digested, the <s>rasa</s> becomes touch-piercing.
When fourteenfold has been digested, it becomes stone-piercing.
When three times fivefold has been digested,

children.text: vedhayenmedinīṃ sarvāṃ sa bhaved bhūcaro rasaḥ
children.translated_text: it can pierce the whole earth together with its mountains, forests, and groves; that <s>rasa</s> becomes earth-moving.
Thus, when digested to the degree of the <s>kalā</s>, it becomes pervading the three worlds.
The great king of <s>rasa</s>, sky-going, when kept in the mouth, grants motion through the sky.

children.text: jāyate ca yathāśaktyā tataḥ sāryaṃ krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: Then, according to one's capacity, it is to be led onward in sequence.
The first <s>sāraṇā</s> (carrying-forward operation) should be with an equal amount of <s>vajrabīja</s>.
The digestion should be performed as before; with a double quantity one should carry it forward.
Again, one should digest it in the same way, and a repeated <s>sāraṇā</s> should be done.

children.text: triguṇena tu tenaiva mukhaṃ baddhvātha bandhayet ||
children.translated_text: With that same material in triple quantity, after closing the mouth, one should bind it.
This is the procedure for a piercing agent ranging from two thousand up to one hundred thousand.
Thus one should again perform <s>sāraṇā</s> for the ten-million-piercing agent.
For <s>rasa</s> digested as a piercing agent from one hundred million up to an <s>arbuda</s>,

children.text: triprakārā prakartavyā sāraṇā tu tridhā tridhā ||
children.translated_text: three kinds of <s>sāraṇā</s> should be performed, each in three forms.
For conch-piercing it is fourfold; beyond that it becomes fivefold.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇā padmavedhe tu mūlavedhe tu saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: For lotus-piercing it is sixfold, and for root-piercing it is sevenfold.
For touch-piercing it is eightfold; for sound-piercing, tenfold.
After that, for the <s>kalā</s>-grade, it is thirteenfold, each according to its <s>kalā</s>.
The <s>sāraṇā</s> should be performed successively, in accordance with one's ability.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā paścādvedhaṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having closed the mouth and bound the <s>rasa</s>, one should afterward arrange the piercing operation.

children.text: caṃdrārke vā bhujaṃge vā krāmaṇena samāyutam
children.translated_text: In moon, sun, or serpent material, it should be furnished with <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrating activation).
Thus, up to the lotus grade, whatever <s>rasa</s> arises from numerical piercing,
one should enclose it in beeswax and apply it in spear-piercing.
All that becomes divine gold; this was taught by <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: dhūmavedhe rasaṃ piṣṭvā tena vastraṃ pralepayet
children.translated_text: For smoke-piercing, one should grind the <s>rasa</s> and smear a cloth with it.
Then, having soaked it in <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> oil, one should make a wick.
When lit, it should be applied to a copper heap that has become leaf-thin.
By the mere odor of that smoke, everything becomes gold.

children.text: sparśavedhī raso yo'sau guṭikāṃ tena kārayet
children.translated_text: With that <s>rasa</s> which is touch-piercing, one should make a pill.
Having cast it into the middle of the eight molten metals, one should take it out.
That becomes divine gold, beyond counting; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: śabdavedhī raso yo'sau guṭikāṃ tena kārayet
children.translated_text: With that <s>rasa</s> which is sound-piercing, one should make a pill.

children.text: dhārayed vaktramadhye tu tato lohāni vedhayet
children.translated_text: One should hold it in the mouth and then pierce the metals.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ jāyate svarṇaṃ śrute śabde na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All that becomes gold when the sound is heard; there is no doubt.

children.text: pāṣāṇavedhako yo'sau parvatāni tu tena vai
children.translated_text: With that which is stone-piercing, one should pierce mountains
heated by fire; everything becomes gold.
That which is earth-piercing, in a measure of half of half a mustard seed,
with that alone one should pierce the whole earth, together with its mountains, forests, and groves.
That earth becomes made of gold; this is true, spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: trailokyavyāpako yo'sau taṃ kare dhārayettu yaḥ
children.translated_text: That which pervades the three worlds, whoever holds it in his hand
becomes a divine sky-goer, with a great body and great strength.
He moves at will, a great hero, and becomes equal to <s>Śiva</s>.
Through his urine and feces, all metals become gold.
They arise so; there is no doubt. Even from contact with his sweat,
he has a body made of <s>rasa</s>, is a great adept, and is honored in all worlds.
He is invulnerable to gods and demons as long as the moon, sun, and earth endure.
Enjoying divine pleasures, he sports like <s>Bhairava</s>.
Three parts purified <s>sūta</s> and one part killed diamond
should be ground with <s>kākinīrajas</s> in a heated mortar for a full day.
With one quarter part of that very substance, one should smear gold leaves.
Magnet, borax, and orpiment, ground with the juices of <s>vyomavallī</s>,
should be applied, in one-eighth part, to the leaves previously smeared.

children.text: ruddhvā svedyaṃ divārātrau karīṣāgnau tataḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed them, they should be steamed day and night in a cow-dung fire; then again,
plantain bulb, <s>sauvīra</s>, and borax, each in equal measure,

children.text: kaṇṭakāryā dravaiḥ piṣṭvā mūṣā lepyā tvanena vai ||
children.translated_text: should be ground with the liquids of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>; the crucible should be smeared with this.
Inside that, what was previously cooked should be sealed and blown with a strong fire.
All that becomes <s>khoṭa</s>; <s>sauvīra</s>, glass, and borax
should be added again and again and blown; the <s>khoṭa</s> becomes like the sun.
This is known as <s>rasabīja</s> (mercurial seed), useful for <s>vedhana</s> (piercing transmutation) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion).
With the moon-metal and sun-metal it becomes a hundred-piercer and produces fine gold.

children.text: atha vakṣye rasendrasya samāṃśasya ca bhakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the eating, by <s>rasendra</s> (lordly mercury), of an equal portion.
The previously described <s>rasabīja</s> should be fed to <s>rasa</s> whose mouth has been opened.
One should make that digest gradually by the method used for mica essence.
When <s>pārada</s> (mercury) consumes it in portions increased five by five,
then with that very seed one should perform the three operations of <s>sāraṇa</s> and <s>ākramaṇa</s>.
After that, having made it digested, one should close its mouth and then bind it.
That <s>rasa</s> becomes <s>śabdavedhin</s> (sound-piercing); this was spoken by <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
For <s>rasendra</s> whose mouth has been opened, the cooked seed, in an equal portion,
should be made to digest after being sprinkled, again by the method of mica essence.
One should place killed diamond, in a sixteenth part, into that <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
<s>Tālaka</s>, <s>ṭaṃkaṇa</s>, and <s>kānta</s> are added, the third and an eighth part.
Having put these into a mortar with juices of <s>vyomavallī</s> for a day,
one should grind all of it and dry it carefully in the shade.
It should be sealed in a crucible smeared with <s>dvandvamelāpa</s> and blown.

children.text: karīṣāgnau divārātrau dhmāte khoṭaṃ bhavettu tat ||
children.translated_text: When blown in a cow-dung fire day and night, that becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> (solid lump).
One should purify it by blowing again and again with glass, borax, and <s>sauvīra</s>.
This is known as <s>rasabīja</s>; as before, it pierces a hundredfold.
This <s>rasarāja</s> (king mercury) comes into being and produces fine gold.
Alternatively, in <s>sūta</s> whose mouth has been opened, one should make it digest for a day as before.
When <s>pārada</s> consumes it in portions increased five by five,

children.text: rasabījena cānyena tridhā sāryaṃ krameṇa vai
children.translated_text: it should be carried through <s>sāraṇa</s> three times, in sequence, with another <s>rasabīja</s>.

children.text: sārite jāraṇā kāryā mukhaṃ baddhvātha bandhayet
children.translated_text: When it has undergone <s>sāraṇa</s>, <s>jāraṇa</s> should be performed; then, having closed the mouth, one should bind it.
It directly becomes <s>śabdavedhin</s> and indeed turns copper into gold.
The powder of the cooked seed, sprinkled as before,
should be fed to <s>sūta</s> whose mouth has been opened, in a sixteenth part of the mercury.
By grinding alone, in warmth and within a two-finger measure, it enters at once.
One should make that seed digest in it by steaming procedures, as with mica essence.

children.text: anena kramayogena samaṃ bījaṃ tu sārayet
children.translated_text: By this ordered method one should conduct an equal amount of seed through <s>sāraṇa</s>.

children.text: tadvad dvādaśabhāgena pakvabījaṃ tu tasya vai ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, with a twelfth part, its cooked seed
should be fed while it is being ground; then it should be digested in the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s>.
By the method of mica essence it should be digested until an equal amount has been digested.
After that, one should add cooked seed in an eighth part of it.
One should grind it in a heated mortar; it certainly enters at once.

children.text: taṃ sūtaṃ sūraṇe kaṃde garbhe kṣiptvā nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: That <s>sūta</s> should be placed in the interior of a <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber and sealed in.

children.text: liptvā kaṃdaṃ puṭe pacyādyathā kaṃdo na dahyate ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared the tuber, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> so that the tuber is not burned.

children.text: tatraiva grasate sūto jīrṇe grāsaṃ tu dāpayet
children.translated_text: There the <s>sūta</s> itself consumes it; when the mouthful has been digested, another should be given.
By this ordered method, again, equal seed in equal measure

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ pakvabījaṃ tu dattvā cāryaṃ ca mardayet
children.translated_text: should be fed and ground after giving cooked seed in a quarter part.

children.text: mūṣāyantre tato jāryaṃ svedanena punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then it should be digested in the crucible apparatus by steaming again and again.
By this ordered method one should make it digest an equal amount of seed.

children.text: evaṃ caturguṇe jīrṇe pakvabīje tu pārade
children.translated_text: Thus, when the cooked seed has been digested fourfold in the <s>pārada</s>,
the <s>rasendra</s> becomes saffron-colored and much stronger.
Mica, <s>bhrāmaka</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, and the eight killed metals,
together with the <s>mahārasa</s> minerals, the subsidiary minerals, and the seed of bitter gourd,
<s>śaṅkhanābhi</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and <s>vajrakanda</s>, each in equal amount,

children.text: mayūrasya tu raktena sarvaṃ pācyaṃ dināvadhi ||
children.translated_text: should all be cooked for a full day with peacock blood.
Then one should grind that <s>khoṭa</s> in peacock blood for two days.
With this, one should then have killed diamond coated.
One should make a crucible shaped like a mango fruit and smeared twice over.
Into its middle one should place the previous <s>sūta</s>, a quarter part, and the coated diamond.
Or one may use diamond-seed smeared with the previous paste,

children.text: athavā dvaṃdvitaṃ vajraṃ samaṃ svarṇena yatkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: or diamond combined in a pair with an equal amount of gold.
Having smeared that with the previous paste, one should place a quarter part there.
Covered, it should be blown gently with the blast directed to the downward-facing crucible-mouth.

children.text: kiṃcit kiṃcid biḍaṃ dattvā jīrṇe tasmātsamuddharet
children.translated_text: Putting in a little <s>biḍa</s> bit by bit, when it has digested one should remove it from there.
Again, placing it in that smeared crucible together with diamond,
one should remove it when the diamond has been digested by the same ordered method as before.
By this ordered method, diamond or diamond-seed,
or diamond combined with gold, should be digested again and again.
It should be digested in <s>rasendra</s> until it is elevenfold.
Well-burned <s>śaṅkhanābhi</s> should be ground for a day with citron juices,
and stirred; with that, very beautiful pearl powder
or else melted pearl should be digested as before by blowing.

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ biḍaliptāyāṃ pādaṃ pādaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a crucible smeared with <s>biḍa</s>, it is added quarter by quarter, very gradually.
It should be digested up to elevenfold by means of the <s>kacchapa</s> apparatus.
One should grind peacock bile equal to the exudate of <s>nīlī</s>.

children.text: indranīlaṃ ca nīlaṃ ca tena liptvātha jārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared <s>indranīla</s> and <s>nīla</s> with that, one should then digest them.
This is done by the ordered method as before, either by blowing or by steaming.
In a crucible smeared with <s>biḍa</s>, it is done elevenfold in sequence.

children.text: drāvitaṃ cendranīlaṃ vā nīlaṃ ca drāvitaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: Or melted <s>indranīla</s> and melted <s>nīla</s>, each in sequence,
combined with <s>rasarāja</s>, should be digested just like mica <s>druti</s> (liquefied essence).

children.text: ityevaṃ jārayennīlaṃ drāvitaṃ kaṭhinaṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should digest <s>nīla</s>, whether melted or hard.
<s>Padmarāga</s>, smeared with peacock bile and human blood,
should be digested into <s>rasarāja</s> up to elevenfold in order.

children.text: jāryaṃ vā drāvitaṃ tattu yathā cābhradrutiḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: Or that melted gem should be digested as previously, just like mica <s>druti</s>.
Equal quantities of nightshade and <s>kuṣṭha</s> are to be treated for a day with the liquids of <s>brahmapuṣpa</s>.

children.text: bhāvitaṃ tena liptaṃ tu puṣparāgaṃ tu jārayet ||
children.translated_text: And with that, when smeared, one should digest <s>puṣparāga</s>.
Whether hard or melted, in due order according to the number of <s>Rudra</s>,
in this way the king of <s>rasa</s>, powerful and mighty, becomes satisfied with gems.
With one-hundredth part of this, mixed with beeswax, one should smear
plates of purified gold, seal them, and cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> furnace.
That gold becomes auspicious, having the appearance of <s>indragopa</s> insects.
With this very gold one should perform the three operations of <s>sāraṇā</s>.
One should place the gem-sated royal <s>sūta</s> in a crucible apparatus.
One should blow it slowly and steadily until only the <s>sūta</s> remains.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā rasaṃ baddhvā dhūmavedhī bhavettu tat
children.translated_text: After closing its mouth and binding the <s>rasa</s>, it becomes smoke-piercing.
By this ordered procedure, again, <s>sāraṇā</s> and <s>jāraṇā</s>
should be done in three ways; after closing its mouth, one should bind it.
This lord of <s>rasa</s> becomes sound-piercing and gives the power of moving through the sky.
Again the threefold <s>sāraṇā</s> should be performed, followed by <s>jāraṇā</s> in sequence.

children.text: tasyaiva tu rasendrasya mukhabandhaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should cause the mouth-sealing of that very lord of <s>rasa</s>.
With it one may pierce everything, mountains, stones, and the earth.
Divine gold is produced, with a brilliance equal to <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold.

children.text: siddhairbhūcarakhecarā śivamukhātprāptā mahājāraṇā kṛtvā tāṃ ca rase rasātalamidaṃ svarṇena pūrṇaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: The great <s>jāraṇā</s>, obtained by accomplished beings who move on earth and in the sky from the mouth of <s>Śiva</s>, was performed in <s>rasa</s>, and this underworld was filled with gold.

children.text: teṣāṃ karma vicārya sāramakhilaṃ spaṣṭīkṛtaṃ tanmayā yaḥ kaścid gurutantramantraniratastasyaiva siddhaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having considered their work, I have made its whole essence clear; it will be accomplished only for one who is devoted to the teacher, tantra, and mantra.

children.text: saṃsāre sārabhūtaṃ sakalasukhakaraṃ suprabhūtaṃ dhanaṃ vai tatsādhyaṃ sādhakendrairgurumukhavidhinā vakṣyate tasya siddhyai
children.translated_text: In this world, wealth that is the very essence, bringing every happiness and very abundant, is to be attained; for its accomplishment it will be taught by foremost practitioners according to the method learned from the teacher's mouth.

children.text: ratnādīnāṃ viśeṣāt karaṇamiha śubhaṃ gaṃdhavādaṃ samagraṃ jñātvā tattat susiddhaṃ hyanubhavapathagaṃ pāvanaṃ paṇḍitānām ||
children.translated_text: Having understood here the auspicious special procedures for gems and the like, the complete doctrine of fragrances, each of those well-accomplished and lying on the path of experience, is purifying for the learned.

children.text: caturguṇena toyena lākṣāṃ piṣṭvā tu taddravaiḥ
children.translated_text: After grinding lac with four times as much water, with those liquids
one should take one hundred <s>palas</s>, strained through cloth, place it in an earthen vessel, and cook it.

children.text: mṛdvagninā pādaśeṣaṃ jātaṃ yāvacca tasya vai
children.translated_text: With a gentle fire, until it is reduced to a quarter,
one should add, one <s>pala</s> each, powders of <s>sarjikā</s>, borax, and <s>lodhra</s>.
One should cook it a little; then, when cool, preserve it in a glass bottle.
One should cook coarse fish skin with water for a day and night.
Having removed it when it has become solid, this is known as fish-blackening, <s>matsyakajjala</s>.
One should put two <s>karṣas</s> of this into that glass bottle.
Having softened hailstones with just that and cooked them well,
one should cook them for a moment in madhūka oil and take them out.
They become rubies, filled with divine splendor.

children.text: nīlīcūrṇaṃ palaikaṃ tu pūrvakūpyāṃ tu taddravam
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of indigo powder is to be put into the same earlier bottle and liquid.

children.text: taddravaṃ dvipalaṃ cūrṇe kṣiptvā sarvaṃ vilolayet ||
children.translated_text: Having put two <s>palas</s> of that liquid into the powder, one should stir everything thoroughly.
Having put hailstones into that, one should cook those that have gone into the former oil.
Those very stones become sapphires; there is no doubt about this.
One should prepare equal powders of madder, orpiment, and indigo.
With the liquids kept in a glass bottle, one should stir all this thoroughly.
Having sprinkled the hailstones with that, one should cook them as before.
By that they all become excellent emeralds.
One should grind <s>matsyakajjala</s> with a decoction of madder.
Having sprinkled the hailstones with that, one should cook them as before.

children.text: gomedāni tu tānyeva pravartante na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those very stones turn into <s>gomeda</s> gems; there is no doubt.
Having ground saffron of <s>rasa</s> with an equal amount of orpiment in one water,
one should add one-eighth part of fish-derived <s>kajjala</s> to it.
One should cook all that for a watch, take it down, and preserve it.
Having sprinkled hailstones with that, one should cook them as before.
They become <s>puṣparāga</s> gems, just as if they had arisen from a mine.
One should add fish-derived <s>kajjala</s> in a portion equal to the indigo powder.

children.text: bījakāṣṭhaṃ ca tulyāṃśaṃ jale sthāpyaṃ dināvadhi ||
children.translated_text: And equal parts of seed-wood should be kept in water for a day.
One should cook all that for a watch, take it down, and preserve it.
Having sprinkled the hailstones with that, one should cook them as before.
They become like blue rubies; there is no doubt.
The coloring substances have been stated separately, each in a glass bottle.
After preserving them carefully, one should apply them when the task arises.

children.text: sūryakāṃtasya madhye tu bilaṃ kuryāt suvartulam
children.translated_text: In the middle of a sun-stone one should make a nicely rounded hollow.
Likewise one should prepare another sun-stone, suitable as a cover.
First one should melt small pearls according to the preceding recipe.
That molten material is to be filled carefully into the hollow of the sun-stone.
Covered with the other sun-stone and kept in heat,
after just one watch it becomes a bound pearl, very beautiful.
Having made a hole, one should then tie it in a very clean piece of cloth.
Together with very clean rice, one should pound it in a mortar.
With a light hand for one watch; then, having taken it out, one should wash it.
One should grind the skins of soap-nut fruits with water.
Washed with that, the pearl becomes beautiful.
One should put in very tiny pearls, powdered,
for a moment into the fresh milk of a cow that has just calved.
Then with that one should make round pellets.
Placed in a glass vessel, they should be dried in the shade for the space of one day.
One should string them with horsehair, making a garland, and then dry them.
They should be kept hanging in the shade until they become hard.
From the belly of a large black fish with a single throat,
one should remove the entrails, and place the earlier garland right there.
One should sew up the belly with thread, enclose it in a vessel,
take it out after the space of a month, and again dry it in the shade.
Pounding and washing should also be done gently, as before.

children.text: bhavanti tāni śubhrāṇi samyaṅ muktāphalāni vai ||
children.translated_text: They indeed become fine, bright pearl-fruits, properly formed.
Taking pearl-oyster shell, or else water-shell,
one should rub its back part in order to remove its blackness.
When those are bright, one should powder them finely, as before, beginning with ewe's milk.
One should carry out the process up to washing, and they indeed become pearls.

children.text: sadya uddhṛtya matsyasya sthūlasya cakṣuṣī haret
children.translated_text: Immediately after taking out the eyes of a large fish, one should remove them.
One should bind each one in cloth and cook it for a day with ewe's milk.
Afterward one should dry them in the shade, then pound and wash them.
One should do these as before, and they indeed become pearls.

children.text: dagdhaśaṃkhaṃ ca daradaṃ samaṃ cūrṇaṃ prakalpayet
children.translated_text: Burnt conch shell and <s>darada</s> should be prepared as a powder in equal parts.
On the fifth day after a she-buffalo has given birth, one should take
her milk; with that very milk the previous powder should be rubbed for one watch.
Having made round pills, one should string them on a copper thread.
With the inner leaves of plantain, using the middle finger, thumb, and forefinger,

children.text: veṣṭayitvā tu tairgrāhyā gulikāstāḥ pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: one should wrap them, and those pills should be taken separately one by one.
They should be repeatedly turned and carefully placed with plantain leaves.

children.text: chāyāśuṣkāḥ śubhāḥ protyās tāmrasūtreṇa vai punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When dried in the shade, they are fine; again they should be strung on a copper thread.
<s>Madhuka</s>, smeared with hot oil, should be gently steamed with smoke.
It becomes coral with the appearance of ruby; there is no doubt about this.
Burnt conch shell together with cinnabar should then be powdered in equal portions.
One should rub it thoroughly with the milk of a ewe that has just given birth.
One should fill it into a hollow made from grass, or into a tube produced from bamboo and the like.
One should place it in a well-fired food vessel, excluding gruel.
After covering it, one should cook it over a gentle fire and take it out at the end of a <s>ghaṭikā</s>.
Corals are produced inside the tube, like ruby.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ pāradaṃ bhāgaṃ caturbhāgaṃ ca ṭaṃkaṇam
children.translated_text: One part impure mercury and four parts borax

children.text: ubhau kṣiptvā lohapātre kṣaṇaṃ mṛdvagninā pacet ||
children.translated_text: should both be put into an iron vessel and cooked for a moment over a gentle fire.
Into that one should put powder of realgar in a tenth part relative to the mercury.
Having stirred it with an iron ladle, one should take it down and let it become quite cool.

children.text: kṛtvātha khaṇḍaśaḥ kṣiptvā kācakūpyāṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Then, having broken it into pieces, one should put it into a glass bottle and seal it.
One should coat the glass bottle properly with cloth and clay.
On all sides, to the measure of a finger's breadth, one should dry it in the shade.
Within a sand-bath apparatus it should be cooked for two days over a gentle fire.
Afterward it should be cooked for five days with the fire gradually increased.
After a week one should take it out; it will be beautiful cinnabar.
One should put a quarter part of ash of tamarind bark into molten lead.
One should cook it in an iron vessel and rub it with an iron ladle.

children.text: caṇḍāgninā dinaikaṃ tu sindūraṃ jāyate śubham ||
children.translated_text: With a fierce fire for one day, fine vermilion is produced.
The ash of red-branching <s>apāmārga</s> and <s>kuṭaja</s>,

children.text: caturthāṃśaṃ drute nāge dattvā mardyaṃ dinadvayam ||
children.translated_text: a quarter part, should be put into molten lead and rubbed for two days.
As before, in an iron vessel, fine vermilion is produced.
As before, by means of the ash of <s>śāka</s> or water-born plants, lead

children.text: sindūraṃ jāyate divyaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: becomes divine vermilion as desired; there is no doubt about this.
One should melt two hundred palas of lead in an iron vessel.
There one should put a quarter part of the ash of <s>vāsaka</s>, including its roots.
One should cook and stir it until it becomes yellow in color.
Then, having made it quite cool, one should again stir it with water.
Having made pills measuring one pala each, one should put them upon ash of <s>vāsā</s>.
When dried in the shade, one should collect them and place them in a new earthen vessel.
Having put them in and sealed it, one should cook it on a stove, windless, with intense fire.

children.text: chidraṃ kuryād bhāṇḍavaktre śalākāṃ lohajāṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: One should make a hole in the mouth of the vessel and insert an iron rod.
When that becomes red in color, one should cook it until then and examine it.
Divine vermilion is produced; this is taught as a perfected formula.
One should put one hundred palas of sea-salt into a new vessel.

children.text: niṣkaṃ niṣkaṃ sūtagaṃdhau kṣiptvā caṇḍāgninā pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having put one <s>niṣka</s> each of mercury and sulphur, one should cook it with a fierce fire.
If, at the end of two watches, one puts an iron spike into it,
and that indeed becomes red in color, then one should stop the fire.
When naturally cooled, it should be taken; it becomes salt born from the ocean.

children.text: āranālaṃ palaikaṃ tu dviniṣkaṃ ca suvarcalam
children.translated_text: One pala of sour gruel, two <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>suvarcala</s>,

children.text: māṣaikaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ piṣṭvā sarvaṃ pātre tu dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: and one <s>māṣa</s> of sulphur should be ground, and all of it should be held in a vessel.

children.text: palaikaṃ saiṃdhavaṃ taptaṃ kṛtvā tatra niṣecayet
children.translated_text: One should make one pala of rock salt hot and sprinkle it there.
It should be heated again and sprinkled again until the liquid dries up.
Then it becomes <s>suvarcala</s>; no deliberation is to be made here.
One part each of asafoetida and lead, and two palas of garlic,
four palas of neem seed, and eight palas of black gram powder,
together with an equal amount of pulp of <s>bilva</s>, should be ground with goat's milk.
All that should be bound tightly within a moist cowhide.
One should place it for three fortnights in a heap of grain; then it becomes <s>hiṅgu</s>.
The exudate of the <s>babbūla</s> tree, and likewise sea salt,

children.text: tvagvarjyaṃ ca kaṇā tulyaṃ meṣīkṣīreṇa peṣayet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>kaṇā</s> with the skin removed, in equal quantity, should be ground with ewe's milk.
One should add purified <s>hiṅgu</s>, one quarter of this lump's amount.
All that, tied up as before in leather for three days,
should be kept hanging in a windless place; the <s>hiṅgu</s> will be like purified <s>hiṅgu</s>.
One <s>pala</s> each of jaggery and dry ginger, two <s>palas</s> each of borax and <s>guggulu</s>,
and two <s>palas</s> of huskless castor-seed kernels,
and two <s>palas</s> of dehulled black gram should be combined and thoroughly ground.

children.text: trikarṣaṃ hiṅgu tanmadhye kṣiptvā toyena lolayet ||
children.translated_text: Having put three <s>karṣas</s> of <s>hiṅgu</s> into the middle of it, one should stir it with water.
All that, tied as before, attains the state of <s>hiṅgu</s> after a week.

children.text: dvipale śuddhahiṃgu syād eḍākṣīraṃ ca viṃśatiḥ
children.translated_text: For two <s>palas</s> there should be purified <s>hiṅgu</s>, and twenty [parts] of <s>eḍā</s> milk.
Powder of wheat and black gram should be four <s>palas</s> each.
All that, stirred together, should be put into the middle of a gourd vessel.
It should be shade-dried until the <s>hiṅgu</s> becomes good.
Powder of <s>dhattūra</s> seed should be impregnated with <s>vajrī</s> milk.

children.text: śoṣyaṃ peṣyaṃ punarbhāvyam evaṃ gharme trisaptadhā ||
children.translated_text: It should be dried, ground, and impregnated again; thus in the sun, twenty-one times.
That should be given as a projection into molten <s>nāga</s> in a tenth part.
One should pour it into <s>snuk</s> milk; that <s>vaṅga</s> becomes excellent.
One should impregnate it with <s>rajanī</s>; that <s>baṅga</s> becomes excellent.
One should impregnate <s>rajanī</s> powder seven times with <s>vajrī</s> milk.
That projection, in a tenth part, should be given into molten <s>nāga</s>.
That projection should be given in a tenth part of the molten <s>nāga</s>.
It should be poured into a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>, and again it should be projected in the same way.

children.text: ṭaṃkaṇaṃ navasāraṃ ca dattvā secyaṃ nṛmūtrake
children.translated_text: Having added borax and <s>navasāra</s>, it should be quenched in human urine.

children.text: drāvitaṃ ca punarḍhālyaṃ nṛmūtre vaṅgatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Melted and again poured into human urine, it attains the state of <s>vaṅga</s>.
Tamarind fruit, deprived of skin and seeds, should be combined with <s>kāñjika</s>.
Having cooked it, one should make it cloth-filtered; sour <s>jambīra</s> juice should be equal to it.
One should collect, as available, sour juices of <s>cāṅgerī</s> and <s>mātuliṅga</s>.
All that should be strained through cloth and cooked until one quarter remains.
<s>Saurāṣṭrī</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, the three alkalis, and the five salts,

children.text: mūlasāraṃ ca tulyāṃśaṃ sarvaṃ cūrṇaṃ vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>mūlasāra</s>, in equal portions, should all be added as powder.
Into the previously cooked material one should add a quarter portion and again cook it on a gentle fire.
Until it becomes thickened, one should stir it with a spoon.
This is called <s>amlavetasa</s>; it becomes supremely excellent.
<s>Triphala</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>koraṇṭa</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and <s>karavīraka</s>,
together with <s>bījāmra</s>, should be in equal portions; these are to be put into <s>bola-kajjala</s>.
After placing it in a copper vessel, it should be rubbed; after five days it becomes ink.
It writes on palm leaves and on birch bark with the highest durability.
One should take four parts of the juice from the fruit of the coconut.

children.text: tanmadhye ghṛtamekaṃ tu kṣiptvā bhāṇḍe vilolayet ||
children.translated_text: Into that one should put one part of ghee and stir it in a vessel.
Into it one should add root of red <s>śākinī</s> in a hundredth part.
One should cook it a little on a gentle fire; all that becomes ghee.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ toyaṃ samaṃ kṛtvā viṃśatyaṃśena cunnakam
