children.translated_text: Having made ghee and water equal, one should add <s>cunnaka</s> in a twentieth part.

children.text: kṣiptvā sarvaṃ tu mṛdbhāṃḍe kṣaṇaṃ hastena mardayet
children.translated_text: Putting everything in an earthen vessel, one should knead it by hand for a moment.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tajjāyate sarvaṃ na cāgniṃ sahate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: All that becomes ghee, and it never withstands fire anywhere.
There should be five <s>palas</s> of ewe's fat and the same amount of sesame oil.
One should cook them on a gentle fire until the foam ceases.

children.text: dviniṣkaṃ kāṃjikaṃ tasmin kṣiptvā vastreṇa cālayet
children.translated_text: Having put two <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>kāñjika</s> into it, one should stir it through a cloth.

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ ca ghṛtaṃ tasmin dadyātsarvaṃ ghṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: One should add a quarter part of ghee into it; everything becomes ghee.
At first one should cook sesame oil until the foam ceases.
One should put <s>guggulu</s> into it to remove a little of the smell.
Having put lime into water in a twentieth part, one should stir it.
The previous oil, well cooled, should be mixed in an amount equal to the water.
One should knead it in an earthen vessel by hand for just a moment.

children.text: ghanībhūte ghṛtaṃ cārdhaṃ kṣiptvā sarvaṃ ghṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When it has thickened, one should add half as much ghee; everything becomes ghee.
Having cut a <s>nimba</s> tree, one should leave one cubit below.
On its top one should make a hole; right there [one should place] fresh <s>guggulu</s>.
One should fill it, close the hole with that piece of wood, and then smear it.
One should seal the joint with clay and salt; when dry, it should be cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
When naturally cooled, it should be taken out; that root becomes sandalwood.
One should cook three <s>palas</s> of rice properly, using fine royal rice grains.

children.text: tad bhaktaṃ śītalaṃ kṛtvā gavāṃ kṣīraiḥ prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having cooled that cooked rice, [one should prepare it] carefully with cow's milk.

children.text: niṣkamātraṃ ca karpūraṃ kṣiptvā tasmiṃśca peṣayet
children.translated_text: After putting a <s>niṣka</s> measure of camphor into it, one should grind it.
With it, one should coat the inside of a dry, thick bamboo tube.
The coating should be a finger's breadth thick, and one should cause it to dry in the shade.
Then, having cut a plantain flower, one should fill it with its exudate.
Again, one should close the mouth of the bamboo tube with a piece of cloth.
After drying it in the sun for three days, one should then bury it in an underground pit.
After three weeks, one should take it out, dry it, and collect it.
The camphor within its cavity should be kept in a camphor vessel.

children.text: karpūraṃ jāyate divyaṃ yathā bījaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Divine camphor arises, just like the seed; there is no doubt.
One should cut up half of a ripe jackfruit and the seeds of one [fruit].

children.text: navabhāṇḍe vinikṣipya niṣkaṃ śuṇṭhī palaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: After putting them in a new vessel, [one should add] a <s>niṣka</s> and likewise one <s>pala</s> of dry ginger.
Having pulverized it, one should put it into that; all of it will become liquid.

children.text: tena ghṛṣṭvā kṣipettasmin caturniṣkaṃ ca candanam ||
children.translated_text: After grinding it with that, one should put four <s>niṣkas</s> of sandalwood into it.
One should cook it over a gentle fire until it has become reddish.
When it is cool, one should place it in a glass vessel, and on top of it put
<s>campaka</s>, <s>ketakī</s>, <s>mallī</s>, and <s>jātī</s> flowers; then again,

children.text: dinaṃ śubhrapaṭe baddhvā mukhaṃ tasyaiva rakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: after tying its mouth with a white cloth for a day, one should keep that very mouth protected.
Then, after discarding the flowers, one should add musk in the measure of one <s>māṣa</s>.
One should put one <s>māṣa</s> of purified camphor into that same mixture.
One should also add proper <s>jāvādi</s> in a twentieth part.
All that should first be churned well in a vessel for <s>jāvādi</s>.
One should wrap that vessel with jasmine flowers for three days.
It becomes good <s>jāvādi</s>, both in colors and in fragrances.
Five <s>palas</s> of <s>madhūka</s> oil, or oil produced from sesame,
and ten <s>palas</s> of <s>muṇḍī</s> extract: one should combine everything together.
Jasmine, <s>mālatī</s>, <s>jātī</s>, <s>ketakī</s>, and <s>śatapattrikā</s>,

children.text: anyāni ca sugandhīni puṣpāṇi tatra nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: and other fragrant flowers as well, should be put there.

children.text: dinaikaṃ mudritaṃ rakṣet puṣpaṃ niṣpīḍya saṃtyajet
children.translated_text: One should keep it sealed for one day; squeeze out the flowers and discard them.
After adding twenty <s>niṣkas</s> of beeswax to it, one should cook it slowly,
until only the oil remains; then one should add half a <s>niṣka</s> of camphor
and one <s>niṣka</s> of <s>mārjārajāvādi</s>, and then take it down from the fire.
Having put it into another vessel and let it cool, one should cook it again.
After removing it in just a moment, one should put it in a <s>jāvādi</s> vessel.

children.text: sāndraṃ bhavati tatsarvaṃ yathā bījaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: All of it becomes thick, like seed; there is no doubt.
The flowers of <s>bakula</s> and <s>ratnamālā</s> should be taken in equal portions.
Their powder should be placed inside a sugarcane stalk whose channel has been hollowed out.

children.text: kṣiptvā tasya mukhaṃ ruddhvā tanmajjābhirmṛdā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After closing its mouth, one should seal it again with its pith and with clay.
One should heat it with a grass fire until the fragrance is not burnt away.

children.text: dravanti tāni puṣpāṇi mukhaṃ bhittvā dravaṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: Those flowers melt; breaking open the mouth, one should take the liquid.
One should pulverize hairless musk-deer skin, in an amount equal to <s>mustā</s>.
One should add good musk in a tenth part of the powder.
All that, ground with the former liquid, should be made into balls.
They should be carefully made somewhat in the form of musk pellets.
All of that should be dried in the shade; the musk-like pellets should be preserved separately.

children.text: guṭikāḥ khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtvā madanaiḥ saha miśrayet
children.translated_text: Having broken the pills into pieces, one should mix them with the musk-like pellets.
Bound in musk-deer skin, it becomes proper <s>mṛgamada</s> (musk).
A coconut shell, or rubbed wood of <s>nimba</s>,
or any white wood whatever, should be prepared with water.
Then one should put into it turmeric equal to one quarter of that measure.

children.text: gairikaṃ vā rajanyardhaṃ tatsarvaṃ kuṃkumaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Or one may use red ochre, half as much as the turmeric; all of that becomes <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron-like pigment).

children.text: pālāśapuṣpajaṃ kvāthaṃ gharme dhāryaṃ tu kharpare
children.translated_text: A decoction made from <s>pālāśa</s> flowers should be kept in the heat in a potsherd.
One should add to it a twentieth part of well-ground white rice.

children.text: taṇḍulārdhaṃ tathā cunnaṃ sarvaṃ kāṣṭhena lolayet
children.translated_text: Likewise, lime in an amount half that of the rice; one should stir everything with a piece of wood.
Until it becomes thick, one should keep stirring it in the heat.
Then, having made pills from that very substance, they become like <s>kuṅkuma</s>.
One should take a quarter part of <s>pālāśa</s> flowers and properly cleaned white rice.

children.text: piṣṭvātha vaṭikāḥ kāryā śoṣyāḥ syuḥ kuṃkumopamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After grinding them, pills should be made; when dried, they become like <s>kuṅkuma</s>.
In order, one should make a preparation of superior quality with musk, <s>śaśikuṅkuma</s>,
<s>nakha</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>sarjarasa</s>, <s>mustā</s>, black <s>aguru</s>, and sugar.
Sandalwood as well: these ten, powdered, should be mixed together.
With <s>guggulu</s> equal to the powder, one should pound everything together.
One should add oil little by little, and on a stone, with an iron pestle,
work it carefully for one day; with it one should make a wick or incense roll.
One should set its tip alight and immediately extinguish the flame.
This is a divine incense for the gods, useful for accomplishing mantras.

children.text: pāṣāṇabhedacūrṇaṃ tu gugguluṃ ca palaṃ palam
children.translated_text: Powder of <s>pāṣāṇabheda</s> and <s>guggulu</s>, one <s>pala</s> each,
<s>māṃsī</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>nakha</s>, <s>bola</s>, sandalwood, <s>aguru</s>, and <s>vālaka</s>,
lac, jaggery, and <s>sarjarasa</s>, combined with sugar and camphor,

children.text: prati niṣkadvayaṃ cūrṇya kastūrī kuṃkumaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: should be powdered in portions of two <s>niṣkas</s> each; musk and <s>kuṅkuma</s> as well
one should add, one <s>māṣa</s> each, and pound everything in a mortar.

children.text: tilatailaṃ kṣipet kiṃcil lohadaṇḍena tad dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: One should add a little sesame oil and pound it firmly with an iron rod.
After pounding it for one watch, the divine incense proclaimed by <s>Śiva</s> is perfected.
It should be offered, made into incense rolls as before, and it makes even non-gods divine.
It produces every good fortune and is the remover of evil for all mantras.

children.text: vajrīkṣīreṇa saṃyuktaṃ śuddhaṃ vastraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: A purified cloth, joined again and again with the milk-latex of <s>vajrī</s>,
should be dried in the sun; this should be done for seven days.
One <s>pala</s> of <s>jātī</s> flowers and one <s>niṣka</s> of powdered borax
should be combined with three <s>niṣkas</s> of honey, and everything should be stirred together.

children.text: mṛtpātre dhārayed gharme ramye vā kācabhājane
children.translated_text: One should keep it in an earthen vessel in the heat, or in a fine glass vessel.
At once one should cover it with a cloth moistened with water.
Those flowers melt; one should use that liquid in preparations.

children.text: anenaiva prakāreṇa puṣpāṇāṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: By this very method, separately for each kind of fragrant flower,
a liquefaction should be made and applied in the arts of perfumery.
The root of <s>mandāra</s>, born among <s>kuśa</s> grass, on the lunar day of <s>Ārdrā</s> or <s>Bharaṇī</s>,
should be carefully gathered upward and placed in a garland of <s>dhava</s>.
The wood that faces a very strong wind should be collected.
One should make a heap of grain; it is an excellent means of increasing grain.
The left eye of a <s>kṛkalāsa</s> lizard, wrapped in gold and consecrated with mantra,
should be placed in a heap of grain; it is an excellent means of increasing grain.

children.text: tasyaiva dakṣiṇaṃ netraṃ hemnāveṣṭya tataḥ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Likewise, one should wrap its right eye in gold and then throw it in.
In whatever substance it may be, or in grain, it causes increase.
When the root of black <s>citraka</s> is placed in any good article,

children.text: tatsarvaṃ cākṣayaṃ nityaṃ vyayīkṛtya na kṣīyate ||
children.translated_text: all that remains inexhaustible always; even when spent, it is not diminished.

children.text: dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ suvarṇaṃ navaratnakam
children.translated_text: Money, grain, ghee, oil, gold, the nine jewels,
and whatever class of substance there is, that remains certainly inexhaustible.
One should place the root of a very white <s>guñjā</s> in water.
Having then placed that root in a heap of grain according to the prescription of the mantra,
that grain constantly increases, though consumed by the thousands.
As the preparation of the <s>guñjā</s> root is stated in the section on mantras,
so it should be carried out here; otherwise success does not occur.

children.text: ādau sarvadiśāntareṣu gamanaṃ kṛtvā guroḥ saṃmukhāt prāptaṃ bhaktibalena yuktividhinā sārātisāraṃ mahat
children.translated_text: First, having gone through all the quarters and received from the teacher's presence, by the power of devotion and by the proper method, the great essence beyond essence,

children.text: tatsarvaṃ dhanavardhanaṃ nigaditaṃ bhūyiṣṭhamadhvāṃ kvacid bhūpānāṃ viduṣāṃ mahāmatimatāṃ vidvān bhavet pālanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: all that has been declared for the increase of wealth; in some very long road, one may become a learned guardian of kings, scholars, and men of great intelligence.

children.text: sāṅgopāṅgam anekayoganicayaṃ sāraṃ varaṃ coddhṛtaṃ yuktaṃ pāradabandhanaṃ mṛduhaṭhāt dṛṣṭaṃ paraṃ yanmayā
children.translated_text: The excellent essence, complete with its limbs and subsidiary limbs and consisting of many sets of procedures, has been extracted; the binding of mercury, properly joined, which I have seen as supreme through gentle and forceful means,

children.text: tatsarvaṃ sugamaṃ pravacmi sahasā siddhānanādāgataṃ pratyakṣānubhavena vārtikagaṇaiḥ sāmrājyadaṃ vīkṣyatāt ||
children.translated_text: all that, easy to accomplish, I shall now proclaim quickly, coming from the teaching of the siddhas; let it be examined, granting sovereignty through direct experience and groups of explanatory verses.
Take one part of purified mercury and an equal amount of borax.
Then grind it with decoctions of the three myrobalans mixed with human urine.
Having made pills of one <s>karṣa</s> each, with black-gram flour mixed with water,
and having smeared them with the visible qualities of mercury, one should dry them in the shade and heat them strongly.
In a furnace-apparatus with a bent tube, one should break open the slag and collect it.
That mercury becomes round in form, abundantly bound as impotent mercury.
With the juices of wild jasmine, or with the juices of <s>kanyā</s>,
or with the juices of <s>hariṇakhurī</s>, one should combine the mercury with human urine.

children.text: tridinaṃ mardayetkhalve mūtraṃ dattvā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: One should grind it in a mortar for three days, adding urine again and again.

children.text: tadvaṭīṃ māṣapiṣṭena liptvā dhāmyaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: That pellet, smeared with black-gram paste, is to be heated as before.
In the same way the mercury becomes bound; it should be purified with glass and borax.
One should grind mercury for a day with juices produced from the root of <s>markaṭī</s>.
The mercury so ground should be placed in a lump made from <s>markaṭī</s> root.
Having enclosed that lump in a diamond crucible, one should heat it with an intense fire.
This becomes bound as a solid lump and is capable of carrying out every operation.

children.text: arkamūlaṃ ravikṣīraiḥ piṣṭvā mūṣāṃ ghanaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>arka</s> root with the milk of <s>arka</s>, one should put it thickly into a crucible.

children.text: tanmadhye jāritaṃ sūtaṃ kṣiptvā ruddhvātha rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed digested mercury in the middle of it, one should close it and then seal it.
One should confine it in an earthen capsule and confine that in an iron capsule.
Then one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; the mercury obtains binding.
One should grind mercury for three days with the juices of <s>jalakumbhī</s>.

children.text: jalakumbhyā dalairmūṣāṃ kṛtvā tatra kṣipettu tat ||
children.translated_text: Having made a crucible from the leaves of <s>jalakumbhī</s>, one should place that mercury there.
Having sealed it in a diamond crucible and dried it in the shade, one should give it a light firing.
Increasing by one <s>utpala</s> at a time, one should cook it with firings twenty times.
Then a <s>gajapuṭa</s> firing is to be given; the mercury becomes properly bound.
Purified mercury is to be ground for three days with the juices of <s>ekavīrā</s>.
One should coat a diamond crucible with the paste of the bulb of <s>ekavīrā</s>.

children.text: tasyāṃ pūrvarasaṃ ruddhvā dhmāte baddho bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having enclosed the preceding mercury in that, when it is heated the mercury becomes bound.
With juices arising from the red milk-bearing bulb, combined with three portions of breast milk,
one should grind mercury for three days, and with the juices of <s>vajrakanda</s> for three days.
One should coat a diamond crucible with the paste of the milk-bearing bulb.

children.text: tatra pūrvarasaṃ ruddhvā dhmāte baddho bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having enclosed the preceding mercury there, when it is heated the mercury becomes bound.
Having made a copper wheel, four finger-breadths wide,

children.text: unnataṃ cāṅgulīkaṃ tu sudṛḍhaṃ vartulaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: and one finger-breadth high, very firm, round, and even,
one should make sulphur, mercury, and blue vitriol into <s>kajjala</s> in a mortar.
That <s>kajjala</s>, equal in amount to the copper, should be placed inside a crucible.

children.text: taṃ cakraṃ mūṣikāvaktre dattvā ruddhvātha śoṣayet
children.translated_text: Having put that wheel at the mouth of the small crucible, one should seal it and then dry it.
One should cook it in a pot-apparatus for two watches with a gentle fire.
Having taken it out, one should repeatedly collect the king of mercury from the wheel.
An equal amount of borax and glass should be applied above and below it.
It is to be heated inside a blind crucible; when this has been done three times,

children.text: rasendro jāyate baddho hyakṣīṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury becomes bound and undiminished; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ samaṃ gaṃdhaṃ dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ ca tālakam
children.translated_text: Take equal amounts of purified mercury and sulphur, and twice as much <s>tālaka</s> as the two.
It is to be ground with juices of <s>unmattaka</s> in a mortar for four watches.
One should distill it in a distillation apparatus for one day with a slow fire.
What has adhered above and what is situated below, all that should be collected.
It should be ground hard with juices of <s>unmattaka</s> for four watches.
That ball should be cooked as before; taking it up again, one should grind it.
Again it should be cooked and again ground; what is above and below should be carefully collected.
This is to continue until everything remains in the lower vessel.
All that should be ground as before, made into a ball, and then dried.
One should grind <s>nalika</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s> thoroughly with sour liquids.

children.text: pītāñjanaṃ vā peṣyaṃ ca tena golaṃ pralepayet
children.translated_text: Or yellow collyrium should be ground, and with that one should coat the pellet.

children.text: vajramūṣodare cātha tena kalkena lepya vai ||
children.translated_text: Then, inside a diamond-crucible, the pellet should indeed be smeared with that paste.
There one should heat the small ball, blowing it with a bent tube.
With the fire of intense heat, it directly becomes bound into a <s>khoṭa</s> (solid lump).

children.text: palaṃ sūtaṃ palaṃ nāgaṃ dvābhyāṃ tulyā manaḥśilā
children.translated_text: One pala of mercury and one pala of lead, with realgar equal to the two,
by the sequence of procedure as before, the mercury becomes bound into a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: nāgaṃ tāraṃ samaṃ drāvyaṃ taccūrṇaṃ palamātrakam
children.translated_text: Lead and silver should be melted in equal amount; their powder should be one pala in measure.
There should be one pala of purified mercury, and realgar equal to all.
By the sequence of procedure as before, the mercury becomes bound into a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: palaṃ sūtaṃ palaṃ tāraṃ piṣṭamamlena kenacit
children.translated_text: One pala of mercury and one pala of silver should be ground with some sour liquid.

children.text: dvābhyāṃ tulyā śilā yojyā pūrvayogena pācayet ||
children.translated_text: Realgar equal to the two should be added, and it should be cooked by the preceding method.

children.text: tāravat svarṇapiṣṭīṃ ca gaṃdhakena ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: As with silver, so too a paste of gold should be treated with sulphur as before.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya satvaṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ kāṃtaṃ ca hāṭakam
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, iron, magnetite, gold,

children.text: śulbaṃ tāraṃ ca mākṣīkaṃ samaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vicūrṇayet
children.translated_text: copper, silver, and pyrite should be finely powdered in equal portions.

children.text: vajramūṣāgataṃ ruddhvā dhmāte khoṭaṃ bhavettu tat ||
children.translated_text: Placed in a diamond-crucible and sealed, when blown upon, that becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: śvetābhrakasya satvaṃ ca tāraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca mākṣikam
children.translated_text: The essence of white mica, silver, iron, and pyrite

children.text: samaṃ cūrṇya kṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ khoṭāṃśaṃ śuddhasūtakam ||
children.translated_text: should be powdered equally and made into a <s>khoṭa</s>; purified mercury should be in the amount of the <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: haritālaṃ dvayostulyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ mardyaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Orpiment, equal to the two, should be rubbed finely as before.
When blown upon in a great fire, that <s>khoṭa</s> becomes mercury.
Mercury and sulphur in equal amount should be rubbed for a day with juices of <s>kanyā</s>.
Having made that into a pellet, one should add twice as much sulphur, above and below in a crucible.

children.text: ruddhvā saṃdhiṃ viśoṣyātha koṣṭhīyantre dṛḍhaṃ dhaman
children.translated_text: After sealing the joint and drying it, one should blow strongly in a furnace-apparatus.
That mercury becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>; this is bound by sulphur.
The decoction of the five parts of <s>rājavṛkṣa</s> should be reduced to one eighth.

children.text: taddravaṃ tu rase kṣiptvā pācyaṃ yāmadvayaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: That liquid should be poured into the mercury, and the auspicious mixture should be cooked for two watches.
This becomes <s>covābaddha</s>, a <s>khoṭa</s> indeed capable of every operation.
Purified mercury should be rubbed for three days with the juices of <s>candravallī</s>.

children.text: ṭaṃkaṇena tu saṃyojya vaṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having mixed it with borax, the learned practitioner should make pills.
When blown upon in a furnace-apparatus, the mercury becomes bound into a <s>khoṭa</s>.
One pala of mercury should be put into oil of <s>bhallātaka</s> nuts.
As long as the oil is cooked, one should keep adding the milky sap of <s>ravi</s>.
One should stir it with an iron rod; the mercury becomes bound into a <s>khoṭa</s>.
One should rub an equal amount for three days with the juices of cotton-plant together with its root.
With borax in a quarter part, one should quickly make pills.
Powder of ant-hill clay, black gram, and wheat
should be rubbed equally with water, and from that one should make a crucible.

children.text: tadantarmarditaṃ sūtaṃ vaṭīṃ kṣiptvā dhamed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Putting the rubbed mercury-pill inside it, one should blow strongly.
That mercury too, placed in a blind crucible, becomes bound into a <s>khoṭa</s>.
There should be five times as much mercury, and twice as much white borax.
There should be the oils of white <s>vātāri</s> and soft horse marrow.
The practitioner should rub it for three days in a mortar with human urine.

children.text: tato godhūmacūrṇaṃ tu kṣiptvā kuryādvaṭīḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having added wheat flour, he should make good pills.
After drying them, he should afterward blow upon them with the addition of glass and borax.
The mercury becomes bound into a <s>khoṭa</s>, powerful and capable of every operation.
It should be rubbed for three days with the juices of <s>karkoṭī</s> and the tuber of <s>lāṅgalī</s>.
One should insert that mercury into the tuber of barren <s>karkoṭakī</s>.
On the outside of the tuber, clay should be smeared on all sides to the measure of a finger's breadth.
When dry, it should be cooked in a husk-heating for three days, turning it over.
Having taken it out, one should again rub it for three days with the previous tuber-juices.
By cooking in a heating-pit as before, mercury becomes killed.
Purified mercury should be rubbed for a week with the juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s>.
Having put it inside the hollow of a <s>kṣīrakanda</s> tuber, one should smear the tuber with clay.
One should cook it for a day in a dung-fire and rub it again as before.

children.text: kaṃde kṣiptvā pacettadvattato mardyaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Putting it into the tuber, one should cook it in the same way; then it should be rubbed as before.

children.text: kṣīrakaṃdodare ruddhvā mṛdā liptaṃ ca śoṣayet
children.translated_text: Having sealed it inside a <s>kṣīrakanda</s> tuber, smeared it with clay, and dried it,
one should cook it properly in a great heating-pit; it certainly becomes killed.
Mercury should be rubbed for three days with the juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s> and <s>kṣīrakanda</s>.

children.text: rasaṃ tatkrauñcapādāntaḥ kṣiptvā pādaṃ mṛdā lipet ||
children.translated_text: Putting it inside a <s>krauñcapāda</s>, one should smear the foot with clay.
One should cook it for a day in a dung-fire and rub it for three days with the former juices.
It should be cooked for a day in the same kind of heating-pit, then rubbed again and cooked.
This becomes mercury-ash, capable of accomplishing every operation.
Now the making of the 'mouth' of the bound <s>khoṭa</s>s that have been stated will be described.
<s>Vacā</s>, the tuber of <s>caṇḍālinī</s>, and the root of <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>,
together with sulphur and borax in equal amount, should be ground with the milky sap of <s>bhānu</s>.

children.text: caṇamātrāṃ vaṭīṃ kṛtvā pūrvasūte drute kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having made a pill the size of a chickpea, one should put it into the previously prepared mercury when molten.
Blowing steadily, one by one, seven pills should be added in order.
It consumes all metals as desired; there is no doubt.
Food should be given according to capacity, and again one should kill it as before.

children.text: mukhaṃ baddhvā niyuñjīta tāre tāmre bhujaṃgame ||
children.translated_text: Having bound its mouth, one should apply it to silver, copper, and lead.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ jāyate svarṇaṃ vedho daśaguṇo mataḥ
children.translated_text: All of that becomes gold; the transmuting power is considered tenfold.
This perfected formula has been explained after being properly seen from the mouth of the teacher.
Mercury, mica, purified sulphur, and the root of <s>tṛṇajyoti</s>,

children.text: tatsarvaṃ mātuliṃgāmlair dinam ekaṃ samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: all that, in equal portions, should be rubbed for one day with sour juice of citron.
One should smear purified copper plates with that paste.
Having sealed them, one should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then, after taking them out again, one should smear them once more.

children.text: evaṃ puṭatraye pakvaṃ tattāmraṃ kāṃcanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When cooked through three such firings, that copper becomes gold.
One should smear copper plates with the milk of red <s>snuhī</s>.
One should make them heated by fire and quench them in that milk.
In this way one should perform smearing, heating, and quenching seven times.

children.text: samāvartya tu tattāmraṃ divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after melting and refining it, that copper becomes divine gold.

children.text: rasakaṃ daradaṃ gaṃdhaṃ gaganaṃ kunaṭī samam
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s>, <s>darada</s>, sulphur, <s>gagana</s>, and <s>kunaṭī</s>, in equal portions,
should be triturated for three days with the milk of red <s>snuk</s>.

children.text: tena vedhyaṃ drutaṃ tāmraṃ nāgaṃ vā tārameva vā
children.translated_text: With that, molten copper, or lead, or silver is to be pierced.
With a thousandth part, it certainly becomes divine gold.
One should triturate <s>rajanī</s> for three days with the milk produced from red <s>snuhī</s>.

children.text: tena nāgasya patrāṇi praliptāni puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Lead plates smeared with it should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: punarlepyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ saptadhā kāṃcanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: They should be smeared again and cooked again; after seven times they become gold.
<s>Sthalapadminī</s> is to be recognized by the appearance of the leaf and flower of a lotus.
When it is broken, red milk flows out; having recognized it, one should then uproot it.

children.text: pāradaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ tālaṃ māhiṣī kunaṭī samam
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulphur, <s>tāla</s>, <s>māhiṣī</s>, and <s>kunaṭī</s>, in equal portions,
together with the previously mentioned <s>padminī</s>, should be triturated for seven days.
With that, copper pierced with a thousandth part becomes gold.

children.text: nāgaṃ baṃgaṃ tīkṣṇasāraṃ tāraṃ ca kramaśa uttaram
children.translated_text: Lead, tin, <s>tīkṣṇasāra</s>, and silver, each successively in increasing order,

children.text: pañcānāṃ tu samaṃ tāmraṃ sarvaṃ mūṣāgataṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: and copper equal to the five should all be placed in a crucible and blown.
It should be exposed through a bent tube until only the silver remains.
That silver becomes like ruby in color; one should melt it again.
It should be carefully pierced with the essence of <s>rasaka</s>, in a fifth part.
It becomes divine gold; this is declared to be a perfected formula.
One should dry in the shade and pulverize the five parts of red <s>citraka</s>.
That projection should be given into molten tin, sealing it again and again three times.
It becomes silver, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
Red <s>citraka</s> root, sour gruel, and purified mercury,
mixed with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil, should all be applied as a paste.
Heated copper plates should be sprinkled or quenched in that twenty-one times.
This copper should be twelve parts, and silver sixteen parts.
Having combined and melted them together, one should make plates from that mixture.
The roots of red <s>citraka</s>, ground with <s>bhallāta</s> oil,
should be used to smear the former plates, which should then be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ trisaptadhā kuryād divyaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: One should do this twenty-one times; it becomes divine gold.
<s>Nāginīkanda</s>, excellent mercury, and red <s>citraka</s> root
should be ground, and with that the aforesaid plates should be smeared.
They should be cooked in the same way with <s>puṭas</s>; thus they become divine gold.
One should fill a copper pot with oils produced from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>.

children.text: mukhaṃ ruddhvā kṣipedbhūmau pṛṣṭhe tuṣapuṭaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed the mouth, one should place it in the ground, with a chaff-firing constantly above it.
Thus, for a period of six months, one should fire it and then take it out in due order.
Outside, in a chaff-firing, one should cook it for three days, day and night.

children.text: tattāmraṃ hāṭakaṃ tulyaṃ samāvartaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: That copper becomes equal to <s>hāṭaka</s> gold; one should subject it to melting and refining.
When placed in <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> oil, everything becomes gold.
One should quench heated copper in the milk produced from <s>kṣīrakanda</s>.
With care, one hundred times, that copper becomes gold.
Sulphur, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, mercury, and red sandalwood
should be triturated continuously for three days with the juices of <s>rudantikā</s>.

children.text: tena tārasya patrāṇi liptvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: With that, one should smear silver plates, seal them, and cook them in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā kuryāt divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: If one does this seven times, it becomes divine gold.
The fruit juice of black or yellow <s>devadālī</s>
should be made equal with the juice of <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>; with that very mixture one should triturate
purified mercury for a week; then one should smear copper with it.
Having sealed it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then one should blow it with an intense fire.

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ tadrasaṃ kṣiptvā divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: When a tenth part of that elixir is added, it becomes divine gold.
Then, with the <s>Vasubhaṭṭa</s> elixir, one should sprinkle the well-heated metal three times.
The metal, split open like salt, becomes soft like wax.
The fruit and root of <s>devadālī</s>, and the juice produced from the fruit of <s>īśvarī</s>,

children.text: piṣṭvā tatkalkavāpena drutaṃ baṃgaṃ dṛḍhaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground; by projection of that paste, molten tin becomes hard.

children.text: bhūyo bhūyas tvayaṃ vāpyastāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: This should be projected again and again; it becomes fine silver.
On the fourteenth or eighth lunar day in the dark fortnight, or during an eclipse,
one should sow white <s>guñjā</s> in a human skull, in pure ground.
One should water it daily until it becomes fruit-bearing.

children.text: mantrapūjāṃ tataḥ kṛtvā puṣye grāhya phalāni vai ||
children.translated_text: Then, after performing mantra-worship, one should gather the fruits under <s>Puṣya</s>.
One pala of purified copper, white, and one hundred and twenty measures,
of each of the former seeds should be properly sealed and strongly blown.
That copper becomes silver, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
That silver becomes gold through a thoroughly purified, bound <s>rītikā</s> process.
Purified <s>tāla</s> should be triturated for one day with the juices of <s>bhūnāga</s>.
That lump should be placed in the middle of an earthen pot, and a portion of <s>tāla</s> should be confined there.
After that, copper plates should be sealed with a lid.

children.text: haṃḍikā bhasmanā pūryā ruddhvā caṇḍāgninā pacet ||
children.translated_text: The pot should be filled with ash, sealed, and cooked with fierce fire.
After five <s>yāmas</s>, one should take it out, combined with <s>niṣkaṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
It should be blown in a closed crucible, and that pill should be taken out.
Having gathered it after it has cooled in its own body, one should heat it openly in a crucible.
Three times one should throw into it the pellet whose opening is directed toward piercing.

children.text: mukhaṃ tasya bhavettīvraṃ śuddhaṃ baṃgaṃ dravatyalam
children.translated_text: Its mouth becomes sharp; it readily melts purified tin.

children.text: yadā na grasate tasmādvaṭī deyā punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it does not swallow, therefore the pill should be given again and again.
When the tin has digested a hundredfold, then copper should be given to it.
By a hundredth part of the molten substance, that silver becomes excellent.

children.text: gaṃdhakaṃ dhūmasāraṃ ca phaṭkarī ṭaṃkaṇaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Sulphur, dhūmasāra, alum, and borax should be equal,
and the kernel of the castor seed should be twice as much as all of them.
Earthworms should be equal to all; one should grind everything together.
Pills the size of chickpeas should be made; this is the celebrated <s>Vaḍavāmukhā</s>.

children.text: śuddhanāgaṃ drutaṃ kṣepyaṃ taile eraṇḍake punaḥ
children.translated_text: Purified molten lead is to be thrown into castor oil again.

children.text: drāvyaṃ drāvyaṃ punaḥ kṣepyaṃ yāvadvāraṃ śṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: It is to be melted, melted again, and poured back repeatedly, until it has been heated the required number of times.
Then, into that molten metal, a <s>Vaḍavāmukhā</s> pill is to be given.
With careful work two or three times, in this way the mouth of lead is produced.
It swallows all metals and various metallic essences.

children.text: yadā na grasate tasmād vaṭī deyā punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it does not swallow, therefore the pill should be given again and again.
Madhūka flowers, licorice, plantain bulb, ghee, and jaggery,
sesame oil, goat's milk, and honey should each be in equal measure.

children.text: tanmadhye kaṭhinaṃ dhātu tridhā siñcyāt sutāpitam
children.translated_text: In the midst of that mixture one should quench a hard metal three times after heating it thoroughly.

children.text: mṛdutvaṃ yāti no citraṃ sūtrayogyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It becomes soft, without wonder; there is no doubt that it is fit for wire.
With the juice called <s>Vasubhadra</s>, after heating well, one should quench it three times.
The metal, split like salt, becomes soft like wax.
One should remove the entrails of a very large frog there,
put powdered borax inside it, place it in a vessel, and bury it in the earth.
After three weeks, having taken it out, the metal goes to softness in that bath.

children.text: svarṇaṃ vā yadi vā raupyaṃ mṛdu syātpatrayogyakam ||
children.translated_text: Whether gold or silver, it becomes soft and fit for making leaf.
With the root of <s>tṛṇajyotī</s> and with citron juice,
one should grind mercury for three days; it swallows mica in an instant.
Fine powder of earthworms should be equal to borax.

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ tu drute nāge vāhyaṃ śataguṇaṃ dhaman ||
children.translated_text: That powder is to be driven into molten lead until it is a hundredfold, while one blows the fire.
When perfected, that becomes what is called <s>Guhya</s>; its swallowing-capacity will now be stated.
With realgar, sulphur, and mākṣika, ground with the liquid of earthworms,
one should coat the womb of a crucible with it and place the substance called <s>Guhya</s> there.
When it has been consumed there, one should add gold little by little, heating and heating.

children.text: grasate bhārasaṃkhyā tu mūṣā lepyā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: It swallows an amount counted by the bhāra; the crucible is to be coated again and again.
This releases it in molten lead; the secret beyond secret has been made known.
Earthworm and borax in equal measure should be made into fine powders.

children.text: taṃ vāhayed drute baṃge yāvacchataguṇaṃ dhaman ||
children.translated_text: One should drive that into molten tin until it is a hundredfold, while heating.
Then one should drive a hundredfold quantity of tin over that very substance.

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ dhamanneva grasate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Little by little, while heating, it certainly swallows; there is no doubt here.
Orpiment and rock salt in equal measure, ground with earthworm liquid,
should be smeared on the inside of the crucible; that tin is to be placed there.

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣipettasmin biḍaṃ dattvā dhamandhaman
children.translated_text: One should add the flux into it little by little, heating and heating.
In this way it swallows an amount counted by the bhāra; this is remembered as <s>Guhyavaṅga</s>.

children.text: drute baṃge vinikṣiptaṃ yāvatsaṃkhyā na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When it has been put into molten tin, whatever the number, there is no doubt.

children.text: tāvad drute na saṃdehaḥ siddhayoga udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So much indeed is present in the molten metal; this is declared to be a perfected formula.
Then, having put it in a buffalo horn, one should grind it and cook it with fire.
Until it becomes one niṣka, it is to be ground while adding more and more.
Then it becomes equal to mercury; taking that, and then an equal amount of it,
mercury, purified gold, and the essence produced from earthworms are to be used.
Forty parts of lead are to be ground with citron juices.
Having dried that ball, then, in a paste produced from earthworms,
one should first smear the inside of a crucible and enclose the ball in it.
One should heat it with an intense fire until nothing at all remains there.
It swallows everything that is given; this is the excellent formula called <s>Guhya</s>.
Now, therefore, I shall explain the excellent binding by a pill.

children.text: samajīrṇaṃ kṛtaṃ vyoma samato rasaṃ jārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made mica digested in equal measure, one should cause it to digest mercury equally.

children.text: ravisaṃkhyāṃśakaṃ śulbaṃ dattvā piṣṭiṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: Adding copper in twelve parts, one should make a paste.
Putting sulphur equal to grain-mica into the copper, one should grind it well.
Having made the two into the shape of a crucible, one should release the paste in the middle.
It should be wrapped in human flesh and likewise in black-gram paste.
The practitioner should cook it in linseed oil for the space of a month.
It is inexhaustible, a <s>Kāmadhenu</s>, and it brings about the fixation of tin.

children.text: pārade jāryaṃ kṛṣṇābhraṃ rukmam aṣṭaguṇaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: If black mica, to be digested in mercury, is combined with eight times as much gold,
colored with the hue of sulphur and wrapped in human flesh,
then smeared with black-gram paste and cooked in linseed oil,
this is known as <s>Kāmadhenu</s>, and it brings about the fixation of lead.
From mercury one should make a beautiful gold paste of one quarter part.
Having smeared the <s>Kāmadhenu</s>, one should apply it in molten lead.

children.text: taṃ nāgaṃ kurute rukmaṃ vāñchitārtheṣu siddhidam
children.translated_text: It turns that lead into gold, granting success in desired aims.
One should carry that <s>Kāmadhenu</s> pill in the mouth every day.
One would not be pierced by weapons and missiles, and would obtain a divine body.
Lead killed by realgar and joined with the king of mercury,
colored with the hue of sulphur and with an equal amount of gold, should be made to penetrate.
The piercing of silver is to be performed; it becomes divine gold.
One should coat sheets of <s>nāga</s> (lead) with <s>śilā</s> and the milk of <s>ravi</s>.
One should calcine them by the method of <s>puṭa</s> firing; it becomes excellent gold.
<s>Darada</s>, repeatedly impregnated in heat with ewe's milk and the sour group,
should be dried and ground in the hot sun through that procedure a hundred times.

children.text: sitasvarṇasya patrāṇi liptvā liptvā puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Having repeatedly coated sheets of white gold, one should cook them in a <s>puṭa</s> firing.

children.text: evaṃ trisaptadhā kuryād divyaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam ||
children.translated_text: One should do this twenty-one times; it becomes excellent gold.
With the root of the grass-kind and with the juice of <s>mātuliṅga</s>,
one should grind <s>sūta</s> (mercury) for three days; it devours <s>gagana</s> (mica) in an instant.

children.text: siddhairgaṇaiḥ suravarai rasasiddhikāmair baddhaṃ haṭhātparamamantrabalena taiśca
children.translated_text: By perfected beings, hosts, and the best of gods who desired accomplishment in <s>rasa</s>, it was bound forcibly by the power of the supreme mantra; and by them,

children.text: tasmād viśiṣṭam anujaiḥ kṛtamantrajāpaiḥ kāryaṃ tato rasavare varabandhanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: therefore, after mantra recitations performed by their followers, a superior binding should then be made upon the excellent <s>rasa</s>.
